articles.title: Autonomous orchestration helps Kubernetes keep up with AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Idle, then spiking: Why AI agents are breaking Kubernetes resource planning
AI agents are changing the economics of cloud infrastructure, and autonomous orchestration is becoming the way platform teams keep up. Agentic workloads sit idle and then spike without warning. That pattern leaves static resource settings either wasteful or likely to fail.
Container orchestration for AI is fast becoming the backbone of production AI, and agents are adding a new layer of strain. Compute costs are climbing and reliability problems are harder to contain because everything an agent does ultimately runs on CPU and memory, according to Yodar Shafrir (pictured), founder and chief executive officer of ScaleOps Inc.
“Agents and all the agent workloads pretty much made everything way more complex when managing infrastructure,” Shafrir said. “Eventually, all the complexity that existed before just got much worse. Today, the compute cost has grown dramatically. Everything that agents execute eventually runs on compute.”
Shafrir spoke with theCUBE Research’s Paul Nashawaty and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how autonomous orchestration lets ScaleOps adjust resources in real time as AI agents spike, cutting both costs and crashes. (* Disclosure below.)
Why autonomous orchestration fits the agentic era
Agents behave differently from traditional microservices. An agent waits for a human or another agent, checks with a large language model and then runs its task in a burst. Teams must provision for the highest spike while the agent holds its memory the whole time, Shafrir explained. When resources fall short, a crashed step has to rerun and burns tokens all over again.
“We actually see that agents crash due to not having enough resources 80% more often compared with traditional microservices,” Shafrir said. “The reliability is much harder to manage.”
For ScaleOps, the answer is to make resource decisions in real time. It adjusts allocations, replicas and node placement for every application, agent and Model Context Protocol server, which the company says cuts cloud costs by 70% to 80%. Customers such as Adobe Inc. and Salesforce Inc. build trust by first running the platform in read-only mode on their hardest environments, according to Shafrir.
“We understand for every application: What is it connected to? What does it communicate with? What is the business state of every application?” Shafrir said. “We learn from historical patterns.”
ScaleOps has also added a capability that lets other workloads use an agent’s resources while it sits idle. It also uses memory swap so an agent gets memory only when it needs it. The company says this makes running agents 90% more cost-efficient without moving off Kubernetes. Given the cost of always-on agents, Shafrir sees autonomous orchestration as the only workable model.
“We are now in a phase where humans and all the traditional scaling capabilities that existed in the past are pretty much irrelevant for today’s world because they’re too static and they require a human to go and configure them,” Shafrir said. “When things are so dynamic, it no longer works the same way.”
Here’s the complete video interview, part of SiliconANGLE’s and theCUBE’s coverage of KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA:

articles.title: Google Messages va enfin corriger un défaut qui agace ses utilisateurs
articles.text:
Fut un temps, Google Messages triait les messages des utilisateurs en fonction de deux onglets : « Personnel » et « Professionnel », ce dernier regroupant les communications commerciales et transactionnelles. Cependant, sans donner d’explication, Google a supprimé ce système de classement en septembre 2023. Les utilisateurs se sont donc retrouvés avec un historique de conversations qui n’était plus catégorisé. Peu pratique et peu clair donc, mais bonne nouvelle, l’entreprise américaine préparerait un nouveau système de catégorisation des messages.
Les messages bientôt répartis en deux catégories
Le média américain Android Authority a exploré le code de la dernière version bêta de Google Messages. Il a ainsi trouvé plusieurs indices qui indiquent un nouveau système de catégorisation des messages sur l’application. Les utilisateurs feraient face à deux sections : « Principale » et « Autres ». Vous l’aurez compris, la catégorie « Principale » regroupe les messages personnels, tandis que la section « Autres » rassemble les messages promotionnels, les éventuels spams ou encore les mises à jour. Une nouveauté bienvenue donc, vu que les messages ne sont actuellement pas du tout triés.
Les utilisateurs pourraient déplacer leurs messages
Toujours selon Android Authority, il serait possible de faire glisser manuellement un message d’une catégorie à l’autre. À titre d’exemple, un message important tombé dans la section « Autres » pourrait être déplacé dans la section « Principale », ou inversement. Deux boutons seraient ainsi proposés : « Déplacer vers Autres » et « Déplacer vers Principal ». L’application prendrait par la suite en compte ce déplacement de conversation en classant les futurs messages de l’expéditeur dans la catégorie sélectionnée. Un bouton « Annuler » permettrait de rétablir la catégorisation initiale.
Il reste maintenant à voir comment Google effectuerait le tri des messages. Le risque est bien entendu qu’un message important ou personnel se retrouve dans la section « Autres », et qu’il passe ainsi inaperçu. En fin de compte, Google reprendrait plus ou moins le système de catégorisation des e-mails d’Outlook, avec ses deux sections : « Prioritaire » et « Autres ».

articles.title: Senha mais usada do mundo em 2026 é velha conhecida • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Senha mais usada do mundo em 2026 é velha conhecida
Sequência numérica lidera ranking pela sétima vez em oito anos. Lista também inclui referências a jogos, memes e celebridades.
“123456” é novamente a senha mais comum do mundo, segundo levantamento da NordPass.
Estudo analisou credenciais expostas em vazamentos de dados de 44 países.
Referências a jogos, filmes, artistas e memes também aparecem entre as combinações identificadas.
A senha mais usada do mundo em 2026 continua sendo a conhecida sequência “123456”. Segundo levantamento da NordPass, a combinação liderou sete das oito edições anuais do ranking, mostrando que muitos usuários ainda recorrem a senhas fáceis de descobrir para proteger suas contas.
O relatório divulgado pela empresa na segunda-feira (16/11) analisou credenciais expostas em vazamentos de dados e repositórios da dark web entre setembro de 2025 e setembro de 2026. O estudo reuniu informações de 44 países.
Mesmo após anos de alertas sobre segurança digital, combinações previsíveis continuam entre as mais utilizadas. As senhas “admin” e “12345678” aparecem na segunda e terceira posições, respectivamente. Segundo a NordPass, essas três combinações mantêm as primeiras colocações do ranking há oito anos.
Outra sequência simples, “1234”, entrou no grupo das cinco mais frequentes. Já a palavra “password”, que significa senha em inglês, caiu da sexta para a sétima posição em relação ao levantamento anterior. O resultado reforça uma tendência observada em pesquisas anteriores.
No Brasil, o cenário também é marcado por escolhas previsíveis. Um levantamento anterior da NordPass identificou referências a Flamengo, Palmeiras, Santos e outros clubes entre as senhas utilizadas por brasileiros.
Como o levantamento considera apenas credenciais encontradas em vazamentos, os resultados não representam necessariamente todas as senhas utilizadas na internet.
A edição de 2026 também analisou a influência da cultura pop sobre as senhas. Entre as combinações identificadas estão referências a jogos como Minecraft e Roblox, o meme “skibiditoilet” e o jogador de basquete LeBron James, citado na senha “Lebron0319”.
Segundo a NordPass, essas escolhas apresentam riscos porque costumam seguir tendências conhecidas. Isso facilita a inclusão de nomes populares em listas utilizadas por ferramentas de tentativa automatizada de senhas.
Para reduzir o risco de invasões, a recomendação é utilizar combinações longas e exclusivas para cada serviço, além de recorrer a gerenciadores de senhas. Reutilizar uma mesma credencial em diferentes contas aumenta as possibilidades de comprometimento quando ocorre um vazamento.
Outra alternativa é ativar a autenticação de dois fatores, que exige uma verificação adicional durante o acesso. O uso de chaves de acesso, ou passkeys, também é recomendado. A tecnologia permite entrar em contas com recursos como biometria ou PIN do dispositivo, reduzindo a dependência das senhas tradicionais.

articles.title: El Apple Watch podrá mostrar por escrito lo que alguien dijo 15 segundos antes
articles.text:
El Apple Watch incorporó dos funciones que escuchan lo que dicen las personas cerca del usuario: Live Rewind muestra por escrito los últimos 15 segundos de una charla y Siri Recap resume las conversaciones del día. Están en versión de prueba pública y se lanzarían antes de que termine el año.
Las dos forman parte de lo que Apple llama Audio Intelligence y funcionan solo en el Apple Watch Series 12 y el Ultra 4, según la página de soporte de la empresa. También exigen un iPhone 16 o posterior con Apple Intelligence, la IA de la compañía.
Por ahora solo funcionan en inglés, no llegarán al inicio a la Unión Europea ni a China y, según Apple, no están disponibles para menores de 18 años. Algunas funciones tienen además un límite diario de uso.
Para activar Live Rewind hay que presionar dos veces la corona digital del reloj. En la pantalla aparece el texto de lo que se dijo en los 15 segundos anteriores, por ejemplo la lista de platos del día que un camarero acaba de recitar. El texto se borra si el usuario no lo guarda en la app de Siri.
Apple asegura que no guarda audio ni identifica a quienes hablan
Siri Recap trabaja en segundo plano. El usuario puede programarlo por horario o por lugar, o encenderlo desde el Centro de control, y al final del día encuentra en la app de Siri resúmenes con un título y puntos clave. Según Apple, se eliminan solos a los siete días si no se guardan.
Apple afirma que ninguna de las dos funciones crea grabaciones de audio. Según la empresa, el sonido pasa a una zona aislada del chip del reloj, se procesa y se descarta, sin que lo pueda consultar el sistema, una aplicación ni la propia Apple. Los resúmenes se generan en servidores privados que, según Apple, no almacenan los datos.
Para avisar a los demás, Live Rewind emite un sonido aunque el reloj esté en silencio y muestra una animación y un indicador de micrófono. Siri Recap, en cambio, no atribuye frases a personas concretas y omite datos financieros, identificaciones oficiales y contraseñas, aunque Apple admite que ese filtro automático puede no eliminar toda la información sensible.
Organizaciones de derechos digitales ponen reparos
La organización Fight for the Future, dedicada a los derechos digitales, cuestiona el consentimiento. “Que el usuario active la función no significa que todos los que están a su alrededor hayan dado su permiso”, dijo a Wired Reem Suleiman, directora sénior de campañas de la organización. “No sabemos qué está captando el reloj”, agregó.
Según Suleiman, funciones de este tipo normalizan la vigilancia ambiental, igual que las gafas inteligentes. Apple, por su parte, recomienda en su documentación tener en cuenta a quienes están cerca en conversaciones que puedan ser privadas o delicadas.
Pruebas de la prensa: útil a medias
Julian Chokkattu, de Wired, probó el reloj una semana y escribió que las funciones no le resultaron muy útiles. Según contó, el texto de Live Rewind se vuelve ilegible con mucho ruido de fondo, 15 segundos le parecieron pocos y usarlo frente a otra persona resulta incómodo. Su esposa le preguntó por qué no pedía que le repitieran.
Asimismo, Chokkattu halló en la app resúmenes de conversaciones que no recordaba: el reloj había captado videos de YouTube e Instagram que estaba viendo. Apple permite editar o borrar esos resúmenes. Con Siri Recap activo todo el día, el periodista no notó una caída relevante de la batería.
En una prueba para el sitio alemán heise online, el periodista Ben Schwan concluyó que los resúmenes sirven, como mucho, para refrescar la memoria. Observó que Siri Recap omitió conversaciones moderadamente privadas y que no se sabe con precisión qué decide incluir. Bloomberg tituló su reseña con una conclusión similar: las funciones aportan poco valor.
Macworld, que evaluó Live Rewind, encontró una transcripción bastante precisa en conversaciones cercanas y claras, pero con fallas cuando la persona hablaba desde seis u ocho metros. Su autor, David Price, sospecha que ese alcance corto responde a la privacidad, aunque no encontró pruebas de que sea deliberado.
MacRumors señaló que la primera versión de prueba de watchOS 27.3 salió el 3 de noviembre y que espera el lanzamiento general en diciembre, junto con iOS 27.3.

articles.title: Google a découvert des agents IA pirates à l'assaut de plusieurs sites français
articles.text:
Google tire la sonnette d’alarme au sujet des cyberattaques animées par l’IA. Dans son nouveau rapport AI Threat Tracker, le Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG), la division de veille du géant américain, révèle avoir franchi un cap inquiétant dans ses découvertes.
« Au cours du dernier trimestre, le GTIG a identifié pour la première fois des acteurs malveillants utilisant des outils reposant sur des LLM (NDLR : large language model) pour automatiser entièrement la découverte et l’exploitation de vulnérabilités, sans humain dans la boucle », écrivent les chercheurs de Google.
 Hackers are now using LLMs to continuously scan software updates, spot newly fixed bugs, and build attacks before teams can apply the fix — all without human involvement. That’s according to the latest report from the Google Threat Intelligence Group.
We're helping defenders…
— News from Google (@NewsFromGoogle) November 16, 2026
Des sites français dans le viseur
La France est en première ligne, indique Google. D’après les données récupérées par les chercheurs, les pirates s’en prennent en priorité à des sites basés en France. L’enquête a commencé par une erreur des pirates. Les chercheurs de Google ont alors découvert un serveur malveillant, laissé accessible en ligne par les truands. À l’intérieur, ils ont trouvé un outil de piratage. En s’appuyant sur différents grands modèles de langage, celui-ci fait travailler plusieurs agents IA ensemble dans le but de commettre des cyberattaques.
Les pirates s’intéressent « particulièrement aux sites web français liés aux secteurs des médias et du divertissement, ainsi qu’au secteur de l’éducation », détaille le rapport. Sur le serveur, Google a aussi trouvé des données dérobées aux victimes. Il est possible que les cybercriminels à l’origine de l’opération proviennent de Russie. En effet, l’outil de piratage basé sur l’IA était configuré en russe. Néanmoins, Google n’attribue l’opération à aucun groupe criminel ni à aucun État.
À lire aussi : Google corrige d’urgence une 8e faille Chrome exploitée par des pirates, installez vite la mise à jour
Des correctifs de sécurité transformés en armes
L’outil est redoutablement simple. L’outil « compare le code avant et après l’annonce des correctifs, analyse les résultats pour identifier des vulnérabilités potentielles, rédige des exploits et les exécute automatiquement sans intervention humaine », explique Google. En clair, les pirates n’ont même plus besoin de dénicher eux-mêmes des failles inédites. Il leur suffit d’attendre qu’un éditeur publie une mise à jour de sécurité, pour en déduire la vulnérabilité qui a été colmatée. Les pirates s’en servent alors pour attaquer les sites qui n’ont pas encore installé la mise à jour.
Les pirates « utilisent ces technologies pour mener leurs opérations à grande vitesse et à grande échelle, sans avoir besoin de vulnérabilités zero-day pour y parvenir », explique John Hultquist, analyste en chef du GTIG. Les hackers n’ont plus besoin de s’embêter à dénicher des failles inconnues. Ils se servent simplement du travail effectué par les chercheurs et les éditeurs pour arriver à leurs fins. Pour John Hultquist, « il est bien plus facile de procéder à la rétro-ingénierie d’un correctif que de rechercher une vulnérabilité zero-day ».
À lire aussi : « Ils se sont fait passer pour des membres de l’équipe » – plusieurs IA Gemini ont lancé une cyberattaque
Une course contre la montre
L’outil déniché par Google n’est pas un cas isolé. Les chercheurs ont aussi découvert que des cybercriminels et des espions ont exploité des outils de piratage dopés à l’IA, comme CAIRN, PentAGI ou CyberStrikeAI, pour faciliter les intrusions. Selon les chercheurs de CrowdStrike, quatre autres gangs ont déjà confié leurs cyberattaques à l’IA au cours des derniers mois. Google a cependant une bonne nouvelle. Selon l’entreprise, les IA exploitées par des hackers ne sont pas infaillibles. Certains des programmes d’attaque générés par l’IA n’ont tout simplement pas fonctionné comme prévu.
Selon Google, l’IA réduit considérablement le délai dont disposent les entreprises pour installer leurs mises à jour avant d’être attaquées. C’est désormais la période entre le correctif d’une faille, et son installation, qui est la plus exploitée par les cybercriminels. Google cite l’exemple de PaperCut, un logiciel de gestion d’imprimantes. Quatre jours seulement après la divulgation de deux failles, la société GreyNoise a repéré une campagne menée avec l’aide de l’IA contre des centaines d’organisations.
« Dans un avenir proche, les entreprises vont subir une pression considérable pour accélérer leurs cycles de déploiement des correctifs de sécurité et pourraient même devoir faire des choix difficiles pour suivre le rythme », prévient John Hultquist.

articles.title: Sony accélère le déploiement de son QSSR (au goût de PS5 Pro) sur PS5 classique
articles.text:
Sony poursuit le déploiement de son QSSR sur les PS5 classiques. Après Marvel's Wolverine et Ghost of Yotei, c'est au tour de Marvel's Spider-Man 2 d'en profiter. Et plusieurs autres jeux sont déjà annoncés, dont Control Resonant.
La PS5 classique n'a pas dit son dernier mot sur le terrain des améliorations graphiques. Annoncé en octobre dernier, le QSSR (pour Quick Spectral Super Resolution) continue de faire son chemin dans la ludothèque de Sony. Cette technologie d'upscaling assistée par l'IA s'inspire directement du PSSR de la PS5 Pro, mais dans une version « allégée », adaptée aux capacités de la console standard.
L'objectif reste néanmoins le même, à savoir reconstruire une image plus détaillée à partir d'une résolution inférieure, tout en améliorant sa stabilité et sa netteté. Le QSSR ne pousse donc pas le traitement aussi loin que son grand frère sur PS5 Pro, mais il permet d'obtenir un rendu plus propre, sans avoir pour cela à changer de machine.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Spider-Man 2 rejoint Wolverine et Ghost of Yotei
Après une première apparition dans Marvel's Wolverine et Ghost of Yotei, le QSSR débarque désormais dans Marvel's Spider-Man 2. La technologie est prise en charge dans les deux modes graphiques du jeu, Fidélité et Performance.
Un ajout intéressant pour le titre d'Insomniac Games, dont les environnements particulièrement détaillés et les déplacements rapides de l'homme-araignée mettent rudement à l'épreuve la stabilité de l'image. Le QSSR doit notamment contribuer à mieux restituer les détails fins et à limiter certains défauts visuels.
Cinq autres jeux vont bientôt profiter du QSSR sur PS5
Sony ne compte visiblement pas s'arrêter en si bon chemin, puisque plusieurs studios ont déjà confirmé leur intention d'intégrer cette technologie QSSR à leurs productions.
C'est notamment le cas de Remedy, qui prévoit de proposer le QSSR dans le récent Control Resonant dès le mois de décembre. Selon les développeurs, cette intégration doit permettre d'obtenir une image visiblement plus stable et détaillée. La vidéo ci-dessus permet de visualiser une partie des bienfaits du QSSR.
D'autres jeux sont également concernés :
- ARC Raiders (Embark Studios)
- The Finals (Embark Studios)
- No Man's Sky (Hello Games)
- Hell Let Loose (Expression Games)
Ces différentes intégrations doivent arriver au cours des prochaines semaines, au gré des mises à jour proposées par les studios.
Alors non, le QSSR ne va pas transformer votre PS5 classique en PS5 Pro, et tous les jeux ne pourront pas nécessairement en profiter. Mais cette déclinaison du PSSR a le mérite d'offrir une forme de « seconde jeunesse » visuelle à certains titres, sans imposer aux joueurs de passer à la caisse pour changer de console.
Concernant la PS5 Pro, depuis plusieurs semaines, la console est en rupture de stock chez de nombreux revendeurs (y compris chez PlayStation), et certains vendeurs n'hésitent pas à faire flamber les prix… jusqu'à 1 500 euros sur Amazon ! Et il y a fort à parier qu'un certain GTA VI, dont la disponibilité est fixée à ce jeudi 19 novembre, n'y est pas totalement étranger.
- Améliorations graphiques significatives
- Technologie PSSR efficace quand bien implémentée
- Efficacité énergétique

articles.title: Xreal Aura Review: Android XR combined with lightweight glasses delivers a true next-gen spatial computing experience
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
If you can get past the $1,000+ price of entry, the Xreal Aura really ups the ante for low-impact spatial computing.
Reasons to buy
- + Lightweight glasses
- + Powerful Computing Puck adds another form of input
- + Familiar Android XR interface+ Access to the vast Android ecosystem
- + Can be used with Macs, Windows, and SteamOS devices
Reasons to avoid
- - $1,099 starting price might scare off potential customers
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
The world of augmented reality (AR) and extended reality (XR) glasses is really starting to get interesting. This is particularly true of so-called “self-contained” systems that don’t rely solely on your smartphone or tablet to deliver content. The Xreal Aura, which was co-developed with Google, is the latest in the Android XR field, and it’s quite an ambitious project.
Although the Aura looks somewhat similar to previous Xreal glasses that we’ve reviewed, the AR goes a step further with a dedicated puck powered by a Qualcomm Snapdragon Reality Elite SoC, hand/finger tracking, and the ability to interface wirelessly with accessories like keyboards and gamepads. The Aura really promises the ability to leave your smartphone at home and serve as the only computing platform you need (with some caveats).
Design of the Xreal Aura
The Aura’s design is clearly an evolution of the Xreal One Series, but with a few key differences. You’ll find the main changes up front, where you’ll now find two forward-facing, high-precision tracking cameras mounted at the corners of the frame. These cameras are used to continually track your head position, giving you the best possible experience for 6 degrees of freedom tracking for your hands and fingers.
At the center of the frame, there is a fully integrated single high-resolution camera for capturing photos or video. This was previously a separate add-on module for Xreal One Series AR glasses. There’s a red LED that illuminates when you’re recording so that people around you are made well aware of what’s going on if they have objections.
Your primary focal point, however, will be looking through the lenses, which are augmented by dual Sony-manufactured micro-OLED displays. You get one micro-OLED display per eye, each offering 1920 x 1200 resolution, a 120 Hz refresh rate, and maximum brightness of 1,050 nits. However, there’s a major upgrade in the field of view (FoV), as the Aura expands to 70 degrees, up from 57 degrees on the One Pro.
The Aura is available in two SKUs to support the interpupillary distance (IPD) of a wide range of people. The Medium SKU supports people with an IPD of 60 to 66 mm, while the Large SKU ranges from 66 mm to 72 mm.
Given that the Aura is the flagship of Xreal’s AR/XR glasses lineup, it comes with electrochromic dimming for the lenses, which can automatically adjust transparency levels, or you can manually make adjustments (there are five levels of transparency available).
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The arms of the Aura look nearly identical to the ones you find on members of the One Series glasses. On the bottom is a red button, which, when pressed, allows you to manually adjust the brightness levels of the Aura. Directly adjacent is a rocker that allows you to control the volume. There’s another button on the top of the right arm that, when pressed once, takes you to the home menu. Double-pressing the button brings up the capture menu for taking pictures or videos with the forward-facing camera.
Bose-tuned speakers are also built into the arms of the Aura and feature an open-ear design so that you can remain engaged with what’s happening in your environment.
Xreal Aura Specifications
| Display | 1920 x 1200 per eye | 
| Display Type | OLED | 
| Brightness | 1050 nits | 
| Field of View | 70 degrees | 
| Refresh Rate | 120 Hz | 
| Degrees of Freedom | 6 DoF | 
| Audio | Dual open-air speakers | 
| Connectivity | USB-C, Bluetooth 5.3, Wi-Fi 6E, GPS | 
| Weight (Aura glasses) | 3.35 ounces (95 grams) | 
| Weight (Computing Puck) | 9.3 ounces (265 grams) | 
| Battery (Computing Puck) | 4,455 mAh | 
Xreal Aura Computing Puck
Xreal takes a two-pronged approach to hardware with the Aura. At a base level, the Aura is powered by the X1S Spatial Coprocessor, which allows you to experience traditional AR functionality with smartphones, tablets, PCs, and Macs, as you would with previous Xreal glasses.
But the real magic happens with the Xreal Computing Puck, which is a separate device that connects to the Aura using a USB-C cable. The puck looks and feels like a slightly oversized smartphone, albeit without a display. In place of the display, you’ll find a large touch-sensitive surface that can be used to interface with the Android XR interface.
The puck is powered by Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon Reality Elite Platform, which delivers 48 TOPS of AI computing power. It comes in 12GB RAM/256GB storage or 16GB RAM/512GB SKUs — our review unit was spec’d with the former. The puck features a 4,455 mAh battery that powers the glasses, and it even incorporates a fingerprint reader for authentication purposes in Android XR. The puck also fully supports Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3; the latter of which is essential for supporting Bluetooth accessories.
The puck is quite beefy, measuring roughly 5.85 x 2.85 x 0.5 inches and weighing 9.3 ounces. I had no issue just slipping the puck into my pants pocket, but Xreal also includes a detachable clip if you want to attach it to your pants pocket or other clothing. The puck also features a cooling fan to keep temperatures in check. Indeed, the device can get warm to the touch (after all, it’s basically a powerful screenless smartphone with a 4,455 mAh battery) during use – which explains why Xreal includes the clip and probably doesn’t want you putting the puck in your pocket, like I was prone to do.
Xreal Game Controller and Keyboard
My Aura review unit also came with an Xreal Keyboard and an Xreal Game Controller. Both connect to the Aura using Bluetooth and were easily set up by pairing them within the Bluetooth menu under Settings.
The keyboard is battery-powered and is recharged using a USB-C port at the top (just above the F7 key). It’s a nifty design that neatly folds when not in use. Interestingly, I couldn’t find a way to “lock” the hinged part of the keyboard when it’s fully extended. Because of this, you can’t use the keyboard sitting on your lap with your legs spread slightly apart, as the keyboard will simply collapse and fall to the floor if you apply any kind of pressure. You’ll either need to put your legs together or place the keyboard on a desk or table, which isn’t exactly ideal if you like the more “freeing” aspect of using XR glasses.
With that said, the keyboard is a lifesaver when it comes to text entry, be it for entering web addresses, writing emails, or anything that requires frequent use of the keyboard. It sure beats waving your fingers around to input text.
The game controller features an Xbox-style layout with four face buttons for gaming, two thumbsticks, a D-pad, and a Google Gemini/Home button. There are two shoulder buttons at the top and two triggers (with modes to function as microswitch triggers or Hall Effect analog triggers). There are also two remappable macro buttons under the shoulder buttons and two additional macro buttons on the underside of the controller (which can be turned off with physical switches).
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Not only does the controller feature built-in rumble, but it also incorporates a 6-axis gyroscope for aiming and finger controls and a 3.5mm headphone jack built into the bottom of the unit. But perhaps the most interesting feature is a magnetic faceplate that breaks into three pieces. The main piece covers the face buttons, D-pad, and thumbsticks. The other two pieces cover the hand grips. You can purchase separate pieces to customize the look of the controller if you wish.
I found the controller comfortable to use, with a nice textured plastic finish for your palms to rest on (the bottom of the controller features a similar texture, but has a rubber coating over the plastic for better grip). And although the controller is designed for Bluetooth use with the Aura, it does feature a USB-C port and a USB dongle for connecting it wirelessly to a PC.
Another nice touch is that Xreal includes a charging dock for the controller that plugs in with a lengthy USB-A to USB-C cable. The controller itself charges with four pogo pins mounted on top of the dock (or via USB-C if you prefer).
Setting up the Xreal Aura
After removing the Aura from its retail box, I wanted to get into the action quickly and didn’t bother initially charging the puck. I used the included USB-C to USB-C cable to plug from the left arm of the Aura into the dedicated USB-C port on the bottom of the puck. Next, I pressed the power button on the puck, after which the glasses sprang to life and began the setup process.
The setup process first had me perform a few gestures with my fingers to properly set up the viewing window for my eyes. Then, the setup program walked me through pointing, pinch, and drag-and-drop gestures to navigate through the user interface. It was also during this time that I was able to set up my Wi-Fi connection and log in to my Google account. Since I’m an iOS user and rarely, if ever, use Android, I couldn’t speed up setup by logging in with a nearby Android device. So I had to log in to my Google account by pointing and pinching with my fingers to enter my email address and password using the on-screen virtual keyboard. It was a tedious process, but I was eventually able to finish once I completed two-step authentication on my iPhone.
Using the Xreal Aura
After taking some time to get used to dragging and pinching through the Android XR interface using my fingers, the experience began to feel almost natural. I was able to pinch to open apps, have multiple apps open at once, and drag or resize windows in my viewing space on command.
I was able to access all the typical stock apps like Chrome, Gmail, and Google Photos, which, of course, carried over my favorites, emails, and photos/vidoes, respectively. I spent quite a bit of time going down memory lane, watching videos of my two sons when they were toddlers among the hundreds of videos I have stored in Google Photos. It was also great to be navigating around the UI or working in the app, then seeing a notification pop up telling me that an email had arrived. I would then pinch the notification with my fingers to open Gmail.
The possibilities of how you can use the Aura are almost endless, and you can even mix other computing devices into the formula. For example, I was able to plug a USB-C cable from my MacBook Air into the second USB-C port on the puck (that’s usually reserved for recharging the puck). In an instant, my MacBook Air’s display was mirrored onto the glasses in front of me. So I could have Google Docs open as I typed, while having the Android XR native Gmail and YouTube apps flanking the virtual MacBook Air display.
It’s a similar experience with handheld gaming consoles. I was successfully able to connect a Lenovo Legion Go S (SteamOS) and an MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ (Windows 11) to the Aura glasses without issue, enjoying a vast library of games in fully immersive glory.
The native gaming experience isn’t bad either; I loaded up games like Fortnite and spent an hour toiling around in Grand Theft Auto III for a nostalgic treat ahead of the release of Grand Theft Auto VI. The Xreal Game Controller made playing these games a breeze.
But I also used the Aura glasses for more mundane tasks. I was able to walk around the house, performing my usual chores, with a shrunken YouTube window playing videos in the top right corner of my field of view. True multitasking is at hand, folks.
I should note that open-air speakers sounded good, but not great. They sounded similar to the Bose-tuned speakers in the older Xreal One Pro. There's a good level of bass, and overall clarity is good. However, if you want a more immersive audio experience, the design of the Aura allows you to easily throw on a pair of headphones or wireless earbuds to compensate for any audio shortcomings.
Bottom Line
The Xrea Aura is a true workhorse when it comes to spatial computing. By putting the bulk of the computing hardware into a smartphone-shaped Computing Puck, you have a low-impact way of experiencing XR without the hassle of wearing a bulky headset.
You can navigate the user interface using your hands, or the touch service of the puck. And for more specialized tasks, Xreal offers its own-branded keyboard and gamepad accessories (although you are free to use your own Bluetooth-enabled accessories).
Not only do you have access to the vast Android app ecosystem, but you can also connect to devices running Windows, macOS, or even SteamOS.
There’s a lot going on with this device, and there are limitless possibilities for how you could use the Aura. The only problem is that most people don’t have limitless funds, so the $1,099 price tag of our review unit (12GB RAM, 256GB of storage) is sure to give many people pause. Stepping up to 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage takes the price to $1,299. If you add in the Xreal Keyboard and Xreal Game Controller, the total cost of our review unit comes in at $1,277 ($1,477 for the 16GB/512GB configuration).
That’s a lot to ask for what is essentially a niche device. However, if you want a truly immersive XR experience that is not weighed down by geeky-looking headsets, it’s hard to argue with what Xreal is offering with the Aura.
Brandon Hill is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware. He has written about PC and Mac tech since the late 1990s with bylines at AnandTech, DailyTech, and Hot Hardware. When he is not consuming copious amounts of tech news, he can be found enjoying the NC mountains or the beach with his wife and two sons.

articles.title: Intesa Sanpaolo Cuts ATM Costs With Quantum-Inspired Algorithms- EE Times
articles.text:
An ATM running out of cash is a problem customers notice immediately. Keeping too much money inside it creates a quieter problem for the bank: Funds sit idle, while replenishment visits add costs. Across hundreds of machines, deciding how much cash to deliver, where, and when becomes a substantial optimization challenge.
Intesa Sanpaolo claimed double-digit cost reductions from a new approach, without compromising service levels. The work emerged from the Italian banking group’s quantum computing research. The calculations, however, run entirely on classical GPUs.
That apparent contradiction gets to the heart of quantum-inspired computing. Researchers can borrow ideas from quantum algorithms and find useful ways to apply them on existing hardware. Whether a quantum processor will eventually improve on those results is a separate question.
According to Davide Corbelletto, quantum specialist and team leader of Intesa Sanpaolo’s Quantum Competence Center, what changed was the approach. “It’s a shift in the way you model the problem you’re trying to solve,” he told EE Times.
A new way of looking at the problem
Intesa selected ATM cash replenishment as a proving ground because it combined business relevance with technical suitability. Its broader outsourced network exceeds 1,000 ATMs. The bank validated the optimization system using a real network comprising hundreds of machines.
Using historical data, the team compared its approach against operational strategies and traditional optimization methods previously employed. Measures included costs, service levels, and the risk of machines running out of cash.
The team expressed the problem as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization, or QUBO, model. Decisions become binary variables, with their costs and interactions combined into an objective for a solver to optimize.
Corbelletto described quantum-inspired computing as starting with an approach conceived for quantum hardware, then reformulating it for classical execution. The adaptation may not deliver all the advantages anticipated from a future quantum implementation. It can nevertheless offer something useful today.
“But if this limited version of the solution is better than the classical one you were using, you still have a kind of advantage,” he said. “And that’s precisely what we demonstrated with the ATM cash flow optimization.”
The bank uses GPU-accelerated classical solvers. Corbelletto also identified FPGAs and specialized ASICs as possible platforms for quantum-inspired methods, depending on the application.
The reported savings establish improvement over Intesa’s previous approach. However, they don’t demonstrate quantum computational advantage or establish that a future quantum implementation will outperform the strongest classical alternatives.
Inspiration without quantum hardware
Banking is not the only area where quantum-inspired algorithms are being developed. A similar path appears in engineering research at TU Delft, although the mathematics differs.
In an interview with EE Times, Matthias Möller, a professor and applied mathematician, described composite material design as a problem involving discrete choices: Successive laminate layers can be oriented at different angles, creating a combinatorial optimization challenge.
The team he’s part of began work with a quantum algorithm and developed it into a quantum-inspired implementation using matrix product states, or MPS. He said Airbus is supporting further research to scale the initially academic work toward practical applications.
The terminology can suggest something exotic happening inside the computer. Möller offered a simpler description: “There’s no quantum magic in it. It just takes inspiration from how a quantum computer would work.”
MPS and the broader family of tensor-network techniques predate the current interest in quantum computing. Möller sees quantum research bringing renewed attention to them, including in computational fluid dynamics. Those methods can run on graphics cards or other classical hardware, although he cautioned that the CFD approaches he discussed are not production-ready.
Their usefulness must ultimately be judged against the application’s requirements. In discussing quantum algorithms, Möller argued that the benefit must be provable. That could mean faster computation or, in optimization, a guaranteed better solution.
Quantum-inspired methods offer a way to explore useful approaches on classical hardware today. Establishing where quantum computers themselves will excel remains an open research challenge, with progress needed in the algorithms as well as the machines.
“It’s not only hardware that has to evolve,” Möller said. “It’s also the algorithm or application side. There are some really hard nuts to be cracked there too.”
The whole workflow counts
For Intesa, the test begins with the ATM system. Quantum-inspired methods have already improved its cash replenishment calculations on GPUs, giving the bank a working solution against which to assess future quantum hardware. Introducing a quantum processor would require evidence of further gains across the banking process.
“Quantum hardware must demonstrate a clear end-to-end advantage in concrete optimization tasks, taking into account problem size, execution times, reliability, and integration with existing classical workflows,” Corbelletto said. For the bank, the relevant measure is whether the complete process improves.
“Preparing the data, encoding it, interfacing with classical systems, and extracting usable results may ultimately cost more than the quantum computation itself,” Corbelletto said. “Quantum computing will become commercially relevant only when the advantage survives the entire workflow and not just a benchmarked kernel of the algorithm.”
The challenge therefore extends beyond reproducing the ATM calculation on different hardware. A quantum implementation must earn its place against the available alternatives, including continuing improvements in classical optimization.
Even clearing that performance hurdle would leave another obstacle. A bank cannot build an operational dependency around a calculation that works only when experimental equipment happens to be available. Corbelletto argued that technical advances must be accompanied by sufficient capacity and dependable access.
“From an industrial perspective, the challenge lies not only in building a better quantum computer but in deploying enough of them to both guarantee high service levels for customers and comply with regulatory requirements regarding business continuity,” he said.
Classical hardware gives Intesa a route to service arrangements appropriate to its operations. Future quantum offerings must satisfy those operational requirements alongside the computational ones.
Preparing for the customer’s test
Intesa continues investigating applications spanning credit risk, fraud detection, derivatives pricing, and portfolio optimization. Corbelletto identified portfolio optimization as a candidate for nearer-term production because the team has developed a promising quantum-inspired prototype.
The bank also experiments across hardware platforms rather than selecting a presumed winning architecture. “Our starting point is always the business need rather than the hardware platform,” Corbelletto said.
Its ATM work provides a practical reason to continue. Investigating quantum methods can produce benefits before suitable quantum hardware arrives. But those benefits also establish a benchmark for the machines that follow.
“The key milestone will not be a laboratory record but a real-world banking use case where the quantum advantage survives the entire workflow, from data preparation to business outcome, and can be reproduced reliably,” Corbelletto said.
“That would be a much stronger signal than any individual hardware announcement.”

articles.title: Malgré son rachat imminent, SFR lance une nouvelle Box 10 avec WiFi 7, braille et e-ink
articles.text:
Pour “offrir le meilleur du Wi-Fi accessible à tous”, SFR lance sa nouvelle Box 10 avancée, mais abordable
En ce 17 novembre 2026 voici la SFR Box 10, la petite sœur plus raisonnable de la SFR Box 10+. De quoi profiter de la dernière technologie de WiFi à un coût moindre.
Alors que son rachat par ses concurrents est toujours plus proche, SFR ne compte pas passer ses derniers mois à ne rien faire. En témoigne en cette mi-novembre l'annonce du lancement dès aujourd'hui d'une nouvelle box pour l'offre SFR Fibre Power. Cette dernière, facturée 36,99 €/mois, accueille désormais la nouvelle Box 10, une version plus raisonnable de la Box 10+ lancée en septembre 2025.
Cette nouvelle déclinaison est certes moins musclée, mais elle permet de profiter de certaines avancées technologiques sans payer un prix premium, tout en modernisant la Box 8 à la traîne par rapport aux solutions de Free, Orange et Bouygues Telecom. L'objectif est ainsi de démocratiser, par exemple, le WiFi 7.
Une modernisation des équipements chez SFR, malgré la fin proche
Si cette technologie sans fil de dernière génération ne concernera pas tout le monde puisqu'il faut disposer d'un appareil compatible pour pouvoir en profiter, son arrivée dans un forfait Internet abordable reste une bonne nouvelle. Cependant, le WiFi 7 de la Box 10 est limité au bi-bande, quand celui de la Box 10+ (proposée dans le forfait SFR Fibre Premium à 45,99 €/mois) est triple-bande.
	
Cette nouvelle Box traduit notre volonté de démocratiser l'accès aux technologies les plus avancées du marché tout en fournissant un équipement écoconçu qui permet à chacun de réduire sa consommation d'énergie au quotidien.
Légèrement plus compacte que sa grande sœur, la Box 10 reprend la plupart des spécificités de la box haut de gamme, comme l'écran tactile E-Ink façon liseuse, sa conception économe en énergie et "écoconçue" à base de matériaux recyclés, son module de connectivité Thread, ou encore son marquage en braille.
En revanche, les amateurs de performances devront faire des concessions. Exit le débit montant et descendant jusqu'à 8 Go/s partagés, pour du 2 Go/s en téléchargement et 1 Go/s en montant. De même, les ports Ethernet passent de un port 10 Go/s et trois ports 1 Go/s à deux 2,5 Go/s et deux 1 Go/s. On reste toutefois sur des performances suffisantes pour la plupart des utilisateurs, basées sur une technologie fibre à la norme GPON et non XGS-PON comme la Box 10+.
L'offre SFR Fibre Power qui intègre cette Box 10 propose également un décodeur SFR Box 8 TV, un répéteur WiFi 7, les appels illimités vers les fixes et mobiles en France et 3 euros de remise sur une option TV ou streaming au choix (Netflix, Disney+, HBO Max ou Ciné+ OCS). Attention aux frais d'ouverture de service à 49€.

articles.title: AMD Completes Acquisition of Taalas to Advance AI Inference Innovation
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
AMD Completes Acquisition of Taalas to Advance AI Inference Innovation
AMD today announced the completion of its acquisition of Taalas, a pioneer in specialized AI inference silicon, further strengthening the company's full-stack AI portfolio and long-term inference roadmap. As demand for AI inference accelerates, Taalas brings differentiated technology and world-class engineering expertise designed to deliver breakthrough performance and efficiency for increasingly specialized AI workloads.
"AI inference is evolving rapidly, and customers need a broad range of compute solutions optimized for their workloads," said Vamsi Boppana, senior vice president of the Artificial Intelligence Group at AMD. "With Taalas now part of AMD, we're expanding our ability to deliver differentiated inference performance and efficiency, while strengthening our full-stack AI platform."AMD plans to integrate Taalas' technology into its accelerator roadmap and develop system-level solutions alongside AMD Instinct GPUs, complementing its broader portfolio of AMD EPYC CPUs, AMD ROCm software and the AMD Helios rackscale solution.
The acquisition also expands AMD's engineering presence in Canada and reinforces its commitment to advancing AI innovation and growing world-class technical talent.

articles.title: El Black Friday de PlayStation desploma el precio de casi todos sus DualSense: hay disponibles hasta ediciones limitadas con descuento
articles.text:
El Black Friday de PlayStation ha empezado con varios descuentos interesantes. Ya os contamos ayer la oferta que hay en PlayStation Plus, pero en esta ocasión nos vamos a centrar en los mandos. Porque sí, este mes de noviembre también es un buen momento para comprar un nuevo DualSense, ya sea para jugar con PlayStation 5 o en otra de las plataformas compatibles: tenemos disponibles varios como este Starlight Blue por 54,99 euros.
PlayStation 5 - Mando inalámbrico DualSense Starlight Blue - Exclusivo para PS5
Un mando inalámbrico cómodo y compatible con PC
El DualSense de PlayStation suele tener varios descuentos a lo largo del año, pero generalmente no como el de este Black Friday. articles.title: Recherches secrètes : Google ajoute un mode « temporaire » à son Mode IA, voici comment l'activer
articles.text:
Une idée de cadeau à garder secrète, une question médicale gênante ou encore une recherche ponctuelle qui n’a rien à faire dans vos recommandations ? Pour ce genre de requête, Google a décidé de lancer les discussions temporaires dans le Mode IA, la version conversationnelle de son moteur de recherche. La fonction est en cours de déploiement dans le monde entier, sur ordinateur comme sur smartphone, et dans toutes les langues où le Mode IA est disponible, dont le français.
Pour l’utiliser, il suffit de cliquer sur l’icône des discussions temporaires, en haut à droite de l’interface du Mode IA, puis de poser ses questions comme d’habitude. La session est alors « déconnectée de votre compte », explique Google : les réponses ne tiennent pas compte de vos préférences passées, les échanges n’influencent pas votre personnalisation future et ils ne sont pas sauvegardés dans votre historique. La discussion disparaît dès que l’onglet est fermé, et l’on retrouve ensuite son Mode IA habituel, sans avoir à modifier le moindre paramètre.
Temporaire ne veut pas dire totalement privé
Google ne précise pas, en revanche, si ces échanges sont conservés pendant un certain temps sur ses serveurs. La nuance a son importance. Dans l’application Gemini, qui propose une fonction similaire depuis l’an dernier, les discussions temporaires sont gardées « jusqu’à 72 heures » pour formuler les réponses et traiter d’éventuels retours, selon Google, même si elles ne servent ni à personnaliser l’assistant ni à entraîner ses modèles. Chez OpenAI, les discussions temporaires de ChatGPT peuvent être conservées jusqu’à 30 jours pour des raisons de sécurité. Une discussion temporaire n’est donc pas une discussion totalement privée : elle évite surtout que vos recherches ressurgissent plus tard dans votre compte.
À lire aussi : Google dévoile Gemini 4 Carbon, l’IA qui veut repousser les limites de l’IA
Cette nouveauté arrive alors que Google pousse de plus en plus son Mode IA, qui capte désormais une part croissante des recherches, au point de bousculer le modèle publicitaire du moteur aux États-Unis.

articles.title: Nvidia at SC26: Agents are the new scientists, and they need a lab - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Nvidia at SC26: Agents are the new scientists, and they need a lab
For most of its history, the high-performance computing market measured progress the same way: how fast a machine could solve a fixed problem. Rankings rose, a new system took the top spot, and the cycle started over. Raw performance remains the foundation of scientific computing, and Nvidia Corp. brought plenty of it to SC26.
But this week, Nvidia argued that speed at solving a single problem is no longer the right way to measure leadership. An equally important question now is how many times a researcher can go from hypothesis to result in a day, and what happens when the “researcher” is an artificial intelligence agent that never sleeps.
That idea ties together Nvidia’s bevy of announcements at the show. The company introduced open science models, a CPU-only supercomputing rack, a new HPC-specific GPU, a batch of CUDA-X libraries, quantum integration for the Slurm workload manager, a quantum co-design platform with IBM and Fermilab, and a co-packaged optics deployment at Lambda. It also marked CUDA’s 20th birthday.
Taken individually, these announcements look like a typical supercomputing show news payload. Taken together, they describe a stack built for a different user, namely the AI agent that reasons through a scientific problem, calls a simulation, reads the result and decides what to try next.
The news in brief
Here’s a summary of what Nvidia announced:
- Nemotron for Science packages the open Nemotron 3.5 Super VL model with LitmusBench v0.2, a new open dataset of nearly 50,000 chemistry-reasoning questions, and post-training recipes for building domain-specific science agents.
- The Vera CPU rack-scale platform packs 192 Vera CPUs, about 300TB of memory, and Quantum-X800 InfiniBand into a liquid-cooled rack designed for unaccelerated workloads, including climate and molecular modeling. Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro will ship it starting in early 2027.
- Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the Vera Rubin family, featuring more than 50,000 CUDA cores and sparse-data acceleration, with a 2028 release.
- New CUDA-X libraries, including cuPhoton, cuPotential and cuSpa, target applications across astrophysics, drug discovery, materials science and single-cell biology.
- Quantum: A modular codesign platform with IBM and Fermilab, a new error-correction decoder and quantum scheduling support in Slurm.
- Lambda is using Nvidia Photonics co-packaged optics switches to connect GB300 NVL72 racks that house more than 10,000 GPUs.
While each announcement is interesting, the more compelling story is what they reveal about where scientific computing is headed. I see five themes.
Theme 1: The loop is the new benchmark
Ian Buck (pictured), Nvidia’s vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, summed up this thesis when introducing Rubin HPC: “For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery.” This marks an important industry shift. Simulation used to be the end product. In an agentic workflow, it’s a tool call within a much larger loop of hypothesis, simulation, and refinement.
When an agent can generate thousands of candidate molecules or material designs, the bottleneck shifts from ideas to the time required to test them. That’s why so much of the SC26 news focuses on loop speed alongside peak flops. Nvidia says cuPhoton cut the time to correlate Event Horizon Telescope black-hole data from more than a month to eight minutes.
At Pacific Fusion, a Nemotron-powered agent running on the same system can analyze plasma simulations as they run, allowing researchers to steer the simulation in real time rather than waiting for it to finish. Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory is using Nvidia’s DAQIRI networking library to move electron-microscopy analysis into the experiment itself, so researchers can decide what to measure next while measurements are being taken.
All of these share the same idea: Shrink the gap between asking a question and getting enough of an answer to ask a better one. For researchers, this should change how they evaluate infrastructure. Single-job time-to-solution is an important metric, but time-to-insight per iteration is equally important and should be tracked.
Theme 2: Small, specialized and open beats big and general for science
The most important data point at SC26 may have come from a startup, not a supercomputer. Lila Sciences post-trained Nemotron with lab feedback, nearly doubling its accuracy on quantum-dot synthesis protocols to 61%, beating GPT-6 Astra’s 54% at what Nvidia states is 10 to 20 times lower inference cost. Therna nearly doubled accuracy over frontier models in predicting mRNA protein-expression ranges. Terray Therapeutics trained the model to extract reactants, products, and conditions from chemistry diagrams.
That’s consistent with what I’ve been hearing across my enterprise clients: frontier models are a great starting point, but domain-tuned open models often win on accuracy and economics in specialized fields. Science pushes this further than most industries for three reasons. Research data is often proprietary or regulated. Experimental feedback serves as a training signal that general-purpose models lack. Labs want models running on infrastructure they control.
That last point is why Nvidia optimized Nemotron 3.5 Super VL to run on a 128GB DGX Spark. KTH Royal Institute of Technology reports that an agent built on it fixed 81% of broken GROMACS molecular-dynamics setups in a single overnight run on a single Spark.
Nvidia releasing the dataset and the recipes, not just the weights, is important here because the model is a commodity, but the know-how to adapt it is what research teams have lacked.
Theme 3: Nvidia wants every processor and the scheduler that runs them
Nvidia is well-known as the industry’s top GPU provider, but it also offers a CPU rack with Vera. Nvidia is now targeting the part of HPC that has never been accelerated, a market x86 has owned for decades. In Nvidia’s own testing, Vera delivered 1.9 times the performance and 2.4 times the performance per watt of x86 on an OpenFOAM airflow simulation.
DKRZ, the German Climate Computing Center, has selected Vera for its HLRE-5 system. The new Fortran compiler beta isn’t all that sexy, but it’s an important piece. Huge amounts of scientific code are written in Fortran, and nobody wants to rewrite it. Removing that friction is how a CPU challenger takes share.
Across the portfolio, Vera handles CPU-bound simulation. Rubin HPC is built for sparse, memory-bound science rather than AI training. DGX systems sit alongside IBM quantum computers. Nvidia is extending Slurm, the open-source scheduler most supercomputing centers already use, to schedule QPUs alongside CPUs and GPUs using familiar commands. Nearly 30 data centers are now deploying more than 50 quantum processors, and Alice & Bob, IBM, IQM, Pasqal and Quantinuum have adopted the expanded Slurm.
Nvidia wants to be the company that coordinates whichever processor the agent needs next. An agent doing drug discovery might call a CPU-bound molecular dynamics job, a GPU-accelerated docking run, and eventually a quantum chemistry routine. The vendor that owns the orchestration owns the workflow. Owning the hardware still matters, but less so than before.
Theme 4: Quantum is becoming a systems problem
The quantum news deserves its own mention because the tone has shifted. Two or three years ago, vendors mostly talked about qubit counts. At SC26, the focus was on error correction, decoding, and integration, which are classical computing problems. Nvidia’s new TCBP-JOBS decoder, available in CUDA-Q QEC 0.9.0, delivers up to 13,000 times faster decoding for error-correction research and reduces some design studies from 12 weeks to 45 minutes. IBM and RIKEN’s hybrid quantum-classical chemistry work, which modeled protein-ligand complexes with up to 12,635 atoms, is a Gordon Bell Prize finalist.
IBM’s Jerry Chow discussed the opportunity: “Scaling quantum and classical together will open new frontiers in high-energy and nuclear physics and beyond.” Nvidia has long embraced a systems approach spanning a broad ecosystem of partners, and IBM adds to that. IBM doesn’t need Nvidia to build qubits; it needs accelerated classical computing to make those qubits useful. That’s a typical position for Nvidia, which becomes essential to quantum, regardless of which qubit approach wins.
Theme 5: Efficiency and resiliency are now science features
Energy used to be a facilities issue in HPC. Now it’s a research constraint because every watt spent on overhead is a watt not available for simulation. Nvidia’s Vera delivers twice the energy efficiency of x86 on the Weather Research and Forecasting model.
Lambda’s deployment demonstrates the same idea at the network layer. Across more than 10,000 GPUs, Lambda used co-packaged optics switches and observed network latency drop by about 4% at rack scale and up to about 10% at pod scale, with a median optics temperature of 36 degrees Celsius versus 51 degrees for pluggable optics. This approach is up to five times more power-efficient and up to 15 times more reliable than pluggables, and engineers can swap the light sources in the field.
As Nvidia’s blog notes, with agentic inference, a single network disruption can cause cascading latency across many agents. When the workload is a continuous loop rather than a batch job, uptime becomes a research metric. Lambda is also the first large-scale neocloud proof point for co-packaged optics, which I expect other GPU clouds will need to address.
The thread that holds it together: CUDA at 20
It’s fitting that Nvidia marked its CUDA software’s 20th anniversary at the same show. CUDA was introduced at SC06, and Nvidia reports that more than 11 million developers now build on it, with more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries. From AlexNet to AlphaFold, the pattern has been the same: hardware draws attention, while libraries create lock-in.
The agentic era raises the stakes for that library catalog. A human scientist might know a handful of tools well. An agent can call any of them, so the size and quality of the toolbox matter even more. Every new CUDA-X library is effectively a new skill for every science agent built on the Nvidia stack. That’s the competitive moat that AMD, Intel, and the custom-silicon players have to cross, and it deepened this week.
What research and IT leaders should be doing:
- Measure iterations, not jobs. Benchmark infrastructure by the number of hypothesis-to-result cycles a team can run per day, including data movement, scheduling, and analysis time.
- Start an open-model post-training pilot. The results from Lila, Therna, and Terray suggest that a domain-tuned open model trained on your experimental data can outperform frontier APIs in both accuracy and cost. Pick one narrow, high-value task and test it.
- Plan for heterogeneous scheduling. If quantum is on your roadmap, even in a research capacity, standardize on schedulers and interfaces (Slurm, QRMI, QDMI) that treat QPUs as another resource rather than as a special project.
- Put CPU-bound HPC back on the evaluation list. Arm-based CPU racks are now a viable alternative for climate, CFD and other unaccelerated codes, especially when power is constrained. Insist on testing your own applications.
- Treat the network as part of the science. Optics reliability and latency directly affect agentic workflows. Ask your cloud and infrastructure providers about their co-packaged optics roadmaps.
Final thoughts
Most of the performance numbers at SC26 are Nvidia’s own or those of its partners. Historically, I have found Nvidia’s numbers to be accurate, but buyers should validate them against their own workloads. Several key products, including Rubin HPC and HLRE-5, won’t arrive until 2028.
Every additional layer Nvidia owns, from CPU to scheduler integration to quantum decoding, raises the familiar question of how open an end-to-end stack can be. Nvidia’s response this week was a strong emphasis on open source: open models, open datasets, open libraries, and contributions to Slurm.
The bigger takeaway is the shift in what Nvidia is selling. For 20 years, it accelerated the computations scientists ran. Now it’s building the stack for an agent to run the scientific method itself: reason, simulate, measure, refine and repeat. If that model takes hold, the winners in scientific computing won’t be the companies with the fastest single chip. They’ll be the ones that make the whole discovery loop spin fastest. Right now, no one is better positioned than Nvidia for that.
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: Apple TV 4K 2026 : la puce A19 a un secret qu'Apple s'est bien gardé d'annoncer
articles.text:
La nouvelle Apple TV serait-elle pas assez performante ? La puce A19 n'est pas strictement identique à celle que l'on trouve dans les iPhone 17.
La nouvelle Apple TV 2026 cache un secret qu'Apple s'est bien gardé d'annoncer quand elle a été dévoilée. En effet, selon des données de diagnostic système, il lui manquerait un cœur sur sa puce A19.
Un cœur en moins
Des données de diagnostic partagées par l'explorateur de code pdfu indiquent que la nouvelle Apple TV 4K utiliserait une puce A19, avec un cœur efficient coupé. La puce compterait donc 5 cœurs au total, contre 6 habituellement, pour les versions commercialisées dans les iPhone sortis l'an passé, notamment l'iPhone 17.
Les fréquences maximales relevées sont de 4,26 GHz pour les cœurs performants et de 2,592 GHz pour les cœurs efficients. Le GPU, doté de cinq cœurs, atteindrait quant à lui 1,47 GHz. Il s'agit de fréquences maximales et non de mesures de performances.
Pourquoi une puce moins performante ?
À l'instar des MacBook Neo, Apple ferait en fait du recyclage avec cette puce. Si les MacBook Neo utilisent une puce A18 Pro défectueuse, avec un cœur qui ne fonctionne pas correctement, la marque à la pomme reproduit l'opération ici. Le cœur désactivé serait en fait défectueux, et le fabricant préfère le couper, afin de proposer des performances correctes, pour des produits qui n'ont pas besoin d'autant de puissance qu'un iPhone.
Ce n'est pas la première fois que la marque à la pomme utilise ce type de puces sur ses Apple TV, sur la version 2022 déjà, dotée de la puce A15, un cœur du CPU était désactivé.
Source : MacRumors

articles.title: Taipei 101 lit up in support of Jensen Huang — skyscraper adorned with messages of support following resignation as Nvidia CEO
articles.text:
Taipei 101 lit up in support of Jensen Huang — skyscraper adorned with messages of support following resignation as Nvidia CEO
Taipei 101 was lit up overnight with messages of support for Huang amid reports that there may be a route back to the Nvidia top job for him.
Following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, a Taiwanese skyscraper became the backdrop for a series of messages in support of the ousted founder, who admitted to having an affair with a woman who has been accused of being a spy for the Chinese government. The U.S. government has since announced a criminal investigation into the company the woman worked for, Megaspeed, over concerns it may have aided in the breaking of export controls related to Nvidia AI chips. Despite that fact, CNA reports that the Taipei 101 building saw messages projected onto its exterior on the night of November 16. The messages included “Taiwan ♡ Jensen,” “Family ♡ Friendship,” and “Thrive Together,” with the driving force likely to be Huang's almost celebrity-like level of fame in the country.
That celebrity status has seen public sympathy for Huang grow within Taiwan, with people within the country's technology industry coming together to fund the project. One technology worker reportedly said that the light show was supposed to “bring back Jensen Huang” and show Taiwan's concern.
That concern may not be needed for too much longer. Recent reports suggest that Huang could be plotting a return to the top job at Nvidia just days after he handed in his resignation. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have already thrown their weight behind the idea of Huang's return to Nvidia. The clamor to force the hand of Nvidia's board has also extended to the White House, with U.S. President Trump also calling for the former CEO to be reinstated. This is despite ongoing uncertainty over whether his love interest was a Chinese spy and, if so, how much Huang may have known about that fact. Trump, however, says that Huang did not put national security at risk.
For its part, it isn't believed that the Nvidia board is seriously considering allowing Huang to pick up where he left off pre-resignation. A source told CNBC that the company is focused on investigating Huang's conduct and a national security investigation and is not discussing his return. That investigation will no doubt also consider reports that Huang had another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive.
For now, Nvidia's former CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO. Kress hasn't had long to settle in ahead of the first big test — the company's first earnings call since the scandal will take place today, November 17.

articles.title: Microsoft rolls out new first-party models and updates to agentic AI continuous improvement - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Microsoft rolls out new first-party models and updates to agentic AI continuous improvement
Microsoft Corp. today rolled out new generative artificial intelligence models and updates to Foundry, the company’s unified enterprise platform that helps developers and organizations ground, test and deploy AI applications and autonomous agents.
Updates to Foundry IQ, part of Microsoft IQ, now provide an enterprise knowledge graph out of the box, delivering a full estate of unstructured and application data to provide rich context for building applications and delivering on essential use cases.
Microsoft also said Foundry now uses existing transparency and observability capabilities to help customers create learning loops. Internal evaluations allow autonomous agents to establish baselines for quality, safety, latency and cost, enabling continuous behavioral improvements.
This includes human annotations, now in preview, that allow experts to rate and comment on agent traces based on business judgment. It feeds back into an improvement loop. It’s combined with optimization tests against evaluations and comparisons against real-world results. Foundry now also has new capabilities to adapt to supported models with organizational data to apply reinforcement learning while Foundry runs compute.
Each improvement becomes the next baseline and teams can continue measuring results and test changes, allowing them to improve quality.
Microsoft’s updated decision model and first-party AI models
Microsoft today announced Decision-1.1 is generally available. It’s a fast, cost-effective model designed to make reliable decisions in software at scale.
The generative AI model can make decisions dynamically at low cost, rather than relying on hard-coded rules, while offering superior decision-making capabilities compared with large language models. LLMs spend a lot of time making decisions in routing, classification, prioritization, verification and workflow control by “thinking it through,” which is unnecessary. Decision models are designed to reach answers quickly within constrained definitions and provide calibrated confidence scores, allowing applications to defer when uncertainty is high.
The new model builds on the previous generation, Microsoft-Decision-1, released in October. The new model delivers a significant improvement in intelligence and speed at a competitive price.
The company said it’s built on a new base, Google LLC’s Gemma 4 26B A4, adding multimodal support so it can analyze images in instructions.
Microsoft also extended its MAI, a Microsoft AI first-party family of models added to Foundry for enterprise trust.
These models include the new MAI-Code-2, which can handle demanding agentic coding work; MAI-Code-2-Flash supports high-volume, everyday coding, so developers can choose between performance and cost. Both are now generally available on GitHub, with Code-2-Flash in private preview in Foundry.
MAI-Image-2.7 and MAI-Image-2.7-Flash are now in preview and offer sharper editing and more consistent image generation. These will help brands maintain a consistent look across campaigns at a lower cost.
In cybersecurity, MAI-Cyber-2-Flash is a purpose-built model for cyber efforts and available in preview in Codename MDASH – the company’s agentic code security system in preview for eligible organizations.
Microsoft Foundry itself now has an expanded model pool featuring the top 50 models, supporting a model router and AI Gateway for intelligence model selection. The Foundry also offers more than 11,000 models from OpenAI Group PBC, Anthropic PBC, Meta Platforms Inc., Mistral AI SAS, the open-source community and others.
The company said supported models can be evaluated and deployed in Foundry as part of the same continuous improvement workflow used for agents.

articles.title: SFR lance la Box 10 : le Wi-Fi 7 n’est plus réservé à son offre haut de gamme
articles.text:
Nous en avions découvert l’existence début octobre grâce à des pages d’assistance, elle est désormais officielle. SFR a annoncé ce mardi le lancement de la Box 10, disponible dès aujourd’hui avec l’offre SFR Fibre Power, facturée 36,99 euros par mois. Elle y remplace la Box 8, une box Wi-Fi 6 sortie il y a plusieurs années, et se positionne sous la Box 10+, le modèle haut de gamme lancé en septembre 2025 avec l’offre Fibre Premium. L’opérateur entend ainsi « démocratiser l’accès aux technologies les plus avancées du marché », selon Pierre Clément, directeur exécutif Grand Public et Entreprises de SFR.
Du W-Fi 7, mais en version allégée
La principale nouveauté de cette Box 10 est l’arrivée du Wi-Fi 7, mais seulement bi-bande. Il exploite les fréquences 2,4 et 5 GHz, là ou la Box 10+ plus premium ajoute la bande des 6 GHz. Cela reste toutefois une amélioration bienvenue et SFR annonce un débit théorique cumulé de 6,8 Gbit/s, soit 25 % de mieux qu’avec la Box 8 précédemment fournie avec cette offre. Un répéteur Wi-Fi 7 est également inclus pour étendre la couverture dans le logement.
Côté fibre, les concessions sont plus nettes et la Box 10 reste compatible uniquement avec la technologie GPON. Elle offre des débits jusqu’à 2 Gbit/s en téléchargement et 1 Gbit/s en envoi, loin des 8 Gbit/s symétriques de la Box 10+, qui profite du XGS-PON. La nouvelle box de l’opérateur au carré rouge dispose de quatre ports Ethernet, deux à 1 Gbit/s et deux à 2,5 Gbit/s. Contrairement à sa grande sœur, elle fait l’impasse sur le port 10 Gbit/s.
Pour les amateurs de domotique, on note l’intégration d’un module Thread pour piloter des objets connectés basse consommation comme des capteurs de mouvement, des prises ou des interrupteurs.
Un écran e-ink, du braille et un mode éco
La Box 10 reprend le design de la Box 10+, dans un format un peu plus compact. On retrouve un petit écran tactile à encre électronique, comme sur une liseuse, qui donne accès aux principales fonctions. Développée avec l’association HandiCaPZéro, elle porte aussi un marquage en braille, et sa connectique a été disposée pour être plus facile à repérer.
La coque est fabriquée en plastique 100 % recyclé, et les pièces métalliques contiennent 46 % de matières recyclées. Le mode éco programmable, activable depuis l’écran ou l’application SFR & Moi, permet de réduire la consommation électrique de la box de près de 40 %, selon SFR, qui annonce 5,9 watts en mode éco contre 9,4 watts en mode standard.
L’offre SFR Fibre Power comprend, en plus de la box et du répéteur, le décodeur SFR Box 8 TV et les appels illimités vers les fixes et mobiles en France. Une remise de 3 euros par mois s’applique sur une option TV ou streaming au choix, parmi Netflix, Disney+, HBO Max ou Ciné+ OCS. À noter que l’offre est assortie d’un engagement de 12 mois, et qu’il faut ajouter 49 euros de frais d’ouverture de service.
Ce lancement intervient dans un contexte particulier pour SFR, qui doit être racheté et découpé entre Bouygues Telecom, Free et Orange. L’opération est toujours entre les mains de l’Autorité de la concurrence, et aucune décision n’est attendue avant plusieurs mois. En attendant, l’opérateur continue donc de renouveler ses équipements.
