articles.title: Microsoft explica el falló en Outlook, Teams y más: “más del 80 % de los servidores no respondieron”
articles.text:
La explicación llegó de parte de Charles Lamanna, vicepresidente ejecutivo de Copilot en la compañía, a través de una publicación en X con un resumen del análisis de causa raíz.
“El incidente del jueves 12 de noviembre de 2026 fue provocado por tres factores principales que, juntos, causaron una caída global en la pasarela de red que da servicio a muchos servicios de Microsoft 365”, escribió Lamanna.
Un defecto oculto desde julio que nadie detectó
El origen del problema fue un fallo “latente” que llevaba tres meses instalado en los servidores sin generar consecuencias visibles. Según detalló Lamanna, se trató de una contención de bloqueo dentro de un proceso interno que provocaba que la máquina quedara fuera de servicio bajo ciertas condiciones de carga.
Ese defecto surgió como resultado de una corrección preparada específicamente para los servidores de la pasarela de red de Microsoft 365, sin relación con otros despliegues de Windows.
El cambio comenzó a implementarse en julio y se propagó de forma global durante varias semanas sin que se observara ningún inconveniente.
“Nuestras pruebas de carga habituales no detectaron el problema latente debido a la diferente mezcla de tráfico y SKUs utilizada en nuestros laboratorios de prueba”, explicó el directivo. El problema se agravaba en máquinas con más núcleos y hardware más moderno, mientras que los laboratorios de la empresa solían priorizar equipos más débiles y con menos núcleos.
Por qué se afectaron tantos servicios
Microsoft 365 mantiene dos sistemas de pasarela de red independientes, pensados para garantizar aislamiento y alta disponibilidad entre servicios.
Unas 15 horas antes de la caída, Teams se transfirió desde la pasarela alternativa hacia la pasarela principal, la misma que también da soporte a Exchange Online. Ese traspaso, parte de las operaciones normales de resiliencia de la compañía, incrementó la carga y modificó los patrones de tráfico habituales.
Al mismo tiempo, cerca del 14% de la capacidad de servidores de esa pasarela estaba fuera de servicio por un problema no vinculado, registrado el día anterior. Microsoft ya trabajaba en devolver esa capacidad mediante procesos rutinarios de mantenimiento, y aclaró que esa reducción “no tuvo impacto por sí sola”.
La combinación de ambos factores sí resultó determinante. “Tomados en conjunto, el aumento de carga y la capacidad reducida de servidores hicieron que la pasarela de red encontrara el error latente de julio”, señaló Lamanna. Las solicitudes se acumularon hasta que los servidores dejaron de responder, justo durante la ventana de mayor tráfico en Estados Unidos.
Los sistemas de gestión de tráfico redirigieron automáticamente a los usuarios hacia otros puntos sanos, un mecanismo que suele evitar interrupciones ante fallos de hardware, software o red. Pero esa redirección aumentó la probabilidad de que el mismo problema se replicara en los servidores restantes.
Así, en menos de dos horas, el defecto antes desconocido alcanzó a toda la flota de servidores y la dejó inoperativa. En su punto más bajo, más del 80% de los servidores no respondía.
Microsoft precisó además que, por un problema adicional, los compartimentos normales que aíslan las distintas particiones de capacidad no lograron contener la falla en cascada, lo que permitió que el impacto se extendiera a toda la infraestructura global de la pasarela de red.
Cómo Microsoft restableció el servicio
La recuperación demandó más tiempo del habitual porque, cada vez que los servidores volvían a estar activos, la demanda de tráfico acumulado los saturaba de inmediato y los dejaba nuevamente sin responder.
Los procesos automatizados de recuperación de la compañía no estaban diseñados para restablecer el servicio desde un estado de falta de respuesta tan generalizado.
A esto se sumó que, al tratarse de un defecto latente desde hacía meses, los mecanismos habituales de reversión, despliegue controlado y banderas de funciones no pudieron revertir el cambio con rapidez.
Una vez que los ingenieros confirmaron el origen del problema, Microsoft desarrolló una actualización que devolvió el código a su estado anterior conocido como estable. Para aplicar la corrección de forma progresiva, la compañía retiró grupos de servidores del servicio, aplicó el cambio, los reinició y luego los reincorporó de manera gradual, en bloques de gran tamaño que llegaron a superar el 50% de una región a la vez.

articles.title: Geometric Future Introduces the Eskimo Ultra 42 AIO and Squama Ultimate 3003-14 Fans
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
Geometric Future Introduces the Eskimo Ultra 42 AIO and Squama Ultimate 3003-14 Fans
Geometric Future, an innovative PC components and peripherals brand, expands its cooling lineup with the launch of high-performance Eskimo Ultra 42 AIO and Squama Ultimate 3003-14 fans. The Eskimo Ultra 42 features a 420 mm radiator, a 2600 RPM pump (1.5 L/min), and a 55.8 x 55.8 mm copper coldplate. Its CNC-machined aluminium housing has a mirror top with ARGB lighting. It includes three interlocking 30 mm-thick Squama Ultimate 3003-14 fans. Also sold separately, these fans deliver up to 106.27 CFM airflow and 4.72 mmH2O pressure using a patented daisy-chaining system. They feature Fluid Dynamic Bearings, a 3-phase 6-pole motor, 800-2400 RPM PWM control, ARGB lighting, and standard or reverse airflow options for high performance and clean cable management.
The Eskimo Ultra 42 is a performance-focused 420 mm liquid cooler designed for both cooling capacity and refined presentation. Its 27 mm aluminium radiator is paired with three 140 mm Squama Ultimate fans, and the pump block features a large, pure-copper contact surface that efficiently transfers heat from the CPU. The CNC-machined, anodized aluminium housing gives the cooler a premium finish, complemented by a mirror-like top surface and a narrow, diffused ARGB accent that adds lighting without overwhelming the overall design.Squama Ultimate 3003-14
The Squama Ultimate 3003-14 is a 140 mm performance fan with a 30 mm thick frame and a 9-blade design, producing up to 106.27 CFM of airflow and 4.72 mmH2O static pressure. It features a patented interconnect system for daisy-chaining multiple fans, Fluid Dynamic Bearings, a three-phase, six-pole motor, and PWM control. Geometric Future's ARGB lighting surrounds the frame, providing a soft glow that enhances the design without overpowering the build. Compatible motherboard software supports synchronization. Available in black and white, with standard and reverse airflow options.

articles.title: EcoFlow Stream 5000 Review: Less than a year after the Stream Ultra X, the new Stream delivers more capacity and greater safety in a smaller footprint
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Stream 5000 is EcoFlow's worthy successor to the Ultra X. It packs 5 kWh of storage into a smaller-than-expected unit, accepts up to 5,000W of solar, and delivers up to 3,000W of AC power. It also costs less per kWh than the Stream Ultra X. The catch is that it is not a plug-in kit and requires an electrician for installation.
Reasons to buy
- + 5 kWh of capacity at a lower cost per kWh than the Ultra X
- + Four MPPT inputs that accept up to 5,000W of solar
- + Up to 3,000W AC output, with installer sign-off or a Stream Gateway
- + Ten-year warranty and a claimed 10,000 cycles
- + Mixes with older Stream units, for up to 90 kWh in total
Reasons to avoid
- - Needs professional installation
- - Heavy at 45.4 kg
- - Not a whole-house backup system
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
EcoFlow Stream Ultra X: 30-second review
The Stream 5000 is the second generation of EcoFlow's modular Stream family. It follows the Ultra X I reviewed not long ago. Except that in many ways this is a very different proposition.
The Ultra X was sold on a plug-and-play promise. In the UK, that promise came with small print, and had the rug pulled from under it just before the regulations changed. The Stream 5000 drops the pretence, making it a home battery designed for professional installation, and its price reflects that.
Inside is a 5 kWh battery, a hybrid inverter and four MPPT solar trackers. Each tracker takes up to 1,250W, so the total solar input reaches 5,000W. That is two and a half times the Ultra X. This unit can output up to 3,000W of AC power once an approved installer signs it off or it is connected to a Stream Gateway. That is enough for a washing machine, a dishwasher and a tumble dryer, though not all at the same time.
Where the previous Stream hardware came in five different flavours, with the Ultra X at the top, this generation has boiled it down to just two options. The Stream 5000, reviewed below, and the Stream 5000 AC. The main difference is that the Stream 5000 has four MPPT inputs for solar, while the AC model omits them but keeps the same battery capacity and inverter. You can add extra battery capacity to both in 5kWh chunks. The Stream 5000 and extra batteries stack physically to connect seamlessly, rather than using an external cable like the previous design.
EcoFlow says you can combine the new units with earlier Stream products to reach up to 90 kWh, if you have somewhere to store that many devices.
The app does the thinking, as before. It watches tariffs, weather and usage, then decides when to charge and when to discharge.
The only disconcerting part is that the Ultra X and the 5000 came out about a year apart, which makes me wonder what they’ll release this time next year.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
That thought aside, the Ultra X was a brilliant piece of hardware that EcoFlow continues to sell, but for a modest amount more, the Stream 5000 goes that extra mile.
EcoFlow Stream 5000: Price & availability
- How much does it cost? £1,599 early bird, for the Stream 5000. £1,499 for the Stream AC 5000
- When is it out? Available now across most of Europe
- Where can you get it? EcoFlow official website and selected European retailers
EcoFlow launched the Stream 5000 with early-bird pricing, which is still active.
In the UK, the Stream 5000 is £1,599, and the Stream 5000 AC is £1,499, which is only £100 more than the launch price of the Ultra X, which had less battery capacity than either of these new batteries.
In Germany, the Stream 5000 starts at €1,399, and the AC version is €1,299.
The maths is where this gets interesting. At £1,599, the Stream 5000 works out at about £320 per kWh. The Stream AC 5000 comes in under £300 per kWh. My Ultra X costs £1,599 for 3.84 kWh, or about £416 per kWh. The smaller Stream Ultra, at £799 for 1.92 kWh, is exactly the same cost per kWh as the Ultra X.
So the bigger battery is the better buy, even if that is not always the case with premium kit.
Extra batteries cost £1299, and each adds the same 5kWh as the base units.
Competition is thin at this size. The Anker Solix Solarbank 4 E5000 Pro is the same capacity solar input and price in the UK and Europe. It stacks like the Stream 5000, but the maximum capacity is 40 kWh.
At the other end of the spectrum is the Tesla Powerwall 3, which offers from 13.5 kWh up to 54 kWh, though installed prices start at around £7,000.
A cost not included in EcoFlow's headline price, and it applies to all these products: the electrician. Retrofit installs of home batteries are often quoted in the thousands, though a unit this size should come in well under that if you have a relatively recent consumer unit.
- Value: 4 / 5
EcoFlow Stream 5000: Specs
| Category | Spec | 
|---|---|
| Battery capacity | 5 kWh (LFP) | 
| Max AC output | 3,000W (installer sign-off or Stream Gateway needed) | 
| Solar input | 5,000W max (4 x MPPT, 1,250W each, 60V max) | 
| Max charging power | 4,000W (Stream AC 5000: 3,000W) | 
| AC charging input | 3,000W | 
| Expandable capacity | Up to 90 kWh (with previous generation Stream units) | 
| Cycle life | Up to 10,000 cycles | 
| Claimed lifespan | Up to 15 years | 
| Warranty | 10 years | 
| IP rating | IP65 | 
| Low temperature charging | Activated below 10°C | 
| Noise level | 30 dB maximum | 
| Dimensions | 295 x 489 x 298 mm | 
| Weight | 45.4 kg (Stream AC 5000: 44.6 kg) | 
| Connectivity | WiFi, EcoFlow app, Gateway for larger systems | 
EcoFlow Stream 5000: Design
- Heavy but more compact than before
- Battery and microinverter in one
- Application controlled
The Stream 5000 follows a new, refined, and functional look. The curved black-and-silver plastic panels of the first Stream generation are gone, replaced by a metal exterior that is undoubtedly more resilient and noticeably more compact.
At 295 x 489 x 298 mm, it is physically smaller than the Ultra X, which measured 420 x 294 x 460 mm. By my sums, that is about 43 litres against 57 litres, even though the Stream 5000 holds 30 per cent more energy. EcoFlow claims it is up to 40 per cent smaller than comparable home batteries, but it’s also a good bit heavier too.
The Stream 5000 weighs 45.4 kg, or a fraction over 100 imperial pounds. That is 6.6 kg heavier than the Ultra X, and I thought that unit needed two people to easily move it.
One annoyance is that the cardboard box it arrives in has hand slots to help you lift it, but they aren’t remotely strong enough, and using them will undoubtedly tear the box.
Personally, I’d keep a dolly handy to move the box to where you intend to deploy it, especially if you are working alone or waiting for help to get it out of the box.
The unit has handholds that can withstand use, but extraction from the box is much safer with a second person around.
Like the Ultra X, the Stream 5000 is IP65 rated. That means it resists dust and water jets from any direction. A label on top suggests that, instead of just dumping it outside, you need a small lean-to roof above the battery for the heaviest deluges, which seems sensible.
My view is that for the winter, you definitely want this unit inside, if only to warm the room it lives in when it gets warm while charging. Conversely, in the summer, outside might be better.
If the weather gets exceptionally cold, when the polar vortex comes to visit, typically batteries don’t do well below certain temperatures.
Therefore, a battery that heats itself before it charges in the cold is a very good idea in a British winter. EcoFlow says low-temperature charging kicks in below 10°C, and the small amount of power that it uses to stay warm makes the cells perform that much better.
The Stream AC 5000 is the same box without the solar inputs. That makes it slightly lighter, at 44.6 kg. It also makes it simpler.
Two things stand out from the Ultra X design. First, the solar side is far more generous. Four inputs at 1,250W each is serious capacity. Second, there is no longer any hint of a socket-in-the-wall approach. This is a unit for a wall bracket, a clean installation and a tidy cable run.
Here’s the breakdown of what each Stream model offers for comparison.
|  | Battery Capacity | Solar Inputs | Solar Input | Max Expansion | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stream 5000 | 5kWh | 4 | 5000W | 90kWh | 
| Stream 5000 AC | 5kWh | 0 | N/A | 90kWh | 
| Stream Ultra X | 3.84kWh | 4 | 2000W | 22kWh | 
| Stream Ultra | 1.92kWh | 4 | 2000W | 12kWh | 
| Stream Pro | 1.92kWh | 3 | 1500W | 11.52kWh | 
| Stream AC Pro | 1.92kWh | 0 | N/A | 11.52kWh | 
| Stream Max | 1.92kWh | 2 | 1000W | N/A | 
The older Stream and the new 5000 designs diverge massively in their interconnection philosophy. On the Stream Ultra X, there are two special inputs that were designed to couple the battery to the mains and to other batteries, in an up-and-down chain.
But the Stream 5000 and its AC brother only have one of these connections, and EcoFlow subtly changed the design so you can hook up prior batteries using the same cable.
The single port on the 5000 is meant to connect it directly to a consumer unit or power gateway, and the batteries stack vertically to integrate electrically.
With just a single unit, unless you are concerned about theft, the bracket isn’t needed, but should you buy additional battery capacity that is added under the Stream 5000 to create a stack, using the bracket would be advisable to stabilise the assembly.
So how do you mix and match older hardware? Well, when you add a Stream 5000 to an existing solution, the EcoFlow software detects the new hardware and defines a ‘system’ where the independent parts work in unison. It’s not necessary for the older batteries to be physically connected to be used, and that also allows them to have their own rules regarding discharge and recharge.
One other change worth noting is that the Ultra X had two AC outputs, whereas the Stream 5000 has just one. But the total power delivery of the Ultra X over AC was only 1200W, and 2300W if you cabled two units together. But the single AC port on the Stream 5000 can output 2500W, making it much more useful.
- Design: 4 / 5
EcoFlow Stream 5000: Features
- 5000W of solar input
- Ten-year warranty
- Up to 90 kWh
Initially, I assumed the solar inputs on the Stream 5000 would be the same as those on the Ultra X, but they aren't.
On the Ultra X, each MPPT port could handle 500W and a maximum of 14A and 60V, with all four handling a maximum of 2000W, or about four 500W solar panels.
These specifications got a major overhaul on the Stream 5000, with each MPPT capable of accepting 1250W, 40A and 60V of input. Therefore, you can much more easily connect solar panels in series without overloading the system.
For testing, EcoFlow sent me two SUNPRO 500W panels with a maximum voltage of 33.38V and a maximum current of 14.98A. I couldn’t connect those panels to the Ultra X because of the amps limit, but I could connect them to the Stream 5000. And using a parallel configuration where the amps double but the volts stay the same, I could hook at least two of these to each MPPT pair.
Looking at these numbers, the sweet spot for panels on the Stream 5000 is 400W or 200W panels with an arrangement where the total watts is less than 1250W, under 40 amps, and volts are under 60. EcoFlow sells a 400W rigid solar panel which is rated at 13.79A and 37.1V, and each MPPT on the Stream 5000 could handle three of those in parallel, to hit 1200W of solar input in total, and 4800W in total with all four MPPTs used with 12 panels.
The panels cost about £150 each, so the panel investment would be £1800, but on a sunny day the system should be able to fully recharge the Stream 5000 in around 90 minutes.
That’s a game changer, certainly, but probably even more significant is the 3,000W output to the grid.
The Ultra X could manage 2,300W on its sockets, but only 800W back into the house.
Having given up the pretence that this is a plug-in solution, although you can run it plugged in with 800W output, either directly wired or via a gateway, this unit can output 3000W into the home electrical system.
There is, however, a condition. EcoFlow says the full 3,000W needs sign-off by an approved installer, or a connection to a Stream Gateway. Without either, expect 800W, just like the Ultra X.
The battery chemistry is LFP, as before. EcoFlow claims up to 10,000 cycles and a life of up to 15 years. That is a big jump over the Ultra X, which was rated for 6,000 cycles to 70 per cent capacity. The warranty remains ten years, but the chemistry of LFP should still offer 60% of the capacity after 10,000 cycles.
For those curious, 10,000 cycles equals 27 years of daily use. This unit is meant to have a product life of around fifteen years, according to EcoFlow, so two full recharge and discharge cycles per day.
EcoFlow has been smart about expansion. The new unit works with the previous generation of Stream products. That means anyone who bought an Ultra X can add a Stream 5000 later, up to a claimed 90 kWh in total. A 5 kWh expansion battery is also available, and for larger systems the Stream Gateway handles the supervision. EcoFlow says it can cope with an EV charger and heat pump too. I don’t have the gateway, an EV charger or a heat pump, but there is clearly some headroom in this system before you need to consider EcoFlow’s Ocean range.
Software is the other half of the story. The EcoFlow app is still the best in this part of the market. It tracks usage, tariffs, and forecasts, and adjusts the battery accordingly. A new Local Mode was released in September, which should keep the system running and controllable if the internet drops.
- Features: 4.5 / 5
EcoFlow Stream 5000: User Experience
- A great app now with free AI
- Get an electrician
- Add Solar later
My usual disclaimer applies. I am not an electrician. Anything here about wiring is my understanding, not a rule, or anything you can take to an insurer after your house burns down.
The key difference from the Ultra X is that EcoFlow is upfront about this. It says the Stream 5000 is professionally installed. There is no pretence of a plug-in option, and there is none of the grey area I had to wade through last time.
That also matches where the law is heading. Plug-in solar has become legal in the UK from 27 August, but the new rules do not cover batteries. You still cannot simply connect a battery to a spare three-pin socket and start storing energy.
Well, you can, but it wouldn’t be covered by current regulations.
Installation is relatively painless if you are a qualified electrician, which I’m not, and involves wiring the provided cable into a fused spur connected to a bi-directional RCD in the consumer unit.
I already had this facility in place from my Ultra X installation, but even if they look the same, they’re subtly different, and I also wanted to retain my two Ultra Xs, so I had an electrician make the changes.
The cost of doing that can vary massively, and is highly dependent on how old your consumer unit is. Before I got the Ultra X, I had an old consumer unit where circuits didn’t have their own dedicated RCDs, but I had that swapped out for a new design where each has an RCD, making this installation much easier and within regulations.
Once everything was wired, the EcoFlow Stream 5000 and both of my EcoFlow Ultra X units wanted firmware updates. And, after those changes were made, the EcoFlow mobile app registered lots of changes and new items which weren’t there previously.
With the Stream 5000 at the helm, the hardware was reorganised around a defined ‘system’ where the Ultra X hardware was merged into the collective solution. Although not physically tied to anything but the house electrics, this allowed the battery capacity across all three batteries to be synced, providing a system of approximately 12,5 kWH.
There are lots of minor changes in the app, but the one that most interested me was that where it used to need a subscription, the AI+ functions are now included for free. In theory, this should mean I can let AI decide when to charge and discharge each day, without having to guess. If you have spare time and love to tinker, then you aren’t forced to use it.
Like the Ultra X, the Stream 5000 follows anti-islanding rules. If the mains fail, it must stop feeding the property to avoid sending electricity to the grid, where someone might be working to restore power.
Those who want a fail-over mode where the home switches to internal power need to consider installing a gateway with that capability. However, the Stream 5000, even with a gateway, can only output 3000W of power, so you need to be careful about the loads if you are cooking.
There is a UPS mode that automatically kicks on the AC power during a power loss, but it can only output 2500W. There is a local mode now, but that's only for when the internet fails, not the power grid.
My system is missing solar, but the plans are in place, and the Stream 5000 is a big part of that. With the solar input on that unit, combined with those on my two Stream Ultra X devices, I have 12 inputs and the potential for 9000W of solar once I’ve deployed the panels to achieve that.
This is where the Stream 5000 becomes a critical component in this scheme. Five kilowatts of solar input means a decent roof array is on the table, and a larger array means more free power, and the 12.5 kWh of total batteries is big enough to carry my household through the more expensive times of the day.
My total daily usage is around 16 kWh, so that’s enough to consider exporting some to the grid between 4 pm and 7 pm, and I’ll certainly consider that once my solar panels are in place.
- User Experience: 4 / 5
EcoFlow Stream 5000: Final verdict
The Ultra X was a clever product held back by a regulatory grey area. Or rather, the government went soft on the plug-in part of the deal just before the regulations changed, unhelpfully.
EcoFlow has stopped trying to sell a home battery as a plug-in gadget. With the Stream 5000, it has built a compact, quiet, well-specified battery that does the job properly. It then priced it attractively and designed it to grow. It also works with the earlier Stream range to an extent, which is a nice touch for anyone who has already bought in, like me.
The weaknesses are few, but I need to mention them. It is heavy, needs an electrician to install it safely, and that adds to the cost. And if you want the whole house to stay on during a blackout, then this probably isn’t the right equipment for you, even with a gateway.
If you want a plug-in system with no electrician involved, none of this applies, and the Ultra X era products remain the nearest fit, with their own caveats. For everyone else, this is the better battery.
My only concern is that the leap from the Ultra X to the 5000 took less than a year, and what EcoFlow will release a year from now. I’m hoping their new compact model doesn’t change dramatically, and that we get a larger 10 kWh extra battery, or the 3 kWh pack mentioned at launch.
The arrival of the Stream 5000 could have made all my previous investments redundant, but it hasn’t. And, given how much of it EcoFlow has sold, the brand seems determined to keep customers on board with each new release. Which, considering how some others operate in the tech space, is a breath of fresh air.
EcoFlow Stream 5000: Report card
| Value | Excellent cost per kWh, before installation | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Design | Compact for its capacity, but heavy | 4 / 5 | 
| Features | Big solar input, strong expansion and more power output | 4.5 / 5 | 
| User Experience | Easy to configure and now has AI management | 4 / 5 | 
| Overall | The best got even better in most respects | 5 / 5 | 
Should I buy a EcoFlow Stream 5000?
Buy it if...
You want a proper home battery without a giant price tag
At about £320 per kWh before installation, it undercuts most of the market, and it still comes with a ten-year warranty.
You plan to add solar
Five kilowatts of solar input and four independent trackers give you room to grow. You can start with the battery and add panels later.
You already own Stream kit
It works with the previous generation, so you can expand an existing system rather than start again.
Don't buy it if...
You want plug-and-play
This is not that. It needs a qualified installer, and the UK rules are clear that plug-in batteries are not yet covered.
You need a full home UPS
Check the specification carefully before you commit, because this system isn’t built to handle all electricity needs should the grid fail.
You have a tired old consumer unit
Budget for an upgrade. It is a cost that will not show up on the EcoFlow price tag, but you still need to pay it.
Mark is an expert on 3D printers, drones and phones. He also covers storage, including SSDs, NAS drives and portable hard drives. He started writing in 1986 and has contributed to MicroMart, PC Format, 3D World, among others.

articles.title: La testosterona es apta para tratar el deseo sexual femenino, pero se receta con geles pensados para hombres
articles.text:
Paula Vázquez estuvo el pasado lunes 16 de noviembre en La Revuelta junto a Carolina Iglesias y Dulceida para hablar de los premios Ídolo. Sin embargo, como es habitual en este programa, hablaron de otros muchos temas que poco tienen que ver con el certamen y terminaron la jugada hablando de sexo. En ese momento, Vázquez aseguró que hasta hace poco tenía la líbido por los suelos, pero que desde que ha descubierto los geles de testosterona su vida sexual ha dado un vuelco en para bien. Al parecer, le ha ido de maravilla, ¿pero hasta qué punto funciona esto que dice?
Conociendo a la testosterona. La testosterona suele asociarse con los hombres, pues sus niveles son mucho mayores en el sexo masculino. Sin embargo, también se encuentra en el femenino y, de hecho, su déficit puede ser perjudicial a muchos niveles. En mujeres, suele alcanzar sus concentraciones máximas entre los 20 y los 40 años. Después, empieza a caer, aunque su declive no está directamente relacionado con la menopausia.
Entre otras funciones, la testosterona se relaciona con el deseo sexual, aunque no siempre su descenso en sangre coincide con la bajada de la líbido. Sin embargo, si lo tenemos en cuenta en conjunto con la caída de estrógenos asociada a la menopausia, que también provoca este tipo de efectos, no es raro que el deseo sexual se reduzca a partir de cierta edad. Dado que la testosterona tiene un papel tan importante en esto, se ha estudiado su administración en mujeres con bajo deseo sexual, con efectos que parecen cuadrar con lo que cuenta Paula Vázquez.
Con evidencia, pero no mucha. Hay varios estudios que apoyan la administración tópica de testosterona mediante geles que se frotan en la barriga, los brazos o las piernas. Paula Vázquez mencionó que ella se la frota en las muñecas, así que puede cuadrar. Es importante destacar que estos estudios van dirigidos a mujeres postmenopáusicas con un deseo sexual de causa desconocida. Esto significa que si el deseo sexual disminuye por el estrés siempre será mejor poner solución a ese estrés. Si no se conoce la causa, se puede probar con la testosterona.
Según explican desde Clínica Mayo, los estudios apoyan su uso en algunas pacientes, pero nunca antes de la menopausia, ya que no hay garantías de su seguridad en esa etapa. La presentadora gallega tiene 50 años, por lo que posiblemente ya haya pasado la menopausia y, efectivamente, sea una paciente elegible para este tratamiento.
Contraindicaciones y efectos adversos. No hay suficientes garantías de que la testosterona sea segura a largo plazo para mujeres con enfermedades cardíacas, vasculares o hepáticas, ni tampoco para las que han tenido cáncer de mama o de útero. Por eso, en esos casos está contraindicada.
En cuanto a los efectos secundarios, más allá de las complicaciones que podría generar en estas pacientes, en general la testosterona puede provocar acné, crecimiento de vello en la cara y el cuerpo y caída del pelo de la cabeza.
Sin medicamentos en España. Cabe destacar que ni en España ni en la Unión Europea existe un producto de testosterona aprobado para mujeres. En caso de que un médico considere útil su administración, puede prescribir geles masculinos a fracciones de dosis, es decir, un uso fuera de indicación. También puede pedirse una fórmula magistral con dosis dirigidas solamente a estas pacientes. Sin embargo, ambos casos son bastante excepcionales, no es algo que se recete ampliamente.
Otros tratamientos. Dado que no se han realizado suficientes estudios a largo plazo y que no está garantizada la seguridad de este tratamiento en mujeres premenopáusicas o con ciertos problemas de salud, este no suele ser un tratamiento de primera elección. Generalmente, se recurre a otras técnicas como la terapia sexual o la administración de algunos antidepresivos que pueden subir la líbido.
En mujeres que sí han superado la menopausia, antes de pasar a la testosterona se puede probar con dosis bajas de estrógenos; ya que, como hemos mencionado anteriormente, su declive también puede relacionarse con el bajo deseo sexual. También son habituales los estrógenos vaginales y el DHEA vaginal (prasterona), que tratan la sequedad y el dolor, causa muy frecuente de bajo deseo en la menopausia. Si duele, no apetece.
En resumen. Ponerse un gel de testosterona en las muñecas no es como aplicarse crema hidratante para no tener piel seca. Es un tratamiento con bastantes efectos secundarios y posibles contraindicaciones, para el que aún no hay suficiente investigación científica. Siempre deberá ser un médico quien decida si una mujer es elegible para este tipo de tratamientos y aun así es posible que no recurra a ellos como primera opción. A Paula Vázquez le ha ido genial para puntuar en La Revuelta, pero debe quedar claro que no es un tratamiento que cualquiera pueda tomar sin ningún tipo de cuidado.

articles.title: Meta leva multa bilionária por acessar fotos de usuários • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Meta leva multa bilionária por acessar fotos de usuários
Itália aplica punição de 805 milhões de euros (R$ 5,1 bilhões) por acesso à galeria de celulares sem consentimento específico.
A Meta terá de pagar 805 milhões de euros (cerca de R$ 5,1 bilhões) na Itália por acessar mídias e metadados armazenados em celulares Android sem consentimento específico dos usuários. De acordo com a autoridade italiana de proteção de dados, cerca de 20 milhões de pessoas foram afetadas pela prática.
Segundo a Reuters, a decisão define, além da multa, que a empresa de Mark Zuckerberg terá 60 dias para desativar por padrão o recurso envolvido e passar a pedir uma autorização separada para acessar a galeria. A empresa contesta e afirma que vai recorrer.
A apuração, vale mencionar, ficou restrita ao acesso às galerias para o recurso de sugestões do Facebook e não analisou o possível uso das mídias para treinar modelos de IA. A Meta afirma que não usa esse tipo de conteúdo para essa finalidade.
A investigação envolve uma função do aplicativo do Facebook para Android disponível desde 2023, que analisa fotos e vídeos armazenados no celular e apresenta parte do conteúdo como sugestão de publicação enquanto o usuário navega. O problema, segundo o órgão regulador, é que o aplicativo não solicita um acesso específico à galeria.
Na avaliação da autoridade italiana, a autorização única, acompanhada de um aviso genérico relacionado a diferentes funcionalidades do app, não deixava claro que as mídias também seriam usadas.
Dentro de 60 dias, o recurso deverá ficar desativado por padrão. Para habilitá-lo, o Facebook terá de apresentar uma solicitação separada, explicar que a função acessa a galeria do aparelho e informar ao usuário como desativá-la posteriormente.
A multa, segundo o órgão, levou em consideração o período que o recurso permaneceu ativo e a falta de cooperação da Meta durante a investigação. A penalidade equivale a cerca de 0,4% a 0,47% da receita anual da Meta, segundo a agência — em 2025, a companhia faturou US$ 201 bilhões e teve um lucro líquido de US$ 60,5 bilhões.
Em resposta à decisão, a Meta afirmou que considera a multa desproporcional e confirmou que recorrerá. A empresa argumenta que “trata-se de um recurso simples” de compartilhamento de fotos e nega que não há consentimento. “Os usuários precisam conceder permissão em seus dispositivos antes que a função possa operar, e podem alterar essa permissão a qualquer momento nas configurações”, afirma.
A penalidade recebida pela Meta está entre as maiores já impostas por autoridades italianas a uma empresa de tecnologia. De acordo com o The Guardian, em 2021, a Amazon recebeu uma multa superior a 1,1 bilhão de euros por violação das regras de concorrência, que acabou sendo reduzida após recurso.
A nova punição também chega poucas semanas depois de outra decisão de grande impacto contra a Meta nos Estados Unidos. No fim de outubro, autoridades do Novo México determinaram que a companhia pagasse US$ 25 bilhões por enganar moradores do estado durante mais de uma década sobre o uso de seus dados.
A Meta também contestou essa decisão e classificou a penalidade como um “imposto” sobre a liberdade de expressão.

articles.title: Black Friday Samsung 2026 : les meilleurs smartphones et tablettes reconditionnés
articles.text:
Black Friday Samsung 2026 : les meilleurs smartphones et tablettes reconditionnés
Pour peu que vous accordiez une certaine importance au marché reconditionné, vous n’êtes pas sans savoir que Samsung est la marque la mieux fournie côté seconde main, et pas seulement sur les Galaxy S. Au même titre, les tablettes Galaxy Tab y décotent fortement, tout comme les formats à part que sont les pliants et les déclinaisons FE.
Alors découvrez ici cinq appareils à surveiller pendant le Black Friday, avec un critère qui sera particulièrement important, surtout pour des appareils plus anciens : la durée de suivi logiciel.
Galaxy Tab S10+ : la tablette à viser en priorité
C’est certainement là l’offre la plus convaincante de la sélection. Sortie fin 2024, la Tab S10+ aligne une dalle AMOLED de 12,4 pouces à 120 Hz, une puce Dimensity 9300+, 12 Go de mémoire vive et un stockage qui démarre à 256 Go. D’autre part, sa batterie de 10 090 mAh peut encaisser plusieurs jours d’usage mixte (notez aussi qu’elle se recharge à 45 W). L’appareil est aussi certifié IP68 et le S Pen est fourni dans la boîte.
Mais son argument majeur reste toutefois ailleurs : Samsung prévoit de la suivre jusqu’en 2031. Autrement dit, vous achetez une tablette d’occasion qui restera à jour pendant cinq années supplémentaires.
Galaxy Tab S9 FE : l’une des moins chères, mais avec une date de péremption
La Tab S9 FE de 2023 reste, encore aujourd’hui, une excellente machine. Son écran AMOLED de 11 pouces à 120 Hz, sa puce Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, sa certification IP68, son lecteur de carte microSD et son S Pen fourni n’ont pas pris une ride, et elle affiche une forte baisse de prix, puisqu’elle a maintenant 3 ans.
Un point doit cependant être abordé, parce qu’il conditionne la durée de vie de votre achat : Samsung a prévu d’arrêter les mises à jour Android de la gamme Tab S9 entre août et octobre 2027, les correctifs de sécurité se prolongeant ensuite. La Tab S9 est donc à envisager si la remise est franche et si vous raisonnez à deux ou trois ans, pas davantage
Galaxy Tab S10 FE : la moins chère, et pourtant la mieux suivie
En voilà, un paradoxe intéressant : la Tab S10 FE, lancée au printemps 2025, est la plus modeste du trio sur le papier (dalle LCD de 10,9 pouces limitée à 90 Hz, puce Exynos 1580, batterie de 8 000 mAh), mais c’est aussi celle que Samsung accompagne le plus longtemps, avec un suivi annoncé jusqu’en 2032.
Alors certes, elle vise clairement la lecture, les séries, les cours et la navigation plutôt que la création graphique, mais il n’en reste pas moins qu’une tablette d’entrée de gamme reconditionnée qui reste à jour six ans de plus, c’est suffisamment rare pour être mentionné.
Galaxy S24 FE : le haut de gamme allégé
Maintenant que nous avons jeté un oeil à tout un tas de tablettes intéressantes, il est temps de passer aux téléphones : de ce point de vue, le S24 FE est la porte d’entrée la plus rationnelle vers l’expérience Galaxy S sans avoir à dépasser un budget trop conséquent. Il reprend l’essentiel : écran Dynamic AMOLED 2X de 6,7 pouces à 120 Hz adaptatif, puce Exynos 2400e, 8 Go de mémoire, et surtout un triple module photo complet avec capteur principal de 50 mégapixels, ultra grand-angle de 12 mégapixels et téléobjectif trois fois de 8 mégapixels.
D’ailleurs, ce téléobjectif est son principal argument : beaucoup de téléphones de cette fourchette de prix y renoncent habituellement. Sa batterie de 4 700 mAh est par ailleurs plus généreuse que celle des Galaxy S24 et S25 standard. En contrepartie, ses 213 g se sentent en main.
Galaxy Z Flip 6 : le pliant, là où le reconditionné prend tout son sens
Si une catégorie justifie l’achat reconditionné, c’est celle des appareils pliants. Vous savez pourquoi ? Parce que ces derniers se vendent très, très cher au moment de leur lancement, et décotent finalement assez vite, ce qui les rend plus accessibles avec un ou deux ans de décalage.
Ainsi, le Z Flip 6 de 2024 a gommé les défauts qui rendaient les premières générations un peu moins certaines. Son écran interne de 6,7 pouces descend à 1 Hz et monte à 120 Hz, sa puce Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 et ses 12 Go de mémoire le placent au niveau d’un haut de gamme classique, et son capteur principal passe à 50 mégapixels, accompagné d’un ultra grand-angle de 12 mégapixels. En prime, vous pourrez bénéficier de 7 ans de mise à jour.
Attention néanmoins à trois réserves à connaître avant de craquer : d’une part, la batterie de 4 000 mAh se recharge seulement à 25 W, l’écran de façade de 3,4 pouces reste limité face à la concurrence, et la certification IP48 protège de l’eau mais pas complètement de la poussière, ce qui est la contrepartie habituelle d’une charnière.
Alors, lequel choisir ?
Pour une tablette polyvalente que vous garderez longtemps, la Tab S10+ est le choix le plus sûr. Si vous visez une grosse remise et que vous changez souvent d’appareil, la Tab S9 FE reste séduisante. Pour un usage familial ou scolaire, la Tab S10 FE coûte moins cher et durera plus longtemps, à condition d’accepter un écran moins bon. Enfin, côté téléphone, le S24 FE est le plus complet pour le prix grâce à son téléobjectif, tandis que le Z Flip 6 reconditionné reste de loin le moyen le plus raisonnable d’accéder à un modèle pliant.
Maintenant, comme toujours sur le reconditionné, l’état cosmétique et la capacité de stockage feront autant varier le prix que le modèle. Ceci étant dit, faites bien attention à vérifier le tarif affiché sur la fiche produit au moment de l’achat, ainsi que l’état retenu et la capacité annoncée pour la batterie.

articles.title: AMD touts the advantages of native FP64 for HPC with its MI430X accelerator at SC26 — company says emulated FP64 is a poor fit for many HPC workloads
articles.text:
AMD attacks Nvidia's FP64 emulation at SC26, touts native double-precision on Instinct MI430X — says Ozaki schemes fit less than 10% of HPC workloads and triple memory use and emulated FP64 is a poor fit for many HPC workloads
AMD says Ozaki FP64 emulation is no replacement for the real thing when it's needed.
As Supercomputing 2026 (SC26) opens in Chicago this week, AMD is indirectly needling Nvidia about the lack of native FP64 data type support in its data center GPU products. FP64, or double-precision floating-point math, is widely used in the high-performance scientific computing and simulation fields that are the focus of SC26. For those customers, AMD is trumpeting the value of its latest Instinct MI430X accelerator for customers that still need native FP64, like national laboratories and supercomputing centers.
Over the past few years, Nvidia has reallocated die area on its data center GPUs to favor the lower-precision matrix math that boosts the operations needed for much of modern AI inference. That reallocation only makes business sense, as the total addressable market for AI compute has exploded while the demand for double-precision math in large supercomputing installations has remained flat by comparison.
To make up for the lack of native FP64 support, Nvidia has turned to techniques that allow it to emulate FP64 operations using methods like the Ozaki schemes. But AMD claims this kind of emulation is nowhere close to a replacement for native double-precision processing for a few reasons—hence continued development of specialized products like the MI430X.
For one, AMD notes that Ozaki emulation assumes that the workload in question resembles a dense general matrix multiply (GEMM). In its own application profiling, the company says "less than 10%" of HPC workloads perform dense GEMM operations, so this emulation is a good replacement for native compute. Dense linear algebra is the one common workload for which AMD says Ozaki emulation is a natural fit.
For workloads like sparse iterative linear algebra, stencils and hydrodynamics, high-order finite element analysis, Monte Carlo and particle transport, and classical molecular dynamics, AMD says developers still need strong FP64 vector performance for the best results.
Furthermore, even for workloads that map well onto GEMM operations, AMD says matrix sizes must be large in order to achieve the best performance, and that might also not be a given for every operation. The operands of those matrices also have to be sized well to the hardware, as incorrectly scaled operands can reduce performance. The FP64 vector math capabilities of the MI430X are insensitive to those operand sizing issues.
Beyond those stumbling blocks, AMD also notes that using Ozaki emulation methods can cause the memory footprint of an application to balloon, requiring up to three times more capacity than native FP64 would.
Since HBM capacity is directly tied to GPUs in modern supercomputing installations, fitting a workload to a machine that can only emulate FP64 operations could have cascading effects on the number of GPUs and compute nodes required, causing knock-on challenges for the floor area, power, and cooling required to support the system.
AMD says the high 432GB of HBM4 memory capacity per MI430X node allows its customers to provision fewer GPUs and compute nodes in a system, saving on networking, power, and floor space.
In addition to its FP64 HPC performance, AMD positions an MI430X-powered supercomputer as an AI inference platform for developing workloads that utilize those models as part of the research process. But there are some key differences between those systems and the Helios rack-scale accelerator powered by MI455X GPUs from the same CDNA 5 architectural family.
Each MI430X GPU offers 9.2 PFLOPS of theoretical FP4 compute performance for inference, but that should be understood in the context of the whopping 40.3 PFLOPS of FP4 compute from each AI-focused MI455X accelerator.
Beyond raw performance, the native scale-up domain size of four MI430Xs over AMD’s Infinity Fabric interconnect when coupled with a sixth-generation EPYC host CPU pales in comparison to the domain size of 72 MI455X accelerators in a Helios rack. AMD says this interconnect is optimized more for latency-sensitive operations rather than a massive scale-up domain.
Of course, every customer and user of such a system will have different requirements, and institutional supercomputing installations usually aren’t trying to do double duty as cloud inference providers.
For scientists and engineers whose AI models of choice work well within the 1.72 TB of aggregate HBM4 capacity and 93.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth offered by four MI430X's working together across the 12.3 Tbps of scale-up bandwidth available within such a node, the inference performance of each node is likely more than up to the task of the kinds of AI applications that need to be run alongside double-precision compute workloads.
In any event, the MI430X can already count several supercomputing design wins in its corner. The upcoming Discovery supercomputer at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, the Alice Recoque installation in France, the LUMI-AI system at Finland’s CSC, and the Herder system in Germany will all take advantage of the native FP64 support offered by the MI430X.
AMD’s continued support for native FP64, even as Nvidia retreats from that capability in its products, will doubtless be a point of pride for its architects and engineers, even as those institutional supercomputers will be dwarfed by both AMD and Nvidia-powered AI inference installations the world over. The company's semi-custom silicon design chops and chiplet experience give it the flexibility needed to tailor products like the MI430X to these specialized markets instead of pursuing a one-size-fits-all approach.
As the Senior Analyst, Graphics at Tom's Hardware, Jeff Kampman covers everything that has to do with graphics cards, gaming performance, and more. From integrated graphics processors to discrete graphics cards to the hyperscale installations powering our AI future, if it's got a GPU in it, Jeff is on it.

articles.title: Data intelligence lifts enterprise AI factory accuracy to 94% - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Dell puts a single gateway between enterprise AI agents and the data they crave
Data intelligence is becoming the deciding layer of the enterprise AI factory as companies learn that racks of graphics processing units deliver little value when agents lack trusted, governed context.
Neocloud providers built the first wave of large-scale AI systems, and core enterprise customers now want the same capabilities inside their own organizations. Dell Technologies Inc. recently extended its AI Data Platform with semantic and knowledge graph features aimed at that market shift. But both the challenge and the opportunity lie in pairing structured and unstructured data so agents get full context while maintaining guardrails and human oversight, according to Srinath Alapati (pictured, right), senior director of product marketing for AI Data Platform at Dell.
“The bottom line is if you feed the wrong data, you get the wrong outcomes,” Alapati said. “What we’ve found is in our own testing — by giving the right context — you can improve the accuracy from roughly 60% to like 94%.”
Alapati, Alison Biers (center), senior director of product marketing for compute, networking and global industries at Dell, and Adam Glick (left), senior director of AI solutions product marketing for compute at Dell, spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how Dell is tying data, infrastructure management and validated designs together to move enterprise AI factories into production. (* Disclosure below.)
How data intelligence feeds the AI factory
Enterprises can’t give agents unfettered access to their systems, which is where Dell’s newly announced Agentic Data Gateway fits. The gateway sits in the orchestration layer as a single point of control, backed by a Model Context Protocol server, Alapati explained. Storage intelligence tells customers what data they hold, who owns it and how large it is, while Dell’s new data intelligence capabilities track lineage and provenance. Hybrid workflows extend that model across the edge, the cloud and the data center, where companies can struggle to meet the data consolidation requirements of other data platform providers.
“They want you to bring all the data to wherever the platform is. That’s not always possible,” Alapati said. “Number one, it’s super expensive. Two is data is always being generated. It’s a never-ending game. You can’t always keep bringing in data, consolidating data. What we do is we only send metadata … That way your data stays where you want to be.”
On the infrastructure side, Dell OpenManage Rack Scale extends management beyond compute endpoints to the network fabric, power and cooling. That gives operators a single operational plane from day zero through day two, according to Biers. A rebuilt, intent-based Dell Fabric Manager replaces the company’s SmartFabric Manager, and Dell’s PowerRack systems treat the full rack as the unit of deployment.
“It is literally six hours from the time it hits your loading dock to full production,” Biers said. “Something that used to take maybe months and months [is] now cut in half, maybe even less.”
More than 6,500 customers now use the Dell AI Factory, and a growing share are core enterprises asking for help putting AI to work, Glick noted. Validated designs built with Nvidia Corp. and other partners cover both the hardware and the full software stack, and Dell is expanding its labs to keep pace with independent software companies joining the ecosystem. Compute still draws most of the attention, but that is only one part of a larger system.
“If you’ve got a factory, compute is your assembly line. It’s the important part,” Glick said. “It’s what you think of when you think of ‘factory’, but that assembly line doesn’t run if you don’t have a warehouse that’s feeding it the raw materials — that’s the data that goes into it.”

articles.title: Half of businesses run workloads in the wrong place — mainly because they can't be bothered to change their ways
articles.text:
Half of businesses run workloads in the wrong place — mainly because they can't be bothered to change their ways
Changing cloud is just too complex
- Unsuitable cloud infrastructure is adding latency and reducing performance
- Enterprises worry they'd have to re-architecture applications just to move
- IT leaders admit they'd like to move, but they just can't handle the complexity
We're already familiar with lifting workloads out of certain environments in favor of digital sovereignty, but new Akamai research has revealed that half of enterprises are running workloads in suboptimal cloud locations despite knowing that alternatives offer better performance or cost.
The report notes that traditional cloud architecture is starting to struggle with modern applications, including real-time APIs, AI and more.
In fact, four in five (82%) enterprises are now missing response time targets for business-critical interactive workloads – but they might be reluctant to change just out of pure simplicity.
Enterprises don't want the hassle of moving cloud providers
Akamai found that storing and processing data in different geographic locations (41%) and longer-than-ideal physical distances between end users and compute (38%) are to blame for these response time issues. But for many, accepting these trade-offs might be more acceptable than migrating workloads to an entirely new cloud vendor.
"As real-time interactions, conversational AI, and microservices become standard, running compute far from where data lives creates delays and inefficiencies that organizations can no longer sustain," Akamai Cloud Product Marketing VP Ari Weil explained.
Four in five (79%) worry doing this could take days, or more, but it's the investments into building applications around the current cloud provider that could be the biggest headache. Two in five (38%) say workloads would need to be re-architected before they can be relocated, with 8% worried they wouldn't even be able to move workloads at all once they've been deployed.
Half of the enterprises Akamai surveyed admitted they've left workloads in non-ideal geographic locations just because relocating them would be too expensive, complicated or disruptive. But if it were easier, three-quarters of IT leaders say they'd deploy compute resources to more geographic locations to reduce latency, improve performance and expand into new markets.

Akamai can't exactly urge enterprises to consider alternative cloud vendors and infrastructure given the circumstances, but the report certainly highlights how interconnected and dependent our tech stacks have become.

articles.title: Mais à quoi peut bien servir l'écran arrière du Xiaomi 18 Pro ?
articles.text:
À l’heure où la quasi-totalité des smartphones haut de gamme se ressemblent, Xiaomi se démarque en intégrant une dalle externe directement sur le bloc photo du Xiaomi 18 Pro. Si l’effet de surprise fonctionne au déballage, la question de l’utilité réelle se pose rapidement. À l’usage, trois fonctionnalités sortent clairement du lot.
https://www.youtube.com/shorts/3VX7iJIqPmc
Le compagnon idéal pour la création de contenu
C’est l’usage le plus pragmatique, et sans doute le plus convaincant. Cet écran arrière fait office de moniteur de contrôle permanent lorsqu’on utilise les capteurs principaux pour se filmer ou se prendre en photo. Fini la perte de qualité inhérente aux caméras frontales : on profite des meilleurs capteurs du téléphone tout en gardant un œil sur son cadrage.
L’interface permet de lancer l’enregistrement vidéo directement depuis le dos de l’appareil et d’ajuster le niveau de zoom à la volée. Pour les créateurs de contenu ou ceux qui utilisent leur smartphone comme caméra d’appoint, le gain de confort et de rapidité est immédiat.
Une touche de personnalisation décalée
Au-delà de la productivité, Xiaomi assume un côté ludique. HyperOS 4 permet d’afficher des animations interactives, notamment de petits animaux virtuels particulièrement réussis qui réagissent au dos du téléphone. Un détail purement cosmétique, certes, mais qui donne au terminal une vraie personnalité et fait sourire autour de soi à chaque fois qu’on le pose face contre table. Un argument qui ne suffira pas à lui seul à justifier les 1 400 euros demandés pour le smartphone, mais qui participe au plaisir d’utilisation.
Des mini-applications générées à la volée par Gemini
C’est probablement la fonctionnalité la plus impressionnante sur le plan technique. En plus des quelques widgets préinstallés (comme un mini-piano ou un jeu de tape-taupe), Xiaomi intègre directement Gemini pour permettre aux utilisateurs de générer leurs propres mini-applications sur mesure pour cet écran secondaire.
Il suffit de décrire l’outil souhaité pour que l’IA se charge du développement. À titre d’exemple, nous avons pu générer un minuteur Pomodoro habillé d’une interface fantasy en quelques lignes de texte. Il faut toutefois s’armer d’un peu de patience : le traitement du prompt et la génération du code prennent entre quatre et cinq minutes. Un délai raisonnable au vu du résultat, d’autant que la fonctionnalité est proposée gratuitement pour le moment.
En résumé, loin d’être un simple artifice marketing, l’écran dorsal du Xiaomi 18 Pro trouve sa légitimité grâce à une intégration logicielle intelligente, mêlant création vidéo de haute volée et personnalisation dopée à l’intelligence artificielle.

articles.title: Un ciberataque alcanzó a 178 sitios de todo el mundo, incluidos BBC, CNN, Zoom e IKEA, para robar criptomonedas e infectar iPhones
articles.text:
El 16 de noviembre, un código malicioso se ejecutó en las páginas de 178 organizaciones, entre ellas Zoom, BBC, CNN, Salesforce, IKEA, HSBC y Equifax, según la empresa de seguridad Report URI. El ciberataque intentaba robar criptomonedas, copiar datos de tarjetas e infectar iPhones y iPads.
El investigador Scott Helme, fundador de Report URI, explicó que los atacantes no vulneraron cada sitio por separado. Escribieron su código en Optimizely Web, una plataforma que las empresas usan para probar distintas versiones de sus páginas. Como el script llegaba desde el servidor de Optimizely, los sitios lo trataban como confiable.
Helme dijo que no se sabe cómo los atacantes obtuvieron acceso a tantas cuentas de clientes sin relación entre sí. Precisó que el servidor de Optimizely entregó exactamente lo que recibió, por lo que no se trató de una alteración de su red de distribución.
Qué hacía el código en cada visita
El programa buscaba direcciones de billeteras de criptomonedas en el texto de la página, en los formularios y en el portapapeles, y las reemplazaba por las del atacante. Quien copiaba una dirección para hacer una transferencia podía pegar otra distinta.
También registraba los números de tarjeta, la fecha de vencimiento y el código de seguridad que el usuario escribía en los formularios propios del sitio. Según Report URI, los pagos hechos en ventanas de procesadores externos quedaban fuera de su alcance. El código además enviaba cookies y capturas de pantalla.
En los dispositivos de Apple, el script cargaba dos conjuntos de herramientas de ataque llamados Coruna y DarkSword. Según Report URI, apuntan a versiones antiguas de iOS. Una página de iPhone con iOS 18.6 o anterior que se recargaba cada 60 segundos era un síntoma visible.
Reuters informó que no pudo confirmar si el código funcionó en cada caso ni cuántas víctimas dejó. El análisis de MATT Research indica que se demostró que los kits se entregaron, pero no una infección exitosa de un dispositivo real.
188 archivos infectados en nueve horas
Report URI revisó 1.611 archivos de Optimizely y encontró 188 infectados, que pertenecían a 178 organizaciones. Por sector, el informe cuenta 32 de banca y finanzas, 23 de tecnología, 20 de comercio minorista, 12 de streaming y 10 de medios. Helme advirtió que la cifra real probablemente sea mayor, porque solo pudo revisar los archivos que encontró a tiempo.
La primera inyección que detectó apareció a las 04:21 (hora UTC) del 16 de noviembre en la página de la BBC. A las 19:25, las billeteras de los atacantes habían recibido unos USD 7.040, casi todos en bitcoin. Los atacantes reconstruyeron el programa 26 veces durante el día.
La limpieza masiva comenzó cerca de las 20:40 UTC. A las 23:11, Report URI observó que todos los archivos estaban limpios. El servidor principal de los atacantes dejó de responder el 17 de noviembre, según el mismo informe, y Optimizely reconoció el incidente en su página de estado.
Las empresas respondieron de forma desigual
Salesforce dijo a Reuters que investigaba cambios no autorizados en los scripts de Optimizely y que los desactivó como medida de precaución. Equifax dejó de usar la plataforma y afirmó que no encontró pruebas de que sus sistemas hubieran sido comprometidos. IKEA indicó que evaluaba el posible impacto en sus servicios y clientes.
El informe midió además las defensas de los sitios afectados. Entre 256 servidores revisados, 68 no tenían una política de seguridad de contenido, la regla que limita qué scripts puede cargar una página. Solo 24, el 15%, bloquearon el código malicioso.
Report URI recomendó a quien visitó alguno de los sitios afectados ese día actualizar el iPhone o iPad, verificar que las transferencias de criptomonedas llegaron a la dirección prevista y revisar los resúmenes de tarjetas. La firma señaló que no puede saber cuántas tarjetas, cookies o capturas se robaron, ni cuántos dispositivos iOS se infectaron antes de que el ataque se detuviera.

articles.title: NVIDIA Establishes National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
NVIDIA Establishes National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee
NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that the Board of Directors has established the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, a new standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the company's national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management. NVIDIA's existing National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will report directly to the Committee and to Interim CEO, Colette Kress, on day-to-day operations.
The Committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson and will also include directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members. It will meet at least quarterly, including with management and in executive session. The Committee will oversee the Company's ongoing efforts to enhance its internal National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team, and work closely with independent third-party experts in law, national security and global trade compliance."NVIDIA recognizes that advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security. As the world's leading advanced computing company, NVIDIA has both a responsibility and an opportunity to lead the industry in addressing these challenges. We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," said Harvey Jones, Chairman of NVIDIA's Board of Directors.
The decision to create this new committee reflects the Board's further commitment to enhance its engagement with relevant government stakeholders, and to demonstrate the highest standards of governance and oversight.
3 Comments on NVIDIA Establishes National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee
But hey, when the guy at the top says "Let them regulate themselves" this is what we get.

articles.title: Top 10 Canal+ : les séries incontournables à ne surtout pas rater en novembre
articles.text:
Canal+ : notre top 10 des meilleures séries à voir en streaming en novembre 2026
Pas besoin de scroller pendant des heures sur l'application Canal+ avant de trouver une bonne série à regarder. Les Numériques vous guide avec sa sélection des 10 meilleures séries à voir en novembre 2026.
Que voir sur Canal+ et son application en novembre 2026 si on aime les séries ? L'offre de la chaîne cryptée est large entre ses propositions exclusives et ses créations originales.
Le catalogue contient aussi de nombreuses séries provenant d'autres plateformes de SVOD comme Apple TV et Paramount+, accessibles aux abonnés via différentes offres Canal+.
Choisir son programme peut donc vite devenir compliqué alors pour vous éviter de chercher pendant de longues minutes, Les Numériques a sélectionné pour vous, comme le mois dernier, son top des 10 séries à ne pas manquer sur Canal+ ce mois-ci.
Pour rappel, les séries Apple TV, Paramount+ et Ciné+ OCS sont accessibles via les offres Canal+ Ciné Séries et Canal+ La Totale.
Quelles sont les meilleures séries à voir sur Canal+ en novembre 2026 ?
Singapura
Justine débarque à Singapour, bien décidée à se réinventer et à offrir un nouveau départ à son couple. Elle découvre la petite communauté très policée des expatriés français et se laisse aussitôt fasciner par Élisa, un esprit libre, fantasque et tourmenté qui détonne dans ce cercle fermé. Lorsque celle-ci est assassinée, Justine se retrouve embarquée aux côtés de l’inspecteur Adam Wong dans une enquête où le vernis de l’expatriation se craquelle peu à peu.
La nouvelle création originale de Canal+ nous emporte dans l'univers des "expats" de la cité-état asiatique. Un monde à part, entre gratte-ciel et mangrove, propice à un thriller moite et suffoquant, où crimes et adultères vont de paire. Une série d'enquête certes un peu trop dans les rails du genre, mais avec un beau récit d'émancipation féminine et un casting solide, dont Naïlia Harzoune (66-5), Soji Arai (Tokyo Vice) et India Hair (Polar Park). Du Canal+ classique certes, mais efficace.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Tulsa King
Dwight "The General" Manfredi est un ancien parrain de la Mafia italienne à New York. Alors qu'il sort de 25 ans de prison pour couvrir son boss, ce dernier l'envoie, le contraint d'aller s'installer à Tulsa, dans l'Oklahoma. Face à cet exil forcé dans un lieu plus qu'improbable, Dwight Manfredi décide de monter son équipe formée de personnes très singulières. Il espère ainsi établir un nouvel empire.
Sylvester Stallone est grandiose dans cette série créée par Taylor Sheridan, le scénariste prolifique derrière Yellowstone. L’acteur de 80 ans donne tout ce qu’il a dans le rôle de ce mafieux prêt à tout pour se construire une nouvelle vie après un quart de siècle derrière barreaux. Il est entouré de second rôles qui lui tiennent tête sans sourciller pour une série pleine de drame, d’action, et de retournements de situation.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Yellowjackets
À la suite d'un accident d'avion, les jeunes membres d'une équipe de football féminin sont contraintes de survivre dans un environnement sauvage et inhospitalier. 30 ans plus tard, on retrouve ce qu'il reste de ses survivantes et découvre comment elles s'en sont sorties.
Yellowjackets rappellera de bons souvenirs aux fans de slashers et d'adolescents massacrés. Mais la série ne s'arrête pas là, et offre une structure narrative avec deux temporalités, l'une en 1996, l'autre en 2021, qui dialoguent et font avancer une histoire mystérieuse de crash d'avion et de cannibalisme. Belle réussite d'horreur, de tension à couper au couteau et de personnages finement écrits, elle vaut aussi le détour pour son casting féminin de qualité : Mélanie Lynskey, Christina Ricci, Juliette Lewis, Ella Purnell, Sophie Thatcher...
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Devil in Disguise
Entre 1972 et 1978, trente-trois jeunes hommes ont été kidnappés, assassinés puis enterrés sous la maison de leur meurtrier John Wayne Gacy. Et pendant toutes ces années, personne ne s'est douté de rien. Sympathique et drôle, cette figure respectée dans sa communauté était même bénévole auprès des enfants malades qu'il divertissait déguisé en clown. À travers les multiples facettes de John Wayne Gacy et les récits bouleversants des victimes et de leurs proches, ce sont les défaillances institutionnelles qui sont pointées, tout comme les occasions manquées et les préjugés de la société qui ont permis à ce meurtrier de continuer à tuer.
Aux antipodes de l'anthologie Monstre de Netflix, cette série examine l'histoire de John Wayne Gacy avec beaucoup de tact et de respect envers ses victimes. Au lieu de verser dans le sensationnalisme, le show se concentre sur le coût humain des crimes de Gacy et trouve en Michael Chernus un interprète aussi glaçant que perturbant. On tient là une série éprouvante, émouvante, mais surtout un récit true crime des plus réfléchis sur le sujet de ce tueur en série notoire.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Apollo has fallen
Zara Taylor du MI6, les services secrets britanniques, et Vincent Taleb, ancien agent de protection rapprochée du ministre français de la Défense, coopèrent de nouveau quand un avion est détourné au large des côtes libyennes. Cette première attaque marque le début d’une vaste conspiration menée par un violent mercenaire russe, Yuri Mishkin. Alors qu’un virus mortel menace de décimer l’Europe, les deux agents doivent agir vite pour stopper Yuri et ses complices, dont un traître dans leurs propres rangs.
Plus ambitieuse, plus rythmée et surtout plus généreuse en action, Apollo Has Fallen corrige en partie les défauts de Paris Has Fallen et franchit un véritable cap. Sans parvenir à se hisser au niveau des meilleures productions du genre, la série Canal+ s'impose néanmoins comme un divertissement solide, efficace et suffisamment spectaculaire pour tenir le spectateur en haleine jusqu'au bout. Une deuxième saison qui montre que la franchise a clairement les moyens de ses ambitions, même si on en attendra plus d'audace dans la mise en scène.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Dark Matter
Jason Dessen, professeur de physique à Chicago, est enlevé un soir alors qu’il rentre chez lui. Lorsqu’il reprend connaissance, son épouse n’est plus la sienne, son fils n’existe pas et il découvre qu’il est devenu un scientifique célèbre à l’origine d’une invention révolutionnaire. Jason comprend bientôt qu’il a été projeté dans une réalité issue d’un choix qu’il aurait pu faire autrefois. Pour retrouver sa véritable famille, il doit traverser différentes versions de son existence et affronter un adversaire qui le connaît mieux que personne.
Adapté du roman de science-fiction de Blake Crouch, ce thriller atmosphérique et époustouflant plonge le spectateur dans une histoire de multivers passionnante. Joel Edgerton, Jennifer Connelly et le reste de la distribution sont impeccables, la mise en scène et les décors sont soignés et l'histoire sur fond de crise existentielle captivera les adeptes de séries aux concepts pointus dès son premier épisode.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
MobLand
MobLand
Harry Da Souza, un homme de main débrouillard, se voit plongé en plein conflit entre deux familles criminelles, qui cherchent à prendre le pouvoir au risque de renverser des empires et de ruiner des vies.
Si l'intrigue de cette nouvelle série sur fond de gangsters londoniens sent un peu le réchauffé et ne révolutionne pas son genre, MobLand se regarde sans déplaisir. Le show vaut surtout le détour pour l'élégance de sa production, son casting soigné et un Tom Hardy fabuleux et charismatique. Bref, une série très solide qui est revenue récemment avec sa deuxième saison.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Slow Horses
Une équipe d’agents secrets britanniques est mise au placard par le MI5 suite aux erreurs qu’ils ont commises en mission. Placés sous les ordres d’un chef aussi brillant qu’irascible, le célèbre Jackson Lamb, ils naviguent dans le monde de l’espionnage, où règnent les faux-semblants, pour défendre la Grande-Bretagne contre les forces ennemies.
Slow Horses met en scène des espions britanniques qui regardent leur carrière mourir. Portée par un Gary Oldman caustique dans le rôle de Jackson Lamb, la série propose une intrigue captivante sur fond d'humour noir pinçant et introduit une galerie de personnages soit résolus à accepter leur sort, soit avides de remonter les échelons du MI5 et de redorer leur blason.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Opérations Spéciales : Lioness
Inspirée d'un programme militaire américain, cette série suit le quotidien de Joe, officier de pointe de la CIA dans la guerre contre le terrorisme, dans sa quête d'équilibre entre sa vie personnelle et professionnelle. Le programme Lioness supervisé fait appel à la jeune Marine Cruz Manuelos, un peu brutale mais passionnée, pour opérer sous couverture aux côtés de Joe et contrecarrer le projet d'un nouveau 11 septembre.
Zoe Saldaña, Nicole Kidman, Dave Annable ou encore Michael Kelly sont au casting de ce thriller explosif signé Taylor Sheridan (Yellowstone). Lioness est une série qui mélange espionnage, opérations militaires et contre-terrorisme dans une intrigue finement ficelée qui tient le spectateur en haleine d'épisode en épisode, avec en son cœur des personnages diablement bien incarnés et surtout très intéressants à découvrir.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Prisoner
Lorsqu'un convoi pénitentiaire est pris d’assaut, Amber Todd, agente chargée du transfert, se retrouve prise au piège avec Tibor Stone - ancien tueur d’élite devenu témoin clé contre Pegasus, le réseau criminel qu’il a autrefois servi. Pourchassés par ce puissant conglomérat du crime et par des autorités corrompues, Amber et Tibor, deux inconnus que tout oppose, sont forcés de fuir ensemble…
Tahar Rahim et Izuka Hoyle forment un duo de choc dans ce thriller d'action bourré d'une tension que seuls les Britanniques semblent parfaitement bien maîtriser. Avec six épisodes au compteur, Prisoner captive l'attention dès ses premières minutes et ne lâche pas son spectateur avant son dénouement, faisant avancer son intrigue à un rythme soutenu et reposant sur une distribution impeccable pour maintenir les yeux du spectateur rivés sur l'écran.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :

articles.title: Los neandertales desaparecieron hace miles de años, pero una pequeña parte de ellos sigue trabajando dentro de nuestro cerebro
articles.text:
Hace decenas de miles de años, cuando el Homo sapiens salió de África y se cruzó con los neandertales en Eurasia, incorporó en su genética pequeños fragmentos de ADN de aquellos parientes extintos. Hoy sabemos que entre el 1 y el 2% del genoma de las poblaciones no africanas procede de aquellos encuentros y ahora sabemos por una investigación muy reciente que una de estas pequeñas variantes moldea nuestra anatomía de la parte posterior de nuestro cerebro y reduce el riesgo de padecer esquizofrenia.
El estudio. Se centró principalmente en el cruce de genomas antiguos con grandes bases de datos biomédicas actuales, lo que ha hecho que los investigadores se centren en el cromosoma 14. Pero la variante identificada no consiste en una mutación que altera la estructura de una proteína, sino en una modificación minúscula en cuatro letras que está involucrada en el desarrollo cerebral y la arquitectura celular.
La relación. Para confirmar que este rasgo procedía del mestizaje con los neandertales y no de un antepasado común mucho más remto los investigadores compararon el tramo genético con secuencias fósiles de alta cobertura. Y aquí vieron que la selección aparece en los cinco genomas neandertales analizados, pero está completamente ausente en los genomas de las poblaciones humanas actuales del África subsahariana.
Su impacto. El efecto de esta herencia genética que nos dejan nuestros antepasados se concentra en la parte trasera del encéfalo, concretamente en el lóbulo occipital y de forma muy marcada en una estructura encargada de procesar la información que llega desde los ojos para darnos la visión.
Lo que se ve es que cada copia heredada de esta variante se asocia con una reducción media de unos 0,85 cm cúbicos del volumen de esta región. Y aunque puede parecer poco, representa el mayor efecto individual heredado hasta la fecha para una sola variante genética sobre el tamaño de esta región.
Lo que ocurre. Al evaluar lo que ocurre cuando se reduce de una manera tan marcada esta zona de nuestro cerebro, se vio que no hay un impacto sobre el rendimiento cognitivo. Pero donde sí aparece una asociación clínica relevante es en el ámbito de la psiquiatría, puesto que, según el análisis realizado, las personas que solo tienen una copia de esta alteración tienen casi un 10% menos de riesgo de desarrollar esquizofrenia que el resto de la población.
Un cambio de paradigma. Este hallazgo introduce un matiz importante en un debate científico que lleva varios años abierto, puesto que este estudio apunta a que la ascendencia neandertal considerada en su conjunto no muestra ninguna tendencia protectora frente a la esquizofrenia. El efecto importante de verdad está en esta pequeña alteración genética.
Esto contrasta con trabajos anteriores que apuntaban ya en 2021 que los pacientes esquizofrénicos parecían tener una menor proporción global de variación genética de origen neandertal que los controles sanos, aunque con una significación estadística muy ajustada. Pero ahora sabemos que las alteraciones puntuales son lo que más nos debe interesar.
La razón. Los moldes endocraneales obtenidos a partir de fósiles demuestran que los neandertales no solo tenían una capacidad craneal media ligeramente superior a la nuestra, sino que contaban con lóbulos occipitales y cortezas visuales proporcionalmente más grandes que los de Homo sapiens, un rasgo que suele interpretarse como una adaptación para procesar mejor la luz tenue en las latitudes altas de Eurasia. Pero entonces: ¿cómo es posible, entonces, que una variante genética heredada precisamente de ellos reduzca el tamaño del lóbulo occipital en los humanos actuales?
Aquí los investigadores argumentan que la arquitectura del cerebro es un rasgo extraordinario donde intervienen muchos genes diferentes. Es por ello que quedarnos con uno de ellos en exclusiva no tiene ningún tipo de sentido, teniendo que entender que es un factor más que nos da información muy valiosa para entender un poco más la herencia que nos dejaron nuestros antepasados.
