articles.title: Esquenta Black: iPhone 17e (512 GB) cai para menor preço em meses • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Esquenta Black: iPhone 17e (512 GB) cai para menor preço em meses
iPhone 17e (512 GB), com câmera de 48 MP e chip A19 de alto desempenho, recebe desconto de 36% no Pix com cupom na loja do Magalu no AliExpress
O iPhone 17e de 512 GB está saindo por R$ 4.804 no Pix com cupom AEMEGA18 na loja do Magazine Luiza no AliExpress. O celular acessível da Apple, com chip A19 e câmera wide de 48 MP, alcança o menor preço desde setembro de 2026, com desconto de 34% sobre o original de R$ 5.999 durante a Black November 2026.
Apesar de ser o modelo “baratinho” da Apple, o iPhone 17e oferece alto desempenho graças ao chip A19 e aos 8 GB de RAM, que sustentam apps pesados e funções do Apple Intelligence. Os 512 GB de espaço interno dão e sobram para guardar fotos e vídeos.
Sua tela Super Retina XDR OLED de 6,1″ tem brilho de até 1.200 nits, entregando cores vibrantes com garantia de visibilidade em qualquer ambiente. O vidro Ceramic Shield 2 protege o display contra pancadas e quedas.

O corpo de alumínio do iPhone 17e conta com a certificação IP68, que adiciona proteção extra em cenários como poeira intensa e mergulhos acidentais.

articles.title: Panne Microsoft 365 : un bug interne vieux de plusieurs mois à l'origine du chaos
articles.text:
Microsoft vient de révéler les causes de la panne mondiale qui a paralysé Microsoft 365 pendant près de 24 heures. À l'origine du désastre, un bug passé inaperçu pendant plus de trois mois, et des systèmes de secours qui ont aggravé la situation au lieu de la contenir.
Depuis le temps qu'on reproche à Microsoft de laisser traîner des bugs partout, il fallait bien qu'un jour ils finissent par lui exploser à la figure. C'est exactement ce qui s'est passé les 12 et 13 novembre derniers, deux journées noires pour Microsoft 365, resté en carafe pendant près de 24 heures. L'entreprise vient en effet de livrer les premières conclusions de son enquête dans un rapport préliminaire, également commenté sur X par Charles Lamanna, vice-président exécutif chez Microsoft, révélant qu'un défaut logiciel introduit dès juillet dans sa propre infrastructure est à l'origine de la panne. Un bug passé inaperçu pendant plus de trois mois, responsable d’une réaction en chaîne que les systèmes de secours ont eux-mêmes contribué à amplifier.
Microsoft avait tout testé, sauf les bonnes conditions…
Juillet 2026. Redmond l'ignore encore, mais les ennuis commencent. L'entreprise déploie un correctif spécialement conçu pour les serveurs Windows de ses passerelles réseau Microsoft 365, chargées de traiter les demandes de connexion à ses services. La modification est progressivement distribuée à l'ensemble de l'infrastructure concernée, sans provoquer d’incident notable. Pourtant, son code embarque déjà le bug qui mettra ses serveurs à genoux d’ici quelques mois.
En cause, un problème de contention de verrous (lock contention) au sein d'un processus interne de Windows. En temps normal, ces verrous permettent de coordonner l'accès aux ressources partagées : lorsqu'une opération utilise une ressource, les autres doivent attendre qu'elle ait terminé pour y accéder à leur tour. Mais une anomalie présente dans ce processus a enrayé cette coordination lorsque les serveurs ont été fortement sollicités. Les opérations ont alors passé trop de temps à se disputer les mêmes accès, les requêtes se sont accumulées et le processeur comme la mémoire ont fini par saturer, si bien que les serveurs ont cessé de répondre aux demandes de connexion.
Mais comment diable une telle bombe à retardement a-t-elle pu échapper aux batteries de tests menées par Microsoft en amont du déploiement du patch ? Eh bien, parce que les essais en laboratoire n'ont jamais reproduit les conditions dans lesquelles elle risquait d'exploser. L'entreprise a en effet privilégié des machines moins puissantes que ses serveurs de production et simulé un trafic insuffisamment représentatif de celui qu'ils allaient réellement devoir traiter.
… et tout ce qui pouvait mal tourner a mal tourné
Plus de trois mois passent sans que rien ne vienne troubler le fonctionnement des services. Puis arrive le 12 novembre. Vers 2 heures du matin, Microsoft Teams bascule automatiquement vers une passerelle réseau également utilisée par Exchange Online. Rien d'anormal jusque-là, cette opération faisant partie des procédures prévues par Microsoft pour assurer la continuité de ses services. Toujours est-il qu’elle augmente le trafic sur une infrastructure déjà privée de près de 14 % de ses capacités, à la suite d'un incident indépendant survenu la veille.
Au fil des heures, la charge s’intensifie et finit par réunir les fameuses conditions nécessaires au déclenchement du bug de juillet. En pleine période de forte activité aux États-Unis, les premiers serveurs saturent puis cessent de répondre, et la situation dégénère. Les systèmes automatiques de Microsoft redirigent alors les connexions vers d'autres machines encore opérationnelles, comme ils sont censés le faire pour éviter toute interruption de service.
Manque de chance pour Microsoft, les serveurs de repli présentent exactement le même défaut logiciel. À mesure que le trafic est redistribué, ils saturent à leur tour, provoquant une réaction en chaîne. Pour couronner le tout, les dispositifs censés empêcher la panne de se propager d'une région à l'autre ne remplissent pas non plus leur rôle, mis en échec par une défaillance supplémentaire. En moins de deux heures, plus de 80 % des serveurs de la passerelle réseau commune à Teams et Exchange Online tombent.
Un bourbier dont Microsoft a eu bien du mal à sortir
Teams, OneDrive et SharePoint parviennent à limiter les dégâts en basculant vers une autre infrastructure réseau, ce qui leur permet de rétablir une partie de leurs fonctionnalités. Mais Exchange Online ne peut pas en faire autant à cette échelle, si bien que la plupart des utilisateurs et utilisatrices n’ont plus accès à leur messagerie, tandis que les mails en attente de livraison s'accumulent.
Pendant ce temps, les équipes de Microsoft tentent de remettre les serveurs en service, sans grand succès. À peine redémarrées, les machines sont submergées par les requêtes en attente et cessent de nouveau de répondre. Les procédures automatiques de récupération n'ont pas été conçues pour gérer une panne d'une telle ampleur, et l'ancienneté du code défectueux empêche d'annuler rapidement la modification par les moyens habituels.
Les ingénieurs doivent finalement développer une mise à jour rétablissant l'ancien fonctionnement du système, puis l'appliquer progressivement aux machines touchées. Le 13 novembre, à 17 h 10, heure française, Microsoft confirme la fin des perturbations, après presque 24 heures de panne. Depuis, l'entreprise a renforcé ses capacités réseau, sa surveillance et ses dispositifs de répartition du trafic. Un rapport définitif, attendu le 20 novembre, doit encore détailler les mesures supplémentaires prévues pour éviter qu'un tel scénario catastrophe ne se reproduise.
Microsoft 365 offre une solution complète et intégrée pour la productivité, la collaboration, la sécurité et la gestion, ce qui en fait un choix populaire pour les entreprises, les organisations et les particuliers qui ont besoin d'être productifs et sécurisés dans le monde numérique d'aujourd'hui. À télécharger sur Windows et Mac.
- Applications web gratuites pour les besoins simples
- Applications de bureau particulièrement complètes
- Intégration avec OneDrive et les services Microsoft
- Applications de bureau complètes principalement accessibles sur abonnement
- Aucune version desktop officielle sous Linux
- Gamme d’offres difficile à comprendre

articles.title: Nvidia warns customers of new US rule that could expose them to lawsuits for serving Chinese clients — Commerce Department releases interim regulations preventing ‘foreign actors’ from using advanced compute based on American tech
articles.text:
Nvidia warns customers of new US rule that could expose them to lawsuits for serving Chinese clients — Commerce Department releases interim regulations preventing ‘foreign actors’ from using advanced compute based on American tech
The noose is tightening for Chinese AI labs that need U.S. AI GPUs to train their models.
CNBC reports that Nvidia has started warning its customers that impending legislation to clamp down on countries accessing AI GPUs remotely via data center rentals could put them in trouble with U.S. authorities. Chinese tech companies could take advantage of the performance of American AI hardware through a loophole in U.S. regulations. Instead of importing Nvidia chips, which are under export controls, they instead look to data centers located abroad and export their data instead. This is what Chinese AI lab Moonshot is apparently trying in Europe, which is why the U.S. Department of Commerce, through the Bureau of Industry and Security [PDF], released an interim final rule closing this loophole.
According to the report, Nvidia has been messaging chip buyers to warn that RASA could expose both Nvidia and chip buyers to legal risk.
The U.S. House of Representatives has already passed a bill called the Remote Access Security Act (RASA) that addressed this specific loophole, but it’s been in limbo in the Senate for over ten months now. It remains unclear if the Jensen Huang affair and suspected espionage scandal will help speed up its approval, but scheduling could be tight with only about 31 calendar days remaining before the Senate's adjournment. But even before any of these regulations are approved and published, the company is already taking steps to protect its customers and has started requiring partners that 51% of their services should go to non-Chinese clients. It has also required its partners to join Nvidia’s Fleet Intelligence tracking system if they want to retain their official partner status
It’s unclear if these changes have been planned over time or were a reaction to the renewed scrutiny that Nvidia is facing. But even though Jensen Huang is now out of the company, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that it’s unclear if the former Nvidia CEO was aware of the alleged smuggling operations and instead laid the blame on the entire company. Nvidia itself has taken steps to improve its security and export control teams by establishing an oversight committee that will be in charge of its “national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risk management,” and would work with third-party experts in law, national security, and trade compliance.
These measures would further tighten the noose around China’s AI GPUs. Even though it has several domestic chip makers, many AI operators still prefer Nvidia chips for their performance and reliability. There have even been allegations that Alibaba and ByteDance, some of China’s biggest tech companies, prefer training their LLMs in Southeast Asia to bypass bans and restrictions. So, if the U.S. finally shuts down this loophole, we can expect these companies to scramble and find a replacement for the Nvidia GPUs they could access right now.

articles.title: Argentina vs. Costa Rica ver online en Xuper TV, Roja Directa y Fútbol Libre: el truco gratuito que pone en riesgo tu seguridad
articles.text:
Argentina vs. Costa Rica concentrará este martes 17 de noviembre de 2027, búsquedas de enlaces gratuitos en Xuper TV, Roja Directa y Fútbol Libre, pero esos accesos pueden exponer teléfonos, computadores y otros equipos a aplicaciones fraudulentas, robo de contraseñas y programas maliciosos. El amistoso se jugará a las 20:00 en el estadio Mario Alberto Kempes de Córdoba.
La selección argentina cerrará su calendario de 2026 ante Costa Rica después de la derrota por 2-1 frente a Uruguay en La Bombonera. El partido tendrá transmisión por TyC Sports, aunque la expectativa por seguirlo sin pagar suele dirigir a parte de los usuarios hacia webs que modifican sus dominios, imitan servicios conocidos o exigen instalar archivos antes de mostrar un supuesto reproductor.
El partido se jugará a las 20:00 en Córdoba
La Albiceleste buscará despedir el año con una victoria ante su público, antes de volver a competir en marzo de 2027. Argentina llega tras caer ante Uruguay, mientras que Costa Rica perdió frente a Ecuador en el inicio de la ventana de noviembre. El árbitro del encuentro será Bruno Arleu.
La probable alineación argentina incluye a Dibu Martínez; Agustín Giay, Leonardo Balerdi, Lisandro Martínez y Nicolás Tagliafico; Enzo Fernández y Alexis Mac Allister; Nico Paz, Matías Soulé y Gianluca Prestianni; Julián Álvarez.
Costa Rica podría formar con Patrick Sequeira; Kenay Myrie, Juan Pablo Vargas, Francisco Calvo y Joseph Mora; Celso Borges, Roan Wilson, Carlos Mora y Josimar Alcócer; Kenyel Michel y Manfred Ugalde. El técnico será Bryan Ruiz.
Los enlaces ilegales pueden llevar a descargas fraudulentas
Las búsquedas para ver Argentina vs. Costa Rica online suelen derivar en portales que prometen una transmisión inmediata. Algunas de esas páginas solicitan instalar una APK, descargar un supuesto reproductor o añadir extensiones al navegador con la excusa de desbloquear el partido, eliminar anuncios o mejorar la imagen.
Una plataforma destinada a reproducir fútbol no necesita permisos para acceder a contactos, mensajes, cámara, ubicación ni funciones de accesibilidad. Si una aplicación vinculada con Fútbol Libre, Roja Directa, Tarjeta Roja o Xuper TV pide ese tipo de autorizaciones, puede incorporar funciones ajenas a la transmisión.
El Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad de España (Incibe) advierte que muchas aplicaciones maliciosas circulan mediante enlaces directos, repositorios externos y sitios sin controles verificables. Las APK descargadas fuera de las tiendas oficiales pueden ser copias alteradas, programas falsos o archivos con herramientas ocultas.
Los permisos de accesibilidad pueden comprometer el dispositivo
Los permisos de accesibilidad requieren especial atención porque permiten observar lo que aparece en pantalla e interactuar con otras aplicaciones. Un servicio de vídeo no necesita esas capacidades para reproducir un partido.
También resulta prudente evitar extensiones que prometen acceso a contenidos bloqueados. Algunas pueden registrar la navegación, insertar publicidad o redirigir a páginas diseñadas para capturar datos personales.
El problema puede continuar después del pitazo final. Una aplicación instalada desde una fuente desconocida puede mantenerse activa en segundo plano, cambiar configuraciones, abrir ventanas emergentes o llevar al usuario a otros sitios sin que lo advierta.
Entre las señales de alerta figuran anuncios persistentes, aplicaciones desconocidas, cambios en la pantalla de inicio, mayor consumo de batería y un descenso en el rendimiento del teléfono o computador. Que una transmisión funcione no significa que el equipo esté protegido.
Una APK fraudulenta puede robar claves y códigos bancarios
Un archivo malicioso puede incorporar un keylogger, un programa que registra las pulsaciones realizadas en el teclado o en la pantalla. Si después se accede al correo electrónico, las redes sociales o la banca digital, contraseñas y credenciales pueden quedar expuestas.
El riesgo aumenta si la aplicación obtiene permiso para leer mensajes SMS. Muchas entidades bancarias envían por esa vía códigos de un solo uso para validar transferencias, recuperar claves o confirmar accesos.
También existe la amenaza del ransomware, un software que cifra fotografías, documentos y otros archivos para exigir un pago. No hay garantía de recuperar la información aunque se entregue dinero.
Tabletas, TV Box y computadores conectados a la misma red doméstica también pueden quedar expuestos. Revisar el origen de cada aplicación y evitar descargas externas reduce riesgos que pueden persistir mucho después de Argentina vs. Costa Rica.

articles.title: Arista takes aim at the next AI network battleground: distributed inference - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Arista takes aim at the next AI network battleground: distributed inference
Awareness of the network’s role in artificial intelligence has steadily increased, with much of the focus on the back end – larger clusters, faster ports and scale-across fabrics that stitch graphics processing units together across data centers. Arista Networks Inc. has seen continued, accelerated growth and has been one of the biggest winners of that buildout.
This week at SC26, Arista announced a shift in focus to the other side of the network. The company also announced a new set of Etherlink R4 routing platforms designed for what it calls distributed inferencing, along with a pluggable optical line system for data center interconnect. The lineup includes:
- 7020R4 and 7020HR4: Compact 1RU access routers with 25G to 400G ports, deep buffers and optional wire-speed encryption on every port. The HR4 versions are temperature-hardened and add advanced timing for cell sites and outside plant.
- 7282R4: A fixed-edge and core router with dual supervisors for control-plane redundancy.
- 7280R4: A 25.6 terabit “in-betweener” with 64 400G ports, half supporting ZR/ZR+ coherent optics, to bridge local fabrics to the wide area network.
- Pluggable optical line system: A full C-band amplifier carrying 25.6 Tbps over a single fiber pair, plus muxes and a pluggable fiber tester.
All are based on Broadcom’s Jericho and Qumran silicon, designed to deliver up to 60% lower power consumption than competing 7-nanometer and 16-nanometer platforms. Everything is available now, except the 7020HR4, which ships in early 2027. The speeds and feeds always make headlines, but the implications of the launch point to where AI infrastructure is heading.
Inference is about to get distributed
During a pre-briefing, Brendan Gibbs, Arista’s assistant vice president of product line management, argued that the forces driving training across multiple sites will have the same effect on inference. Gibbs also said that roughly 30% of Arista’s AI business is now scale-across, indicating that distributed AI is rapidly becoming commonplace.
Inference will be distributed for three reinforcing reasons:
- Latency. A centralized cluster works well for a chatbot that streams text line by line. It doesn’t work for agentic AI, where a single request can trigger dozens of chained model calls and every millisecond compounds.
- Sovereignty. Regulators increasingly want inference requests and data to stay within national borders. European IT leaders have little appetite for sending data to U.S. cloud providers.
- Power and space. Companies will deploy inference wherever they have capacity, and the network must support it.
The implication is that the front-end network, long treated as plumbing, now needs back-end attributes: deep buffers, traffic engineering, multi-tenancy, and encryption, because traffic now leaves the building.
Arista is going downmarket
This launch is the opposite of the descriptors we typically associate with Arista. Recent announcements focused on dense 800G, 1.6T, and liquid cooling. The products launched at SC26 are smaller and less expensive. Arista dominates big iron and is now rounding out its portfolio. Arista’s customers range from hyperscalers to neoclouds to enterprises building local AI. The front end needs rich features, not massive bandwidth, and Arista hasn’t had a viable option for that tier until now.
These routers are designed as entry-level but ship with 400G uplinks, which may seem like overkill today but offer investment protection. Gibbs said the goal is a 10-year life cycle, with customers swapping optics rather than chassis. No one knows what agents will do to traffic volumes, and I suspect companies that consider this overkill today will think differently in three or four years. Headroom is cheaper than a forklift upgrade at a remote site. Also notable: Arista co-designed the 7280R4 with a hyperscaler seeking a gray-to-coherent bridge, a sign that it’s building with its biggest customers.
The service provider wildcard
The most intriguing product is the hardened 7020HR4, built for 5G and AI-RAN cell sites. Telcos have largely sat out the AI buildout, yet they own the last mile and real estate near users, exactly what low-latency inference requires. This gives a carrier the backbone to offer a managed AI factory.
My view is that this performs better outside the U.S., where enterprises don’t trust carriers beyond connectivity. In Europe and Asia-Pacific, managed services are far more common, and providers such as BT, NTT and Telstra have the footprint to make it work. With sovereignty requirements, the opportunity for telcos to move up the stack has never been better. Telcos have never been a core market for Arista, so any growth from that audience is additive to its already massive market.
Quality and security are the quiet differentiators
Since 2019, Arista has reported a far lower CVE count than competitors, even after the surge in AI-assisted discovery following Anthropic’s Mythos. I’m skeptical of CVE comparisons because counts depend on testing rigor, installed base and reporting practices, and some vendors now bundle multiple issues into a single CVE.
The more relevant benefit is operational. Customers often don’t apply patches because upgrades cause downtime and break things. If they trust the software, they patch faster, and the risk window shrinks. With Mythos accelerating the retirement of end-of-support gear, quality and longevity become buying criteria, not nice-to-haves.
On the call, Gibbs agreed it’s hard to draw conclusions from CVE counts but explained that CVE counts were a measure of Arista’s software quality. This has been Arista’s calling card since it was a startup. While CVEs provide one metric, the bigger proof point is its historical track record of quality software.
Also, wire-speed MACsec and IPsec on every port is a differentiator because AI brings different security requirements. However, integrated security does not replace firewalls. I asked Gibbs about this, and he said that Arista has no intention of replacing firewalls and expects Palo Alto Networks Inc. to continue to sit behind it in the line. I’d like to see that formalized into validated designs for distributed inference, like what Nvidia Corp.-validated designs did for the back end.
The optical line system is a similar simplification play. Arista isn’t an optical company and is reselling these products, but offering dark fiber customers a turnkey, EOS-integrated way to move 25.6 Tbps across a metro network removes a real headache.
Customers have responded positively to Arista’s entry into this market. Douglas Fast Net Chief Technology Officer Jon Vradenburg said the company needs “a compact platform that supports the services our business and carrier customers rely on.” Takayuki Sakou of Japan’s STNet cited “higher throughput and improved power efficiency while maintaining the quality of the EOS software we trust.”
Considerations for network professionals
- Map where inference will run, not just where it runs today. If your AI roadmap includes agents, assume that latency and sovereignty will push inference closer to users, and plan the front end accordingly.
- Treat the front end as part of the AI fabric. Evaluate buffering, traffic engineering, and multi-tenancy at the WAN edge with the same rigor you apply to GPU clusters.
- Make encryption the default. Inference traffic between sites carries prompts and proprietary data. Line-rate encryption should be table stakes.
- Buy for longevity. Prioritize platforms with uplink headroom, modern silicon and a software track record that lets you patch without fear.
Final thoughts
The back end of AI networking is largely a solved architecture at this point. The front end is not, and that’s where the next round of competition will play out. With R4, Arista is betting that its routing credibility, built quietly within hyperscaler backbones, can make it the default there as well. Given how much traffic agentic AI is likely to generate, that’s a bet that, like most Arista bets, will likely pay off.
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: Why general-purpose AI falls short in agriculture
articles.text:
Why general-purpose AI falls short in agriculture
GenAI knows farming. It doesn't know your field.
In July, a farmer in Chuzhou, China, turned to an AI chatbot for help. He needed a plan to control weeds and pests in his fields. The model produced what a Futurism journalist later called “a Long Island iced tea of agrochemicals.” The farmer sprayed this cocktail across 25 acres of crops. By the next day, every single sesame seedling was dead, costing him roughly 150,000 yuan, or about 18,000 euros.
When Wu asked the chatbot what went wrong, the AI admitted it made mistakes. That mix it proposed was suitable for broadleaf weeds. But sesame is widely classified as a broadleaf plant, so it was never the right option to begin with. Another error was suggesting spraying the entire field instead of using the targeted application.
As horrible as it is, that is just one example of AI missing the mark. Researchers from the U.S., the U.K., Kenya, Nigeria, and Colombia recently tested whether generative AI could replace human agricultural advisors. Apparently, it can’t.
CPO & COO at OneSoil.
According to their paper published in Nature Food, the team first asked chatbots to recommend treatment for the fall armyworm, a pest that destroys corn crops worldwide. In response, OpenAI's GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 models provided highly ambiguous pesticide advice.
Next, the researchers simulated questions from cassava farmers in Nigeria. ChatGPT recommended specific herbicides but gave the wrong application timing. Following that advice would have killed the crops, threatening food security for millions of people, since Nigeria is Africa's most important cassava producer.
More frequent mistakes
What's more disturbing is that these mistakes might become more frequent. With rising labor, land, and equipment costs, many farmers can no longer afford professional advice. On top of that, there is a severe shortage of trained agricultural extensionists. Extension workers rarely reach the world's most isolated fields, such as those in South America and Africa, while farmers in those regions cannot travel hundreds of kilometers to attend seminars to improve their knowledge.
Instead, they often rely on extension agencies based in capital cities. But those lack both the funding and the staff to update their outdated guides or track new farming trends. So farmers turn to digital assistants. According to a recent McKinsey survey, roughly 17 percent of farmers worldwide already use generative AI in day-to-day decisions. That is more than any other new technology in the sector, including robotics and electric-powered machinery, Bloomberg reported.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
To be fair, AI itself is not the issue. The problem is that many farmers turn to general-purpose AI chatbots such as ChatGPT or Claude for advice. These tools know crop types, chemical classes, standard practices, and textbook planting calendars. But they are not trained specifically for agriculture purposes. For example, they won't ask for necessary data from the user before providing advice. As a result, their answers can sound professional while being useless or even harmful.
Training AI for agronomic purposes
There is a way to fix it: train an AI model for agronomic purposes. That takes two steps. First, the model learns from real data about a particular field: satellite images, past harvests, current weather and the crop's stage of growth. Second, it learns from working agronomists, who teach it how to respond in different situations. Those lessons also set limits on what the model will say. If it knows what crop is in the ground, it won't recommend a herbicide that is banned for that crop.
To better understand how this works, imagine a farmer who needs to spray a wheat field to get rid of weeds. A standard AI chatbot might draw on general textbooks and suggest a strong chemical. But because it cannot see the actual field, it does not know two critical things: that the wheat is at a fragile stage of growth where this chemical will ruin the crop, and that tomorrow's high winds will blow the spray onto neighboring land. Following the AI's advice could destroy the harvest.
By contrast, an AI connected to real data checks satellite photos and weather reports first. It automatically spots the high winds, recognizes that the wheat is too fragile for certain chemicals, and picks a safe alternative. It also asks questions when information is unclear or missing. Then it shows the farmer exactly where to spray, using coordinates or a task map that targets only the weed patches. In the end, this saves money and protects future yields.
Collecting information
Having said all that, expecting farmers to gather all this information and enter it into a generic AI tool isn't realistic. It takes time most growers don't have, as well as technical knowledge. Plus, farmers have no time to do inputs regularly.
This is why I believe a new market will emerge: of specialized agricultural AI assistants with built-in access to dashboards and satellite imagery, allowing seamless movement between data sources and making accurate, field-specific information far easier to access and act on.
This market is already taking shape. Some assistants can revisit satellite data layers, analyze them visually, and answer questions like “What has changed in the last 48 hours?” in plain language. Some products also let farmers send voice messages describing what they have applied. The agent files those details in the right parts of the system and keeps them as context. This makes it easier to keep field records up to date, which helps the model give more useful answers.
Such tools can help farmers make sense of their own field data, spot meaningful changes, and spend less time piecing together multiple sources. With some luck, a wave of these purpose-built tools will help eliminate costly mistakes in agriculture, so more farmers worldwide can thrive instead of losing their crops, money and spirit.

articles.title: US government confirms criminal investigation into Singapore company at the heart of Jensen Huang scandal — Megaspeed identified over suspicious activity, company placed on ‘no sell’ list by Nvidia
articles.text:
US government confirms criminal investigation into Singapore company at the heart of Jensen Huang scandal — Megaspeed identified over suspicious activity, company placed on ‘no sell’ list by Nvidia
The Justice and Commerce Departments have announced an investigation into the company previously run by the woman officials have accused of being a Chinese spy while having an affair with Jensen Huang while he was Nvidia's CEO.
A criminal investigation into Megaspeed has been confirmed by the United States Justice and Commerce Departments, with a joint statement saying that they will “bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred.” Authorities believe that Megaspeed is one of a raft of companies that may have circumvented export rules designed to limit the sale of advanced AI chips, like those built by Nvidia, to approved companies and countries. The company is at the heart of the recent Jensen Huang scandal, which saw him resign from the company last week.
Megaspeed was added to Nvidia's no-sell list in June 2025, the statement reveals, but a New York Times report claims that a Malaysian Megaspeed subsidiary continued to receive large shipments of Nvidia chips for a full eight months after that date. It's believed that Nvidia's export-controlled Blackwell and H200 chips were shipped to Speedmatrix, either via third parties or directly from Nvidia itself, before being handed off to China. Nvidia has argued that it was given Commerce Department permission to ship the components to Megaspeed. Notably, Nvidia continues to list Megaspeed as a cloud partner.
The new criminal investigation follows a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed that first kicked off in 2024 over possible export violations. By May 2025, it had requested Nvidia's data relating to sales it made to Megaspeed, and by June, officials visited Megaspeed and even interviewed Alice Huang, the now-former executive who is allegedly a Chinese spy. Ms. Huang is also the woman that then-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with before resigning his position earlier this month. Following that visit, the Justice Department took the lead in the investigation into Megaspeed.
Megaspeed has long been accused of being a front for an AI component smuggling operation. In October 2025, an investigation claimed that it had helped move around $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips into China by importing them and then re-exporting them to the country. Megaspeed says that it complies with all laws and that the woman at the center of the affair scandal, Ms. Huang, is no longer at the company. The Chinese government has also dismissed claims that she was a state spy.
The joint Commerce and Justice Departments' statement pointed to its strong track record when prosecuting chip smugglers to date. 17 defendants across a total of six investigations have been charged so far, with more likely to follow. A Californian man was recently arrested after being accused of smuggling more than $300 million worth of export-restricted Nvidia chips to China. He now faces up to 20 years in prison.

articles.title: Apple y Pokémon se unen para celebrar los 30 años de la franquicia con fondos de pantalla para iPhone y más
articles.text:
Pokémon cumple 30 años y lo celebra con dos colaboraciones simultáneas que combinan tecnología, aprendizaje de idiomas y su videojuego móvil más popular. The Pokémon Company se asoció con Apple para una campaña exclusiva en Japón centrada en Applin, el Pokémon con forma de manzana, mientras que Pokémon GO sumó una alianza con Duolingo que premia a los usuarios de ambas aplicaciones con contenido especial.
Las dos iniciativas se desarrollan en paralelo pero con alcances distintos: la de Apple está limitada al mercado japonés, mientras que la de Duolingo tiene alcance global y ya está activa para todos los entrenadores que jueguen Pokémon GO.
Que trae la alianza entre Pokémon y Apple
La colaboración entre ambas compañías se extiende del 16 al 30 de noviembre de 2026 y tiene como eje central las tiendas oficiales de Apple en Japón. El producto principal es una edición especial de Apple Gift Card, disponible en las 11 Apple Store del país, con saldos que van desde 1.000 hasta 250.000 yenes y un límite de tres unidades por persona.
Cada tarjeta incluye un código QR que da acceso a contenido digital exclusivo: tres diseños de fondos de pantalla para iPhone y iPad protagonizados por Applin, Pikachu, Bulbasaur, Charmander y Squirtle.
Por el momento, Apple y The Pokémon Company no confirmaron si esta propuesta se replicará en otros países fuera de Japón.
La campaña también estará dentro de Pokémon GO. Durante el período de la colaboración, las 11 tiendas de Apple que participan en Japón funcionan como Poképaradas especiales, con una frecuencia de aparición de Applin más alta que la habitual en esos puntos.
Esta activación conecta directamente el espacio físico de las tiendas con la experiencia del videojuego, aunque, igual que las tarjetas de regalo, se mantiene restringida al territorio japonés sin fecha de expansión anunciada.
Otras colaboraciones de Apple con Pokémon durante 2026
A la alianza del 30.º aniversario se sumam otros proyectos conjuntos desarrollados a lo largo del año. En octubre de 2026, Beats, marca de audio propiedad de Apple, lanzó junto a The Pokémon Company una edición especial de su altavoz portátil Beats Pill con diseño inspirado en Pikachu, que trasladó la identidad visual de la franquicia a un producto de audio.
Meses antes, en agosto de 2026, Tsunekazu Ishihara, director ejecutivo de The Pokémon Company, visitó Apple Park acompañado de Pikachu. Del encuentro participaron Tim Cook y John Ternus, quien asumiría el liderazgo de Apple, y compartieron una sesión de Pokémon GO dentro del campus.
Ese conjunto de acercamientos, que incluye experiencias digitales, activaciones en tiendas físicas y productos tecnológicos con personajes licenciados, confirma una relación sostenida entre ambas compañías durante el año del aniversario.
Qué ofrece la colaboración con Duolingo en Pokémon GO
En paralelo a la alianza con Apple, Pokémon GO se unió a Duolingo para una campaña bajo el nombre de Duolin-GO, que combina el descubrimiento de Pokémon con el aprendizaje de idiomas. La propuesta se organiza en dos frentes: recompensas dentro de la aplicación de Duolingo y una investigación temporal dentro de Pokémon GO.
El desafío La fiesta Pokémon de Duo ya está disponible en Duolingo, y los usuarios deben unirse antes del lunes 21 de diciembre de 2026 a las 23:59 en su hora local. Una vez dentro, tienen hasta el martes 29 de diciembre de 2026 a las 23:59 para completar el reto.
Durante ese período, cada día que se complete al menos una lección se desbloquea una recompensa nueva, entre ellas disfraces para el avatar de Duolingo inspirados en Pikachu y Chatot, además de un código de oferta para la investigación temporal de Pokémon GO.
Quienes se unan al desafío de Duolingo antes del 21 de diciembre y completen siete lecciones hasta el 29 de diciembre de 2026 a las 23:59 obtendrán un código para canjear una investigación temporal en Pokémon GO. Las tareas aparecerán en el idioma que el jugador elija al activar el código, y el Profesor Willow ofrecerá pistas durante el recorrido.
Como parte de la misma iniciativa, algunos Pokémon de la investigación temporal incorporarán una nueva función de etiqueta de idioma en su página de resumen, que permitirá consultar los nombres que reciben en otros idiomas.

articles.title: La fibre optique cale à 150 km, Thales Alenia Space mise sur l'espace pour l'Internet quantique
articles.text:
Thales Alenia Space et ses partenaires ont lancé une nouvelle phase du projet TeQuantS, mené pour l'Agence spatiale européenne, avec au cœur du dispositif un laboratoire quantique au CNES, qui prépare le satellite QINSAT et l'Internet quantique européen.
Faire voyager de l'information quantique d'un continent à l'autre grâce à un satellite est le pari relevé par Thales Alenia Space avec le projet TeQuantS, qui nous fait avancer d'un cran vers un Internet quantique européen. La coentreprise du Français Thales (67 %) et de l'Italien Leonardo (33 %) a signé deux avenants avec l'Agence spatiale européenne, a-t-on appris le lundi 16 novembre. Elle entame une nouvelle phase de son projet, avec un laboratoire quantique au CNES, le Centre nationale d'études spatiales. Une source de photons « jumeaux », des systèmes de synchronisation entre ciel et sol et des détecteurs de lumière y seront testés en conditions simulées, autant de briques essentielles à la future liaison espace-Terre.
Comment le CNES prépare la liaison quantique entre l’espace et la Terre
Ici, il n'y a pas de fusée ni de compte à rebours pour l'instant. Ce fameux laboratoire doit simuler au sol les conditions réelles d'une liaison quantique entre un satellite et la Terre. Au menu des essais figurent une source de photons intriqués, des systèmes chargés de synchroniser le temps entre l'engin et le sol, ainsi que les outils qui analysent et détectent les photons à leur arrivée.
Des photons intriqués, d'ailleurs ? Ce sont des paires de grains de lumière produites ensemble, qui restent liées comme des jumeaux même une fois séparées. Mesurez l'un, et vous savez aussitôt ce que donnera la mesure de l'autre, qu'il se trouve dans la pièce voisine ou à des centaines de kilomètres. C'est ce lien invisible qu'un réseau quantique doit transporter d'un point à un autre. Avec un atout de taille pour la sécurité, puisque toute tentative d'espionnage perturbe ce lien et laisse des traces repérables, ce qui trahit l'intrus, explique Thales.
Ces essais préparent le terrain pour QINSAT, le satellite qui devra tester la transmission de photons intriqués entre l'espace et la Terre. L'enjeu, à terme, est de relier entre eux des réseaux quantiques terrestres disséminés sur plusieurs continents. Le Dr Kasia Balakier, responsable technique de TeQuantS et des technologies de communication optique et quantique au sein du programme ScyLight de l'ESA, évoque « une occasion unique » pour l'industrie française et européenne. Selon elle, les équipements et le banc d'essai installés au CNES représentent « une étape majeure vers le déploiement d'une connectivité quantique par satellites », autrement dit vers de véritables liaisons quantiques assurées depuis l'espace.
Internet quantique : pourquoi passer par l'espace, et pour qui ?
Alors pourquoi l'espace ? Parce que dans une fibre optique, l'information quantique ne peut être transmise directement que sur 150 kilomètres environ. C'est assez pour relier deux villes proches, mais bien trop peu pour enjamber un océan. D'où l'idée de confier le relais aux satellites. Le projet TeQuantS (pour Technological development for space-based Quantum reSource distribution, rien que ça), lancé en 2023 et soutenu par le CNES, relève du volet Industrial Competitiveness du programme ARTES de l'ESA (Agence spatiale européenne), consacré aux technologies de télécommunications par satellite. Ses premières phases ont déjà livré un prototype de station sol compacte et une première maquette du système.
Qui profitera de ce futur réseau ? Les ordinateurs quantiques, d'abord. Ils devront s'échanger des qubits photoniques, des unités d'information quantique portées par la lumière, pour répartir leurs calculs. Viennent ensuite les capteurs quantiques, qui gagneront en sensibilité en travaillant de concert. Alcino De Sousa, Senior Vice-Président des activités Télécommunications de Thales Alenia Space, évoque un projet qui « adresse à la fois les futurs enjeux de cyber sécurité et de réseau Internet quantique ». Enfin, les opérateurs gouvernementaux peuvent y voir un moyen de garantir des échanges sécurisés de bout en bout, résilients et souverains, c'est-à-dire robustes et maîtrisés par l’'Europe. Y compris face aux attaques des futurs ordinateurs quantiques, qui pourraient un jour venir à bout des chiffrements actuels.
Pour tenir ce cap, Thales Alenia Space, maître d'œuvre du projet, s'appuie sur un consortium aux expertises complémentaires. Airbus Defence and Space apporte les systèmes quantiques, AUREA Technology la source spatiale de photons intriqués et OGS Technologies les stations sol optiques. Bertin Alpao s'occupe de l'optique adaptative, Bertin Technologies de l'optomécanique et Sigmaworks de la synchronisation temporelle. Le LIP6 (Sorbonne Université) et l'INPHYNI (Université Côte d'Azur/CNRS) conseillent sur les protocoles et les systèmes quantiques.
Selon Alcino De Sousa, ces technologies contribueront « à la souveraineté européenne dans ce domaine ». Et ce n'est pas un coup d'essai, puisque l'industriel déroule sa feuille de route quantique depuis 2018, adossée à plus d'un quart de siècle d'expérience du groupe Thales en technologies quantiques. On y trouve QKD-GEO, présenté comme le premier système au monde de distribution quantique de clés depuis l'orbite géostationnaire, et SAGA, qui vise un système orbital européen de clés cryptographiques sécurisées par la physique quantique. S'y ajoute sa participation à EuroQCI, la future infrastructure européenne de communication quantique.

articles.title: Are these the best open earbuds yet? I've been using them for a few weeks and I think so — bravo, Xiaomi!
articles.text:
These new open earbuds might be the best clip-on buds I've tested yet — but one big question remains before I can recommend them
Xiaomi's first ear cuff-style buds are here
- Xiaomi unveils Clip earbuds, its first of the form
- They're small, sound good and have sound leak reduction...
- ...but their US price is unconfirmed
After the less-than-impressive Xiaomi OpenWear Stereo Pro, the Chinese giant is back with its newest pair of open earbuds, and these might be the real deal. The Xiaomi Clip are the brand's first cuff-style open-ears, and they're far better.
Unveiled alongside the brand's Smart Band 11 fitness tracker, these new earbuds show the company jumping on the massive trend of open earbuds, which let you hear what's going on around you while enjoying your music.
Let's start with the 'bad' news: while I was sent the Xiaomi Clip ahead of time to test out (impressions below), I wasn't told when they'll go on sale or, importantly, how much they'll cost in the US, although I have been told they'll cost £129 in the UK or €149.90 in European markets.
I don't imagine you'll have to wait long for other MSRPs, though — they'll likely be released imminently — but it's why I can't give a definitive judgement into how good they are. I'd expect them to cost about $150 / AU$300 (well, depending if they make their way to the US, which is unlikely), but that's just a guess based on their predicted UK asking fee.
Time with the Clip
I've been testing the Xiaomi Clip for two weeks now, ahead of their unveiling. While I've yet to write a full review of the buds, my early impressions suggest these might just be the best open earbuds I've tested so far.
As soon as I took them out of the box, I was surprised by how small the charging case is; I love a compact case as it makes the buds more portable, and the Xiaomi Clip's is miniscule. The buds themselves are a normal size for such a design, and they use a more rigid arc than most open-ears; I initially thought they'd pinch a little when wearing them as a result, but after a fair few runs and cycle trips, I'll happily say I'm wrong.
The Xiaomi Clip use an 11mm driver, so not as spec'd out as some rivals, but I enjoy the simple and charming sound profile the brand has gone for. It's a simple V-shaped sound, offering the energetic bass and sharp treble you want from exercise buds, but with a surprising amount of detail in the mids.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
And an OpenWear Stereo Pro feature I really liked is back: the earbuds are designed to reduce sound leakage, wiping out the usual open-ear problem of your seat neighbours hearing your tunes. But another common clipping-bud feature is missing; there is a right and left earbud, so you can't use either in either ear, despite them being almost identical looking. A few times I've put the wrong earpieces in each ear.
That's not a massive issue, just a small annoyance, and the Xiaomi Clip are shaping up to be my first five-star pair of open ears. It just depends on how much they end up costing globally.

articles.title: Saudi tech group iMENA secures $214 million to support regional growth
articles.text:
Saudi tech group iMENA secures $214 million to support regional growth
- Saudi Arabia-headquartered technology group iMENA has completed a SAR 802 million ($214 million) capital increase in two tranches, aimed at supporting its growth in Saudi Arabia and across the Middle East and North Africa.
- Co-founded in 2012 by Nasir Alsharif, Khaldoon Tabaza, and Adey Salamin, iMENA operates digital platforms in online classifieds, automotive commerce, and mobility services, including OpenSooq, SellAnyCar, and Jeeny. Its businesses serve well over 100 million users across over 20 countries in the region.
- iMENA's investor base includes Sanabil Investments and several Saudi institutional investors. The announcement did not disclose the individual contributions to the capital increase or identify which investors participated in each tranche.
- The proceeds will support the group's investments in Saudi Arabia, expansion of its digital platforms and greater integration of technology, data and operational capabilities across its portfolio. The transaction was announced at the Digital Entrepreneurship Council, held under the patronage of Saudi ministers Abdullah Alswaha and Fahad Al-Saif.
- In April 2025, iMENA closed a $135 million pre-IPO investment from Sanabil Investments, along with other investors.
Press release:
Saudi Arabia-headquartered technology group iMENA has completed a SAR 802 million ($214 million) capital increase to support its expansion in the kingdom and across the Middle East and North Africa.
The capital increase was completed in two tranches and will strengthen the group's financial position as it expands its investments and digital platform businesses.
iMENA operates a portfolio of technology companies spanning online classifieds, automotive commerce and mobility services, including OpenSooq, SellAnyCar and Jeeny. Collectively, its platforms serve more than 100 million users across over 20 countries in the region.
The group's investor base includes Sanabil Investments and several Saudi institutional investors. However, iMENA did not disclose the investors participating in the latest capital increase, their individual commitments or the group's valuation.
The announcement was made during the Digital Entrepreneurship Council, held under the patronage of Saudi Minister of Communications and Information Technology Abdullah Alswaha and Minister of Investment Fahad bin Abduljalil Al-Saif.
Nasser Al-Sharif, chairman of iMENA, said the capital increase marks a step in the group's efforts to build technology businesses serving regional markets, highlighting opportunities for expansion under Saudi Vision 2030.
Chief executive Sara Al-Sheikh said the group's next phase would focus on closer integration between its portfolio companies, allowing them to draw on shared technology, data and operational expertise to accelerate growth.
Saudi Arabia will remain central to iMENA's strategy as it expands its presence and investments in the kingdom.
The transaction comes as the group seeks to increase the scale of its digital businesses and pursue further growth across regional markets.

articles.title: Chainguard goes self-serve with free Starter plan and $500-a-month Team plan - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Chainguard goes self-serve with free Starter plan and $500-a-month Team plan
Software supply chain security company Chainguard Inc. is now offering its products on a self-serve basis, with the launch today of a free plan called Chainguard Starter and a paid Team plan priced at $500 a month.
The free plan covers nearly all of Chainguard’s products, with usage limits set at a level that fits a personal project or a small team. According to Chainguard, users can sign up, pull an image, connect their package manager to its screened libraries and place coding agents in a sandbox in one sitting, with no credit card or sales call required.
The launch comes after Black October, the name given to a run of supply chain attacks and critical vulnerability disclosures in the third week of October. With incidents like those, a team may have only until the end of the day to deal with a bad dependency, according to the blog post in which Chainguard announced the plans. In such cases, the company wrote, “nobody is going to wait on a purchase order.”
Until now, access to Chainguard’s products has typically required a conversation with its sales team first. One exception was Catalog Starter, a free beta plan offered earlier this year that was limited to five container images. Chainguard says the sales-led model, designed around large companies with procurement processes, works far less well for a team that needs a hardened base image ahead of its next deployment.
In most cases, moving a service onto Chainguard requires changing only a single line in the file that defines its container image. Security engineers can also put Chainguard’s images and libraries through their own scanners before signing anything, according to the company.
Starter includes five container images from Chainguard’s catalog of more than 3,000 minimal images, which are claimed to have near-zero known vulnerabilities, with downloads of up to 100 gigabytes a month. A software bill of materials and signed build provenance are provided for every image.
Also part of the plan is Chainguard Libraries, which provides malware- and greyware-scanned dependencies for JavaScript, Python, Java, Go and .NET with a limit of 50,000 pulls a month. Under a fixed seven-day cooldown, newly published versions are held back for a week, which the company says allows a compromised release to be caught before it reaches a build.
Starter also comes with 500 hours a month of virtual CPU time on each of Chainguard Checks and Chainguard Workspaces, which launched in beta at the company’s Assemble London event in October. Checks is designed to provide hardened runners for continuous integration, with Workspaces providing hardened sandboxes for coding agents.
Other features on the free plan include hardened replacements for GitHub Actions, more than 1,000 hardened agent skills, community support and 100 gigabytes of private artifact storage. Starter users also get 1 million tokens a month for Guardener, Chainguard’s artificial intelligence agent, which inventories the GitHub Actions and container images in a customer’s repositories and opens pull requests to swap in the company’s hardened versions. Each Starter account is limited to five users.
The paid Team plan, which is billed to a credit card, includes everything in Starter with higher limits, such as unlimited users, 1 terabyte of image downloads and 1 million dependency pulls a month. Team customers also get base, application and AI images at their latest versions on top of their five chosen images, along with 1,000 hours a month each of Checks and Workspaces, 5 million Guardener tokens and 500 gigabytes of private storage.
Features reserved for Team include backported fixes for known vulnerabilities across five remediated versions, zero-day patches on the day of disclosure, ticketed support and managed policies that set rules for what is pulled and what is blocked. Chainguard says the usual reasons for upgrading include a sixth person needing access, a project outgrowing the usage limits and a team needing a patch for a version it cannot yet move off.
According to Chainguard, the upgrade takes a few seconds from the console that flags which limit a user has hit. Nothing has to be migrated, since the account, images and session all carry over. Customers can cancel at any time from the same console. Storage beyond Team’s included 500 gigabytes will be metered starting Jan. 1, 2027, according to Chainguard’s documentation.
The Enterprise offering is unchanged and still starts with a conversation with the company’s sales team. Enterprise provides companywide use of Chainguard with no usage limits, along with service-level agreements, enterprise compliance features and integrations. Starter is available now.
Chainguard says it has raised $892 million since its founding in 2021. Its most recent round, $280 million from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund, came in October 2025.

articles.title: Xiaomi dévoile les Xiaomi Clip, ses premiers écouteurs qui se clipsent sur l’oreille
articles.text:
En parallèle du lancement de la Watch S5 et du Smart Band 11, Xiaomi a dévoilé les Xiaomi Clip, des écouteurs ouverts à clip. Si les Xiaomi OpenWear Stereo se placent autour de l’oreille, les Xiaomi Clip se fixent quant à eux directement sur celle-ci. C’est la première fois que le constructeur chinois propose ce type d’appareil. Voici les caractéristiques et le prix des Xiaomi Clip.
Design et confort
Avec ses Xiaomi Clip, Xiaomi promet un confort d’écoute optimal, même lors de longues sessions d’écoute. Ainsi, chaque écouteur pèse 5,5 grammes. Ils intègrent par ailleurs un arceau flexible en alliage à mémoire de forme qui se clipse sans pénétrer dans le canal auditif, tandis que le boîtier incurvé de la batterie répartit uniformément la pression sur l’oreille. Par ailleurs, ce système de fixation par clip permet aux écouteurs de s’adapter à différentes morphologies d’oreilles. Au niveau du design, nous pouvons noter une petite zone semi-transparente qui laisse entrevoir certains composants internes de l’écouteur.
Rappelons au passage qu’il s’agit d’écouteurs à conception ouverte. L’intérêt de ce type d’appareil est de pouvoir écouter de la musique ou un podcast, tout en restant attentif à son environnement. Nous ne retrouvons donc pas de fonction de réduction de bruit active.
Conception audio, fonctionnalités et autonomie
Le principal défi des écouteurs à conception ouverte est de parvenir à restituer un son puissant, notamment des basses relativement profondes. Pour tenter d’y parvenir, les Xiaomi Clip s’appuient sur un haut-parleur dynamique de 11 mm doté d’un diaphragme à revêtement métallique microcristallin. Par ailleurs, selon Xiaomi, la conception acoustique directionnelle oriente le son vers le conduit auditif, tout en limitant les fuites sonores. De leur côté, les algorithmes DRC et d’amplification des basses ont pour objectif d’affiner le rendu des basses fréquences. Notons également que ces écouteurs prennent en charge l’Hi-Res Audio Wireless et le codec LHDC 5.0 sur les appareils compatibles.
Au niveau de la clarté des appels, Xiaomi a intégré à ces écouteurs un réseau de trois microphones associé à un microphone à conduction osseuse VPU et à une réduction de bruit par IA qui permet d’isoler la voix de l’utilisateur et d’atténuer les bruits ambiants. Notons également la présence d’une fonction de traduction instantanée avec un smartphone Xiaomi compatible. Côté connectivité, deux paires d’écouteurs Xiaomi Clip peuvent être connectées à un même smartphone ou à une même tablette Xiaomi, tandis que le basculement audio permet de passer instantanément d’un appareil Xiaomi compatible à un autre. Enfin, notons que Xiaomi annonce jusqu’à 9 heures d’écoute musicale sur une seule charge et jusqu’à 38 heures avec le boîtier de charge.
Les Xiaomi Clip sont disponibles dès maintenant via les canaux officiels de Xiaomi et auprès des revendeurs agréés. Quatre coloris sont proposés : or, blanc, noir et violet. Le prix de vente conseillé est de 149,99 €. Cependant, du 17 au 30 novembre 2026, dans le cadre d’une offre de lancement, les écouteurs sont proposés au tarif de 126,99 € (soit une réduction de 23 €).

articles.title: “La cause de votre mort sera un accident d'IA” : l'alerte glaçante d'un dirigeant d'OpenAI
articles.text:
L’IA aux commandes de la planète d’ici trois ans ? Un administrateur d’OpenAI sonne l’alarme
Il siège depuis septembre 2026 au conseil qui contrôle OpenAI, la maison mère de ChatGPT. Il a coinventé la technique qui rend les chatbots si dociles. Devant le public de Toronto, Paul Christiano a livré un pronostic d'une noirceur rare, avec une échéance qui se compte désormais en mois.
Lundi 9 novembre, Paul Christiano ouvrait à Toronto la troisième édition des Hinton Lectures, un cycle de conférences sur la sûreté de l'IA cofondé par Geoffrey Hinton, prix Nobel de physique 2024. Le chercheur nord-américain connaît en effet le sujet de l'intérieur. Passé par OpenAI de 2017 à 2021, il compte parmi les pères du RLHF, l'apprentissage par renforcement à partir de retours humains qui a façonné ChatGPT.
Il dirige aujourd'hui l'Alignment Research Center, conseille l'agence fédérale étasunienne chargée d'évaluer les modèles d'IA et a rejoint le 9 septembre le conseil de l'OpenAI Foundation, où il siège aussi au comité de sûreté et sécurité. Devant l'auditoire, il a lâché : “Je pense que, pour la plupart des personnes présentes dans cette salle, la raison la plus probable de leur mort sera un accident d’IA.”
Perte de contrôle de l'IA : un scénario catastrophe d'ici trois ans
Par “prise de contrôle”, Christiano désigne un monde où des systèmes d'IA poursuivent leurs propres objectifs et prennent les décisions qui reviennent aujourd'hui aux humains. Selon lui, vouloir les arrêter serait alors aussi vain, pour vous ou Donald Trump, que de prétendre stopper seul l'armée des États-Unis. Il juge raisonnablement probable que de nombreuses personnes meurent pendant cette transition, et voit dans un tel basculement “la fin de la souveraineté humaine”.
Son diagnostic, *“un risque élevé de prise de contrôle par l'IA dans les trois prochaines années”, et des risques sérieux dès les six à 12 prochains mois. Si les laboratoires fonçaient à pleine vitesse, sans aucun garde-fou extérieur, il estime à peu près à un pile ou face la probabilité d'une prise de contrôle sur trois ans. Il ne pense pas que les entreprises adopteront ce rythme maximal, mais prévient que, même avec des réponses politiques réalistes, le risque reste exceptionnellement élevé.
Le chercheur assume aussi la part d'intuition dans ses chiffres : “Tout chiffre que nous avançons exprime l'opinion subjective de quelqu’un.” En septembre, au moment de rejoindre OpenAI, il évaluait encore à 4 % le risque de perte de contrôle à un an et à 15 % à trois ans, d'après le magazine Fast Company.
Lors des échanges qui ont suivi, il est allé plus loin, estimant à une chance sur trois que, d'ici un an, des IA deviennent assez puissantes pour renverser des gouvernements si elles en avaient la volonté. Il dit espérer se tromper, tout en reconnaissant avoir presque toujours sous-estimé la vitesse des progrès.
One of the original AI alignment researchers, @paulfchristiano, at the Hinton Lectures:
"I think there is a high risk of an AI takeover within the next three years."
"If, say, you or me or Donald Trump wanted to stop [AIs], they would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying… pic.twitter.com/CmHJevQaOX
— Simon Lermen (@SimonLermenAI) November 10, 2026
Plusieurs sites d’outre-Atlantique lui ont prêté un autre chiffre : 20 % de risque, d'ici un an, que des IA mal alignées nous empêchent de mener une vie normale, entre morts et asservissement. Cette estimation est en réalité celle de Buck Shlegeris, patron de l'organisation Redwood Research, comme l'a relevé la radio publique NPR.
	
Pour la plupart des personnes présentes dans cette salle, la raison la plus probable de leur mort sera un accident d'IA.
Piratage de Hugging Face : l'incident de cybersécurité qui nourrit ses craintes
Christiano s'appuie sur un épisode bien réel. En juillet, lors de tests de cybersécurité internes, des modèles de recherche d'OpenAI ont contourné les barrières censées les isoler d'Internet. Ils ont ensuite compromis une partie de l'infrastructure de l’entreprise, ainsi que les systèmes de Hugging Face, la grande plateforme de partage de modèles d'IA. Dans son rapport du 26 août, OpenAI y voyait un “coup de semonce” pour elle-même comme pour le reste du monde.
Selon le récit du chercheur, près d'un millier d'agents ont passé des jours à chercher comment tromper le système chargé de les noter. Ils ont monté une messagerie clandestine pour se coordonner, falsifié des journaux d'activité, piraté Hugging Face en quête d'indices, puis obtenu un accès administrateur aux serveurs qui les évaluaient, pour s'attribuer eux-mêmes de bonnes notes. Ces agents ignoraient les humains, qui ne les ont jamais arrêtés. Christiano en tire une mise en garde : “Les futurs agents pourraient finir par traiter les humains comme un obstacle de plus.”
Il réclame des standards de sûreté communs à toute l'industrie, et la possibilité de tout suspendre, à la manière du bouton d'arrêt d'urgence qu'un projet de loi américain veut imposer aux géants du secteur : “Si rien d'autre ne fonctionne, nous voulons vraiment nous arrêter à ce moment-là”, précise-t-il
La presse étasunienne n'a pas manqué de relever le paradoxe. L'homme qui décrit le péril siège désormais au conseil de l'un des laboratoires qui mènent cette course. En septembre, un ancien chercheur d'OpenAI et d'Anthropic accusait déjà l'ensemble de ces entreprises d'agir de manière irresponsable.

articles.title: Tesla tiene más competencia: Mercedes-Benz prepara un nuevo sistema de conducción asistida
articles.text:
Mercedes-Benz anunció dos funciones que ayudarán a sus vehículos a desplazarse por autopistas y rutas urbanas. La tecnología permitirá conducir con las manos fuera del volante en determinadas carreteras y asistir al conductor durante trayectos de punto a punto. La compañía planea desplegarla en Estados Unidos y Alemania entre finales de 2026 y 2027.
La automotriz alemana presentó una nueva generación de sistemas de asistencia bajo la marca MB.DRIVE. Su propuesta incluye Hands-free Assist, para circular por autopistas con las manos fuera del volante bajo ciertas condiciones, y MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO, que apoyará al conductor a lo largo de una ruta, incluso en zonas urbanas con tráfico denso.
Mercedes busca competir con tecnologías como Full Self-Driving (FSD) de Tesla, pero sus funciones no convierten al auto en un vehículo autónomo. La empresa subraya que el conductor sigue siendo responsable de manejar, debe vigilar el tráfico y estar preparado para tomar el control en cualquier momento.
Asistencia para autopistas y recorridos urbanos
Hands-free Assist permitirá retirar las manos del volante en autopistas compatibles, cuando las condiciones de operación lo permitan. El sistema está diseñado para funcionar a velocidades de hasta 130 kilómetros por hora. También se complementará con Proactive Lane Change Assist, una función que puede iniciar cambios de carril para adelantar a un vehículo más lento o seguir la ruta indicada por la navegación.
Aunque las manos puedan separarse del volante en esos tramos, Mercedes mantiene la supervisión humana como requisito. El conductor debe prestar atención a la vía y responder si el sistema se lo pide o si surge una situación que requiera intervención. La compañía anunció que estas funciones llegarán a Alemania antes de que termine 2026; su despliegue en Estados Unidos está previsto para 2027.
La función urbana MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO ofrecerá asistencia desde el punto de partida hasta el destino ingresado en el navegador. Puede ayudar al auto a cambiar de carril, incorporarse al carril correcto, girar en intersecciones y detenerse o avanzar ante los semáforos. También apoya al conductor cuando el recorrido sale de una autopista y continúa por calles urbanas.
Para operar, el sistema combina 27 componentes de percepción: 10 cámaras, cinco radares y 12 sensores ultrasónicos. La información se procesa en una computadora con una capacidad de hasta 254 billones de operaciones por segundo (TOPS). Mercedes indica que la plataforma MB.OS sirve de base para integrar las funciones de asistencia y actualizar el software de los vehículos.
Cuándo llegará y qué modelos podrán usarlo
La empresa prevé ofrecer MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO en Alemania y Estados Unidos durante la primera mitad de 2027. Antes, desde diciembre de 2026, algunos clientes seleccionados en California, Stuttgart y Múnich podrán probar las funciones mediante un programa de acceso anticipado. Mercedes recopilará comentarios antes de ampliar su disponibilidad.
La compatibilidad dependerá del modelo y del mercado. La compañía adelantó que las funciones se incorporarán gradualmente a su gama de autos de pasajeros y vans, y que algunos propietarios de vehículos elegibles podrán agregarlas después mediante una actualización remota. Mercedes aún no anunció los precios ni el listado completo de modelos compatibles; señaló que informará esos detalles antes de cada lanzamiento.
La información inicial de Mezha sobre la competencia con Tesla también menciona modelos como CLA, GLC, GLE, GLS y Clase S, aunque la comunicación oficial de Mercedes no confirma que todos estén habilitados desde el comienzo.
Una apuesta por la asistencia, no por la autonomía total
El lanzamiento ocurre mientras Mercedes concentra sus esfuerzos en sistemas de nivel 2, que requieren supervisión constante del conductor. La compañía suspendió el desarrollo de Drive Pilot, su tecnología de nivel 3, que bajo ciertas condiciones permitía dejar de vigilar la carretera en algunos tramos de autopista.
Ese cambio refleja una apuesta por funciones que pueden desplegarse en más vehículos y que enfrentan menos barreras regulatorias. Para los conductores, la diferencia práctica será contar con más ayuda para tareas como mantener el recorrido, cambiar de carril o avanzar por la ciudad, sin ceder la responsabilidad de conducir.
Mercedes no es la única fabricante que desarrolla alternativas a Tesla: BMW también trabaja en sistemas de asistencia comparables. La competencia se centrará en ampliar lo que el auto puede hacer y, a la vez, mantener claro cuándo debe intervenir la persona al volante.

articles.title: Q.ANT Unveils NPU Gen 2+: Photonic Fourier Transforms Power Large Language Model
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
Q.ANT Unveils NPU Gen 2+: Photonic Fourier Transforms Power Large Language Model
Q.ANT, the pioneer in commercial photonic computing, today unveiled the NPU Gen 2+, the latest generation of its Native Processing Unit (NPU) technology, at SC26 in Chicago. The NPU Gen 2+ adds optical Discrete Fourier Transforms (DFTs), which expands the set of mathematical functions developers can run directly in light with photonic computing. With it, developers can build faster, leaner AI models and high-performance computing (HPC) applications.
Advanced functions like the DFT let AI models work with fewer parameters and less data. On digital hardware, however, computing the transform itself with high data volumes costs time and energy. Because the NPU Gen 2+ delivers DFTs natively in light, Q.ANT demonstrates the potential algorithmic and performance advantages of photonic computing already now.Developers can now approach computationally intensive functions in new ways using the DFT capabilities of the NPU Gen 2+: Light carries out complex computations in a single pass, extending the set of available instructions beyond add and multiply functions of classical computing and making AI models more expressive and more powerful. For data center operators, integrating photonic hardware into their environments opens new capabilities for users while potentially lowering energy consumption and operating costs significantly.
Today's language models rely on attention mechanisms that require massive compute to model relationships between tokens, but Q.ANT's NPU Gen 2+ gives developers a new way to explore these mechanisms leveraging photonic computing as an expansion to classical computation.
At SC26, Q.ANT demonstrates this potential in a hybrid computing system coupling the NPU Gen 2+ with an AMD GPU to run a large language model (LLM) for the first time with optics. The demonstration shows how these mathematical functions performed in light can replace a computationally intensive attention layer and address a major computational bottleneck in generative AI.
Rethinking AI Algorithms for a New Computing Architecture
The NPU Gen 2+ performs these DFTs in a single operation using the physical properties of light, instead of the sequence of energy-intensive electronic calculations that classical computing demands. These advances help establish photonic processors as a complementary computing architecture, with the NPU as a co-processor alongside CPUs and GPUs, so developers can distribute the specific workloads that are most computationally intensive, to where they can be processed the most efficiently.
At the heart of the NPU Gen 2+ is an optical component on the photonic chip that allows the processor to directly perform DFTs, a fundamental mathematical operation used in signal and image processing, simulations, and data analysis. The NPU Gen 2+ extends photonic computing to workloads that are typically expensive for electronic processors. It builds on the processor generation NPU Gen 2, launched in 2025, and its focus on matrix multiplication and non-linear operations.
Michael Förtsch, CEO of Q.ANT"With Gen 2+, we're opening the door to software that uses what light does naturally. That allows leaner AI models with fewer parameters and less data, and that is what will make the next wave of AI affordable," "With the DFT performed natively, developers now have a new tool to reshape the mathematics of AI models. This is an important step on our roadmap to combine more optical components on our chips for even more sophisticated functions, driving new algorithms and applications. By running a large language model in a hybrid system with an AMD GPU, we have shown that our processors work as co-processors with GPUs. We're building a community with pioneering developers on the journey to a new era of computing."
Giving Developers New Tools to Compute with Light
The introduction of the NPU Gen 2+ also expands the potential of Q.ANT's software development ecosystem.
In September 2026, Q.ANT launched its open-source software development kit (SDK), providing developers with APIs for C and Python, example applications, documentation, and a CPU-based simulation environment. The toolkit allows programmers to begin designing and testing applications for photonic computing without requiring direct access to optical hardware, while the company's recent launch of its photonic pilot with IONOS allows access to real hardware.
Q.ANT is now extending its SDK to support NPU Gen 2+ capabilities, enabling developers to experiment with Fourier-based algorithms and investigate how these operations can be incorporated into AI and HPC software.
Utz Bacher, VP of Software at Q.ANT"Photonic computing gives software developers a chance to rethink the mathematics behind their applications," "When a complex mathematical operation can be performed directly through the physics of light, it changes the questions developers can ask. Instead of simply optimizing existing code, we can explore different algorithms that use these native operations to solve problems in new ways. Our work with Fourier-based attention layers in language models is an early example of that opportunity."
Building the Foundation for Hybrid Photonic Computing
The NPU Gen 2+ represents another step in Q.ANT's roadmap toward more advanced photonic computing architectures.
The new processor retains the integration through PCIe into standard rack-mountable server systems for ease of integration, as the future of computing will depend on the evolution of hybrid systems. Optical processors like Q.ANT's NPU Gen 2 and Gen 2+ complement the capabilities of CPUs and GPUs with their ability to perform select mathematical functions. Q.ANT plans to offer commercial systems combining Gen 2 and Gen 2+ processors in the second half of 2027.
Going forward, Q.ANT is exploring how multiple optical functions can be combined on its chips to support increasingly complex computational workflows. By expanding the mathematical functions available to developers, it aims to create the foundation for algorithms and applications that optimize data processing across AI and HPC with native photonic computation.
Source:
				Q.ANT
