articles.title: Gigabyte prépare ses PC portables Intel Nova Lake et AMD Zen 6 : une fuite relance l’attente
articles.text:
Gigabyte aura semble-t-il de belles choses à nous montrer au CES. Une fuite en provenance de Russie nous renseigne sur la gamme pratiquement complète de PC portables gamers et créatifs attendus chez la marque taïwanaise début 2027. Voici ce que l’on apprend.
Des PC portables pour les joueurs, qu’ils soient fortunés ou qu'ils le soient un peu moins, mais aussi pour les créateurs de contenus ou les mordus d’IA locale. C’est ce que l’on retient d’une liste, a priori complète, ou presque, ayant fuité cette semaine pour les modèles Gigabyte attendus dans les prochains mois.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Gigabyte exposé par l’EEC
Cette fuite nous provient en l’occurrence d’une source officielle : l’EEC (Eurasian Economic Commission). Il s’agit de l’organe de régulation de l’Union économique eurasiatique (qui réunit la Russie, la Biélorussie, le Kazakhstan, l’Arménie et le Kirghizistan).
Les appareils qui utilisent du chiffrement, comme les PC portables, les smartphones ou les tablettes, doivent obligatoirement y être déclarés avant de pouvoir être commercialisés sur ces différents marchés, ce qui explique les nombreuses fuites de produits n’ayant pas encore été annoncés émanant de cette source.
Ces précisions étant faites, on apprend que Gigabyte nous préparerait une trentaine de nouveaux appareils au total, répartis au sein de ses gammes Aorus, Eagle, Gaming et Aero. Ces modèles représente selon toute logique la prochaine génération d’appareils de la marque, attendue début 2027 lors du CES. Nous devrions donc avoir l’opportunité d’en découvrir au moins une partie à Las Vegas, en janvier.
Une trentaine de nouveaux laptops en fuite, dont un modèle RTX Spark
On vous passe le décryptage fastidieux des différents suffixes de ces appareils, renvoyant tantôt à des configuration Intel, tantôt à de possibles configurations AMD, ou carrément à de nouvelles lignées, mais l’on retient que Gigabyte ferait cohabiter de nouveau des processeurs AMD (potentiellement Zen 6) et Intel (potentiellement Nova Lake) sur ses PC portable gaming haut de gamme, dont le futur Aorus Master 16 Gen 3. Ce dernier pourrait d’ailleurs s’équiper de RTX 5070 Ti, 5080 ou 5090 côté GPU, en fonction des options choisies.
Sur le milieu de gamme, représenté notamment par la lignée « Gaming », Gigabyte miserait une nouvelle fois sur des RTX 5050 et 5060, voire 5070. En d’autres termes, il y aurait peu de changement de ce point de vue face au milieu de gamme actuel de la marque… même si l'on peut s’attendre à des évolutions côté affichage ou châssis par rapport à certains modèles comme le très bon Gigabyte Gaming 16 que nous testions l’année dernière.
Plus intéressant, certains documents de l’EEC font mention d’un « AERO AION GR6XK Copilot+ PC » basé sur une plateforme à la mode : RTX Spark. L’appareil serait donc le premier à s'équiper d’une puce NVIDIA N1X chez Gigabyte. On a hâte d’en savoir plus.
Source : VideoCardz

articles.title: Amazon plans $7B renewable energy investment in India by 2030
articles.text:
Amazon plans $7B renewable energy investment in India by 2030
The proposed investment will be over and above the USD 4 billion the company has already contracted in renewable energy projects in India, Amazon said on Tuesday, making it one of the country's largest corporate purchasers of carbon-free energy.
E-commerce giant Amazon plans to invest an additional $7 billion in renewable energy projects in India by 2030, expanding its presence in the country's clean energy market as it seeks to meet growing electricity requirements and reduce the carbon intensity of power used across its operations.
The proposed investment will be over and above the $4 billion the company has already contracted in renewable energy projects in India, Amazon said on Tuesday, making it one of the country's largest corporate purchasers of carbon-free energy.
The company also announced four new utility-scale wind and solar projects with a combined capacity of 934 megawatts (MW) across Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. The projects have been secured through power purchase agreements (PPAs) and form part of its existing $4 billion contracted investment portfolio.
The projects comprise a 234 MW wind farm in Karnataka, Amazon's largest contracted wind project in Asia to date; a 200 MW hybrid wind and solar project, also in Karnataka; a 300 MW solar project in Madhya Pradesh; and a 200 MW solar project in Rajasthan.
Once operational, Amazon's contracted renewable energy projects in India will have a combined capacity of more than 2 gigawatts (GW), equivalent to the annual electricity requirements of more than 3.5 million Indian households, the company said in a statement.
Amazon did not provide a breakdown of the proposed $7 billion investment, identify the projects it intends to develop under the additional commitment or specify the timeline for deploying the capital beyond its 2030 target.
The investment forms part of a broader global push by Amazon to decarbonise the electricity powering its operations. The company on Tuesday announced a target to reduce the carbon intensity of electricity used across its operations by 65 per cent by 2030, compared with a 2019 baseline.
The target means each unit of electricity consumed by the company would be associated with 65 per cent fewer carbon emissions by the end of the decade. It is part of Amazon's broader Climate Pledge commitment to achieve net-zero carbon emissions across its operations by 2040.
"Our renewable energy investments in India reflect years of sustained effort, planning, and collaboration across the industry. This additional investment of USD 7 billion underlines our long-term commitment, helping bring additional wind and solar capacity online while contributing to India's energy security and long-term renewable energy ambitions," Kara Hurst, Amazon's chief sustainability officer, said.
Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi welcomed the investment, saying it would support India's clean energy ambitions, strengthen energy security and demonstrate growing confidence among global companies in the country's renewable energy sector, according to the statement.
Amazon's Indian renewable energy portfolio currently includes 14 utility-scale wind and solar projects, alongside 43 on-site solar installations across its facilities. Together, the 57 projects are intended to expand carbon-free electricity supply to the grid as well as meet part of the company's operational energy requirements.
Globally, Amazon has contracted more than 700 wind and solar projects with a combined capacity exceeding 40 GW, making it one of the world's largest corporate purchasers of carbon-free energy.
The company's sustainability investments in India extend to transportation, water management and packaging.
Amazon said it had deployed more than 15,000 electric vehicles across more than 500 Indian cities and was working with Tata Motors to introduce 3,000 electric trucks, which it described as the largest planned electric truck fleet by an e-commerce company in India.
It also said it had achieved water-positive status in India in 2025, ahead of its 2027 target, replenishing more than 120% of the water consumed across its direct operations. Its water replenishment projects, backed by investments exceeding Rs 62 crore, are expected to replenish more than 4 billion litres annually.
In packaging, more than half of Amazon's customer orders in India are shipped in reduced or original packaging, while the company is collaborating with IIT Roorkee to develop alternative packaging materials using agricultural residue.
The renewable energy commitment comes as India seeks to expand non-fossil-fuel electricity generation to meet rising power demand while advancing its longer-term emissions reduction and net-zero objectives. Large corporate power purchase agreements can provide long-term demand visibility for renewable energy developers and support investment in new generation capacity.

articles.title: La ciencia quiere jubilar el IMC como medida de la obesidad. Pero sustituirlo por una cinta métrica tampoco es tan sencillo
articles.text:
Durante mucho tiempo, para determinar si una persona tenía obesidad o no, se ha usado el cálculo del IMC, dividiendo el peso en kilos por el cuadrado de la altura en metros. Sin embargo, son muchas las voces que han ido surgiendo en contra de ceñirse únicamente a esta medida, apostando más por el perímetro de la cintura o por un conjunto de datos interrelacionados.
Viene de lejos. La recomendación no es una ocurrencia divulgativa, sino el reflejo directo de un macroestudio publicado en la revista Nature. Un trabajo que supone un nuevo paradigma para redefinir la obesidad, puesto que, tras analizar datos de 844.108 adultos, se ha visto qué ocurre cuando se cruza el clásico índice de masa corporal con el perímetro de la cintura y el índice cintura-talla.
El resultado confirma que el IMC, utilizado en solitario, sobrestimaba la obesidad en entre un 1,2 % y un 3,1 % de los participantes, pero lo más preocupante es que deja escapar entre un 5,2 % y un 8,6 % de los casos reales de exceso de grasa.
¿Por qué pasa? El problema del IMC es matemático y anatómico, puesto que en su concepción nunca fue diseñado para evaluar el estado de salud de una persona en concreto. Y es que la fórmula es ciega a la composición corporal, ya que no distingue si un kilo extra corresponde a masa muscular, tejido óseo o grasa, ni tampoco revela dónde se almacena esa grasa.
Desde el punto de vista fisiopatológico, la diferencia es bastante importante porque la grasa subcutánea no es tan "mala" si la comparamos con la grasa visceral que se infiltra en el abdomen y en el hígado, que sí dispara la inflamación crónica o la resistencia a la insulina.
Se ha ido estudiando. La ciencia lleva más de 15 años acumulando pruebas de esta ceguera individual y ya en 2010 un metaanálisis evaluó el rendimiento del punto de corte de IMC de 30 que marca la obesidad. Aquí lo que se vio es que este índice pasaba por alto a más de la mitad de las personas con un exceso real de grasa corporal.
Se desmorona. Ante todas estas pruebas que hemos recopilado, las instituciones médicas han empezado a desmontar el monopolio del IMC, aunque no sin problemas. En junio de 2023, la AMA aprobó una política oficial reconociendo las severas limitaciones que tiene el IMC e instando a usar los indicadores de grasa visceral, composición corporal, masa grasa relativa o el perímetro de cintura.
El paso más ambicioso llegó en 2025 cuando un artículo publicado por The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology apuntó a la necesidad de jubilar el IMC como criterio diagnóstico aislado, ya que para diagnosticar obesidad es necesario medir directamente la grasa corporal total, combinar el IMC con al menos una medida antropométrica adicional o cumplir dos criterios antropométricos independientemente del peso.
El segundo cambio consiste en dividir la condición en dos categorías: obesidad preclínica, cuando existe exceso de grasa pero los órganos y tejidos funcionan con normalidad, y obesidad clínica, cuando esa adiposidad ya está provocando alteraciones funcionales o enfermedades crónicas.
La cinta métrica tampoco. Si el IMC resulta insuficiente, la tentación inmediata en consulta y en casa es sustituirlo por una simple cinta métrica alrededor del abdomen. Pero la evidencia fisiológica recuerda que el perímetro de la cintura tiene sus propias limitaciones técnicas y dista de ser una medida perfecta de la grasa peligrosa.
El primer problema es que una cinta métrica rodea todo el contorno abdominal sin poder distinguir qué parte del volumen corresponde a grasa visceral, que está alojada en profundidad entre las vísceras, y qué parte es simple grasa subcutánea situada justo bajo la piel. Dicho de otro modo, medir la cintura sigue siendo, en gran medida, un reflejo de la grasa subcutánea abdominal más que una ventana directa al tejido adiposo metabólicamente tóxico.
Otro problema. Hay que tener en cuenta que tampoco existe un protocolo anatómico universalmente aceptado para colocar la cinta. Mientras unas guías indican medir en el punto medio entre la última costilla y la cresta ilíaca, otras toman como referencia el ombligo, la parte más estrecha del torso o el borde superior de la cresta ilíaca.
Y esto es importante, puesto que, según el punto anatómico elegido, la proporción de personas clasificadas con perímetro de cintura elevado fluctúa entre un 10 % y un 20 % en mujeres y entre un 6 % y un 10 % en hombres, y en todos los puntos analizados la medición sigue correlacionando mejor con la grasa subcutánea que con la visceral.

articles.title: SEC reportedly investigating Nvidia amid Huang exit | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The Securities and Exchange Commission is opening a civil probe into Nvidia over whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, according to The Wall Street Journal.
The investigation adds to Nvidia’s stack of drama after CEO Jensen Huang resigned following news of his extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based data company Megaspeed.
The Commerce Department has been investigating Megaspeed since late 2024 under suspicion that the company diverted some of its Nvidia chips to China, which would violate U.S. export laws.
Congress has also demanded that Huang answer questions about his affair and how it might have affected his stance that export restrictions should be loosened. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent put it more bluntly over the weekend, accusing Nvidia of knowingly selling powerful chips to China to “goose their revenues and their earnings.”
The news of the SEC probe also comes as Nvidia reports earnings to a market that has seen its stock fall more than 10% since Huang departed. The chipmaker reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago.

articles.title: LanceDB raises $57.5M to accelerate AI model training with multimodal data platform - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
LanceDB raises $57.5M to accelerate AI model training with multimodal data platform
LanceDB Inc., the developer of database technology designed to speed up artificial intelligence models, today announced it has raised $57.5 million in early-stage funding to bring a multimodal lakehouse to researchers, model builders and platform teams.
Bessemer Venture Partners and Innovation Endeavors led the Series B round. Other investors in the round included Theory Ventures, Dimension, Swift Ventures, CRV and Y Combinator, bringing the company’s total funding to $98.5 million.
AI is making it easier to create and interpret increasingly complex forms of data, but creating it also brings an infrastructure problem. LanceDB is tackling this problem by providing a unified multimodal data lakehouse, giving researchers, enterprise outfits and AI agents a unified way to access, find, prepare and train on that data without spending weeks managing the underlying infrastructure.
“Typically, research teams have to put different parts of their dataset in different places, and they lose weeks or months getting a whole training dataset ready for that single training run at the end of the day,” co-founder and Chief Executive Chang She told SiliconANGLE in an interview. “There’s a missing data layer for AI today, and that’s what we’re trying to build.”
LanceDB’s technology is built on Lance, an open-source data format designed for AI workloads that combines structured information with images, video and other large files. Unlike traditional analytics formats optimized for processing entire tables, Lance supports the rapid retrieval and modification of individual records, making it particularly useful for searching and preparing massive training datasets.
The company built this format into a large-scale data lakehouse for retrieval, which is needed for the sheer scale of information needed to train modern AI models. A lakehouse combines the flexibility of a data lake, which can store enormous amounts of raw information, with database-style capabilities for organizing, querying and managing that data.
“Part of what makes multimodal data different and more difficult is the size of the data,” She explained.
By bringing multimodality to the lakehouse format, LanceDB brings different forms of AI training data into a single platform, allowing developers to search, organize and prepare their datasets without maintaining separate systems for each data type. It can connect directly to customers’ existing cloud storage, where the data remains, while distributing computational workloads across the infrastructure required to process it.
The challenge of multimodal data for AI
Multimodal AI involves more than combining text, audio, images and video. Autonomous vehicles, robotics and world models also involve three-dimensional sensor information, geospatial coordinates, time-series data and annotations that explain what the sensors are detecting.
For example, a self-driving car doesn’t merely capture an image. Its sensors might produce a three-dimensional representation of the surrounding environment, which then needs to be associated with information that identifies roads, pedestrians, vegetation and other objects.
The sheer amount of data included in lidar 3D clouds, images, video, audio and more can take up, on average, 10 to 20 petabytes of data in a single table for many large training workflows, with some becoming even larger – potentially approaching 80 to 100 petabytes. Researchers and model builders may maintain huge pools of data across different systems because conventional platforms weren’t designed around the requirements of multimodal AI.
Researchers must then assemble, reconcile and store different components of a training dataset to enrich it for training. The curation itself can take weeks or months just to move, prepare and process. LanceDB’s answer is to manage the infrastructure itself without ever copying or moving data from enterprise or research storage, giving it a single unified access point.
“The data stays in place,” She explained. “It remains yours. We don’t need to copy it.”
In short, LanceDB isn’t simply introducing a new way to store data; the objective is to provide a way to access the data less often, without needing to copy, convert or move it through network infrastructure. This greatly speeds up what She refers to as the “AI flywheel,” which is currently driven by feeding AI models good data as quickly as possible to mint and roll them out.
“The faster we can make that spin, the faster research teams can get to higher quality models and allow us to make even more interesting AI applications,” She said.
Notable customers include Runway AI Inc., which adopted LanceDB’s enterprise platform as its AI training needs expanded. Netflix Inc. built a media data lake on the technology for content creation. And Microsoft Corp. uses the platform as a data layer for training models on tens of billions of rows of image and code data. The platform lets these organizations consolidate data management, search, curation and feature engineering into a unified workflow, helping researchers prepare training datasets at petabyte scale without juggling separate infrastructure systems.
“A training example at Runway doesn’t stay still,” said Runway Chief Technology Officer Kamil Sindi. “It starts as a video and a prompt, then we add embeddings, resolution and duration metadata, whatever the next experiment needs. We first started using the Lance format in 2024 because it was the only option that handled unstructured data, column appends, distributed reads and ad-hoc SQL all at once. We’ve since become a LanceDB Enterprise customer.”
She said LanceDB intends to use the new funding to expand its multimodal data platform and accelerate the AI model development cycle, particularly by improving large-scale data curation, feature engineering and data loading to keep thousands of graphics processing units supplied efficiently during training. The company will also deepen its support for emerging AI workloads, including video generation, world models and robotics, where researchers must manage growing volumes of first-person sensor data, synthetic data and other multimodal information.

articles.title: Votre Mac va vous faire réfléchir avant de laisser une IA prendre les commandes
articles.text:
Apple teste de nouveaux contrôles pour mieux encadrer l’accès des applications aux fichiers et aux autres logiciels du Mac. Avec la deuxième bêta de macOS 27.3, l’utilisateur est davantage invité à limiter les permissions plutôt qu’à donner les clés de toute sa machine.
L’IA s’installe sur nos ordinateurs, mais Apple n’entend pas lui dérouler le tapis rouge sans quelques contrôles à l’entrée. Le constructeur, qui fait de la protection des données un argument de vente, voit les assistants réclamer des accès toujours plus larges pour travailler à notre place. Avec macOS 27.3, il commence à mettre en œuvre le durcissement annoncé début octobre. Les utilisateurs pourront toujours accorder ces permissions, mais le système fera davantage pour leur expliquer ce qu’ils s’apprêtent à autoriser.
Donner accès à un dossier plutôt qu’à tout le disque
Apple détaille aujourd’hui les changements introduits avec macOS 27.3 bêta 2. Deux catégories sont concernées : l’accès complet au disque et les permissions permettant de contrôler l’ordinateur et d’accéder aux données.
Le système encourage désormais à sélectionner uniquement les dossiers ou les applications nécessaires au travail demandé. Il propose aussi de configurer une application pour qu’elle sollicite l’autorisation à chaque accès, plutôt que de lui accorder une permission permanente.
La distinction est importante : consulter des fichiers et prendre la main sur un autre logiciel ne sont pas la même opération. Apple sépare ainsi le réglage « Device Control and Data Access » en deux sections, « System & App Protection Override » et « Accessibility ». Un indicateur signale également lorsqu’une application en contrôle une autre.
L’objectif est de mieux montrer la portée des autorisations avant leur validation. Pour un assistant chargé de ranger un dossier de factures, un accès limité peut suffire. Lui permettre de consulter beaucoup plus de données mérite une décision distincte.
Un nouveau réglage pensé pour les agents IA : Apple prépare-t-elle le terrain pour le sien ?
Ces changements apparaîtront lors de nouvelles demandes de permissions. Les accès accordés avant macOS 27.3 restent valables : installer la mise à jour ne retirera donc pas automatiquement les droits déjà confiés à des applications.
Les agents IA sont particulièrement concernés par les risques d’un accès étendu, mais les nouveaux contrôles s’appliquent aussi à d’autres logiciels. Des dispositions spécifiques sont prévues pour les applications de sauvegarde et les technologies d’assistance, dont certaines fonctions nécessitent justement des permissions importantes.
Est-ce qu’Apple prépare le terrain avant le lancement de son propre agent IA ? Rien n’est moins sûr, mais Siri AI, lancé cette année, pourrait progressivement évoluer vers l’IA agentique et aider l’utilisateur en effectuant de nombreuses tâches sur le Mac, tout en préservant la confidentialité de ses données.
Quoi qu'il en soit, les développeurs devront adapter leurs écrans de configuration et prévoir que leur logiciel fonctionne avec un accès limité. Une application ne devrait pas se retrouver inutilisable simplement parce que son propriétaire refuse de lui ouvrir tous ses dossiers.
Ces nouveautés restent pour l’instant en bêta. En attendant leur arrivée en version stable, les autorisations existantes peuvent déjà être vérifiées dans Réglages Système > Confidentialité et sécurité. Le nouvel avertissement ne reviendra pas sur les clics que l’on a déjà faits, mais mieux vaut jeter un œil de temps en temps, histoire de vérifier qu’une app que l'on n'utilise plus ne se montre pas un peu trop curieuse.

articles.title: Cómo activar el ‘modo ultra rápido’ para que las páginas web carguen más rápido en el celular
articles.text:
Navegar desde el celular debería ser instantáneo, pero en la práctica muchas páginas tardan en cargar, las imágenes aparecen a destiempo y los textos saltan en la pantalla mientras uno intenta leer. Activar el modo ultra rápido de Google Chrome permite revertir buena parte de ese problema con ajustes que casi nadie conoce.
El fenómeno no depende solo de la potencia del teléfono. Los procesadores móviles priorizan el ahorro de batería por encima de la velocidad, lo que limita su capacidad para ejecutar scripts pesados y renderizar sitios diseñados originalmente para computadoras de escritorio.
Cómo activar la precarga de páginas en Chrome
Google Chrome permite habilitar una función de “carga previa” que descarga de forma automática los contenidos de las páginas visitadas con frecuencia, antes de que el usuario ingrese a ellas, siempre que exista una conexión Wi-Fi disponible.
En dispositivos Android, el proceso se replica dentro de Configuración, en las “Opciones Avanzadas” de la sección Privacidad, bajo el nombre “Utilizar un servicio de predicciones para que las páginas se carguen más rápido”.
En equipos con sistema operativo de Apple, el recorrido cambia levemente: hay que abrir Chrome, ingresar a Ajustes y Configuración, y dentro del apartado “Ancho de banda”, en “Opciones avanzadas”, activar “Precargar páginas web”.
Con esta configuración activa, Chrome descarga contenidos en segundo plano únicamente cuando detecta una red Wi-Fi y mientras el usuario no esté utilizando todo el ancho de banda disponible, para evitar consumos de datos innecesarios.
Otros ajustes y hábitos para mantener la velocidad
Quienes buscan un paso adicional pueden escribir chrome://flags en la barra de direcciones de navegadores basados en Chromium, como Google Chrome o Microsoft Edge, tanto en Android como en iOS. Allí es posible habilitar funciones como la aceleración por GPU o el protocolo QUIC experimental, que permiten que el procesador gráfico del teléfono ayude a renderizar las páginas con mayor fluidez.
Instalar un bloqueador de publicidad y rastreadores también resulta determinante, este tipo de herramientas puede reducir el consumo de datos hasta en un 50%, al evitar la descarga de scripts de seguimiento y telemetría que sobrecargan el procesador.
Mantener el sistema y el navegador actualizados también mejora el rendimiento, dado que cada actualización incluye optimizaciones en motores de JavaScript como V8, usado por Chrome, que agilizan la ejecución de código sin exigir más batería.
Por último, se recomienda desactivar la sincronización constante de historiales y contraseñas en redes móviles inestables, así como cerrar las pestañas acumuladas, ya que cada una consume memoria RAM y procesos en segundo plano que ralentizan el funcionamiento general del teléfono.
Cómo Google mide el rendimiento de las páginas web
Para medir ese rendimiento, Google desarrolló un estándar llamado Web Vitals, que evalúa la experiencia real del usuario a través de tres indicadores.
El LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) mide cuánto tarda en aparecer el elemento visual más grande de la pantalla, algo que se deteriora cuando las imágenes no están comprimidas en formatos modernos como WebP o AVIF.
El INP (Interaction to Next Paint) evalúa la rapidez de respuesta ante un toque en la pantalla. Cuando una página ejecuta demasiado código en segundo plano, el procesador del teléfono bloquea esa reacción.
El tercer indicador, el CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift), mide la estabilidad visual: ocurre cuando el usuario intenta tocar un enlace y la página se mueve de golpe, lo que suele terminar en un clic accidental sobre un anuncio. Este problema se agrava en pantallas táctiles pequeñas, donde no se reservan los espacios para imágenes o publicidades antes de que carguen.
Las páginas web cargan más lento en el celular porque los procesadores móviles priorizan ahorrar batería antes que velocidad, y porque muchos sitios se diseñan pensando en computadoras, con scripts e imágenes sin optimizar que saturan la red y bloquean el procesamiento del teléfono.

articles.title: Lo de Pattinson como Bond no es casual, porque todas las películas las protagonizan los mismos: Zendaya, Holland, Hathaway, Pugh...
articles.text:
Las dos películas más taquilleras del año comparten tres actores, las dos más esperadas de diciembre comparten una actriz y el nuevo James Bond ha coincidido con Zendaya en tres estrenos en 2026. La impresión que dan estos nuevos repartos de jóvenes estrellas es que Hollywood tiene actualmente un reparto fijo y con muy pocas variables.
Pattinson 007. Amazon MGM Studios acaba de anunciar que Robert Pattinson será el nuevo James Bond en la próxima película de la franquicia, que dirigirá Denis Villeneuve, un papel que el actor describe como "el honor de una vida". El propio comunicado repasa un año especialmente fértil para el intérprete: 'El drama', 'La Odisea', 'Primetime' y 'Dune: Parte Tres', que llega en diciembre. Todo ello compaginado con el rodaje de 'The Batman Part II'.
Cambio de planes. En septiembre de 2025, el equipo de Villeneuve buscaba a un británico poco conocido de entre veintitantos y treinta y pocos años. Por contra, Pattinson tiene 40 y lleva la capa de Batman desde 2022, y ya se habla de él como el actor más asentado que ha recibido nunca el papel. El fichaje interesa sobre todo por lo que retrata: en una saga donde el personaje siempre ha ido por delante del actor, el papel ha acabado recalando dentro del grupo reducido de intérpretes que copa los grandes estrenos del año.
Zendaya es el núcleo. Este año, Zendaya ha sido Emma en 'El drama', Atenea en 'La Odisea' y MJ en 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day', y cerrará 2026 como Chani en 'Dune: Parte Tres'. Coincide con Pattinson en tres de esos cuatro títulos. ¿Más casos? Tom Holland es su compañero de reparto en dos: Telémaco en 'La Odisea' y Peter Parker en la de Spider-Man. Ojo a Jon Bernthal también: Menelao en ‘La Odisea’ y Punisher en ‘Brand New Day’. Visto de otro modo: dos de las películas más taquilleras del año comparten tres actores.
Y muchos más nombres propios: Anne Hathaway suma cinco estrenos, entre ellos ‘El diablo viste de Prada 2’ y la película de Nolan. Florence Pugh hizo un cameo en ‘Spider-Man’ y el 18 de diciembre estrena el mismo día ‘Dune: Parte Tres’ y ‘Vengadores: Doomsday’. En esta última coincide con Pedro Pascal, que en mayo protagonizó ‘The Mandalorian and Grogu’. Timothée Chalamet entró en 2026 con ‘Marty Supreme’, la película más taquillera de la historia de A24, y lo cierra con ‘Dune: Parte Tres’.
¿Por qué existe esta concentración de actores? Fácil: la taquilla. 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' (2.521 millones de dólares), ‘La Odisea’ (1.805 millones) y ‘El diablo viste de Prada 2’ (693 millones) suman 5.020 millones este año: el 47% de lo que recaudan las diez películas más taquilleras del año, y el 64% si solo se cuentan las siete de imagen real. Universal comunicó en septiembre que ‘La Odisea’ ya era la película más taquillera de su historia, y el primer fin de semana en que coincidió con ‘Spider-Man’ ambas se repartieron el 94,6% de la recaudación.
Concentración de poder. Un estudio de la Universidad de California contó 128 estrenos de los grandes estudios en 2006 y 66 en 2025, y sus autoras lo atribuyen a una estrategia deliberada de concentrar el dinero y las pantallas en cada título. En taquilla se nota: en 2019 hubo 20 películas que superaron los diez millones de entradas, y en 2025 fueron 12. Una lectura posible es que, con la mitad de estrenos que hace veinte años, cada película pesa el doble en las cuentas del estudio.
Y detrás de la cámara, igual. El circuito también es reducido al otro lado de la cámara. Nolan, que ya funciona como una franquicia en sí mismo, y Villeneuve se reparten a Pattinson y a Zendaya, y Bond ha ido a parar al actor con el que Villeneuve acababa de rodar 'Dune'. Todo eso impacta en los calendarios: ha habido retrasos en rodajes y estrenos porque Hathaway ha tenido que promocionar cinco películas en seis meses.
Una cuestión de público. Todos estos intérpretes apelan a públicos distintos. La generación Z es la que más entradas compra y adora a Zendaya y a Holland, los millennials veneran a Hathaway y a Pascal, y Pattinson conecta con los dos públicos. Sin embargo, no siempre funciona: Pascal no evitó que ‘The Mandalorian and Grogu’ firmara el peor estreno de Star Wars en la era Disney. Y Pattinson no salvó ‘Mickey 17’, mientras que el casi siempre infalible Tom Cruise encaja con ‘Digger’ una pérdida que se estima en unos 250 millones.
Excepciones que confirman la regla. 'Obsession', la película de terror del youtuber Curry Barker, se rodó en 20 días con 750.000 dólares con un reparto mayoritariamente desconocido. Es la décima película más taquillera del año, con 521 millones recaudados. Este año, los directores formados en YouTube están ganando a Disney en taquilla. El círculo de elegidos, en cualquier caso, busca rápido nuevos miembros: al parecer su protagonista, Inde Navarrette, ya prepara su debut en Marvel.

articles.title: Gemini Notebook peut désormais transformer vos projets et cours en sites web interactifs
articles.text:
Gemini Notebook permet dès aujourd’hui à ses utilisateurs de transformer leurs sources de recherche, leurs notes ou tout autre corpus documentaire en un site web interactif. L’objectif est double : faciliter la gestion de projets et mieux comprendre des sujets complexes. Cette fonctionnalité est disponible dès maintenant auprès des utilisateurs web.
Gemini Notebook vous permet dorénavant de transformer des sources en site web
Pour bénéficier de cette fonctionnalité, il suffit de taper dans le chat « créez-moi un site » et de décrire ses besoins et les spécificités du futur site, en fonction de son corpus de sources. À titre d’exemple, l’utilisateur peut créer des présentations visuelles explicatives, des tableaux de bord interactifs, des lignes du temps, des tableaux périodiques interactifs ou encore des outils de suivi détaillant des tâches à effectuer et des échéances à respecter.
Il s’agit donc d’un outil qui s’adresse aussi bien aux étudiants qu’aux professionnels. Les étudiants peuvent ainsi transformer un cours complexe en site interactif et didactique, tandis que les professionnels peuvent, par exemple, créer un site web entièrement dédié au suivi d’un projet ou aux performances de vente d’un trimestre, simplement en donnant quelques indications à Gemini Notebook.
Une fois le site terminé, il est par ailleurs possible de l’ouvrir dans un nouvel onglet afin de l’utiliser indépendamment de Gemini Notebook. L’utilisateur peut également partager le site qu’il a créé avec d’autres personnes.
Une disponibilité sur le web, mais pas encore sur mobile
Cette nouvelle fonctionnalité est déployée mondialement dès aujourd’hui auprès des utilisateurs web de Gemini Notebook, y compris pour les abonnés à Google Workspace. Google précise que cette fonctionnalité arrivera également sur la version mobile, mais sans donner de date de disponibilité. Pour accéder à cette fonctionnalité, il ne faut donc pas cliquer sur un bouton ou télécharger une extension : le simple prompt « créez-moi un site » suffit. Auparavant, créer un site demandait de sérieuses compétences et connaissances. Aujourd’hui, quelques mots suffisent à transformer un cours ou un projet complexe en site web complet et interactif.

articles.title: Qual é o melhor notebook para comprar agora? Saiba como escolher • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Resumo IA
- O Dell 15 é indicado para uso diário, com opções de processadores Intel Core i3, i5 e i7, memória RAM de até 16 GB e armazenamento SSD de até 1 TB.
- O Alienware 15 é indicado para jogos e aplicações gráficas pesadas, com processadores Intel Core i5 e i7, placas de vídeo Nvidia GeForce RTX 3050 e 4050.
- A escolha do notebook ideal depende do uso, com o Dell 15 sendo uma boa opção para estudantes e profissionais, enquanto o Alienware 15 é mais indicado para jogos e aplicações gráficas pesadas.
A escolha de um notebook novo vai além do processo: quem precisa dele para estudar tem prioridades diferentes de quem pretende jogar ou editar vídeos. Por isso, entender as especificações de cada aparelho é importante para encontrar o melhor modelo para você.
No Brasil, a Dell oferece as melhores opções para diferentes perfis, como o Dell 15, voltado à produtividade e às tarefas cotidianas, e o Alienware 15, para programas que exigem maior capacidade de processamento. Ambos contam com processadores Intel combinados a diferentes configurações de hardware, permitindo escolher o conjunto mais adequado para cada tipo de uso.
Como escolher o melhor notebook?
Antes de comparar modelos, é importante identificar quais atividades farão parte do uso. Isso ajuda a definir quanto investir em processamento, memória e armazenamento. Observe especificações como:
- Processador (CPU): responsável pela execução das instruções dos programas.
- Memória RAM: mantém temporariamente os dados usados pelos programas em execução.
- Armazenamento (SSD): são mais rápidos que os discos rígidos tradicionais (HDs) e influenciam na velocidade de carregamento do sistema.
- Placa de Vìdeo (GPU): pode ser integrada ao processador ou dedicada. No segundo caso, como a família NVIDIA GeForce RTX, o usuário tem maior suporte a jogos, modelagem 3D e programas que requerem processamento gráfico alto.
Com isso em mente, entenda como o Dell 15 e o Alienware 15 combinam os componentes para atender à sua necessidade.
Dell 15: melhor notebook para uso diário
A linha Dell 15 reúne características que atendem bem a quem procura um notebook tanto para atividades profissionais e estudos, quanto para entretenimento. O modelo oferece diferentes configurações, com os chips:
- Intel Core 3 100U: seis núcleos e frequência de até 4,7 GHz, para tarefas cotidianas como navegar na internet, preparar documentos e acompanhar aulas.
- Intel Core i5-1334U (13ª geração): dez núcleos e frequência de até 4,6 GHz, oferecendo capacidade adicional para multitarefas e rotinas profissionais mais intensas.
- Intel Core i7-1355U (13ª geração): dez núcleos e frequência de até 5 GHz, ampliando as possibilidades de uso em aplicações mais exigentes.
Os dispositivos incluem 8 GB ou 16 GB de RAM DDR5, com configurações de 512 GB ou 1 TB.
Em todo caso, o Dell 15 conta com um painel Full HD (1920 x 1080 pixels) de 15,6 polegadas, com taxa de atualização de 120 Hz e tecnologia ComfortView, oferecendo bom espaço para trabalho, usabilidade fluida e conforto para usos prolongados.
O modelo inclui também:
- Câmera HD integrada, para videoconferências
- Conexão Wi-Fi 6
- Teclado padrão ABNT2
- Portas USB-A, USB-C, HDMI e leitor de cartões SD
Conheça as configurações do Dell 15 disponíveis no Brasil.
Alienware 15: notebook gamer com placa de vídeo Nvidia
Quem quer ir além e executar tarefas que exigem mais desempenho, o Alienware 15 é uma alternativa da Dell que une processadores Intel Core com placas de vídeo dedicadas da Nvidia. A estrutura do notebook e os componentes são desenvolvidos para lidar com cargas maiores de processamento, como jogos e programas que usam aceleração gráfica.
Confira as principais configurações do Alienware 15 no Brasil:
- Processadores: Intel Core 5 210H (8 núcleos, até 4,8 GHz) ou Intel Core 7 240H (10 núcleos, até 5,2 GHz), ambos da Série 2.
- Placa de vídeo: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 ou RTX 4050, ambas com 6 GB de memória GDDR6.
- Memória RAM: 8 GB ou 16 GB DDR5.
- Armazenamento: SSD de 512 GB ou 1 TB.
- Tela: 15,3 polegadas, resolução WUXGA (1920 × 1200 pixels) e taxa de atualização de 165 Hz.
- Conectividade e portas: Wi-Fi 6, USB-A, USB-C, HDMI 2.1 e Ethernet RJ-45.
Com as placas de vídeo Nvidia, o Alienware 15 é compatível com tecnologias como ray tracing, para simulação de efeitos de iluminação, e o DLSS, que usa técnicas de IA para melhorar o desempenho e a qualidade das imagens em jogos.
Outro destaque é a tela, um painel de 15,3 polegadas com taxa de atualização de 165 Hz e proporção de 16:10, oferecendo mais espaço vertical para jogos, programas de edição e outras aplicações profissionais.
Para acompanhar o desempenho dos componentes, o Alienware 15 também conta com o Alienware Cryo-tech, desenvolvido para dissipar com eficiência o calor produzido pelo processador e pela placa de vídeo nas sessões mais exigentes.
Confira as versões do Alienware 15 na Dell Brasil.
Perguntas frequentes: como escolher o melhor notebook
Qual é o melhor notebook para estudar e trabalhar?
O Dell 15 é uma boa opção para estudantes e profissionais que usam navegadores, editores de texto e planilhas, videochamadas e outros apps de produtividade.
Qual notebook Dell é indicado para jogos?
O Alienware 15 é indicado para quem busca um notebook gamer com boas especificações para jogos e aplicações gráficas pesadas, com placas de vídeo Nvidia GeForce RTX 3050 e RTX 4050.
É melhor comprar um notebook com 8 GB ou 16 GB de RAM?
Para atividades básicas, como estudar, navegar na internet e trabalhar com documentos, 8 GB podem ser suficientes. Os 16 GB são recomendados para quem costuma executar muitos programas ao mesmo tempo ou deseja mais capacidade para multitarefas e aplicações exigentes.
Qual a diferença entre o SSD e memória RAM?
Mais RAM facilita a execução simultânea de tarefas, enquanto um SSD rápido reduz o tempo de inicialização e carregamento dos programas.
Preciso de uma placa de vídeo dedicada no notebook?
Depende do uso. Quem pretende usar programas ou jogos que exigem maior processamento gráfico pode se beneficiar de um notebook com GPU dedicada, como o Alienware 15.

articles.title: Meet Kandao Focus & Focus SE: 4K AI Webcams
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
Meet Kandao Focus & Focus SE: 4K AI Webcams
KanDao Technology, a global pioneer in the video camera and imaging industry, has launched Kandao Focus & Focus SE, the 4K AI webcam. This series of webcams is designed to provide a professional image experience at an affordable price for everyday work, study, and content creation. Although it's Kandao's first exploration in the webcam field, the Focus has already won the 2026 Red Dot Design Award.
The 4K AI webcams are designed for video conferencing, live streaming, online teaching, and content creation. AI tracking and built-in 2-axis gimbal detect presenter's movement and keep it always in frame. With gesture control, fast autofocus, landscape and portrait shooting, and multiple modes for different scenarios, the Kandao Focus makes presentations clearer and everyday workflows easier.
Dan Chen, CEO of Kandao Technology"Our experience in imaging, AI, and video conferencing has helped us to rethink what a webcam can offer. We aim to bring versatile features together in one camera to support different uses and make everyday workflows easier,"
Professional Imaging in Any Light
Kandao Focus series uses a 1/1.5-inch CMOS sensor, larger than those found in many webcams in the same price range. Combined with an f/1.6 aperture, it captures more light for brighter, cleaner, and more detailed images in low-light conditions.
4K @ 30 FPS captures fine textures and important details with clarity. PDAF autofocus locks onto subjects quickly and keeps them sharp during live commerce.
HDR mode balances highlights and shadows for more true-to-life images in challenging lighting, including overexposed, backlit, and low-light environments.
AI Tracking and Gesture Control for Presentations
The Focus features a motorized 2-axis gimbal that tracks the presenter's movements in real time. Whether teachers move around the room while teaching online or instructors demonstrate yoga poses during a live stream, Focus keeps them in frame and centered.
The Focus SE features a manually adjustable 2-axis gimbal with up to 270 degrees of tilt and 180 degrees of pan. Users can effortlessly adjust the camera angle to suit their needs.
Users can control the camera with three hand gestures:
- Open Palm: Turn AI tracking on or off. AI tracking is only available on the Focus model.
- L-shaped Gesture: Move your hand up or down to zoom in or out.
- V-shaped Gesture: Automatically detect the whiteboard and zoom in on its content.
Multiple Modes for Different Scenarios
The Kandao Focus series offers multiple modes for different uses.
- Deskview Mode: Tilt the camera toward your desk to show a top-down view of your sketches.
- Whiteboard Mode: Show the V-shaped gesture, the camera automatically detects whiteboard and enlarges the content.
- Portrait Mode: Rotate the camera to switch from 16:9 to 9:16 and record 4K vertical video without cropping or reformatting in post-production.
- Privacy Mode: Press the button and tilt the Focus series 90 degrees to enter standby mode with audio muting.
Kandao Focus Series Officially Launches
The Focus and Focus SE are now available in the United States, priced at $139 and $119, respectively.
For other regions, Kandao will gradually announce the local pricing and roll out sales in the coming months.

articles.title: How we test enterprise SSDs — our new test suite pushes enterprise and data center SSDs to their limits
articles.text:
How we test enterprise SSDs — our new test suite pushes enterprise and data center SSDs to their limits
Our enterprise and data center SSD reviews show how a drive performs in real-world service, not just on its best day.
After a hiatus of several years, Tom's Hardware is expanding its in-depth testing and analysis to enterprise and data center SSDs. Consumer SSDs and conventional hard drives lack the performance and endurance for extensive AI workloads. This has increased demand for enterprise SSDs. Form factors like U.2, U.3, E3.S, and E1.S, once rare, are now common in high-end workstations and home labs. These enterprise storage solutions provide higher capacities, better performance, and greater reliability than consumer drives.
Comprehensive reviews of enterprise and data center SSDs are therefore more important than ever. Buying a drive of this caliber is a major decision and a significant investment for organizations of all sizes. With this latest venture, Tom's Hardware will continue to help buyers make informed decisions with comprehensive reviews and performance analyses.
Inside The Tom's Hardware Enterprise SSD Test System
Reviewing enterprise and data center SSDs required us to build a workstation that could truly challenge these drives. This project would not have been possible without the support of several component makers, including Asus, Corsair, G.Skill, Icy Dock, and Noctua, who made the workstation a reality, a challenging prospect in the current market.
The Xeon 658X, a 24-core, 48-thread chip from the Granite Rapids family with a 4.9 GHz boost clock speed, powers the testing workstation. Single-core performance and total core count matter just as much when reviewing storage. Clock speed determines how many IOPS one core can push and how fast it answers a single request, while 24 cores let us spread a drive's load across eight fio jobs and later test several drives at once. The Xeon 658X ticks all those boxes.
We've entrusted the Xeon 658X's cooling to Noctua's NH-U14S DX-4677 air cooler, which supports both LGA4677 and LGA4710 sockets. The single-tower CPU air cooler delivers high-performance cooling at very low noise levels thanks to its dual NF-A15 140mm cooling fans.

With its server-grade components and robust enterprise features, the Asus Pro WS W890E-Sage SE is the ideal motherboard to pair with the Xeon 658X. Its extensive feature set includes an onboard MCIO x8 connection, split into x4/x4, that allows for evaluating two U.2 or U.3 drives. The board also provides seven PCIe 5.0 expansion slots (six at x16 and one at x8) to fully leverage the Xeon 658X’s 128 PCIe 5.0 lanes, so the SSDs and graphics cards never hit bandwidth limits.
We're still in need of support for an RTX Pro graphics card, which would be an invaluable asset for enterprise SSD reviews for real-world AI workloads, but our current test platform allows us to test the most important aspects of performance.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Despite the memory and storage shortage, G.Skill and Corsair have stepped up to provide crucial components for our enterprise SSD test bench. G.Skill sent a G5 DDR5-6400 C32 64GB (4x16GB) R-DIMM memory kit, which runs at the stock DDR5-5600 speed. The decision to keep it at the JEDEC baseline has nothing to do with the memory kit: Memory frequency does not affect performance in enterprise SSD tests.
Meanwhile, Corsair provided the speedy MP700 Pro XT 2TB, one of the best SSDs, as the test bench's primary storage. The PCIe 5.0 drive delivers sequential read and write speeds up to 14,900 MB/s and 14,500 MB/s, respectively, and keeps the workstation snappy, especially when it hammers enterprise drives all day long.
No power supply is better suited to the job than the Corsair HX1500i. It offers a massive 1,500W capacity with plenty of headroom for future upgrades, and it runs quietly and stably, two qualities that matter when you keep the test system running for countless hours. It is an 80 Plus Platinum power supply with at least 89% efficiency at full load.

Testing enterprise drives in a standard PCIe expansion slot is more convenient. For that purpose, Icy Dock has provided us with the ExpressSlot Elite MB221E5P-B and MB303E5P-B to accept one and two E1.S SSDs. Unlike other generic designs on the market, these adapters feature tool-less installation mechanisms that don't require removing them from the PCIe expansion slot, and they include 50mm fans for active cooling.
The list also included the ToughArmor MB218E5P-B, a 5.25-inch drive bay that supports up to eight E1.S SSDs for future projects exploring RAID arrays. To test E3.S drives, we use a JMT ADT-R27C adapter strapped to a Noctua NF-F12 industrialPPC-24V-3000 IP67 PWM cooling fan, which can run at 12V and still provide substantial airflow to actively cool the SSDs under evaluation.
A TGDGamer E-ATX test bench houses the hardware for the enterprise SSD system. It may not look flashy, but it does the job, and that is what matters. As an open-air test bench, it is easy to install and remove hardware, and it eliminates variables when it comes to heat generation and buildup. The test bench also supports motherboard form factors up to SSI-EEB, so the Asus Pro WS W890E-Sage SE feels right at home.
Inside the Torture Chamber: Assembling an Enterprise-Grade Benchmark Suite
A spec sheet only tells you what a drive can do on its best day. The real world is not as pretty. The drive is mostly full, garbage collection is constantly at work, and multiple workloads are hitting it simultaneously. Our enterprise benchmark suite is built to measure the drive in service: at steady state, under load, through write bursts, and with other jobs running. Every drive gets the same automated run on the same test bench. Every result is stored with the exact parameters that produced it, so we can trace how we got there.
This can take some time. A full run takes most of a day on a 7.68TB PCIe 5.0 drive, and it writes the drive end-to-end many times over. To make life a bit easier on us, the benchmark can be run unattended, and it’s crash-resumable from the last stage. A shorter express mode handles bench checks and quick triage. When a result looks odd, express runs and variant runs, which repeat just the tests in question or change one setting, help us find the cause before we take it to the vendor.
One OS, One Engine
One OS, One Engine
We run the bench on a custom Debian 13 image that we build and maintain ourselves, with the suite copied in at build time. This image gets installed on the bench’s OS drive, and the kernel is pinned so every drive has the same software stack. Right now that’s Linux 7.2.6 from Debian backports, because Debian 13’s stock 6.12 kernel predates support for the Asus Pro WS W890E-Sage SE’s Intel E610 10GbE controller. The suite is also designed to be run remotely if needed, but we need a tester at the bench to switch the drives, of course.
Debian is our pick over Ubuntu for a few reasons: it has fewer background services, no Snap, and no unattended upgrades by default. We hold the kernel so nothing changes between runs. We remove AppArmor and turn off scheduled jobs that could fire mid-run, like the weekly TRIM timer and the drive-health service that polls every drive, and the suite records any that are still running. The suite also turns off NVMe autonomous power-state transitions (APST) at the start of every run and checks that the drive reports it off, so no drive drops into a low-power state during an idle gap and adds wake-up latency to the next I/O.
Every test runs in fio 3.42, using io_uring and direct I/O against the raw block device. This means no filesystem and no page cache sitting between fio and the drive; the bench’s 64GB of RAM never caches a byte of test data. We compile fio from source because Debian’s packaged version lacks SPRandom, which we’ll get to in short order.
Some enterprise storage reviews run application profiles in Oracle’s Vdbench, but we decided to go full fio. This makes for a more consistent suite with one set of latency accounting across every chart. And fio is open source and actively maintained, while Vdbench hasn’t had a new release since 2018. Vdbench profiles are built from the same parts fio uses, such as read/write ratio, block-size mix, and random or sequential access, and our mixed-workload sweeps cover the common read/write ratios at 4K and 8K, though not mixed-block-size profiles. Running Vdbench ourselves wouldn’t make our results comparable to other outlets’ anyway, since they use different hardware, preconditioning, and profile definitions.
Steady State or Nothing
Steady State or Nothing
A key element of benchmarking SSDs is making sure the test drive is at steady state, with the performance it can sustain rather than the peak you can see after a fresh erase. Our first stage is a secure erase using nvme format. If a drive refuses, the suite falls back to a plain format, then a full-drive discard, and records which one it used.
Next comes preconditioning. SPRandom, SanDisk’s open-source contribution to fio, is a faster alternative to filling the drive over and over for hours. It takes user capacity and over-provisioning (OP) as inputs, which SanDisk says lets it reach a steady-state layout in just one pass. Overprovisioning (OP) is inferred from the capacity point or given by the tester. NVMe drives don’t report their raw flash, so a 7.68TB drive like our first one, assumed to sit on 8TiB of actual NAND, works out to having about 14.5% OP.
We don’t take SPRandom’s result on faith. A steady-state gate follows, running 4K random writes at queue depth 256 (QD256) until the drive’s write speed stops moving. It uses the two tests from the Storage Networking Industry Association’s (SNIA) steady-state rule, with limits ten times tighter, applied to the last 30 minutes: split into five six-minute rounds, the round averages must sit within 2% of one another, and the trend line across the window can’t move more than 1%.
That takes a while, but that’s the point: an earlier, looser version of the gate passed our first drive while its write speed was still climbing. The whole settling curve is saved with every run, and a drive that doesn’t settle within three hours is marked as not reaching steady state, though the run continues. As a backstop, the suite repeats the four-corner 4K write after the random sweep, hours later, and flags the run if the two results differ by more than 3%.
The suite also checks its own results as it goes. If a test’s slowest moment falls below 70% of its average, that test is run again on the spot. If a point in the random sweep lands more than 10% off the curve set by its neighbors, it’s measured again before the drive is erased for the sequential tests. Both results are kept, and any re-test is noted in the review.
Following the random tests, the tool erases the drive again and writes it end to end once, with 128K sequential writes at QD64. We run it before the sequential and AI tests, so the drive is conditioned with the kind of I/O we’re about to measure. It matters because sequential writes can swing wildly on a randomly written drive: on our first test drive, the fastest result was more than three times the slowest. After a sequential fill, they held flat from QD2 through QD1024, at both 128K and 1MB.
Drives are formatted to 512-byte logical blocks when they support it, so our block size sweep can go down to 512-byte transfers, which a 4K-native namespace can’t issue. SNIA’s enterprise IOPS test uses 512-byte transfers too, and Kioxia pitches 512-byte access for its GP Series, which is aimed at GPU-initiated storage. Drives without a 512-byte format are tested as shipped, and their sub-4K results are marked unsupported. The switch happens in the same format command as the secure erase, so it adds no time.
Measuring The Drive, Not The Bench
Measuring The Drive, Not The Bench
A fast enough SSD will happily benchmark your host, or your tools, instead, and our early runs turned up three ways that could happen. The first is CPU idle states, or C-states: waking our Xeon 658X cores from their deepest idle state can take up to 170 microseconds, and at QD1 that directly impacts the results. Holding the cores awake for the whole run cut the first drive’s average 4K QD1 read latency by about a sixth.
The second is the CPU itself: a single fio job can saturate its core well short of what a PCIe 5.0 drive can manage. Split across eight jobs, the same test runs several times faster, so random tests now spread their queue depth across up to eight fio jobs. That’s also why fast cores, and enough of them, matter for this test bench.
The third is fio itself. By default, fio seeds its random generator the same way every run, so it replays the same sequence of random offsets, and each random write test rewrites the previous test’s blocks in the same order. On our first drive, that was the main reason 4K random writes came in at more than twice the sustained figure. Every random test now runs with a fresh random seed.
What we don’t change matters, too. Completions arrive by interrupt rather than polling, and the IOMMU stays in its default mode, because that’s how most applications use a drive. On our first drive, polling and IOMMU passthrough would each have shaved some latency off 4K QD1 writes.
Interrupts also set a ceiling at the other end of the scale: this bench tops out near 2.8 million 4K random read IOPS, and adding fio jobs doesn’t lift it, though polling does. So on the fastest drives, our 4K random read result can sit below the spec sheet’s, and that’s our bench’s limit, not the drive’s. Our low queue depth latencies, writes especially, run higher than a tuned host would show, but they’re closer to what you’d actually see. To show the drive’s limit at both ends, the suite repeats three tests with polled I/O at the end of the random stage: the 4K random read peak, plus 4K random reads and writes at QD1. Those results get their own charts and never mix into the main ones.
What We Test, How, and Why
What We Test, How, and Why
| Test | What it runs | Why it’s there | 
|---|---|---|
| Four corners | 4K random read and write at QD256; 128K and 1MB sequential read and write at QD64 | The headline numbers, measured on a preconditioned drive instead of fresh out of the box | 
| Random and mixed sweeps | 4K and 8K, QD1 to QD4096, eight read/write mixes from 100% read to 100% write | Servers rarely run flat out; QD1 is what latency-bound software feels, and 8K is a common database page size | 
| Drive limit (polled) | 4K random read at QD1024 across eight jobs, plus 4K random read and write at QD1, all with polled I/O | What the drive can do with the host’s interrupt overhead out of the way; the results to set against a spec sheet | 
| Sequential sweep | 128K and 1MB sequential reads and writes, QD1 to QD1024 | How much parallelism a drive needs to reach full speed; low queue depths are what a single restore or scan gets | 
| Block size sweep | Random reads and writes from 512 bytes to 1MB at QD32 | Writes smaller than a drive’s mapping unit can pay a read-modify-write penalty; large blocks show its bandwidth cap | 
| Tail latency | 4K and 8K reads and writes at QD1, QD4, and QD16, from the median (P50) to the 99.999th percentile (P99.999) | Averages hide the stalls applications notice; at a million IOPS, the slowest 0.001% is still ten requests a second | 
| Saturation curve | 4K 70/30 at 13 queue depths from QD1 to QD4096, plotted as a share of the drive’s own peak | Finds the load where latency starts to climb | 
| Sustained write | One hour of 4K random writes at QD256 | Whether sustained writes hold a flat line or sawtooth as garbage collection struggles | 
| Write-to-read recovery | 4K QD1 reads for four minutes right after a heavy write burst | How far reads drop after heavy writes, and how fast they recover | 
| Idle recovery | Write bursts after idle gaps of 0 to 300 seconds | How much write speed a quiet spell buys back | 
| Database I/O patterns (simulated) | 4K QD1 log writes with a sync after each, a random 8K 70/30 mix at QD16, and a 256K sequential read scan | Log-write latency, page I/O, and analytics scans, without benchmarking a database’s RAM cache | 
| AI checkpoints | Checkpoint-sized saves and restores modeled on 8B- and 70B-class models (105GiB over eight writers, 912GiB over 64) | Time until the slowest writer finishes, which is when a real checkpoint would be done | 
| Checkpoint interference | A fixed 4K read load, alone and during a checkpoint save | What a checkpoint does to serving traffic on the same drive | 
| Thermals | Drive temperature through the hour-long sustained write test | Measured against the drive’s own warning and critical thresholds | 
Some things are out of scope by design. We review drives; we don’t certify them. That rules out dual-port failover, power-loss validation, and single-root I/O virtualization (SR-IOV), which belong in a qualification lab. We’ll add tests when they prove themselves on the bench. Many of the tests in the table are old standbys and still earn their place. Others are newer and require further explanation.
For one, we chart latency against load: the 70/30 4K mix from the random sweep, at 13 queue depths from QD1 to QD4096, with throughput shown as a share of the drive’s own peak. Tail latency climbs as the load grows, and the point where it turns sharply upward (on our first drive, that was write latency) represents the practical operating ceiling, or the load you can plan a server around without giving up low latency.
We also test write-to-read recovery, which measures how a drive’s reads hold up after a heavy write burst. A few minutes of 4K random writes at QD256 leave the drive with cleanup to do, and QD1 reads are then timed over the next four minutes. If a drive is still busy collecting garbage, it will read slower before climbing back; the extent and duration of the drop are the result.
Idle recovery measures what downtime buys back. After a minute of sustained writes, the drive sits idle for anywhere from zero to five minutes, then a 10-second write burst, logged second by second, shows whether background cleanup freed enough blocks to run faster.
Checkpoint interference shows what an AI checkpoint does to anything else sharing the drive. A light 4K read load, which stands in for inference or database queries, runs alone, and then again during a checkpoint save. Each read is timed from when it was due, not when it was sent, so reads stuck waiting behind a stalled one count too.
Lastly, we test thermals. Drive temperature is tracked through the hour-long sustained write test and charted against the drive's own warning and critical thresholds.
The full process means every drive is treated the same and compared fairly, with a method built to give the same results run after run. This allows us to provide a level playing field built on accurate and repeatable performance characterization.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: Meta testet neue Messenger-App auf Instagram-Basis
articles.text:
Konkurrenz für Whatsapp: Meta testet neue Messenger-App auf Instagram-Basis
Direktnachrichten (DM) auf Instagram erfreuen sich bei Nutzer:innen offenbar großer Beliebtheit. In den vergangenen Jahren haben einige Entwickler:innen versucht, per DM zu kommunizieren, ohne ablenkende Reels oder Posts angezeigt zu bekommen. Eine Lösung, um die DM-Funktionen verschiedener Messenger-Apps zu vereinen, ist etwa Beeper.
Messenger-App auf Instagram-DM-Basis
Jetzt scheint Meta auf die entsprechende Nachfrage der Instagram-Nutzer:innen zu reagieren. Mit Direct bringt der Facebook-Konzern eine eigenständige Messenger-App an den Start, die auf den Instagram-Direktnachrichten basiert.
Zunächst handelt es sich dabei aber lediglich um einen Test für Nutzer:innen in der Türkei und Thailand, wie der Konzern mitteilt. Ob und wann die Direct-App auch in anderen Ländern wie Deutschland angeboten wird, dürfte auch vom Erfolg des Experiments abhängen. Meta hat sich dazu bisher nicht offiziell geäußert.
Macht Direct künftig Whatsapp Konkurrenz?
Interessant ist der Direct-Start vor allem deswegen, weil Instagram-Chef Adam Mosseri zuletzt solchen eigenständigen Nachrichtensystemen für verschiedene Meta-Dienste eher skeptisch gegenüberstand, wie etwa techbook.de schreibt. Weil Interessierte nicht zwingend auf ein Instagram-Konto angewiesen sind, könnte Direct auf längere Sicht dem Meta-Dienst Whatsapp Konkurrenz machen.
Eine Anmeldung zu der neuen Messenger-App ist mit den Instagram-Logindaten möglich. Dann werden bisherige Kontakte und Chats übertragen. Wer kein Instragram-Konto hat, kann sich per E-Mail-Adresse oder Telefonnummer anmelden. Neue Kontakte lassen sich dann über die Instagram-Nutzer:innennamen oder per QR-Code manuell hinzufügen.
Optisch erinnert Direct stark an Instagrams Nachrichtenfunktion. Bekannte Funktionen wie individuelle Chat-Hintergründe, kreative Optioen wie Zeichnen und Sticker erstellen sowie das Veröffentlichen kurzer Statusmeldungen (Notes) bleiben erhalten.
Daten- und Jugendschutz im Fokus
Meta legt bei Direct aber zudem einen großen Wert auf Daten- und Jugendschutzmaßnahmen. So müssen Direct-Nutzer:innen mindestens 13 Jahre alt sein. Eltern können über Aufsichtsfunktionen Gesprächskontakte einsehen und Zeitlimits setzen.
Verdächtige oder unangemessene Interaktionen mit jungen Nutzer:innen will Meta technisch erkennen können. Darüber hinaus sollen nur Kontakte oder schon verbundene Personen Chats starten oder Nutzer:innen zu Gruppen hinzufügen können.

articles.title: Google joins the tech outage trend by announcing it's not having one | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Was Google feeling a little left out of the recent wave of tech outages? The company took to X on Tuesday to announce that its Gmail service is actually running just fine. In a post, the company said it was not currently seeing evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption and reminded users they could always check Gmail’s real-time status on its online dashboard.
As it turns out, the company was trying to head off reports of a Gmail outage that began circulating on X on Tuesday around the same time that Apple was seeing a number of verified outages of its own. While some posts on the social network suggested Gmail was experiencing a disruption, others said they were not having any problems.
The concerns seemed to stem from an X post by Downdetector, a crowdsourced website where users can report service disruptions themselves and see if others are having problems. Downdetector is not an official source for verifying or understanding the true scope of internet outages, and as people become more concerned about possible cyberattacks, the site’s data may become less valuable over time if every minor glitch and hiccup is reported as an “outage” by non-technical users.
The fact that Google had to announce it was not having an outage speaks to the growing anxiety around the reliability of major tech services. Over the past week, Apple and Microsoft experienced outages, a FAA network failure led to a nationwide ground stop, and some banks and airlines also reported disruptions.
However, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on Fox Business Tuesday that the U.S. is not currently facing coordinated cyberattacks. He told the outlet, “We do not see the indicia of a coordinated cyberattack — let me just be clear about that — and we do not see the indicia of state-sponsored activity here.”
Instead, Clayton attributed the rise in issues to businesses patching their systems. The patching may be a downstream effect of AI, as newer models have become increasingly adept at uncovering previously unknown vulnerabilities. “They’re upgrading them, they’re putting patches in place,” he said, adding that this is happening at “a much larger scale” than before.
As a result, some of the systems are “not coming back as expected in all cases,” he added.

articles.title: 12 fantastic foodie gifts for keen home cooks
articles.text:
Looking for a gift for a keen home cook? Here are 12 foodie gadgets and accessories I'd love to add to my kitchen
Kitchen kit that won't end up gathering dust at the back of a cupboard
Choosing a gift for an enthusiastic home cook can feel challenging — you want something they won't already have, and which will be genuinely useful, rather than ending up relegated to the back of an inaccessible cupboard, gathering dust. Below, I've rounded up some gadgets and accessories that would certainly make a welcome addition to my own kitchen.
Two of my most-used kitchen utensils are a silicone mini-spatula and spoon, and a set of narrow measuring spoons. The former are great for getting the dregs of sauces and condiments out of tubs and jars, and the latter perfect for measuring spices out of narrow jars (traditional, rounded measuring spoons are almost always too wide to fit, even though spices are exactly the sort of thing you want to be able to measure precisely). Incidentally, both of those were gifts, and I wouldn't have thought to buy either myself — but they've ended up being invaluable.
If you want to spend a bit more money, you can't go wrong with Le Creuset cookware for a cast-iron investment, or a Meater smart thermometer if your recipient is also a gadget fan. One of our writers recently tried out the Ninja vertical waffle maker, and I've been thinking about it ever since, so while it's not exactly a kitchen essential, I absolutely wouldn't complain if someone decided to buy me one.

articles.title: Este es el valor de la criptomoneda Bitcoin este 17 de noviembre
articles.text:
El bitcoin, la primera moneda virtual lanzada al mercado, fue creado por Satoshi Nakamoto (pseudónimo) en 2008 tras la crisis financiera que afectó al mundo; esta divisa digital tenía como base un ideal libertario y buscaba poner en jaque a las instituciones monetarias y financieras tradicionales.
Conocido en el mundo de los mercados bajo las siglas BTC, el bitcoin utiliza la criptografía para garantizar que su gestión sea descentralizada, es decir, que no pueda ser regulado por ninguna institución u organismo bancario, lo que a su vez hace que las criptomonedas sean volátiles.
A pesar del avance y alcance que ha tenido el Bitcoin y otros activos digitales de gran talla como Ethereum, organismos como el Banco Mundial, el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) y el Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) aún se muestran dudosos sobre los "pros" de este tipo de criptomonedas.
La victoria electoral de Donald Trump significó un movimiento positivo para las principales criptomonedas del mercado. A finales de 2024, bitcoin registró un nuevo máximo histórico que logró superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad, después de que el presidente estadounidense reiteró su idea de crear una reserva estratégica de la criptodivisa en Estados Unidos.
Las divisas digitales serán un foco de atención durante este año, las iniciativas del presidente de Estados Unidos y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de inteligencia artificial fungirán un papel importante en la cotización de estos activos. Después del lanzamiento del nuevo modelo de IA chino DeepSeek, BTC y otras criptos cayeron en la mayoría de los mercados de valores.
Valor de la criptomoneda Bitcoin
La cotización de bitcoin para este día a las 14:00 horas (UTC) es de 65038.71 dólares, lo que significa que la criptomoneda tuvo un cambio de 1.52% en las últimas 24 horas.
Por otro lado, registró un cambio de 0.0% con respecto a su valor hace una hora. En cuanto a su popularidad, se ubica en la posición #1.
Bitcoin alcanzó su máximo histórico
En marzo del año pasado el bitcoin ha logrado un nuevo máximo histórico, superando los valores anteriores y reafirmándose como la criptomoneda más importante en el mercado, acercándose a los 73 mil dólares. Este récord se obtuvo en medio de un flujo sin precedentes de inversiones hacia las criptomonedas, un acontecimiento notable para el sector financiero digital.
El aumento en el valor de bitcoin ocurre en un contexto donde hay un entrante masivo de capital hacia las criptomonedas, lo que indica un creciente interés y confianza de los inversores en estos activos. La subida del precio beneficia no solo a bitcoin sino que también tiene un impacto positivo en el mercado de las criptomonedas en general, favoreciendo una mayor estabilidad y visibilidad, de acuerdo a un análisis de Bloomberg.
Expertos financiaron este aumento a diferentes factores, como la adopción institucional de las criptomonedas, la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión debido a la incertidumbre económica mundial y la innovación continua en la tecnología blockchain que respalda a bitcoin y otras divisas digitales. Esta combinación de factores ha creado un entorno propicio para el crecimiento continuo en el valor de Bitcoin.
Cómo adquirir criptomonedas
Para comprarlas e intercambiarlas se utilizan portales especializados. Su valor varía en función de la oferta, de la demanda y del compromiso de los usuarios, por lo que puede cambiar más rápido que el dinero tradicional, pero mientras más gente esté interesada y quiera comprar determinada divisa, mayor será su valor.
No obstante, quien invierte en este tipo de monedas digitales debe tener muy claro que esta forma trae consigo un elevado riesgo al capital, pues, así como puede haber un incremento, también puede tener inesperadamente un desplome y acabar con los ahorros de sus usuarios.
Para almacenarlas, los usuarios deben contar con un monedero digital o wallet, que en realidad es un software a través del cual es posible guardar, enviar y hacer transacciones de las criptomonedas. En realidad, este tipo de monederos sólo guarda las claves que marcan la propiedad y el derecho de una persona sobre cierta criptomoneda, por lo que estos códigos son los que en realidad se deben proteger.

articles.title: Redbrick Offices raises Rs 630 Cr in equity led by India SME Investments and Abakkus
articles.text:
Redbrick Offices raises Rs 630 Cr in equity led by India SME Investments and Abakkus
Redbrick said it plans to use the capital to expand its managed offices portfolio from about 6.5 million sq. ft. to more than 10 million sq. ft. over the next 18 to 24 months, while investing in technology, design and service delivery to cater to enterprise and GCC clients.
Redbrick Offices has raised about $72 million (Rs 630 crore) in equity across its Series A and A1 funding rounds, the company said. The funding comprises a large primary infusion and a smaller secondary component.
India SME Investments led the Series A round in March 2026, while the Series A1 round was recently led by Abakkus’s Four2Eight Opportunities Fund. Evolvence Equity Partners, IIFL Capital Asset Management and UTI Alternatives, among others, also participated in the extended round. India SME Investments made a follow-on investment as part of Series A1. UTI Alternatives had earlier invested in the company through a structured convertible debenture issuance in March 2025.
Redbrick said it plans to use the capital to expand its managed offices portfolio from about 6.5 million sq. ft. to more than 10 million sq. ft. over the next 18 to 24 months. It will also use the funds to serve workspace requirements of large enterprises and global capability centres (GCCs), and to invest in technology infrastructure, design, and service delivery. The company said it is open to strategic partnerships and acquisitions that fit its growth plans.
The fundraise comes as India’s flexible office market crosses 100 million sq. ft., driven by demand from large enterprises and GCCs, according to the company.
“This investment marks an important milestone in our journey,” said Ayush Goenka, chairman and managing director of Redbrick Offices. He said the backing from India SME, Abakkus and other investors validates the company’s focus on improving unit economics and on demand-backed, profitable growth.
Ankit Aggarwal, senior vice president and senior fund manager for private equity at Abakkus, called Redbrick a capital-efficient business that has scaled while remaining profitable. He said flexible, asset-light corporate spaces are becoming a core part of real estate strategy for multinationals and GCCs in India.
Mitin Jain, founder and managing partner of India SME Investments, said the firm’s March 2026 decision to back Redbrick was based on its belief in Goenka and the management team’s record of building a sizeable, bootstrapped business with a focus on profitable growth.
Ladderup Corporate Advisory and IIFL Capital Services were financial advisers to the company, and Rajani Associates was its legal adviser.
Redbrick Offices operates about 6.5 million sq. ft. across more than 70 centres in over eight Indian cities, with more than 1.15 lakh seats. It builds Grade-A offices to client specifications and provides facilities management and hospitality-led services through its wholly owned subsidiary, Snow White Technologies & Services Private Limited. Its clients include GCCs, Fortune 500 companies, large enterprises, BFSI firms and US-based multinationals.
