articles.title: Cut generative AI costs: Code for rules, models for judgment | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Cut generative AI costs: Code for rules, models for judgment
The biggest cost lever in a generative AI system is whether you call a model at all. We often see teams route every task through a large language model (LLM), including input validation, formatting, and routing. Each call is cheap in isolation, but at production scale these small costs become one of the largest line items in the architecture. Wherever a deterministic rule can do the job, skipping the model saves money, cuts latency, and removes a source of non-determinism. In this post, you learn how to decide whether each step in a workflow needs a model at all. You can then map each option to AWS: deterministic code, a constrained decision call, or a right-sized model on Amazon Bedrock.
Why unneeded model calls add up
The pattern usually starts in a prototype. A model call works for one step, so it becomes the default for the next. Those steps include validating input, reformatting a request body, and picking a route. At prototype volume, nobody notices the cost.
At production volume, unneeded model calls cost you in three ways:
- Spend grows with request count, even for low-value steps.
- Latency stacks, because every model call in a chain adds hundreds of milliseconds.
- Output can vary, because the same input can return a different answer. That makes testing harder and audits slower.
Each new model launch then restarts the debate about which model to use. The earlier question, whether the step needs a model at all, goes unasked.
Cost guidance, including the AWS Well-Architected Generative AI Lens, often starts at model selection. This post starts one step earlier: Does the step need a model at all?
How to decide whether a step needs a model
Figure 1 shows the whole decision as a flowchart with three labeled lanes: Runs as code, Questions, and Runs on a model. Take each workflow step through three questions in order, and stop at the first option that meets the step’s requirements:
- Can a rule check success, such as a format, a schema, a keyword, or a range? If a rule settles only part of the step, a fast path runs the rule first.
- Can a model write the rule once, such as a regular expression or a JSON schema?
- Does the step pick one answer from a fixed list, such as a route, a class, or yes or no?
If the answer to all three is no, the step is open-ended and runs on a right-sized model.
Consider a customer support assistant. The following table shows how five of its steps go through the chart.
| # | Step | Path through the chart | Where it runs | 
| 1 | Check an order number’s format | A rule can check success. | Amazon API Gateway REST API request validation, or an AWS Lambda function | 
| 2 | Route a message by intent | A rule settles part of it. A keyword match on the fast path resolves messages such as “refund”, and the residual goes to the third question. | An AWS Step Functions Choice state that uses JSONata. The residual goes to a constrained decision call. | 
| 3 | Extract a tracking number from a carrier email | A model can write the rule once. It drafts a regular expression, and you review and commit it. | Code, as a committed pattern in AWS Lambda | 
| 4 | Pick one of four support queues for a ticket | The answer comes from a fixed list. | A constrained decision call. Unsure answers escalate to the right-sized model. | 
| 5 | Draft a reply to the customer | The task is open-ended. | The right-sized model, the smallest Amazon Bedrock model that meets the requirements | 
You can use a model when a task is open-ended, ambiguous, or generative: summarizing a document, drafting a reply, extracting meaning from prose. Use deterministic code when the task has a checkable rule: an email format, a schema, an exact keyword, a numeric range. The following table shows what you trade away when you send a rule-shaped task to a model.
| Property | Deterministic code | Model call | 
| Cost per invocation | Typically orders of magnitude lower | Per-token, non-trivial at scale | 
| Latency | Single-digit milliseconds or less | Hundreds of milliseconds | 
| Correctness on a well-specified rule | Exact for the rule as written | High, but with a non-zero error rate | 
| Auditability | The rule sits in source control | Harder to explain to an auditor | 
| Behavior over time | Stable until you change it | Changes when you move to a new model version, or when a version is retired | 
A model can also hallucinate and return different answers to the same input. A temperature of 0 makes varied answers less likely, but it doesn’t guarantee identical output. Amazon Bedrock model evaluation and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails help you measure and contain these risks. A rule has neither problem, which is one reason regulated workloads favor rules. A useful test: If you can write the acceptance test as a rule, you can usually write the step as a rule. For more information, refer to Orchestration models: From rule-based to AI-native in AWS Prescriptive Guidance.
Decide, don’t generate
Most routing and classification steps sit between a rule and open-ended generation. A rule can’t decide every case, but these steps don’t need generated text either. They need one answer from a fixed list of options that you define in advance, like the support queues in the preceding example. Use a component that limits its output to the allowed answers and gives you a signal for when to escalate. Confident answers proceed, and uncertain ones escalate. The AWS Well-Architected Agentic AI Lens describes this tiered, confidence-based escalation. On AWS, you can build it four ways:
- A small Amazon Bedrock model with structured outputs – The answer is limited to an enum of options, plus an ‘unsure’ option that triggers escalation. This is the model’s own judgment, not a calibrated score, so check it against labeled data before you use it to decide escalation.
- Embedding similarity – Embed the input with an Amazon Bedrock embeddings model and pick the nearest labeled example. Use the similarity score as an escalation signal, and set its threshold on labeled data.
- Strands Decider, an experimental open source decision model under the Apache License 2.0 – It picks from options or scores against a rubric, and it returns a calibrated confidence with each answer. Its README reports that answers at a confidence of 0.9 or more are right about 95 percent of the time on short classification tasks. Because the model is experimental, validate that result on your own data before you use it in production. You host it yourself, for example on an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint, by following the deployment guides in its repository.
- A trained classifier on Amazon SageMaker AI – It returns class probabilities with low latency and cost once you have labeled training data.
The following JSON schema limits a structured-output answer to four queues plus ‘unsure’. Amazon Bedrock requires every object in the schema to set additionalProperties to false.
Whichever option you choose, check its escalation signal against your own labeled data, and set any threshold there. Keep your authorization decisions, such as a refund limit, in a rule.
The deterministic fast-path pattern
Many cost patterns focus on routing between models. The fast path goes one level earlier: Run the deterministic check first, and send only what the rule can’t settle to a model. Intent routing is one example. Many messages carry an unambiguous signal, such as “refund” or “reset my password”, which a keyword match resolves in single-digit milliseconds or less. If rules resolve 95 percent of requests, only 1 in 20 requests reaches a model, before any savings from model selection. (Illustrative arithmetic, not a benchmark.)
On AWS, you compose this from existing building blocks:
- AWS Step Functions Choice states branch before the workflow invokes any model.
- AWS Lambda hosts rules that need more than a Choice state, such as validation and schema checks.
- Amazon API Gateway (REST API) request validation rejects malformed input before any compute runs.
- A constrained decision call or an Amazon Bedrock model handles only the residual.
The following Choice state is a keyword fast path. It uses JSONata to send refund and password-reset messages straight to code, and it sends everything else to the constrained decision call.
You can also let a model write the rule once instead of running it every time. Have it draft a regular expression or a JSON schema, review it, and commit it. At runtime the rule runs at rule speed and cost. Review a model-written regular expression, and test it against known good and bad inputs. Avoid nested quantifiers such as (a+)+, which can make matching very slow on some inputs (regular expression denial of service, or ReDoS).
When you do generate, Amazon Bedrock structured outputs constrain a response to a JSON schema that you define. The response then matches the schema, so your code can parse it without custom parsing logic (check content for correctness). Keep range checks, such as numeric bounds and length limits, in code. For supported models and schema features, refer to Get validated JSON results from models.
If your rules live in configuration, allow only known primitives, such as regular expressions, schema checks, keyword lists, and range checks. Never run arbitrary code from a configuration file.
When you do need a model, right-size it
Choose the cheapest and fastest model that meets your quality floor. That is often not the newest or largest model. The Generative AI Lens covers this in its best practice on right-sizing model selection. Effective cost optimization strategies for Amazon Bedrock covers it in depth. Define the requirements before you compare models:
- Quality floor: The minimum acceptable output quality, measured on a golden evaluation set (labeled examples of the task with known-correct answers).
- Cost ceiling: The most you pay per request or per successful outcome.
- Latency target: The p95 or p99 response time the experience can tolerate.
- Compliance constraints: Requirements such as data residency that can rule out candidates.
Amazon Bedrock offers many model families and sizes behind one API, so you can right-size each task without changing your integration. Amazon Bedrock Intelligent Prompt Routing routes each request to a suitable model within a supported model family. Amazon Bedrock Model Distillation transfers knowledge from a larger model to a smaller, cheaper one for your use case. Model providers evaluate a new frontier model on broad benchmarks, but your workload is one task with one quality floor. A larger model can add cost and latency without improving that task. Before you switch, evaluate each launch against your requirements, such as quality on your golden evaluation set and your latency target.
Treat model choice as tested configuration
The Generative AI Lens recommends testing candidate models against your ground truth data and having a way to update the model quickly. Go further and treat the decision as a tested configuration:
- Keep a golden evaluation set per task, with labeled ground truth, and run it in continuous integration.
- Gate on your requirements. Treat a cheaper model that drops below the quality floor as a regression.
- Put the model behind a configuration flag so that you can reverse a swap.
- Verify with the right oracle. Check rules against ground truth. Reserve model-as-judge evaluation for open-ended outputs.
- Watch for drift. Sample some rule-resolved requests through a model in shadow mode, and reclassify a step when they disagree.
Putting it into practice
Spend model capacity where judgment is needed, and nowhere else. You can get there in four steps:
- Instrument – Tag every call as deterministic code, a constrained decision call, or a model call. Track cost per successful outcome.
- Move the rules to code – Run rule-checkable steps on AWS Lambda or AWS Step Functions. This is usually the largest and safest win.
- Add constrained decision calls – Route fixed-choice steps through a call that escalates when it is unsure.
- Test before you switch models – Run every new model through your golden evaluation set before it becomes the default.
Conclusion
In this post, you learned how to decide whether a workflow step needs a model at all. Rules belong in deterministic code, and fixed choices belong in a constrained decision call. Open-ended work goes to a right-sized Amazon Bedrock model. Aim to meet each requirement at the lowest cost and latency that your quality floor allows. Ask whether a step needs a model before you ask which one.
For more information, refer to these posts on the AWS Artificial Intelligence Blog:
- Use decision models with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations.
- Use Amazon Bedrock Intelligent Prompt Routing for cost and latency benefits.
- Structured outputs on Amazon Bedrock: Schema-compliant AI responses.
- Fix evaluation bias to unlock better models on Amazon Bedrock.
To try a constrained decision call, open the Amazon Bedrock console, or deploy Strands Decider from its GitHub repository.
Start with one high-volume workflow and measure how much of it never needed a model.

articles.title: Ticketmaster, NHL lobby Alberta over ticket reselling bill
articles.text:
The provincial government of Alberta is considering new measures to address high ticket resale prices, as new regulations are being debated in the provincial legislature. However, the National Hockey League (NHL) and its ticket partner, Ticketmaster, are lobbying officials to ensure the proposed consumer protection laws don’t conflict with business interests.
Dave Nally, the minister of Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, introduced a new piece of legislation, Bill 34, on Oct. 28 that would require all ticket resellers to disclose all associated prices and fees.
This new bill doesn’t include a price cap on resale tickets, but one could come into effect later. The government added that the legislation opens the door to additional protections, which will be determined through future consultations. Alongside this, members of the official opposition criticized the legislation’s lack of concrete price caps during a Nov. 3 debate in the legislature.
According to Alberta’s lobbyist registry, the NHL registered to lobby the provincial government on Nov. 2. on consumer protection and resale tickets to “ensure the interests of the NHL (e.g., World Cup of Hockey 2028, Calgary Flames, Edmonton Oilers) are not negatively impacted.”
Ticketmaster, unsurprisingly, registered to lobby the Alberta government back in August and sought to meet with officials to “discuss the government’s ongoing consideration of measures to protect consumers in live event ticketing.”
The NHL and Ticketmaster work together to manage an official ticket resale platform, the NHL Ticket Exchange. However, the exchange has no cap on ticket resale, and both organizations profit off resale according to the Investigative Journalism Foundation (IJF).
Interestingly, the IJF also noted that a private members’ bill voted down by the UCP caucus would’ve banned secondary ticket platforms from charging a fee to transfer a ticket.
Now, as pointed out by the IJF, ice-level tickets for the Calgary Flames’ final home game of the season, and the last game at the Scotiabank Saddledome, are anywhere between $1,200 and $11,800 for verified resale. Alongside this, there is a pair of tickets in section 119 priced at a whopping $23,600, with $20,000 as the face value and $3,600 as the service fee. For comparison, this used 2020 Toyota Corolla on Clutch is going for $390 more than these tickets.
However, this is a special-occasion game, as it is the last game at the iconic stadium, originally built for the 1988 Calgary Winter Olympics. In other words, it’s not entirely reflective of a typical ticket resale.
Looking at other regular-season games, like this Thursday’s home match against the Minnesota Wild, shows that verified resale tickets like Section 119, Row 5, Seats 9-10 are going for $290 apiece.
For context, Ontario already capped the price of resale tickets in April, when Bill 97 was enacted.
Source: Investigative Journalism Foundation
Image Credit: Ticketmaster

articles.title: Exclusive: Envoy targets defense contractors and semiconductor fabs with Visitors Critical - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: Envoy targets defense contractors and semiconductor fabs with Visitors Critical
Workplace management platform company Envoy Inc. today launched Visitors Critical, a new tier of its visitor management service for defense contractors, semiconductor fabs and other high-security sites.
The new tier is aimed at a problem Envoy says is common at those sites, where visitor security is still run across email, spreadsheets and separate systems and letting the wrong person in can be costly. Penalties, debarment or a lost facility clearance are all possible after a wrong entry at a compliance-driven site. The person who signed the authorization can also be held liable, according to the company, which noted that settlements under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations have reached $51 million.
“We’ve spent the last 13 years building Envoy to deliver the highest levels of security, safety and compliance in a way that feels natural to the people using it,” said founder and Chief Executive Larry Gadea, who worked as an engineer at Google LLC and Twitter Inc. before starting the company in 2013.
Visitors Critical scans a visitor’s government-issued ID and matches their face to the photo on it. Names are also screened against denied-party and export-control lists through Visual Compliance and Descartes MK, both from The Descartes Systems Group Inc. Contractor qualifications are checked through ISN Software Corp. From there, visits are sent for approval based on the organization’s own written policies. The approver’s reasoning is then kept on record in case of an audit.
Among Envoy’s existing customers is Attalon Inc., the former aerospace and defense business of Coherent Corp. Every visitor to all 12 of Attalon’s sites has their ID scanned by Envoy before being screened against denied-party lists. Tim Carr, Attalon’s director of security and environment, health and safety, said that an auditor who inspects one site “has effectively inspected them all.”
The launch comes as new Envoy research of 1,000 security leaders found that 62% of enterprise leaders are very confident they would pass a physical security audit without preparation. Some 63% of that group had a security incident in the past year. At sensitive workplaces, 44% of leaders could not say with confidence who was in their building the previous day.
Visitors Critical is available now. Hardware-based ID verification, which uses supported readers to authenticate the document itself and catch forged IDs, is being offered through an early access program.
Envoy claims more than 16,000 workplaces in 170 countries as customers, including 92 of the Fortune 500. The company launched Response, a threat intelligence and incident management product, in August. It raised $111 million in a Series C round in January 2022 at a $1.4 billion valuation.

articles.title: Diese 5-Minuten-Übung verändert, wie du mit ChatGPT arbeitest
articles.text:
ChatGPT wie einen Kollegen nutzen: Diese 5-Minuten-Übung empfiehlt ein Stanford-Professor
Im Frühjahr 2025 ist Jeremy Utley, Professor am Hasso Plattner Institute of Design der Stanford-Uni, mit seinem Videointerview „How Stanford Teaches KI-Powered Creativity in Just 13 Minutes“ viral gegangen. Das Video ist über 2,3 Millionen Mal angeschaut worden.
KI-Chatbot als Teamkollegen behandeln
Darin erklärt Utley, dass eine kleine Verschiebung des Mindsets im Umgang mit KI-Chatbots einen großen Unterschied bezüglich des Outputs mache. Statt KI nur als Werkzeug zu nutzen, würden High-Performer ChatGPT und Co wie eine:n Teamkolleg:in behandeln, so Utley.
Als Beispiel führt Utley das Verfassen einer E-Mail an. Normalerweise würden Nutzer:innen die KI einfach bitten, ihnen eine Antwort zu schreiben und wären mit dem Output schnell zufriedenzustellen. Um das volle Potenzial aus den Chatbots zu kitzeln, sollte die KI aber zur Zusammenarbeit eingeladen werden, wie es vonseiten der Stanford-Uni heißt.
Laut Utley gibt man dabei der KI die Erlaubnis, Fragen zu stellen. Ein entsprechender Prompt könnte so lauten: „Hilf mir, auf diese E-Mail zu antworten. Stelle mir alle Fragen, die du benötigst, um den Kontext zu erhalten“. Ebenfalls möglich ist, das Output des einen KI-Chatbots der Konkurrenz, etwa Gemini oder Claude, vorzulegen und um eine kritische Einschätzung zu bitten.
Positives Feedback fördert Ideenfindung
Selbst die Eigenart großer Sprachmodelle, Nutzer:innen überwiegend positiv und unkritisch gegenüberzutreten, lässt sich Utley zufolge als Kreativitätsbooster nutzen. Wenn ChatGPT alle Ideen wunderbar finde, fühle man sich vielleicht weniger gehemmt oder eingeschränkt bei der Ausarbeitung weiterer, zunächst abwegig erscheinender Ideen.
Die wahre Magie, so Utley, entstehe aber erst dann, wenn Nutzer:innen der KI beigebracht hätten, wer sie sind. Dazu gehöre der persönliche Geschmack, der Ton, der Stil oder Kriterien dafür, was gut ist oder aussieht. Der Output klinge dann menschlicher. Letztlich könne KI auch dazu beitragen, mögliche Engpässe im kreativen Denken zu überwinden.
Emotionale Entscheidungen diskutieren
Um herauszufinden, wie sich KI-Zusammenarbeit wirklich anfühlt, hat Utley sich eine fünfminütige Übung ausgedacht. Dabei geht es darum, mit ChatGPT und Co eine emotionale Entscheidung zu diskutieren, für die normalerweise eine nahe Person konsultiert würde. Beispiele: Ein schwieriges Gespräch, eine Entscheidung über die weitere Karriereplanung oder die Frage, ob man ein neues Projekt übernehmen sollte.
Der Prompt könnte dann so aussehen: „Ich kämpfe mit einer Entscheidung. Bevor du mir einen Rat gibst, stelle mir bitte drei Fragen, um meine Situation besser zu verstehen“. Dann sollen Nutzer:innen einfach ganz normal mit dem KI-Chatbot plaudern. Utley zufolge sei diese Übung meist der Augenöffner für Menschen, die Zweifel an seinem Konzept hätten.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 28.02.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.
ernsthaft?
dann war ich dem schon vorraus. genauso kommuniziere ich seid Anbeginn mit LLM und lasse LLM a LLM b überprüfen.
oder lasse sie zusammen arbeiten.
und behandel AI wie einen Partner nicht wie ein Werkzeug.
ein kreativer Partner. dazu muß man aber schon auch selbst kreativ sein.

articles.title: Attention à ce GTA 6 qui circule avant la sortie du jeu : c’est un piège pour voler vos données
articles.text:
Le jeu le plus attendu de la décennie, GTA VI, débarque ce jeudi sur PS5 et Xbox Series. Un événement mondial pour les joueurs…et les cybercriminels qui tentent de profiter de leur impatience. Spécialiste en sécurité, Avast alerte sur l’existence d’une campagne qui promet de télécharger la version complète du jeu avant tout le monde, et gratuitement.
Une offre évidemment trop belle pour être vraie. À la place du jeu de Rockstar, les victimes récupèrent un logiciel malveillant.
Un PDF, un faux site et une fausse page Google Drive
Comme à chaque lancement très attendu, ce type de piège se dévoile. Avast explique que l’arnaque commence par un document PDF soigné, présenté comme un « guide de téléchargement » de GTA 6, qui reprend les informations officielles sur le jeu, ses personnages et sa date de sortie pour paraître crédible. Un gros bouton « Download now » renvoie vers un site baptisé Getallsoft (ou Getarsoft ou dans le PDF), qui se présente comme une plateforme de téléchargement de logiciels et affirme que GTA 6 y est « disponible en téléchargement gratuit ». En cliquant de nouveau, l’internaute atterrit sur une page imitant Google Drive, qui héberge une archive ZIP de plus de 700 Mo censée contenir le jeu.
Une fois lancé, le contenu de l’archive installe en réalité un infostealer. Ce type de malware est conçu pour aspirer discrètement les données stockées sur l’ordinateur, comme les identifiants et mots de passe enregistrés dans le navigateur, les cookies de session ou encore des informations bancaires, qui sont ensuite revendues ou exploitées par les pirates. Avast avait déjà repéré, il y a quelques semaines, plus de 200 noms de domaine liés à GTA 6 créés en seulement 24 heures. Près de 10 % présentaient un risque élevé ou moyen, à base de fausses précommandes, de sites imitant les boutiques de Rockstar ou de PlayStation, ainsi que de faux jeux-concours.
Il n’existe aucune version PC de GTA 6
Pour éviter de tomber dans le piège, un détail suffit pourtant. GTA 6 ne sortira jeudi que sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series X|S, et Rockstar n’a annoncé aucune version PC à ce jour. Un fichier ZIP à installer sur un ordinateur ne peut donc pas contenir le jeu. Même sur console, le téléchargement passe exclusivement par le PlayStation Store ou le Microsoft Store, y compris pour les versions vendues en boîte. Rappelons que ces dernières ne contiennent qu’un code. Enfin, le jeu pèse plus de 200 Go, bien loin des 700 Mo de l’archive proposée par les escrocs.

articles.title: “Des systèmes d’IA qui se construisent eux-mêmes” : même le créateur de Claude prend peur et active ses garde-fous les plus stricts
articles.text:
“Des systèmes d’IA qui se construisent eux-mêmes” : même le créateur de Claude prend peur et active ses garde-fous les plus stricts
Le créateur de Claude, Anthropic, l'écrit noir sur blanc dans ses documents officiels : ses IA font désormais progresser la recherche à un rythme qu'il juge assez inquiétant pour activer ses garde-fous les plus stricts. L'aveu tient en quelques lignes, perdues parmi les facteurs de risque.
Le 10 novembre, Anthropic a transmis au gendarme boursier américain, la SEC, une nouvelle version du prospectus qui précède son entrée en Bourse. Une phrase y a changé de sens. Le 2 novembre, l'entreprise écrivait encore qu'elle pourrait "imminemment" atteindre le seuil de progrès spectaculairement accéléré par l'IA prévu par sa politique de développement responsable, la RSP. Huit jours plus tard, elle affirme l'avoir atteint. Gizmodo a relevé ce glissement le 16 novembre.
Un seuil fixé au doublement du rythme de progrès
La RSP place la barre à un doublement du rythme d'amélioration des modèles par rapport à une période de référence, à condition que l'automatisation de la recherche par l'IA explique plausiblement ce bond. Le texte s'applique dès qu'Anthropic "observe ou anticipe" une telle accélération. La société a retenu la seconde voie : sa décision s'appuie sur ce qu'elle attend de ses futurs modèles et sur sa cadence globale de progression. Dès juin, elle avait publié des chiffres montrant que Claude commençait à construire sa propre successeure, du code produit par l'IA jusqu'à sa contribution aux travaux de recherche.
Le prospectus contient un aveu plus troublant encore. Ses instruments de mesure reposant sur des indicateurs à retardement, Anthropic reconnaît que "par le passé, nous n'avons pas identifié, et pourrions à l'avenir ne pas identifier, une accélération significative de notre rythme de développement avant qu'elle ne se soit produite". Le document envisage même le pire : si les capacités de ses modèles venaient à dépasser ses mesures de sécurité, l'entreprise pourrait se retrouver incapable d'évaluer ou de contenir les risques qui en découlent.
Pour l'organisme indépendant METR, qui a eu un accès privilégié aux données internes du laboratoire du 12 août au 29 octobre, le compte y est presque. Il chiffre l'accélération à 1,9 fois le rythme passé, dans une fourchette de 1,5 à 2,8. Environ 80 % de ce gain viendrait de l'usage de l'IA par les équipes.
Pendant la tournée de présentation aux investisseurs, Tom Brown, cofondateur et directeur du calcul, en a donné un exemple saisissant. Selon lui, le modèle Mythos a fait tourner Claude sur les puces AMD MI355X en trois jours, alors qu'il fallait auparavant six à douze mois. Le chantier ne portait que sur le traitement des requêtes d'un seul modèle, mais le dirigeant insiste : tout s'est fait "pratiquement sans intervention humaine".
Sécurité renforcée et rythme modulé
Franchir ce cap entraîne des obligations. D'après la lecture de la RSP par Gizmodo, Anthropic doit viser des niveaux de sécurité "sans précédent" et obtenir une visibilité totale sur le comportement de ses modèles. Ses équipes d'attaque internes doivent aussi devenir assez redoutables pour rendre superflus les chasseurs de failles extérieurs. Le prospectus exclut de laisser Claude concevoir seul ses successeurs sans "supervision humaine significative", et l'entreprise songe à réviser sa charte pour "garder les humains aux commandes" du développement de ses modèles les plus avancés.
Dans leur lettre aux investisseurs, les sept cofondateurs jugent qu'il faudra peut-être "moduler le rythme extrêmement rapide auquel les capacités de l'IA se démultiplient, en particulier lorsque ce mouvement est porté par des systèmes d'IA qui se construisent eux-mêmes". Dario Amodei, son patron, appelait déjà en septembre les laboratoires à lever le pied face à des modèles de plus en plus aptes à s'améliorer seuls.
	
Moduler le rythme extrêmement rapide auquel les capacités de l’IA se démultiplient, en particulier lorsque ce mouvement est porté par des systèmes d’IA qui se construisent eux-mêmes.
Le ton n'a rien de nouveau chez Anthropic, dont les documents boursiers évoquaient déjà des risques existentiels et une IA capable de résister à son propre arrêt. Ces alertes répétées laissent sceptiques une partie des observateurs, qui y voient aussi un argument de vente à deux jours des débuts de l'action au Nasdaq, prévus le 19 novembre. L'offre s'adresse d'ailleurs aux particuliers de neuf pays européens, dont la France. D'autres, comme cet ancien chercheur passé par OpenAI et Anthropic, estiment au contraire qu'aucun laboratoire ne prend ces risques assez au sérieux.

articles.title: How AI could reshape jobs, investing, and wealth creation in India
articles.text:
How AI could reshape jobs, investing, and wealth creation in India
At TechSparks 2026, Angel One Group CEO Ambarish Kenghe discussed how AI could change the nature of work, make investing more accessible, and create opportunities in healthcare, transportation, fintech and beyond.
AI is changing how people work, how businesses build products, and how investors identify opportunities. As the technology becomes more accessible, the question is how more Indians can participate in the wealth it creates.
At TechSparks 2026, Ambarish Kenghe, Group CEO of Angel One, joined Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project, for a fireside chat on investing in India’s AI decade. The conversation covered the future of jobs, AI’s role in making investing more accessible, and the sectors where new opportunities could emerge.
Will AI create more jobs than it replaces?
For Kenghe, the answer lies partly in how technology has changed economies in the past.
He pointed to Jevons paradox, named after British economist William Stanley Jevons, who observed that improvements in steam engine efficiency led to an increase in coal consumption rather than a decline. As engines became more efficient, their use expanded.
Kenghe believes AI could have a similar effect. Citing data from Anthropic, he noted that 57% of the work done with Claude involves augmentation, while 43% involves automation. As AI makes knowledge work more productive, demand for such work could increase in ways that are difficult to predict.
He cited banking as an example. When ATMs and computerized systems began replacing manual transactions at bank counters, it seemed likely that fewer employees would be needed. Instead, banking jobs increased as the industry expanded and new requirements emerged.
Kenghe believes AI could have a similar impact, allowing people to work on problems that have remained unresolved.
However, the transition will require workers to adapt.
“While the demand for knowledge work will go up a lot with AI, each of us will have to transform because it’s not that we will do the same kind of job. We can’t become more efficient tellers. We will have to get to a very different level of operation, and what we do will change. How it will change, only time will tell,” he said.
Making investing more accessible
The conversation then turned to how more Indians could participate in wealth creation.
Kenghe identified three challenges: access, information, and intelligence.
Access to investing has become considerably easier. People can now complete their KYC on their phones and start investing without the physical paperwork and complicated procedures that were once required.
However, access alone does not guarantee participation. Many people know about the stock market but lack the information or confidence to make investment decisions.
“The two other issues which are not fully solved are information and intelligence, and I think AI is solving it in a big way,” Kenghe said.
He cited Angel One’s Ask Angel, an AI-powered tool that allows users to ask questions and receive relevant information. The tool does not provide investment advice because of regulatory restrictions.
Kenghe also believes AI could help reduce some of the advantages institutional investors have over individual investors. Institutions typically have access to more capital, sophisticated technology, and specialized teams. While AI cannot eliminate these differences, it could make information and tools more widely available.
He compared this development to the evolution of computing. The computer used aboard the Apollo mission had far less computing power than modern devices. Today, smartphones offer computing capabilities that far exceed what was available during that mission.
He believes investing could undergo a similar change as AI tools become more accessible.
Citing a SEBI study, Kenghe said 63% of Indian households are aware of the stock market, but only 9.5% invest in it. Better access to information and intelligence could encourage more people to participate.
However, broader participation will not necessarily lead to equal wealth creation. AI could democratize access to investing without socialising wealth. Individual investors would still need to make decisions based on their available capital and appetite for risk.
Building products that solve real problems
Drawing on his experience building Google Pay, Kenghe discussed what it takes to create products that consumers want to use.
For him, the starting point is identifying a genuine problem and solving it well.
A product may be complex behind the scenes, but the experience should be simple for the user. In payments, for example, people want to transfer money quickly and reliably while knowing their transactions are secure.
Adding features serves little purpose if the basic experience does not work.
Kenghe said identifying the right problem is often the harder task. Founders can become distracted by new technologies and trends, but product development should begin with understanding what users need.
Where the next opportunities lie
When Sharma asked about untapped areas for innovation, Kenghe pointed to opportunities beyond building increasingly large AI models.
He cited Jev AI, a model focused on efficiency rather than competing directly on size, as an example of an alternative approach to AI development. He also mentioned Instinct as another example of companies approaching the technology differently.
Healthcare, he believes, offers considerable scope for specialized AI models.
“I don't see anybody coming out with a kick-ass, dedicated healthcare model. You could actually create models that are dedicated to certain diseases, certain areas,” he said.
Rather than approaching healthcare as a single, broad problem, Kenghe suggested developing models focused on specific diseases or areas of care.
He also identified transportation and logistics as sectors with significant opportunities. While self-driving technology is beginning to develop, he believes there is still considerable room for innovation, particularly in India, where traffic and logistics costs remain major challenges.
Other areas he is optimistic about include space exploration, with the long-term possibility of space-based data centres, and fintech.
Balancing ambition with data
For entrepreneurs, identifying an opportunity is only the beginning. They must also make decisions amid uncertainty.
Kenghe believes data should inform these decisions without determining every move.
It can help founders understand market conditions, assess risks, and make more rational choices. But data cannot provide every answer, particularly when entrepreneurs are building something new.
“Entrepreneurs are entrepreneurs because their emotion brings in the passion. Take the emotion out of it, perhaps the passion comes out as well,” he said.
Kenghe believes founders need to balance that passion with evidence. Regularly reviewing data can help them make informed decisions and remain grounded, while recognizing its limitations leaves room for instinct, conviction, and the risks involved in building a business.

articles.title: Ya son oficiales: Xiaomi presenta sus nuevos auriculares con formato clip y llegan junto con un estuche tipo joyero
articles.text:
Quizás la nueva generación de móviles haya opacado la presentación de otros dispositivos, pero no podemos obviarlos. Uno de los más atractivos son los Xiaomi Clip, unos auriculares que, por 149,99 euros introducen a la marca en este tipo de formato tan característico que llevamos un tiempo viendo en otras marcas.
Xiaomi Clip
Xiaomi salta al formato tipo clip
Los Xiaomi Clip, como bien indica su nombre, son unos auriculares de tipo clip que son ideales para utilizar diariamente en entornos donde no queremos estar completamente inmersos. No se introducen en el oído, sino que se apoyan sobre las orejas para ofrecer un mejor confort.
Evidentemente, esto evita que tengamos una reducción pasiva del ruido, así como cancelación activa de ruido (ANC). Son auriculares orientados a ser cómodos y para ello, según la propia marca, cuentan con memoria para adaptarse mejor a cada persona.
También resulta curioso su estuche de carga que llega, en este caso, con un formato tipo joyero. Dicho estuche, además, incorpora una batería que ofrece una autonomía teórica de hasta 38 horas. Con una sola carga, los auriculares ofrecen una autonomía teórica de hasta 9 horas de uso.
Entre otras características, los auriculares son compatibles con el códec LHDC 5.0 y con conectividad Bluetooth 5.4. Ofrecen resistencia al agua y al polvo (IP57), incorporan un driver dinámico de 11 mm, son compatibles con la red Buscar de Apple y permiten conectarse dos unidades a un mismo dispositivo para compartir el audio.
En cuanto a su disponibilidad, los Xiaomi Clip ya están disponibles en cuatro colores: Dorado, Morado, Blanco Perla y Negro. Su precio oficial es de 149,99 euros.

articles.title: Gemini Notebook peut désormais créer un site interactif à partir de vos documents et c’est bluffant
articles.text:
Google vient d’ajouter une fonction plus que prometteuse à Gemini Notebook : le service peut désormais générer des sites web interactifs à partir des documents d’un projet.
Récemment renommé Gemini Notebook, l’ex-NotebookLM ne cesse de s’améliorer. L’équipe en charge de son développement a remplacé les plafonds journaliers de l’outil par de nouvelles limites basées sur la puissance de calcul. Elle a ensuite lancé un catalogue de manuels gratuits, hélas réservés aux américains et aux indiens. Cette semaine, Gemini Notebook vient d’ajouter une nouvelle corde à son arc.
Gemini Notebook transforme vos notes en site web
Google vient de faire une annonce qui devrait intéresser beaucoup de monde : « Dès aujourd’hui, Gemini Notebook peut transformer vos sources en sites interactifs pour vous aider à comprendre rapidement des informations complexes. » La fonctionnalité, qui est en cours de déploiement dans le monde entier, permet de générer des pages web sur la base d’un simple prompt. Une fois créées, celles-ci s'ouvrent dans un nouvel onglet.
Google, qui travaillait déjà sur cette fonction en août, a en tête plusieurs usages : la création de frises, de tableaux périodiques interactifs, de tableaux de bord, d'outils de suivi de projet et bien plus encore. Le tout peut notamment être partagé et servir de base à un travail collectif.
Une fonctionnalité puissante qui nécessite des requêtes précises
Gemini Notebook peut, certes, faire des merveilles avec vos notes mais encore faut-il savoir s’en servir : Google conseille aux utilisateurs de fournir « une description de ce que vous souhaitez créer pour le travail ou les études ». Pour obtenir un bon résultat, la précision est donc de mise et les demandes trop vagues, à proscrire.
Cette nouvelle fonctionnalité s’ajoute à la longue liste d’options déjà disponibles dans Gemini Notebook : création de résumés vidéos, d’infographies, de tableaux de données, de diaporamas et bien plus encore. Elle arrivera dans les prochains jours chez tous les utilisateurs de plus de 18 ans, abonnés Google Workspace compris.
- Réponses liées aux sources
- Nombreux formats de fichiers
- Génération audio et visuelle
La fonction est, pour l'heure, disponible uniquement en version web. Les adeptes de l'application mobile ne sont pas oubliés, mais ils devront patienter encore un peu : Google indique en effet dans son annonce que la nouveauté sera bientôt disponible en version mobile, sans préciser de date.
Bien sûr, il faut garder à l'esprit que Gemini Notebook peut se tromper, comme tous les services boostés à l'intelligence artificielle. Pensez donc à bien vérifier le résultat produit pour éviter les mauvaises surprises.

articles.title: SSSTC Introduces PCIe Gen4 QLC SSDs for AI PCs and Industrial Applications
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
SSSTC Introduces PCIe Gen4 QLC SSDs for AI PCs and Industrial Applications
Solid State Storage Technology Corporation (SSSTC), a subsidiary of Kioxia Corporation, today announced the PQ2 series, the company's first industrial-grade QLC SSD. Featuring a PCIe Gen 4 x4 interface and BiCS FLASH generation 8 QLC flash memory, PQ2 combines responsive data access with industrial-grade reliability.
Designed for read-intensive workloads, PQ2 supports AI PC tasks such as loading locally stored AI models and accessing application data. The series is also suitable for point-of-sale (POS) terminals, thin clients, and networking devices, as well as boot storage in embedded systems.The PQ2 series uses Kioxia 4-bit-per-cell QLC NAND flash memory. The NAND flash memory incorporates CMOS directly Bonded to Array (CBA) technology, which enhances memory density, performance, and power efficiency.
PQ2 also features a DRAM-less design incorporating proven Host Memory Buffer (HMB) technology. The series offers M.2 2280 and M.2 2230 form factors, with capacity options of 512 GB, 1 TB, and 2 TB, giving system designers flexible storage configurations for compact devices and embedded platforms.
PQ2 supports NVMe 2.0d and delivers sequential read and write speeds of up to 7,000 MB/s and 6,200 MB/s, respectively. Its 4 KiB random read and write performance reaches up to 1,000 KIOPS each, supporting frequent access to operating systems, applications, and stored data.
Designed for industrial environments, PQ2 features vibration and shock resistance and operates at temperatures ranging from 0 °C to 85 °C. The series has a rated mean time between failures (MTBF) of 3 million hours.
For data protection, PQ2 includes AES 256-bit hardware encryption, with optional support for TCG Opal and TCG Pyrite to address different system security requirements.
For more information about the PQ2 series and configuration options, please contact SSSTC.

articles.title: “Trump was in bed with Jensen”: Critics balk at Huang’s wish to return to Nvidia
articles.text:
On Monday, large trucks began circling the streets of Washington, DC, carrying billboards urging Congress to investigate the Trump administration’s ties with Nvidia’s disgraced CEO Jensen Huang.
“Jensen was in bed with a spy from China,” the billboards created by the Tech Oversight Project (TOP) alleged. “Trump was in bed with Jensen.” TOP is a nonprofit that describes itself as “dedicated to reining in Big Tech.”
Currently, Trump is supporting a campaign to bring back Huang as Nvidia’s CEO—despite many Republicans calling it a “horrible idea.” Breaking his silence, Huang issued a statement Tuesday saying he would be “honored” to return, but the board said reinstatement is not under consideration as an internal investigation into US spying claims remains ongoing. Huang used the moment to say that his interests align with the US’s, saying:
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia.
Trump may have learned as early as this spring that Huang was potentially the target of Chinese espionage, but the president claimed recently that he didn’t know Huang was potentially exposed to a Chinese spy as he was becoming a prominent part of Trump’s inner circle, CNN reported.
If Trump wasn’t adequately briefed, it raises question about whether the White House acted with “sufficient urgency” to address a serious espionage threat, CNN said. But if Trump is deflecting, an even “graver question” will emerge about why Trump didn’t act on information and instead continued to keep Huang close, CNN said.
Instead of distancing himself from the Nvidia CEO, Trump invited Huang to sit at the head table during a state dinner with China’s president Xi Jinping, and last month, Trump awarded Huang the National Medal of Science, the nation’s highest scientiﬁc honor, for his AI achievements.
“Not only has he continued to do nothing, he’s invited that very CEO into the White House and on state visits to China with him,” Sacha Haworth, TOP’s founder and CEO, told Ars. “And the question we all have to ask is ‘why on Earth would he do that?’”
Trump officials accused of “corruption”
What Trump and Nvidia knew—and when—have become central questions for some Republicans, as well as top Democrats who plan to investigate the scandal when they assume control of key committees in Congress next year. Andrew Yoon, head of research for a nonprofit called CivAI, which warns the public of dangers from AI, told Ars that Huang doesn’t need to be compromised by China to have endangered the US. Prioritizing boosting profits over national security alone is “pretty concerning.”
“I think the most notable thing here is that Jensen Huang has been at the absolute forefront of lobbying to be able to sell chips to China,” Yoon said. “He has leveraged his very deep relationships with government, especially President Trump, in order to be able to sell as many Nvidia chips to China as he can get away with. If he could be selling Blackwell chips to China, I’m sure he would be.”
Yoon noted that evidencesuggests some Chinese AI models have been trained on Blackwell chips. Even with China’s push to prioritize domestic chipmakers like Huawei, Nvidia chips remain “indispensable” to China’s frontier AI goals, Yoon said. And national security experts fear that access to high-end chips will help China advance its military AI or gain economic ground.
The White House isn’t commenting on Trump’s relationship with Huang. Among the lawmakers accusing the Trump administration of “corruption” is Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), The Wall Street Journal reported. He has already asked the White House to “preserve all communications” between Trump and Huang.
Other lawmakers are “seeking more information about what Trump knew about the relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang,” the former Megaspeed CEO whom Huang admitted to having an affair with. They also want to know more about “the administration’s failure to stop artiﬁcial-intelligence chips from going to China,” WSJ reported, and Nvidia’s reportedly $25 million donation to the White House ballroom.
“It is not just an intelligence issue; it’s also a potential corruption issue,” Blumenthal said. “There needs to be a really penetrating, comprehensive investigation of all the possible compromises of our intelligence that may have occurred, but also… that Donald Trump is so high on the head of Nvidia, and now is potentially linked to intelligence compromises.”
Trump officials profit off Nvidia policies
Trump has profited off Nvidia’s success while in office, buying “millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares in his personal brokerage accounts since returning to oﬃce in 2025,” the WSJ reported. The White House maintains that the president has no role in managing his stock portfolio.
Other officials advising Trump on AI also benefited from relaxing export curbs, TOP said. On Tuesday, the group issued a report summarizing what the public knows about potential conflicts of interest of two Trump officials: former White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.
Haworth, TOP’s founder, told Ars she’s concerned that Sacks and Lutnick abused their power to convince Trump to let Nvidia sell cutting-edge technology to China, while standing to “gain astronomical amounts of money.”
“The public is outraged by Nvidia’s CEO for compromising our national security, but we didn’t get here because of Jensen Huang’s missteps alone,” Haworth said. If “Nvidia was knowingly doing business with companies tied to illegal chip sales and smuggling with China,” then “the Trump administration was asleep at the wheel,” she said.
“White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick were protecting their own fortunes rather than looking out for Americans,” Haworth said.
If the US fails to hold them accountable for alleged conflicts of interest, “it would send a signal that powerful men once again cannot be held to account and that powerful men are protecting powerful men,” Haworth said.
Nvidia “lucky” to have Sacks
Detailing Sacks’ alleged conflicts, the group cited New York Times reporting that the former AI czar had long supported Huang’s stance that allowing Nvidia to sell more chips in China would help the US stay ahead in the AI race. After Sacks became Trump’s key AI advisor, Huang quickly forged a “tight bond” with him, and “both stood to benefit” from their push to sell chips to China, TOP reported.
Also notably, while advising the White House, Sacks opposed policies such as the Trump administration’s recent move to cut off China’s remote access to US-made chips through now-restricted Southeast Asian data centers. Citing Sacks’ alignment with Huang, TOP reported that after just one meeting with the two men, Trump decided to allow Nvidia to sell AI chips to China that the Biden administration had previously blocked.
Huang valued his alliance with Sacks, TOP noted, citing reporting that showed Huang declaring last year that Nvidia was “lucky” to have Sacks advising Trump. But TOP is concerned that the alliance was built on mutual financial interest and that Sacks took a part-time role in the Trump administration to avoid divestments or disclosure requirements that might have revealed the extent of his possible conflicts of interest.
TOP flagged two areas it believes warrant Congressional investigation. While advising Trump to embrace AI deregulation, Sacks and his firm, Craft Ventures, continued investing substantially in AI. Sacks also stood to benefit from pushing Trump to integrate AI into warfare and national security tools, TOP’s report said. Craft Ventures has invested in Palantir, “a Peter Thiel-founded government contractor seen as a ‘rising star’ in the US Defense Tech World and holding hundreds of millions in US government defense contracts,” TOP said.
Lutnick “benefited greatly”
Even within the Trump administration, officials have turned on Commerce Secretary Lutnick, seemingly looking to blame him for mishandling the Nvidia spying investigation and allowing Trump to maintain close ties with Huang despite apparent intelligence risks.
Lutnick has bragged publicly that he promised Huang “really easy access to the President” after joining the administration, TOP reported. That alliance helped push Trump to approve the sale of Nvidia H200s to China, TOP said. And that seemed to directly benefit Lutnick, TOP said, because before he was confirmed as secretary, he was CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, which held $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock.
“In his role as Secretary, Lutnick is responsible for policing exports of sensitive technology to adversaries and global rivals, like China,” TOP reported. “Lutnick and the company he controls benefited greatly from opening sales of Nvidia chips to China.”
After Lutnick was required to hand that company over to his son, Cantor Fitzgerald “maintained extensive commercial ties to Nvidia, helping arrange billions of dollars in financing for companies in its AI business universe and repeatedly hosting its top executives,” TOP noted.
Those investments shifted substantially around the same time that Lutnick began facing pressure to “crack down on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company suspected of funneling Nvidia’s advanced artificial intelligence chips to China,” TOP reported. Cantor Fitzgerald “reduced its Nvidia holdings by nearly 50 percent between September 2025 and March 2026,” TOP said.
However, when Trump was reportedly first told of the spying allegations this spring, Cantor Fitzgerald again continued to boost Nvidia. Most prominently, the company helped “finance the expansion of one of Nvidia’s newest business partners, IREN,” facilitating a five-year, $3.4 billion deal between Nvidia and the Australia-based cloud computing provider.
Among those now criticizing Lutnick for weak enforcement of export controls that appeared designed to protect Huang’s bottom line is Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. But even with scrutiny coming from within the Trump administration, not everyone is convinced that Lutnick did anything wrong. Yoon suggested that, given Lutnick’s long career, there may be normal explanations for potential financial conflicts.
“Maybe a separate question is ‘should people with a long storied history in business and industry be working in government at this level?’” Yoon said.
Probes may delay Huang’s return
Haworth said the next 48 hours will be critical in determining whether Huang succeeds in returning to Nvidia.
“I think it’s going to be incumbent on the incoming Democratic leadership to insist that whether or not he returns, investigations will follow,” Haworth said.
But Yoon thinks Nvidia is unlikely to bring Huang back any time soon, despite current evidence suggesting that “Nvidia’s actions here have been perfectly legal” and that “influencing a political system for your financial interests is very much legal in the United States.”
It seems “untenable for Nvidia to continue doing what they’re doing,” Yoon said. Zooming out even more, he suggested the scandal showed that the entire AI industry can no longer afford to operate under a profit motive alone, so long as governments continue positioning the technology as a strategic asset.
If US investigations expose corruption, bribery, treason, or other crimes, Nvidia risks losing some of its dominant stake in the GPU market. On Tuesday, The Information reported that some Nvidia customers had already lost trust and were looking to Google and AMD for more stability.
Nvidia has also been accused of intervening in a Commerce investigation, which Yoon said could also be “pretty consequential” if any evidence bears that out.
“I think it’s pretty unlikely that Huang makes it back to Nvidia any time soon,” Yoon said. “Maybe he goes on a redemption tour and comes back in five years or something, but I’m not really seeing a path forward for him right now.”
Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

articles.title: Apple outage hits iCloud, Apple Pay, and more [Update]
articles.text:
Update Nov. 17, 2026 at 3:28p.m. ET: In a statement to MobileSyrup, Apple said: “Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning. We’re working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible”
Apple is the latest company impacted by an outage amid a wild week of problems plaguing tech companies.
An Apple status page confirmed that several of the company’s services are impacted, including iCloud and iCloud Mail, AppleCare on Device, Apple School Manager, and Schoolwork. The status page also notes an issue with iCloud accounts and sign-in.
Further, the website Downdetector.ca showed spiking outage reports for iCloud and Apple Pay.
However, user reports on social media indicate the problem is more widespread. Some report problems with activating Apple products, signing in with Apple, App Store issues, Apple Music, and more.
Update Nov. 17, 2026, at 2:46 p.m. ET: In a statement to Bloomberg, Apple said “many” of its systems are running again, and blamed the outage on “an internal update.”
The Apple outage is the latest in a swath of recent outages, which included last week’s massive Microsoft outage, outages plaguing U.S. banks, and even an outage at the U.S. National Security Agency (NSA).
Both the Microsoft and banking outages were linked to software bugs, with the Microsoft one notably caused by a months-old bug that was triggered by a perfect storm of circumstances. While the outages don’t appear to be part of a cyberattack or related to artificial intelligence at this time, the sheer number of outages over the last week is certainly concerning.
And that’s not even getting into the huge malware attack we reported this morning or other ongoing security issues, like a recent breach of Canadian internet company Oxio.

articles.title: Waymo suspends freeway rides nationwide after California DMV order | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Waymo robotaxis are no longer allowed to operate on California freeways after the state’s Department of Motor Vehicles restricted the Alphabet-owned company’s operations following several incidents that raised safety concerns.
California’s DMV, which regulates the testing and deployment of autonomous vehicles in the state, issued the operational restrictions on Waymo on November 11. However, the restrictions weren’t made public until Tuesday. San Francisco Business Times was the first to report the order.
The DMV confirmed the new restrictions to TechCrunch, stating that the department took action after three Waymo autonomous vehicles entered an active construction closure on U.S. Route 101 near Burlingame, and another separate incident involving California Highway Patrol vehicles on Highway 280 in San Francisco.
Waymo has complied and is preventing its robotaxis from accessing freeways in any of the markets it operates in, including those outside of California. Waymo currently has commercial operations in 15 U.S. cities.
The DMV said Waymo’s freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety.
“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present, despite a prior restriction and corrective actions implemented following similar incidents that occurred on May 18, 2026,” according to an emailed statement sent to TechCrunch.
The DMV said the restrictions will remain in place until Waymo can demonstrate that it has taken “effective corrective actions” to address the deficiencies.
Waymo spokesperson Dana Gallagher told TechCrunch the company has temporarily restricted freeway operations across its other operating markets to evaluate its performance.
“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do,” Gallagher said in a statement. “Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”
Waymo began offering freeway rides in late 2025, a commercial milestone that has been central to its expansion in major metro areas. Freeway access allows Waymo to connect riders to airports and other destinations more efficiently, slashing travel times by avoiding slower surface streets.
That has been particularly important in the San Francisco Bay Area because Waymo’s service area stretches from the city south to Silicon Valley. Freeway access has dramatically shortened trips across the Peninsula that previously took 45 minutes or more than an hour.
In May, Waymo abruptly stopped operating on highways. The company didn’t cite a specific reason at the time, but several social media posts showed Waymo robotaxis driving through traffic cones and struggling to navigate construction zones.
Waymo robotaxis returned to freeways in July after the company said it updated the self-driving software system to improve performance around freeway construction zones.

articles.title: Japan’s most powerful supercomputer may have been hacked, over 4,000 users’ personal data stolen — investigation opened into Fugaku breach after unauthorized software installed
articles.text:
Japan’s most powerful supercomputer may have been hacked, over 4,000 users’ personal data stolen — investigation opened into Fugaku breach after unauthorized software installed
The Fugaku supercomputer, operated by the national research institute Riken, has been breached, with users' data, including names, emails, and more, stolen.
Fugaku, Japan's most powerful supercomputer and the ninth-fastest on the planet, has suffered a suspected data breach. The news was announced by its operator, Riken, which is the country's national research institute, with the outfit also confirming that personal information relating to more than 4,000 users of Fugaku was potentially taken during the breach. Further, the information of 375 users of Riken's Rikyu AI supercomputer was also possibly taken. The personal information includes names, email addresses, research files, and even the authentication information that was used to access the supercomputers and related services. The Japan Times reports that the operators of Fugaku first became aware of suspicious communications on November 12, with those suspicions then triggering an investigation.
By November 14, the investigation had confirmed that unauthorized access to Fugaku had taken place, with access also blocked at that time. The investigation identified that hackers had used the supercomputer's externally accessible operational status dashboard as the springboard for the hack between November 10 and November 13. Now taken offline while security concerns are addressed, the dashboard allowed the hackers to gain access to the system's internal network, but beyond that, details are scarce. Riken does not yet know — or at least, it isn't saying — the full story of how the hackers gained access to Fugaku as a whole. But it has confirmed that some servers had unauthorized software installed.
Following the discovery of the breach, Riken reported the incident to Japan's Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT). Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara has since confirmed that MEXT and Riken were working together to investigate what happened and ascertain the full scope of the breach itself. “Fugaku plays a vital role in our country’s research and development infrastructure, so it is important that they prioritize security while limiting the impact on research activities,” Kihara is reported to have said.
Located at Riken’s Center for Computational Science in Kobe, Fugaku officially came online in March of 2021 after being developed in collaboration with Fujitsu for a cost of around ¥130 billion (approximately $817 million in 2026). It became the world's fastest supercomputer before being overtaken by Frontier, an exascale supercomputer housed at the Department of Energy's Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility (OLCF) in Tennessee.
The fastest supercomputer currently in operation is China's LineShine. It recently retained its crown as the fastest on the planet amid a move away from traditional supercomputers to AI data centers.

articles.title: Nearly half of LinkedIn users would like to start their own business — with younger workers particularly keen
articles.text:
Nearly half of LinkedIn users would like to start their own business — with younger workers particularly keen
More younger people are starting businesses
- Gen Z and Millennials are among the most likely to start their own businesses
- More founders are becoming content creators on social media networks
- AI can help run your business, but human authenticity is sought-after by customers
Almost half (46%) of global respondents in a recent LinkedIn survey said they wanted to start their own business – a figure that grows to two in three (63%) Millennials and three in four (72%) Gen Z.
But aspirations aside, the social networking platform also revealed that one in two Gen Z even plan to l launch their business within the next three years, demonstrating that action is being taken to fulfill dreams.
Consequently, the platform has seen a 125% increase in the number of Founder profiles in the US since 2022 – or a 275% increase among US Gen Z respondents.
LinkedIn says more young people are starting their own businesses
LinkedIn thanked AI for lowering many barriers to entry, with 53% agreeing there are more opportunities to become an entrepreneur today than just five years ago. An overwhelming majority (92%) of small business owners now use AI, with benefits including faster launches (28%), launching with less capital (27%) and eliminating the need for a technical co-founder (27%).
But novel technologies aside, LinkedIn also says platforms like itself also play a role – 60% said social media makes it easier to find and reach customers where they are, and 42% noted that digital platforms have helped them to establish reputations.
Putting the two concepts together, LinkedIn also argues that professional networks have become more valuable as AI adoption has grown – something that four in five (78%) small business owners agreed with. Founders are especially fond of human networks when it comes to seeking peer advice on critical business decisions.
Entrepreneurs are increasingly turning to multiple revenue streams
The report found that 70% of SMB owners now have multiple revenue streams, which can often include one primary business and other smaller streams of revenue through consultancy or freelance work. Greater control and flexibility (47%) and higher earnings potential (41%) were among the biggest influencers for extra work.

Video is also continuing to see considerable growth, with 73% of founders now describing themselves as content creators, up from 59% in a study just six months earlier. This could be a consequence of an increasingly digital, AI-driven world, in which consumers are seeking more human connections. Three in four (77%) founders agree their personal brand directly contributes credibility to their business.
In other words, we're living in a business world where AI assistance and human authenticity not only can, but must, coexist.
"Our research shows the relationships you create, the reputation you build and the people you can turn to for advice become even more valuable as AI helps support the everyday mechanics of a business," Senior Director for Economic Research Sharat Raghavan explained.

articles.title: Le hacker de GTA 6 plaide coupable : il a bien piraté Rockstar Games en 2022
articles.text:
Le 18 septembre 2022, Rockstar Games était victime de l’une des fuites les plus importantes de l’histoire du jeu vidéo. Arion Kurtaj, alors âgé de 17 ans, a récupéré 90 séquences de gameplay. Arrêté et condamné depuis, il est repassé devant la justice pénale et pour la première fois, il a reconnu les faits.
Arion Kurtaj reconnaît enfin le piratage de Rockstar Games
Fin 2022, Arion Kurtaj, alors âgé de 17 ans, est impliqué dans les intrusions du groupe Lapsus$ contre Nvidia, BT/EE, Revolut. Il est arrêté et placé en détention provisoire, puis libéré sous caution dans l’attente de son procès. Une période durant laquelle il est hébergé dans un hôtel sous protection policière, puisque menacé par d’autres pirates à propos de bitcoins volés.
Privé d’ordinateur, Arion Kurtaj a utilisé un Amazon Fire Stick à l’arrière de la télévision de sa chambre, un clavier et une souris et a piraté Rockstar Games. Avec ce hack, il a récupéré 90 séquences de gameplay de GTA VI, accède au canal de communication interne de l’entreprise et menace de publier le code s’il n’est pas contacté. Faute de réponse, le jeune homme a diffusé toutes les vidéos et le code source sur un forum.
Sauf qu’il est repéré et devra rendre des comptes. En 2023 lors de son procès, les médecins ont estimé que la gravité de son autisme rendait Arion Kurtaj inapte à être jugé dans un procès pénal ordinaire. En décembre de la même année, le jury a conclu qu’Arion Kurtaj a bien commis ces actes et a prononcé une ordonnance d’hospitalisation sécurisée à durée indéterminée. Pour lui, le jeune hacker représentait toujours un danger ; il pourrait retomber dans le cybercrime.
Mais voilà, fin 2025, une évaluation médicale de routine l’a déclaré apte à être jugé. Une décision qui a entraîné son transfert d’un hôpital sécurisé vers une prison classique en janvier dernier. Ce changement de statut médical a permis l’ouverture d’une procédure pénale classique devant la Woolwich Crown Court. Le 16 novembre, Arion Kurtaj a enfin plaidé coupable pour l’ensemble des chefs d’accusation, dont le piratage de Rockstar Games, en plus des attaques contre Uber, BT/EE et Revolut.
Désormais âgé de 21 ans, le hacker recevra sa sentence le 23 novembre prochain selon plusieurs médias. Le tribunal devra déterminer la peine appropriée ; les préjudices causés s’élèveraient à 10 millions de livres sterling. À noter qu’Arion Kurtaj a commis des violences physiques en détention et avait réussi à s’y procurer un téléphone portable, ce qui est interdit.
Un traumatisme pour les développeurs de GTA VI (et pour les fans)
Ce nouveau procès s’est ouvert en marge de la sortie de GTA VI, le jeu vidéo le plus attendu de tous les temps qu’Arion Kurtaj avait fait fuiter en 2022. Face à l’ampleur de ce piratage et des séquences du jeu, Rockstar Games avait dû confirmer l’authenticité de ces extraits, tout en précisant que le jeu était encore en développement. L’éditeur ne prévoyait pas du tout de parler de GTA VI aussi tôt : la première bande-annonce n’est arrivée que le 5 décembre 2023, plus d’un an après la fuite.
L’entreprise a estimé le coût de cette attaque à environ 5 millions de dollars, ce qui comprend notamment des milliers d’heures de travail pour ses équipes. En effet, il a fallu analyser l’ampleur de la compromission, sécuriser les systèmes et surtout gérer les conséquences de la publication de ces extraits du jeu. Un traumatisme pour les développeurs du jeu, mais aussi pour les fans : beaucoup auraient préféré que ce soit le studio qui montre en premier le jeu, pour respecter son travail. Une blessure qui va s’atténuer avec l’excitation de la sortie du jeu ce jeudi 19 novembre, 13 ans après l’arrivée d’un certain GTA V.

articles.title: Sony releases new PS5 firmware as hackers set their sights on GTA VI
articles.text:
Grand Theft Hacking: Console makers have always played a dangerous game of cat and mouse with firmware hackers, and the stakes are even higher now that AI-assisted exploit development is becoming a reality. With the release of Grand Theft Auto VI fast approaching, Sony is working hard to patch every vulnerability it can find to keep hackers at bay.
Sony recently released a new system update for the PlayStation 5. Firmware version 26.07-14.23.00 includes only some vaguely described "security fixes" to the console's system. However, the timing of the release suggests that the new firmware could be intended to do more than simply patch a few unnamed vulnerabilities in the PS5's software.
The 26.07-14.23.00 update weighs in at more than 1GB and arrives just a couple of days before GTA VI is set to land on PS5 and Xbox consoles. The generation-defining crime adventure is expected to reinvigorate the entire gaming industry, but hackers could spoil the party by releasing a working pirated copy of the game in record time.
Fueled by the growing popularity of vibe coding and Sony's controversial stance toward physical gaming, crackers are now targeting the PS5 platform with unprecedented focus. The Relapse exploit provided a new avenue for jailbreaking PS5 consoles running firmware versions released before September 2026, while more recent firmware releases have proved somewhat harder to crack. Nevertheless, hackers are still finding ways to break through.
The new 26.07-14.23.00 firmware arrived just a day after the previous version, 14.22, following claims by a PS5 developer that they had dumped a game's binary using an undisclosed exploit on a console running that firmware. No conclusive evidence has emerged regarding the jailbreak status of version 14.22, but the PS5 piracy community continues to search for opportunities to breach Sony's DRM defenses.
We don't know whether GTA VI will require the latest firmware version to run on the PS5. The game's preload is now available, and Rockstar will likely continue updating its files until its November 19 launch. The 14.23 firmware could simply be Sony's attempt to block potential hacking attempts targeting one of the most important releases of the ninth console generation.
Either way, the industry is well aware that things are looking increasingly bleak for its traditional, closed-console business model.
Former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that creating a PC port of GTA VI through vibe coding would be difficult, but that people would try anyway. In a recent interview, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick acknowledged that combating piracy across the GTA franchise is becoming increasingly challenging. However, he believes the publisher will ultimately be able to "manage" the threat and turn GTA VI into another money-printing machine.

articles.title: Spara's Scout AI assistant acts on sales opportunities before reps know to look - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Spara’s Scout AI assistant acts on sales opportunities before reps know to look
Artificial intelligence sales agent startup Spara Inc. today introduced Scout, an AI assistant designed to act on sales opportunities before salespeople know to look for them.
Working around the clock, the new service analyzes context from customer conversations, emails and customer relationship management data to identify opportunities, prepare personalized outreach and complete work before reps realize it needs doing.
Scout is aimed at addressing a limitation of most AI assistants, which still require users to tell them what to do, according to Spara. The service instead works within the daily workflows of salespeople, providing an always-on partner that keeps track of customers and helps move work forward without constant direction.
Signals analyzed continuously by Scout include job changes, company news, buying signals and CRM activity across a salesperson’s accounts. From there, the service determines when to engage customers and prospects, as well as who to contact. Instead of requiring another platform to manage, Scout delivers its findings through Salesforce Inc.’s Slack and text messages.
Over time, Scout retains what it learns about each account, along with the salesperson’s preferences and previous outreach. Doing so is said to allow the service to anticipate next steps and deliver more relevant recommendations.
Outreach messages are drafted in the salesperson’s voice, with reps kept in control of what gets sent. Going beyond recommendations, Scout can join customer calls and contribute to conversations in real time, helping salespeople move opportunities forward.
“Sales has always been a game of speed, timing and relationships, but there’s only so much one person can keep track of in a day,” said David Walker, co-founder and chief executive of Spara. “Even the best sales organizations can’t realistically give every rep the support they need to act on every opportunity at exactly the right moment.”
Spara also released early results from users of the new service. Salespeople using Scout were found to have increased the number of personalized emails sent eightfold in their first two weeks of use. Outreach generated by Scout drew a 10.5% reply rate, against 3.5% for traditional sales sequences, according to the company. Early users also booked 29% more meetings.
Chris Brown, a partner at Spara investor Inspired Capital who has worked with the team since the beginning, said Spara has built agents that go-to-market teams trust with their most important customer conversations. Scout is now “putting that trust to work for individual sellers,” he added.
Scout is available for free starting today at spara.com/scout.
Founded by Walker and Zander Pease, Spara offers a platform for building AI agents that carry out sales work across chat, email, text messaging, voice and interactive product demos. The agents handle tasks ranging from engaging and qualifying leads to following up with prospects, booking meetings and managing renewals. Notable customers include Justworks Inc., Rho Technologies Inc. and Mindbody Inc.
Spara launched in September 2025 with $15 million in seed funding. Including additional funding since then, the company has raised $20 million to date, with Radical Ventures and Inspired Capital leading the seed round.
