articles.title: Monitor gamer IPS: 8 modelos para comprar em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Monitor gamer IPS: 8 modelos para comprar em 2026
Guia reúne telas IPS de 120 Hz a 300 Hz com baixo tempo de resposta e fidelidade de cor para jogos competitivos, campanhas imersivas e uso diário em 2026
Escolher um monitor gamer IPS em 2026 exige equilibrar taxa de atualização, tempo de resposta e precisão cromática de acordo com o perfil de jogo.
Os painéis IPS (In-Plane Switching) consolidaram-se como o padrão preferido para setups versáteis porque oferecem amplos ângulos de visão de 178° e cobertura de cores superior aos painéis TN e VA tradicionais, sem sacrificar a agilidade exigida em títulos competitivos.
Nesta lista, selecionamos 8 modelos disponíveis no mercado brasileiro que cobrem diferentes faixas de desempenho e orçamento, partindo de opções de entrada de 120 Hz até telas avançadas de 300 Hz com retroiluminação MiniLED e resolução Quad HD.
O TCL 25G64 eleva o patamar dos monitores competitivos ao combinar um painel IPS Full HD (1920 x 1080) de 25 polegadas com retroiluminação QD-MiniLED, taxa de atualização de 300 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms (GtG).
Essa combinação elimina rastros em movimentos bruscos de câmera em jogos de tiro em primeira pessoa (FPS), enquanto o controle local de iluminação proporciona pretos mais profundos e brilho máximo de 600 nits com certificação HDR600.
Para quem busca fidelidade visual além da velocidade, o modelo entrega profundidade de cor de 10 bits, cobertura de 96% do espectro DCI-P3 e calibração de fábrica com precisão Delta E menor que 2.
A conectividade inclui duas portas HDMI 2.1 e uma DisplayPort, acompanhadas de base ergonômica com ajuste de altura e compatibilidade com AMD FreeSync Premium.
Voltado para jogadores que priorizam definição de imagem sem abrir mão da fluidez, o AOC Agon Q27G4F traz tela Fast IPS de 27 polegadas com resolução Quad HD (2560 x 1440 pixels), taxa de atualização de 180 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms GtG (0,5 ms MPRT).
A maior densidade de pixels garante nitidez superior para identificar alvos a longa distância e amplia a área útil de trabalho no dia a dia. O painel cobre 120% do espaço de cores sRGB, conta com brilho típico de 300 cd/m² e suporte a HDR10, entregando tonalidades vibrantes em jogos de mundo aberto.
Compatível com NVIDIA G-SYNC e Adaptive Sync para evitar cortes na imagem (screen tearing), o modelo ainda se destaca pela base completa com ajustes de altura, inclinação, giro e rotação (pivô), além de entradas DisplayPort 1.4 e HDMI 2.0.
O Samsung Odyssey G40 de 25 polegadas é projetado especificamente para o cenário de eSports, operando com painel IPS Full HD, taxa de atualização nativa de 240 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms (GtG).
O formato compacto de 25 polegadas mantém toda a ação dentro do campo de visão periférico do jogador, permitindo reações imediatas em partidas ranqueadas de alto nível.
Com brilho típico de 400 cd/m² e suporte a FreeSync Premium e G-SYNC Compatible, o monitor mantém boa visibilidade mesmo em ambientes bastante iluminados e sincroniza os quadros da GPU sem engasgos.
O conjunto oferece duas entradas HDMI, uma DisplayPort e suporte ergonomicamente ajustável em altura, inclinação e modo retrato.
O Dell SE2426HG entrega especificações de nível competitivo em um chassi sóbrio de 24 polegadas, equipado com painel IPS Full HD de 240 Hz e tempo de resposta de 0,5 ms. Essa configuração garante transições de pixels limpas e baixa latência de entrada, atendendo jogadores de títulos competitivos que buscam alto desempenho com investimento controlado.
O modelo integra suporte a AMD FreeSync, compatibilidade com HDR10 e tecnologias de conforto visual, como tela antirreflexo, redução de luz azul e operação livre de cintilação (Flicker-Free). Conta ainda com conectividade DisplayPort 1.4, HDMI e furação padrão VESA 100 x 100 mm para instalação em braços articulados.
Posicionando-se acima do padrão tradicional de 144 Hz e 180 Hz, o AOC Agon 24G42HE apresenta tela IPS de 23,8 polegadas com resolução Full HD, taxa de atualização de 200 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms GtG (0,3 ms MPRT). O ganho extra de frequência proporciona rastreamento de alvos mais suave e resposta rápida aos comandos do mouse.
Com brilho de 300 cd/m², contraste estático de 1000:1 e cobertura de 116% do padrão sRGB, o painel reproduz cores vivas em jogos e conteúdos multimídia.
O monitor possui certificação NVIDIA G-SYNC Compatible, design sem bordas em três lados, entradas HDMI 2.0 e DisplayPort 1.4, além de ajuste de inclinação e suporte VESA.
O LG UltraGear 24GS60F-B equilibra velocidade e precisão cromática em um painel IPS de 24 polegadas (23,8 polegadas visíveis) com resolução Full HD, taxa de atualização de 180 Hz e tempo de resposta real de 1 ms (GtG). A combinação reduz o efeito fantasma (ghosting) em cenas rápidas sem comprometer a estabilidade das cores.
O display cobre 99% da gama sRGB, suporta HDR10 e oferece ampla compatibilidade com NVIDIA G-SYNC e AMD FreeSync. Entre os recursos voltados para jogos estão o Dynamic Action Sync (redução de atraso de entrada), o Black Stabilizer (clareamento de áreas escuras) e mira integrada na tela, conectados via HDMI 2.0 e DisplayPort 1.4.
Para quem prefere uma área de visualização maior mantendo a resolução Full HD, o LG UltraGear 27G411B traz tela IPS de 27 polegadas com taxa de atualização nativa de 144 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms com Motion Blur Reduction (5 ms GtG nativo).
O tamanho ampliado favorece a imersão em jogos de corrida, RPGs e consumo de vídeos, sem exigir uma placa de vídeo topo de linha para empurrar os quadros.
O painel apresenta contraste estático de 1500:1 — superior à média da categoria IPS —, cobertura de 99% sRGB, suporte a HDR10 e sincronização adaptativa via NVIDIA G-SYNC Compatible e AMD FreeSync.
A construção inclui bordas finas em três lados, entradas HDMI e DisplayPort, saída para fones de ouvido e padrão VESA 100 x 100 mm.
O Samsung Essential S3 LS24F320GALMZD é o modelo mais básico da lista, mas ainda usa painel IPS e resolução Full HD, se saindo melhor para jogos casuais, trabalho remoto e uso multimídia.
A taxa de atualização menor que a de modelos gamer avançados limita o apelo competitivo. Mesmo assim, recursos como FreeSync, baixo input lag e boa reprodução de cores ajudam em consoles, notebooks e PCs simples.
A indicação é para quem quer gastar pouco e evitar painéis de qualidade inferior. O Essential S3 funciona como monitor IPS de entrada para jogar ocasionalmente, estudar e montar um setup econômico em 2026.
A escolha do monitor gamer IPS ideal depende da potência da sua placa de vídeo (GPU), dos gêneros de jogos praticados e do espaço disponível na mesa. Antes de fechar a compra, avalie quatro critérios técnicos fundamentais:
Na faixa de entrada intermediária, modelos de 24 polegadas Full HD entre 180 Hz e 200 Hz, como o LG UltraGear 24GS60F-B e o AOC Agon 24G42HE, oferecem o equilíbrio mais eficiente entre preço e desempenho.
Ambos entregam painéis IPS rápidos de 1 ms GtG, boa cobertura de cores sRGB e sincronização adaptativa sem exigir placas de vídeo avançadas.
Para quem busca salto de resolução e ergonomia completa pagando menos que em modelos OLED, o AOC Agon Q27G4F (27″ QHD 180 Hz) destaca-se como a opção mais equilibrada da categoria intermediária.
A taxa de atualização ideal começa em 144 Hz para jogos competitivos. Esse patamar já oferece movimentos mais suaves que 60 Hz ou 75 Hz e melhora a resposta visual em partidas rápidas.
Monitores de 180 Hz são o ponto de equilíbrio em 2026, pois entregam fluidez alta sem exigir tanto quanto 240 Hz. Eles combinam bem com placas de vídeo intermediárias em Full HD.
Modelos de 240 Hz, como o Samsung Odyssey G40, fazem mais sentido para jogadores de e-sports. Para aproveitar a tela, o PC precisa manter taxas próximas em jogos como CS2, Valorant e Overwatch 2.
Os painéis IPS dominam o mercado de monitores gamer por equilibrarem velocidade e qualidade de imagem, mas apresentam limitações físicas inerentes à tecnologia LCD:
O monitor OLED entrega contraste praticamente infinito, pretos reais e tempo de resposta extremamente rápido. Em jogos HDR, terror e single-player cinematográfico, a imagem costuma ser superior à de um IPS tradicional.
O monitor IPS vence em preço, disponibilidade e menor risco de burn-in. Para uso prolongado com HUD fixo, planilhas, navegador e barra de tarefas, ele tende a ser uma escolha mais tranquila.
Em 2026, OLED é a opção premium para quem busca qualidade máxima. IPS continua sendo a melhor compra racional para a maioria, especialmente em monitores Full HD e QHD com 144 Hz a 240 Hz.
O monitor IPS é melhor para quem prioriza cores, ângulo de visão e resposta mais previsível em jogos rápidos. Nossa equipe prefere IPS para FPS competitivo, uso misto e setups com duas telas.
Já o monitor VA oferece contraste maior, com pretos mais profundos e imagem forte em filmes ou jogos escuros. Porém, alguns modelos podem apresentar ghosting em transições rápidas, especialmente em cenas com tons escuros.
A escolha depende do perfil do jogador. Para e-sports e versatilidade, IPS é mais seguro; para imersão, contraste e consumo de mídia, VA pode agradar mais se o modelo tiver boa resposta.

articles.title: Lapsus$ hacker pleads guilty to breaching Rockstar and leaking GTA 6 footage from a hotel TV
articles.text:
What just happened? Four years ago, Arion Kurtaj hacked into Rockstar Games using an Amazon Fire Stick, a hotel television, and a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, stealing footage of the unreleased Grand Theft Auto 6. This week, the 21-year-old from Oxford pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the breach, as well as several other cyber attacks he carried out at the ages of 16 and 17 as a member of the hacking group Lapsus$.
The plea follows an unusual legal process: Kurtaj was initially committed to a secure hospital but was later deemed fit to stand trial.
When he targeted Rockstar, Kurtaj was already on bail for other hacking offences. Police had seized his computer and placed him in a Travelodge in Bicester. The move was intended to protect him from rival hackers who had threatened to attack him over his stolen Bitcoin.
The hotel room did little to stop him. Kurtaj plugged a Fire Stick, a consumer device used to stream video, into the room's television. He then connected a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse and used the setup to access Rockstar's internal systems.
He stole internal company data, including 90 clips showing nearly an hour of gameplay from the unfinished title. He also accessed Rockstar's internal Slack messaging system and posted a demand: "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code."
Rockstar did not respond. Kurtaj subsequently posted the clips and source code on a forum under the name TeaPotUberHacker. The company said the breach cost $5 million to address and required thousands of hours of staff time. The leak also revealed something Rockstar had been keeping under wraps for marketing reasons: one of the game's playable characters is a woman.
Rockstar was not his only target. Kurtaj also admitted to hacking BT/EE, Revolut and Uber. In those cases, he used social engineering – manipulating people rather than exploiting software vulnerabilities – to gain access to internal systems. During the Uber attack, the court heard, he posted a picture of a penis in an attempt to pressure the company into paying a ransom.
The financial damage across the companies is estimated at approximately £10 million. Kurtaj and other Lapsus$ members also used stolen corporate data to target cryptocurrency investors. Prosecutors said the group stole at least $300,000 from individual victims.
The road to this week's guilty plea was a long one. When the case first came before the court in 2023, doctors found that Kurtaj's autism was too severe for him to participate in a conventional criminal trial. The court instead held a trial of the facts, in which the jury determines whether the defendant carried out the alleged acts, rather than whether he had the criminal intent required for a conviction. In December 2023, the court ordered that he remain in a secure hospital indefinitely, unless doctors determined that he was no longer a danger.
A routine assessment late last year reversed that decision, finding him fit to face a criminal trial. He was transferred to a conventional prison in January, and a trial was scheduled at Woolwich Crown Court. He ultimately pleaded guilty to every count.
In the dock, Kurtaj had short hair and an unkempt beard. He wore a suit and a white shirt buttoned to the collar, without a tie. He blinked frequently during the hearing, stood to confirm his name and entered his pleas without showing any emotion.
The charges also covered his conduct in custody. He pleaded guilty to physically assaulting prison workers, including several biting incidents. He was also caught with a mobile phone in prison after sending police a taunting text message and posting updates on Snapchat. He will be sentenced at a later date.

articles.title: Announcing AI data preparation capabilities in Amazon SageMaker: Build high-quality datasets for model development workflows | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Announcing AI data preparation capabilities in Amazon SageMaker: Build high-quality datasets for model development workflows
Teams that ship generative AI to production know that a model is only as good as its data. That is why preparing high-quality training and evaluation data comes first. Fine-tuning an open-weight model, running reinforcement learning, or building an evaluation suite all depend on data that is accurate, well-labeled, and representative of your task. For narrow, well-defined tasks, a smaller model customized on clean, task-specific data can often match or exceed the accuracy of a larger general-purpose model prompted into shape, at a lower cost per inference.
In practice, though, preparing that data is often the slowest part of the project. Labeled examples are scarce or expensive, and privacy rules limit what you can use. Quality problems such as duplicates, label noise, and answer leakage go unnoticed until a training run disappoints, and every training technique expects data in its own format. As a result, data scientists spend weeks wrangling data instead of building models.
Today, we’re expanding Amazon SageMaker AI with new AI data preparation capabilities for model development workflows. You can generate synthetic examples, assess and improve existing datasets, and bring expert feedback into the process through Python SDK APIs and the AWS AI-ML agent skill. You work in your notebook or IDE, with specifications and code that you can inspect and change.
Prepare data without hand-building pipelines
With AI Data Preparation capabilities, you don’t need to stitch together labeling tools, generation scripts, and validation jobs. Each capability is a standalone building block. You can use one of them on its own or chain them together according to the workflow you want.
- Auto-labeling: Label data at scale from an unlabeled dataset, a small labeled seed set, or no labels at all. Built-in task types include classification, named entity recognition, extractive question answering, ordinal rating, and summarization, and you can define custom tasks. You describe the task in a short labeling spec, which is validated against your own examples before the full dataset is labeled. For tasks with a fixed set of possible answers, such as classification, named entity recognition, and extractive question answering, a jury of several models labels each row, and their level of agreement becomes that row’s confidence score.
- Human review: Rows below your confidence threshold go to a review queue in Amazon SageMaker Studio, which uses the open-source Label Studio Community Edition. Outside subject matter experts can access the review app through the link in the partner app box in SageMaker Studio. Reviewer corrections feed back into auto-labeling, and you can generate consensus metrics and labeling reports.
- Synthetic data generation: Generate training, evaluation, and test data from a specification. You can ground the output in your own seed data and documents, and the service generates a code-based data generation pipeline that you can review, modify, reuse, and scale.
- Data quality evaluation: Check datasets against your own business rules, built-in metrics, and LLM-as-a-judge metrics. Find duplicates and near-duplicates, and surface issues you didn’t think to check for, such as label noise or answer leakage.
- Data transformation: Clean and reshape data for your target training technique. Describe the change in plain language and have the code generated for you, use built-in operations such as dedupe, merge, split, and filter, or run your own Python at scale.
You work wherever you already work. Use the SageMaker Python SDK directly or provide your coding agent the AI-ML skill in the agent toolkit and let your agent invoke the APIs according to established data science best practices. Describe what you need, and the agent selects and runs the right capability in SageMaker Studio JupyterLab, Kiro, or your local IDE with your coding assistant of choice.
For teams building specialized models, the hardest part is often finding enough task-specific data. Splunk, a Cisco company, faced exactly this when building evaluation models for its Agent Observability product.
        “For Splunk Agent Observability, our ability to train robust GenAI Eval models relies on access to high-quality, diverse datasets which are hard to curate for very specific tasks. Amazon SageMaker AI data preparation capabilities for synthetic data generation is meaningfully helping us scale these capabilities. We’ve been able to generate statistically representative synthetic datasets reliably and fast, while preserving the underlying patterns our models depend on. The seamless integration with the rest of our SageMaker workflow means our data scientists and customers spend less time wrangling data and more time building models that drive real enterprise value through Splunk.”
— Yash Sheth, Director of Engineering, Splunk Agent Observability
Chain capabilities from raw data to training
The value grows when you combine the capabilities. Some common patterns:
Build a golden evaluation dataset: Auto-label your raw data from a small seed set. High-confidence rows are accepted automatically, and low-confidence rows go to human reviewers. Their corrections improve the next labeling pass, resulting in a trusted, human-validated dataset to benchmark your models against.
Go from raw documents to a trained model in one workflow:
- Generate data: Synthetic data generation creates task-specific examples grounded in your documents and seed data.
- Transform it: Data transformation reshapes the data into the format your training technique expects, such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT), direct preference optimization (DPO), or reinforcement learning (RL).
- Validate it: Data quality evaluation checks the dataset for duplicates, leakage, and rule violations before you spend compute on training.
- Train: Train with SageMaker AI model customization.
How it works
Consider a team preparing data to evaluate agentic customer support assistants. Its product guide says that a factory reset erases saved settings. The team wants to test whether the assistant preserves that warning when answering reset questions.
One pass through the preparation workflow looks like this:
- Define the requirements: Supply the product guide as context and describe the questions and reference answers you need. Include the requirement that answers about a factory reset preserve the warning about saved settings. Review the specification produced with your coding agent.
- Generate and inspect a sample: Generate a small batch and check the records against the guide. Review the generation and check the code. Confirm that the examples cover the intended questions and that the reference answers follow the source material.
- Assess and review: Run a data quality assessment and inspect the record-level findings. Ask a subject matter expert to review ambiguous answers or disputed assessments. Use the results and annotations to request improvement recommendations.
- Apply changes and repeat: Revise the specification if the requirements need clarification or transform the dataset to address issues such as duplicates. Generate additional examples where needed, then reassess the revised dataset before using it to evaluate the assistant.
This example workflow illustrates how the capabilities fit together.
Keep control of your preparation workflow and data
With the AI-ML skill, you describe the task in natural language while your coding agent helps build specifications, prepare code, and coordinate the data preparation steps. You can open those artifacts to see how the workflow is configured and make changes directly.
If you prefer to invoke the APIs yourself, use the Python SDK APIs to call individual capabilities from your own code. The SDK APIs take a specification as input, so we recommend creating it with the help of an agent. You can add quality assessment to an existing process, generate data for a new task, or combine several operations. You choose the preparation steps your project needs and how they fit into your model customization and evaluation processes.
AI Data Preparation runs with an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) execution role that you control. Your source data, generated datasets, and labels stay in your own Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) buckets, in the AWS Region you choose.
Get started today
The AI data preparation capabilities are generally available in the US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon) Regions.
There are two ways to get started:
- With your coding agent – Set up the data preparation skills in your supported notebook or IDE. Describe one training or evaluation task and review the resulting specification before generating a sample.
- With Python – Use the SageMaker Python SDK directly to run individual data preparation capabilities from your own code. The SDK takes a specification as input, so we recommend creating your specifications with the AI-ML skill first, then using the SDK to run them in your workflow.
For more information, see the Amazon SageMaker AI documentation.

articles.title: Apple services, including iCloud, App Store, Apple Music, and more, hit by outage | TechCrunch
articles.text:
After a recent slew of tech outages, service disruptions, and flight chaos this week, now it’s Apple customers who are facing technical issues.
The iPhone maker’s System Status page indicates that there are issues with iCloud’s Account & Sign In services affecting “all users,” which could make the service slow or unavailable. The App Store, AppleCare on Device, and Apple Music are also experiencing issues, the page indicates.
Like all major tech companies, Apple faces outages and other technical issues affecting its cloud services at times. However, today’s issues are likely more noticeable to end users because problems with iCloud can lead to account sign-in problems. This could cause your iPhone to ask for your Apple ID and password, and you could see other attempts to sign in to services with your Apple account information fail.
On Reddit, some folks also noted that they were unable to activate a new iPhone, which is likely related to these ongoing issues.
Given the recent increase in AI-driven cyberattacks, users across social media have already begun to speculate about the cause. In particular, users are expressing concerns about the Apple outage, as it arrives only days after technical failures at Microsoft led to its cloud systems that power flagship services like Outlook and Teams failing due to cascading software issues.
Similarly, a brief outage of Chase’s banking app this week garnered attention, as did an ongoing partial outage (at the time of publication) of the National Security Agency’s internal classified network, both of which were blamed on software glitches.
So far, none of the outages in the past week have been attributed to cyberattacks, but rather to technical problems.
Apple responded to TechCrunch’s request for comment (which it initially gave to Bloomberg), noting that the outages were caused by an internal update and not a cyberattack. “Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning. We’re working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible,” the statement read.
After the initial outages were reported, Apple’s status page was updated to include other outages impacting Apple School Manager, iCloud Mail, iCloud Web Apps (iCloud.com), Schoolwork, and the Volume Purchase Program.
This article was updated after publication with the status of the outages.

articles.title: OpenAI sued by California after admitting to 80 loss-of-control incidents
articles.text:
California sued OpenAI yesterday, alleging it has tried to evade responsibility for the Hugging Face attack and about 80 other incidents in which the company lost control of its AI. The lawsuit was filed under the state’s public nuisance and unfair competition laws.
The July 2026 hack of Hugging Face and other attacks carried out by OpenAI’s autonomous agents “may just be the tip of the iceberg,” said a lawsuit filed in a state court by California Attorney General Rob Bonta. “OpenAI recently admitted to the Attorney General’s Office that it has lost control of its autonomous AI agents over 80 times during testing.”
OpenAI had publicly reported only 27 such incidents, showing that “OpenAI’s public reports do not represent the full scope of loss-of-control incidents involving OpenAI’s models that have impacted third parties,” the lawsuit said. OpenAI “knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it,” Bonta said in a press release.
OpenAI models are “able to find novel vulnerabilities in computer networks, quickly break down defenses, and autonomously carry out cyberattacks,” Bonta’s lawsuit said. OpenAI puts safeguards in its publicly released models to prevent this behavior, “but deliberately omits or removes these protections while experimenting with and training its models,” the lawsuit said.
In the attack on Hugging Face, OpenAI agents “employed complicated hacking methodologies and involved coordinated actions by hundreds of individual autonomous AI agents that should have been contained in OpenAI’s research environment,” the lawsuit said.
Known attacks “include unauthorized access of and cyberattacks on databases containing code that powers countless applications; informational websites that are trusted and valuable resources for the public; and foreign government databases storing sensitive health information,” the lawsuit said. “Swarms of OpenAI’s experimental AI agents have even compromised OpenAI’s own internal infrastructure, in an attack that managed to obtain administrator-level access to critical OpenAI systems.”

articles.title: Big malware attack hits Zoom, BBC, CNN and many more: report
articles.text:
A massive malware attack has reportedly hit over 170 sites around the world.
According to Report URI, a company that sells malicious script detectors, sites like Zoom, BBC, CNN, Ikea, Salesforce and many more were found to be carrying infected JavaScript. Two Canadian-specific sites, Starbucks Canada and Equifax Canada, are also said to be affected.
Per Report URI, this malicious script is capable of a range of dangerous actions, including targeting users’ addresses and card numbers and, on mobile, exploiting kits.
This is a big one.
We found malicious JavaScript being served through Optimizely to some of the world’s largest websites.
178 organisations affected, with everything from crypto theft and card skimming to iOS exploits.
Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, IKEA, Equifax, Ledger. The list goes on… Full list in the post.
https://t.co/f8iiN3nrZ7
— Scott Helme (@Scott_Helme) November 16, 2026
Report URI says this came through the AI-powered Optimizely Web experimentation platform, while threat intelligence firm Mallory found other causes, including Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly. An Optimizely spokesperson told Gizmodo it identified a security incident, deployed a fix and notified affected customers accordingly.
If you happened to visit any of these sites recently, you may want to update your device and monitor your bank records just in case there’s any unusual activity. The original Report URI story also has a full list of each affected site broken down by category.

articles.title: Apple vuelve al centro de la polémica por un inesperado problema del iPhone Duo
articles.text:
Apple ha sido señalada de intentar silenciar a un proveedor en plena crisis del iPhone Duo. Un reporte afirma que los de Cupertino enfrentan acusaciones de presionar a uno de sus proveedores para que retirara una declaración pública relacionada con el plegable. Hace unas semanas, Apple reconoció que hay problemas con algunas pantallas del iPhone Duo, pero no quiere que nadie de la cadena de producción se pronuncie sobre el asunto.
Según informa MacRumors, Fine M-Tec, la empresa que fabrica las placas metálicas que se utilizan en la estructura del iPhone Duo, publicó un comunicado a finales de octubre. Si hacemos memoria, en ese tiempo comenzaron a surgir reportes sobre pantallas que se abultaban y se rompían, las cuales se volvieron virales en cuestión de minutos. Algunos expertos apuntaban a que el problema se encontraba en uno de los componentes de la bisagra, por lo que Fine M-Tec decidió dar la cara.
"Los problemas de calidad conocidos que han ocurrido recientemente en algunos productos no están causados por defectos en las piezas que suministramos", mencionó la compañía en un comunicado en su web. Fine M-Tech nunca mencionó a Apple o el iPhone Duo, aunque advirtió que podría ejercer acciones legales contra quienes difundieran información falsa sobre sus componentes.
En esa semana, Apple publicó otro comunicado en donde aceptó que había fallos en un número limitado de unidades del iPhone Duo y se comprometió a resolverlos. La tecnológica también habría metido presión al proveedor surcoreano por hablar de más.
El fallo de pantalla que persigue al iPhone Duo
En una columna publicada en The Elec, el periodista Kim Geon reveló que un representante de Fine M-Tec se puso en contacto con él para pedirle que eliminara un artículo relacionado con las declaraciones de la compañía. Según el reporte, Apple consideró inapropiado que su proveedor negara públicamente su responsabilidad en el crackgate. "Tú no tienes problemas, pero nosotros sí", dijo el representante a Geon, refiriéndose a lo que podría pasar si se mantenían en línea estos artículos.
Si bien Apple no ha confirmado que pidió a su proveedor que eliminara las declaraciones, la acción no sorprende a nadie. La tecnológica ya había aceptado que había problemas con la pantalla del Duo, pero minimizó el hecho y no habló sobre las causas. Es probable que Apple, en su intento por controlar la información, llamara a sus proveedores para que cerraran la boca.
El crackgate ha sido uno de los fallos más notables del iPhone desde el Antennagate que vimos en el iPhone 4. Los primeros casos aparecieron a los pocos días del lanzamiento del pegable, en donde usuarios de distintos países reportaron grietas en la pantalla, casi siempre alrededor de la zona de la bisagra. En la mayoría de los casos, el daño estaba acompañado por líneas de píxeles brillantes o fallos que inutilizaban parcialmente el panel.
“Somos conscientes de un problema que afecta a la pantalla interna de un pequeño número de unidades iPhone Duo. Si los usuarios experimentan problemas con la pantalla de su iPhone Duo, deberían contactar con AppleCare para solicitar un reemplazo”, dijo Apple en su momento. La compañía confirmó que investigarían el origen del fallo, recopilando los móviles dañados para entender qué ocurría.

articles.title: Ask Maps: Wie du via Google Maps jetzt auch Termine buchen kannst
articles.text:
Mit neuen KI-Funktionen: So will Google Maps den Planungsstress auf Reisen reduzieren
Kurz vor Weihnachten sind die Deutschen so viel unterwegs wie zu kaum einer anderen Zeit im Jahr. Auf den Straßen führen Staus zu Verzögerungen, und auch Busse und Bahnen sind so voll wie nie. Laut einer repräsentativen Umfrage des ADAC Südbayern zum Mobilitätsverhalten in der Weihnachtszeit besuchten im vergangenen Jahr 43 Prozent der Deutschen Verwandte oder Freund:innen. Am häufigsten reisten die 18- bis 29-Jährigen. Google Maps will diesem Reisestress jetzt etwas entgegensetzen und weitet die neue „Ask Maps“-Funktion auf weitere Länder aus. Sie soll unter anderem dabei helfen, Reiserouten zu erstellen und freie Termine zu finden.
Google Maps bekommt agentische Funktionen
Google Maps ist die mit Abstand beliebteste App zum Routenplanen – in Deutschland wie international. Laut Angaben des Tech-Konzerns verwenden sie mehr als zwei Milliarden Menschen pro Monat. Im Jahr 2024 sollen Nutzer:innen eine Billion Routenkilometer geplant haben. Zusätzlich sind 250 Millionen Geschäfte und Orte eingezeichnet, die direkt in der App Informationen zu ihrem Angebot, ihren Preisen und ihren verfügbaren Terminen bereitstellen. Mit der Funktion „Ask Maps” können Nutzer:innen jetzt detaillierte Reisepläne erstellen und Echtzeit-Informationen zur Route erhalten. Das soll unter anderem dabei helfen, den anstehenden Weihnachtseinkauf zu machen. Aber auch größere Trips sollen mit der neuen Funktion planbar sein.
„Du erhältst einen Tagesplan mit Insidertipps und nummerierten Markierungen auf der Karte für jeden Halt, sodass du dir den Plan leicht vorstellen kannst“, heißt es in einem Google-Blogbeitrag. Sobald Nutzer:innen mit einem Reiseplan zufrieden sind, können sie diesen auch mit anderen Personen teilen. Bevor sie losfahren, rufen sie die App auf und wählen ihren Reiseplan aus. Er liefert Informationen zu Parkmöglichkeiten oder Ladestationen sowie Echtzeitdaten zu Wetter, möglichen Verzögerungen und Mautgebühren. Sogar die Stimmung am nächsten geplanten Stopp soll angezeigt werden. Unterwegs können Nutzer:innen den Zeitplan auch spontan anpassen und beispielsweise einen Aussichtspunkt oder ein Restaurant für das Mittagessen auf dem Weg hinzufügen.
„Ask Maps“ jetzt auch in Deutschland verfügbar
Die agentischen Funktionen von „Ask Maps“ sollen besonders nützlich sein. Nutzer:innen können damit online Termine für Kosmetik, Tierpflege oder Autoreparaturen vereinbaren. Im Google-Blogbeitrag wird erklärt, wie die App beispielsweise mit dem Befehl „Finde für mich einen Termin für eine Maniküre um 16 Uhr in meiner Nähe“ genutzt werden kann. Die Funktion soll daraufhin freie Termine bei Salons im Umkreis anzeigen, sodass Nutzer:innen schnell entscheiden können, wo sie buchen möchten. Der Google-Maps-Agent soll sogar in der Lage sein, lokale Unternehmen direkt anzurufen. Auch Restaurantreservierungen sind möglich. Dafür greift der Maps-Agent auf bestehende Listen mit Lieblingsrestaurants zu und prüft automatisch die Verfügbarkeiten.
Die Funktion war seit März 2026 in den USA und in Indien auf Android- und iOS-Geräten verfügbar. Jetzt weitet Google das Feature auf weitere Regionen aus, darunter auch Deutschland. Reisepläne und die Listensuche sollen jetzt in mehr als 200 Ländern und Regionen verfügbar sein. Nützliche Routentipps sowie die Suche nach Terminen führt Google zunächst testweise in den USA ein. Weitere Regionen sollen in Kürze folgen. Der Veröffentlichungszeitpunkt ist nicht zufällig gewählt: Google hofft, dass viele die App verwenden, um ihre Weihnachtseinkäufe zu planen. Auch sollen Nutzer:innen die neuen Funktionen verwenden, um pünktlich an Heiligabend mit ihrer Familie unter dem Weihnachtsbaum sitzen können.

articles.title: 3 enterprise AI infrastructure insights - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Three insights you might have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of Dell’s “AI Leadership Symposium”
Moving enterprise AI workloads into production introduces practical challenges for chief information officers. Those challenges include managing costs, scaling enterprise AI infrastructure and establishing governance models to keep agents in check and data secure.
Cost and control were major themes of discussion at Dell Technologies Inc.’s “AI Leadership Symposium.” Expanding AI workloads can drive up infrastructure and model costs, while deploying autonomous agents introduces new questions about security, oversight and data access.
At the same time, organizations are exploring different ways to run AI, from private cloud environments to models operating directly on devices. That is creating demand for enterprise AI infrastructure and partnerships that can accommodate a wider range of deployment needs.
“No one is asking whether to adopt AI; that’s pretty much a done deal,” said John Furrier, executive analyst at theCUBE Research. “They’re asking who controls it, where it runs and whose law it operates.”
Furrier spoke with industry experts from Dell, Deepgram Inc., Singulr AI Inc., MisaLabs Inc. and Intel Corp., among others, during the AI Leadership Symposium. The interviews covered the infrastructure, partnerships and computing power needed to scale AI. (* Disclosure below.)
Here’s theCUBE’s complete keynote analysis from John Furrier:
Insight #1: Token costs push enterprises to rethink AI budgets.
Cloud token bills remain a major pressure point on enterprise AI budgets. That’s leading some businesses to look for ways to relieve that pressure, according to Helen O’Sullivan, AI business development manager and solutions specialist at Dell.
“A lot of our customers I support in the Bay Area, they’re dealing with this real immediate struggle of running through their token budget in a matter of weeks that they had allotted for months,” she told theCUBE. “You still use those frontier models, but you use the open source and infrastructure on-prem to at least eliminate some of the token stress and token maxing going on right now.”
Organizations can also make better use of existing data center capacity when evaluating enterprise AI infrastructure investments. Dell and Intel are helping customers evaluate those options, according to Tim Wood, sales director for the Northwest region at Intel, who joined O’Sullivan during the discussion.
“A lot of enterprises already have [central processing units] in their data center,” he said. “There may be existing resources and headroom in the infrastructure they already have that’s capable of doing some of these next-generation apps and workloads.”
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video interview with Helen O’Sullivan and Tim Wood:
Insight #2: Speed raises the stakes for AI agent governance and security.
As companies deploy more AI agents, they need better ways to monitor what those agents actually do and ensure their actions align with company policies and intentions. That means introducing runtime governance that can assess AI agent behavior during execution, according to Shiv Agarwal, co-founder and chief executive officer of Singulr AI Inc., who spoke alongside Sri Viswanath, founder and chief executive officer of Sycamore Labs Inc., and Victor Jakubiuk, co-founder of MisaLabs Inc.
“[It’s] as simple as an action where it reaches out to the internet to get some data or sends out an email to a private account or something,” Agarwal told theCUBE. “That could be deeply hidden inside an agentic action.”
Good AI governance also means setting boundaries around where models can access data and how they process it. CIOs often prefer virtual private clouds to keep sensitive information within a controlled environment, according to Viswanath.
“They’re also trying to architect in a way that all of the data stays there,” he said. “They don’t trust sending it outside because then we don’t know where it goes.”
The pace of AI development complicates those governance efforts. Companies need to ensure their systems behave as intended even as AI capabilities evolve, according to Jakubiuk.
“AI has no limit to the speed of development, speed of progress,” he said. “As an enterprise, as that AI lead, you want to be able to take the latest and greatest and stay on top.”
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video interview with Victor Jakubiuk, Shiv Agarwal and Sri Viswanath:
Insight #3: Silicon Valley’s build-it-yourself culture reshapes enterprise AI infrastructure.
Deepgram is working with Dell and Fortanix Inc. to bring its voice AI models beyond the cloud and onto customer devices. Potential applications range from interactive voice response systems for small businesses to AI-enabled laptops for students, according to Nick Mann, staff technical program manager at Deepgram.

“For us, that notion of ecosystem is starting to change,” he told theCUBE. “Today we’re here with Intel [Corp.], we’re here with SHI [International Corp.], we’re here with Microsoft [Corp.]. But that ecosystem also now is starting to bleed into private equity and venture capital.”

articles.title: Google to keep Gemini chats for 2 months, up from 72 hours, even with history off | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google is extending how long it keeps temporary Gemini chats and conversations made with chat history turned off to around two months, saying the change aims to improve safety and security as AI systems become more capable.
The change, which will roll out globally in the Gemini app over the coming weeks, marks a significant increase from the previous 72-hour retention period mentioned in Google’s Gemini Apps Privacy Hub, according to an archived version from November 12.
OpenAI, by comparison, says it may keep temporary chats in ChatGPT for up to 30 days, whereas Anthropic retains incognito chats in Claude for 30 days by default. However, companies may keep some data longer for legal or safety reasons, or to investigate policy violations.
Google did not answer questions about what prompted the change and whether it would affect how conversations are accessed or reviewed, instead pointing to a blog post that says chats are kept longer to respond to users, process feedback, and protect its services and users. Its updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub also cites potential system failures as a reason for retaining chats and says temporary conversations are not used to train AI models.
The longer retention period comes as Google introduces separate settings for Gemini’s chat history and AI training. Until now, both were tied to a single “Keep Activity” setting. Users will now be able to keep their conversations in their chat history without using them to train Google’s generative AI models.
Google says both new settings will be turned off by default for users who previously disabled Keep Activity. For those who had Keep Activity turned on, their chat history will remain enabled. They can, though, decide separately whether Google can use their conversations to train AI models.

articles.title: Home Assistant lance un boîtier à 59 € pour connecter vos anciens appareils plutôt que les remplacer
articles.text:
Nabu Casa dévoile le Connect AUX-2, un boîtier capable de raccorder des équipements audio, des téléviseurs ou certains systèmes de chauffage à Home Assistant. Vendu 59 €, il mise sur leurs connexions existantes pour leur ajouter des fonctions domotiques, sous réserve de compatibilité.
Un amplificateur qui sonne toujours aussi bien, un téléviseur parfaitement fonctionnel, mais une application abandonnée ou aucune fonction connectée : faut-il vraiment tout remplacer ? Avec le Connect AUX-2, Home Assistant propose de conserver le matériel et de revoir sa façon de communiquer. Le petit boîtier ne rendra pas chaque appareil intelligent par magie, mais ses différentes prises lui ouvrent plusieurs portes dans la maison.
De la chaîne hi-fi au chauffage, plusieurs façons de reprendre la main
Nabu Casa présente un accessoire qui combine diffusion musicale, commandes filaires et relais pour les équipements domotiques.
Pour l’audio, le Connect AUX-2 reçoit la musique par le réseau, puis l’envoie vers un amplificateur ou des enceintes actives grâce à une sortie analogique ou optique. Music Assistant permet de réunir fichiers locaux et services de streaming, mais aussi de synchroniser la lecture avec d’autres enceintes compatibles. Une installation hi-fi ancienne peut ainsi rejoindre un système multiroom.
Ses deux ports série RS-232 servent, eux, à transmettre des commandes aux appareils compatibles. Sur un amplificateur, cela peut permettre de gérer l’allumage, le volume ou la source. Certains téléviseurs, équipements de chauffage et onduleurs solaires disposent également d’une connexion exploitable. Un adaptateur USB supplémentaire permet d’étendre les possibilités au RS-485, notamment pour des équipements Modbus.
Le boîtier fait aussi office de relais Bluetooth pour les accessoires domotiques. Enfin, son port USB peut accueillir un adaptateur Z-Wave, vendu séparément, afin de l’installer à un meilleur endroit que celui où se trouve le serveur Home Assistant.
Un accessoire polyvalent, à condition de vérifier ses appareils
Pour utiliser cet appareil, il n’existe qu’une condition indispensable : le Connect AUX-2 nécessite une installation Home Assistant en version 2026.9 ou ultérieure. Il complète donc le système domotique, sans remplacer la machine qui l’héberge. La plateforme poursuit ainsi son développement matériel, parallèlement aux évolutions de son interface et de l’organisation des appareils.
La présence d’un port série ne suffit pas non plus : l’équipement doit disposer d’une intégration compatible. Côté audio, le boîtier n’amplifie pas le son et ne transmet ni ne reçoit de musique en Bluetooth. Le Thread n’est pas pris en charge, tandis que l’utilisation d’un adaptateur Zigbee reste encore peu éprouvée.
Pour l’installation, on peut choisir le Wi-Fi avec une alimentation USB-C, ou l’Ethernet. Avec un équipement réseau PoE, un seul câble assure la connexion et l’alimentation.
Le Connect AUX-2 est référencé à 59 € TTC, avec une disponibilité dépendante des réapprovisionnements. Les câbles audio et série sont, quant à eux, à acheter séparément. Avant de commander, mieux vaut commencer par regarder derrière les appareils que l’on souhaite conserver.
- Contrôle centralisé des appareils connectés.
- Automatisations intelligentes basées sur les routines.
- Intégration transparente avec de nombreuses marques.

Microsoft a injecté des milliards dans OpenAI, celui qui a annoncé GPT-6.2 Astra et Sol ce soir, et passe désormais ses keynotes à expliquer qu’il fait presque aussi bien pour beaucoup moins cher.

    Pour aller plus loin
Microsoft dévoile sept modèles d’IA maison pour s’émanciper d’OpenAI et partir chasser sur les terres d’Anthropic et de Google
            
La division, dirigée par Mustafa Suleyman (cofondateur de DeepMind), n’en est pas à son coup d’essai. En juin, à la conférence Build, elle avait déjà sorti sept modèles d’un coup, dont MAI-Thinking-1, son premier modèle capable de « raisonner » par étapes.
Du 19 au 30 novembre, le Plaud Note Pro passe à 149 € au lieu de 189 € ! Il enregistre vos réunions, les transcrit et les synthétise pour vous, il suffit d’appuyer sur un bouton. Les Plaud Note, NotePin et NotePin S sont aussi à -20 %. Bref, c’est le moment d’arrêter de perdre du temps au travail !
Ce rythme découle de la renégociation de l’accord avec OpenAI fin 2025, qui autorise Microsoft à développer ses propres modèles de pointe tout en restant actionnaire d’OpenAI, à hauteur d’environ 27 %.
La nouvelle fournée, détaillée dans un article de Microsoft AI et annoncée sur X, porte le préfixe MAI. Les versions « Flash » désignent des déclinaisons plus légères et moins chères, pensées pour encaisser un gros volume de requêtes.
Sept modèles taillés pour coûter moins cher
- MAI Code 2 : l’assistant de programmation, intégré à GitHub Copilot.
- MAI Code 2 Flash : sa version légère pour les corrections rapides, dans GitHub Copilot et en aperçu dans Microsoft Foundry, la plateforme cloud de Microsoft pour les développeurs.
- MAI Cyber 2 Flash : un agent qui scrute en continu de grandes bases de code à la recherche de failles.
- MAI Image 2.7 : génération et retouche d’images.
- MAI Realtime 1 : la conversation vocale en temps réel, le modèle écoutant et répondant directement à l’oral.
- Dragon Copilot Transcribe : la transcription des consultations médicales.
- Decision 1.1 : un aiguilleur qui confie chaque requête au modèle le moins cher capable d’y répondre.
Selon Microsoft, MAI Code 2 atteint 98 % des performances de GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI) pour environ 40 % de son prix, et 96 % de celles de Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) pour 5 % du prix. Ces scores sont des moyennes sur quatre benchmarks de programmation, des séries d’exercices standardisés qui permettent de comparer les modèles entre eux.
MAI Code 2 Flash se mesure à GPT-6 Luna pour 65 % de son prix, et à Claude Haiku 5.5 pour 20 %. MAI Image 2.7 se classe, d’après l’entreprise, premier en retouche d’images chez Artificial Analysis, et MAI Realtime 1 démarre à 0,01 dollar la minute.
Six mois après Build, Microsoft montre surtout qu’il peut remplacer une partie des modèles qu’il achète par les siens, au moins pour les tâches du quotidien.
Pour OpenAI, voir son partenaire historique et actionnaire publier des comparatifs de prix à son désavantage a quelque chose d’un peu cruel. Il faudra voir si ces pourcentages tiennent face aux tests indépendants, qui choisissent rarement leurs benchmarks avec autant de soin.

articles.title: GTA 6 depuis votre lit ? Le PlayStation Portal tombe en promo
articles.text:
Le PlayStation Portal est actuellement affiché à 249,99 € chez Cdiscount, et passe à 239,99 € avec le code 10DES99 à saisir dans le panier jusqu’à ce mardi soir minuit. Il s’agit de son prix de vente habituel depuis la hausse décidée par Sony en avril 2026.
La PS5 dans le salon, le jeu partout dans la maison
Le principe du PlayStation Portal est simple. On prend une manette DualSense, on la coupe en deux et on glisse un écran LCD de 8 pouces au milieu. L’accessoire affiche les jeux de votre PS5 en Full HD et jusqu’à 60 images par seconde, avec le retour haptique et les gâchettes adaptatives de la manette. Le tout se fait en lecture à distance, via le Wi-Fi.
De quoi lancer GTA 6 depuis votre lit pendant que quelqu’un d’autre regarde un film sur la télé, ou continuer une partie sans quitter le canapé de la chambre. Le Portal a aussi beaucoup évolué depuis sa sortie. Depuis novembre 2025, il peut lancer certains jeux en streaming dans le cloud, sans passer par la PS5, à condition d’être abonné au PlayStation Plus Premium. Et une mise à jour de mars 2026 a ajouté un mode 1080p de meilleure qualité.
Dix euros de moins, ça compte ?
Sorti à 219,99 € en 2023, le PlayStation Portal coûte 249,99 € depuis la hausse de prix du 2 avril 2026. Avec le code 10DES99, il redescend à 239,99 €. La remise reste modeste, mais l’accessoire fait rarement l’objet de promotions.
Le Portal reste pensé comme un compagnon de la PS5. Il s’apprécie surtout à la maison, avec une bonne connexion Wi-Fi, et c’est dans ce cadre qu’il prend tout son sens, pour jouer depuis la chambre pendant que la télé du salon est occupée, par exemple. Sony a bien présenté un nouveau modèle avec du stockage interne, mais il est pour l’instant réservé au Japon et à la Corée du Sud, sans sortie prévue en Europe. Le modèle actuel reste donc la seule option chez nous, et le voir en promotion n’arrive pas si souvent.
L’offre est vendue et expédiée par Cdiscount, avec la livraison gratuite en point retrait.

articles.title: Getting AI out of the demo and into businesses globally | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Getting AI out of the demo and into businesses globally
AWS Forward Deployed Engineering is now available in 15 countries including U.S., Mexico, Brazil, Canada, Australia, Singapore, India, South Korea, Japan, UK, Germany, Netherlands, France, Sweden, and Saudi Arabia for commercial and public sector customers; and powered by dozens of built in production-ready accelerators.
Every enterprise I talk to has built something with AI that works. A prototype that reads a claim. An agent that resolves a card dispute. A model that answers a customer question in seconds.
The prototype works. The demo impresses stakeholders. Then the organization tries to put it into production, and the real problems begin. Production data is messier than the test set. Auditors want to know why the agent made each decision. Volume grows from a pilot group to the whole company. The rules that matter most turn out to live in people’s heads.
None of these are model problems. They’re business problems, and they decide whether AI ever pays off. The stretch from demo to production is the last mile, where most AI stalls. It’s also where our teams spend their time.
We launched AWS Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) in June to close that gap. Since then, we’ve worked through these problems with commercial and public sector customers in financial services, healthcare, sports, media, retail, and more. Here’s what we’ve learned, and how it shaped what we built.
The problem has three layers
Model providers, cloud providers, and consulting firms are all embedding engineers with customers. At AWS FDE, we measure success by what remains after our engineers leave: a foundation your team owns, workflows that keep learning, and governance you can trust.
Across customers, the hardest problems show up in three layers: the foundation, the workflows, and governance. Each one is harder than it looks, and each one builds on the one before it. That holds whether you’re starting fresh or building on existing systems. On a greenfield build, you can move fast, but there’s no foundation to stand on yet. On a brownfield system, agents must work within decades of data, rules, and integrations.
Layer one: A foundation that compounds
Before an agent can do useful work at scale, it needs a foundation: identity, security, context, governance, and operational controls. That foundation must be production-ready from day one and shared by every use case that follows. Context is often the biggest gap. Most customers have data spread across systems and no common ontology, the shared model of how the business works that agents need to reason over.
Without a shared foundation, the second pilot costs nearly as much as the first. Integrations get rebuilt, and lessons fail to carry forward. Most organizations reach a point where they stop and build the foundation first, so each new use case starts from what the last one built instead of from scratch. We call this the AI reset.
Samsung Life Insurance had four affiliates, each building its own AI point solutions from scratch. In 45 days, the FDE team built a governed agentic platform with a single control plane and compliance built in. New agents now deploy through registration and policy assignment instead of a rebuild.
Layer two: Automating workflows
Next is the work itself: High-volume, rule-heavy processes such as claims processing, know your customer (KYC) reviews, card disputes, loan origination, invoice reconciliation, permitting, and customer service. This is where AI can deliver immediate and measurable outcomes. The payoff is fast, but the knowledge that drives these processes rarely lives in a system. It lives with the people who do the work.
The hard part isn’t automation itself. It is uncovering the business rules behind each decision. When an invoice and a purchase order disagree, which record wins? When can an exception clear on its own, and when does it need a person? Experienced employees answer these questions from judgment, and that judgment is rarely written down.
Sometimes the knowledge is buried in the systems themselves.
Rio Tinto Iron Ore runs one of the world’s most complex mine-to-ship supply chains on a 30-year-old Oracle system. That system has more than 5,000 database tables and 140 applications. Mapping it had been a multi-month exercise. The FDE team built agents that mapped it in weeks, surfacing the dependencies that Rio Tinto’s teams could validate and build against.
Mapping what exists is only the start. The biggest opportunities emerge when organizations stop asking how AI can make existing work more efficient and start asking how it can change how work gets done.
Layer three: Governance that holds up as everything changes
Governance isn’t a phase of the project. It’s part of the architecture. As agents multiply, so do security risks, costs, and decisions you must explain. Every agent needs its own identity, permissions, and audit trail, separate from human identity. And because the models underneath are probabilistic, agents need monitoring that keeps their results predictable and auditable long after launch.
The system also must keep working as everything around it changes. Models drift, business rules shift, data formats change, and regulations tighten. New security issues appear, and code falls out of date. As newer models arrive, the instructions and tooling around them will change too. You need evaluations and guardrails that keep agents predictable where they must be and creative where they can be.
When governance comes at the end, it becomes the gate that stops production. When it’s built in from day one, it’s what lets your business move fast.
Marsh, a leading global professional services firm, needed agents that would hold up under its own audit standards. The FDE team built those controls in from the start, and the first use case reached production about two months after work began. Efficiency gains in the targeted areas have been as much as 70 percent, with some process steps moving from hours to seconds. Marsh has since expanded the work and keeps extending the system itself.
How we solve it: Speed, scale, and control
Our perspective comes from building and running these systems ourselves. AWS FDE pairs a small team of AWS engineers, scientists, and product managers with your engineers and a crew of specialized AI agents. Many of our FDEs come from the service teams that build Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Kiro, AWS Quick, and AWS Security Hub. They’ve built and run AI products at AWS scale, and they bring those engineering practices into your environment. Together, our teams take a high-value business problem to production in 45-day sprints, in your own AWS account. Customers shouldn’t need to choose between speed, scale, and control. FDE is built to deliver all three.
Speed – You might come to us with a broad goal or an ambiguous problem. We refine it with your business stakeholders, then build in your environment from day one, on your data and through your identity and security controls. We build in short cycles alongside the people who do the work. Each cycle puts real cases in front of them, and the unwritten rules come out as they react. We capture those rules in a living context, so the system keeps learning after we step back. Nothing gets rebuilt between prototype and production. You see working demos throughout, evaluations track progress against the outcomes you care about, and you have a production system within a quarter or less.
Scale – A point solution can move fast on one use case but leaves no foundation for the next five. Every FDE team works the same way, using the AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC), the method our own service teams use to take a broad problem to a working outcome. We deploy an opinionated AWS stack that reflects what we’ve learned building AI services, adapted to your environment: a living context of how your business works, a workbench where your engineers and agent crews build, a runtime on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and a control tower for governance, outcomes, cost, and agent performance. Accelerators for common tasks, such as document processing and customer sentiment analysis, handle the standard pieces, so each new workload can focus on what’s specific to your business. The opinionated AWS stack, context, and controls carry from one use case to the next.
Your context is what makes scaling possible. Say your first use case is a sales automation workflow. Because its context lives in your AWS account, the next use case, supply chain optimization, builds on it instead of starting over. Your context, tools, and AWS services all sit in one place, so each use case is faster to build than the last.
Control – You own what we build. Everything runs in your AWS account under your identity, network, and security controls. Your engineers work alongside ours from the first sprint, learning both the architecture and the delivery approach on a real business problem. They can then run and extend the solution long after the engagement ends. When we step back, your team runs the system from a control tower, a single view to govern, secure, and monitor every agent. We measure success by how much your team can build without us.
After the first or second project, we want you running AI software factories of your own. One financial services customer did exactly that with AI-DLC, with agents and engineers building together. Throughput rose 53%, and code reviews got 56% faster.
You also keep your choices open. Models are improving fast. When a better or more cost-effective model arrives, you can adopt it through Amazon Bedrock without rebuilding, so you control both capability and cost. You can also bring your own coding agents. Our opinionated AWS stack, adapted to your environment, connects to your systems through APIs, open standards, and connectors, and it works in hybrid environments. You keep the tools and partners you already use.
A flywheel where everyone gets better
Your team gets better. Your capability grows with every use case. The living context, the opinionated AWS stack, and your team’s skills carry forward, so the second use case doesn’t rebuild what the first one built.
AWS Services get better. Our engineers bring what they learn from customers back into the products. You build on the latest services, not a custom solution that falls out of date.
All of AWS works around you. Customer development engineering explores early ideas, FDE takes the hardest problems to production, AWS Professional Services and AWS Partners extend the work across your organization, and AWS Support keeps it running. You get the full depth of AWS behind your AI, and you stay in control of how you use it.
What’s new, and how to start
AWS FDE is now available in 15 countries to commercial and public sector customers, and it’s simpler to buy. Each 45-day sprint has a set price under the FDE Terms and is billed through your AWS account.
We work with customers wherever they are in their transformation. For customers starting out, we build a secure, governed foundation and the first workflows on it. For those ready to change how work gets done, we rebuild workflows such as claims processing and KYC reviews, along with the ones their customers use directly, like shopping and issue resolution. Agents then run the work. For those held back by legacy applications, we work with their engineers to build software factories they can reuse for each new workflow. For those already scaling in production, we keep systems secure with agents that find and fix issues, and we lower the cost per outcome.
If you’re ready to start, talk with your AWS account team. Bring an executive who owns the outcome and engineers ready to build alongside ours. We’ve learned where projects stall before they start, so our agents take on much of the setup, like access, data, and security checks. Work can begin within days. Then we agree together on what the first sprint will deliver and how we’ll measure success.
The gap between AI that works and AI that changes business outcomes is real. It is an engineering, operational, and organizational one, and our teams help customers close it every day. The organizations that succeed with AI won’t necessarily have the most advanced models. They’ll be the ones that build the foundation, workflows, and governance to scale AI across the business.
We’re still early, and we learn something new with every customer. The models will continue to evolve, and so will the tools around them. What should last is a foundation you own, workflows that keep learning, and governance you can trust. That’s what we mean by what remains after our engineers leave.
To get started, contact your AWS account team or learn more about AWS FDE.

articles.title: SuperDial revamps its healthcare voice agent platform to stop AI bots wasting time calling each other - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
SuperDial revamps its healthcare voice agent platform to stop AI bots wasting time calling each other
SuperDial Inc., the creator of voice-first artificial intelligence agents for automating healthcare workflows, is overhauling its platform with a new Agent-to-Agent RCM architecture.
The goal is to eliminate the compute inefficiencies that have arisen as autonomous workers become more prevalent in the industry.
The startup, which raised $15 million in a Series A funding round last year, is best known for its voice agents that automate payer operations, revenue cycle management and administrative outreach. It aims to alleviate the time-consuming burden of having to call health insurance providers, waste time on hold, navigate phone trees and check online portals for information. Traditionally, SuperDial has seen itself as a voice-first platform that’s focused on call automation, but the shift to its Agent-to-Agent RCM architecture suggests it wants to deemphasize phone calls as much as possible.
The company is addressing the friction that has emerged from the slightly dystopian reality that both healthcare providers and insurance payers have largely replaced humans with AI agents in order to automate routine calls. But the fact that agents are handling the calls on both sides creates huge inefficiencies, resulting in those bots wasting time and compute resources as they engage in unnecessary robotic conversations. Rather than streamline insurance eligibility checks, claim follow-ups and prior authorizations, those agents find themselves stuck in multi-minute phone exchanges to relay structured data verbally that both sides already possess.
SuperDial founder and Chief Executive Sam Schwager refers to these scenarios as the “bot wars,” and says they’re increasingly engaging in relentless and destructive battles with one another that cost both healthcare providers and insurance companies money.
“One side deploys AI to secure approvals and payment for care,” he said. “The other deploys AI to review those requests and, at times, deny them. Neither has a reason to stop. Every extra round costs more in AI spend, pulls in staff on both sides to handle what the bots can’t settle, and can delay payment and care. The result is more friction, not less.”
Calling a truce
With Agent-to-Agent RCM, SuperDial is trying to sidestep the bot wars by no longer defaulting to outbound calls. Instead, it acts as a kind of omnichannel orchestration layer, where success is determined by the number of requests resolved, rather than completed phone calls. When a revenue cycle team initiates a request, SuperDial’s agents will first check the relevant electronic data interchange feeds and application programming interfaces to find the information they need.
If they find it, great, but if not, they will then try the payer’s web portals. If they’re still out of luck after exhausting all options for digital retrieval, only then will they proceed to place a voice call. Those calls are more efficient too, since SuperDial’s agents will retain all of the context from their initial search, so they only need to query the agent on the other side of the line for the information that’s missing.
Schwager said Agent-to-Agent RCM puts more emphasis on resolution, allowing a provider’s agent and a payer’s system to connect and work together to resolve administrative requests with less work on both sides.
“The difference between this and the bot wars is the definition of done,” he said. “Two agents were optimizing for their own side of the exchange, but now those two agents are optimizing for a usable answer — that is, the information the provider needs to move the account forward, delivered in response to a request the payer can actually answer.”
For customers, life becomes much simpler. All they have to do is tell SuperDial what it needs to know, and its agents will work to get the answers in the fastest time and most efficient manner possible. “How we get the answer is our problem, not theirs,” Schwager said.
Schwager said the industry needs to move away from the idea that healthcare administration can be improved by having two bots argue with each other faster. “If an agent already has the information, that context should travel with the request,” he explained. “If a digital channel can answer it, there should be no call. The goal is fewer exchanges, not faster ones.”
The company’s long-term goal is to create an AI-native network that facilitates seamless, automated payer-provider communications. The goal is to eliminate repetitive inquiries and cut down on the administrative delays that can negatively impact patient outcomes, Schwager added.
SuperDial says it’s already having a big impact. Since it founded its platform in 2021, it has handled more than 10 million automated calls between healthcare providers and insurance firms – interactions that would once have been made by humans. Had humans made those calls, it would have been much slower, because SuperDial says its agents average about four minutes per call when dealing with insurers’ automated voice systems, compared with 17 minutes or more when reaching a human representative.
With its architectural overhaul, SuperDial is now targeting insurers, in addition to the healthcare providers it already serves. Earlier this year, it announced it had signed a key deal with Guardian Life Insurance Co. of America to modernize its dental provider data attestation workflows.

articles.title: XUPER TV, Cuevana y Pelisplus: páginas que prometen películas gratis pero terminan robando contraseñas
articles.text:
Las plataformas que ofrecen películas, series y transmisiones deportivas sin suscripción, como XUPER TV, Cuevana y Pelisplus forman parte de un circuito de páginas piratas que puede exponer a los usuarios a fraudes, programas maliciosos y robo de datos personales.
El riesgo aumenta cuando esos sitios derivan a descargas externas o piden instalar aplicaciones fuera de las tiendas oficiales. ESET advierte que este tipo de archivos carece, en muchos casos, de los controles de revisión que aplican Google Play Store y App Store, lo que facilita la distribución de software potencialmente peligroso.
Cuáles son los riesgos de descargar apps desde páginas piratas
Las tiendas oficiales aplican controles técnicos y políticas de seguridad antes de publicar una aplicación. Esas revisiones no garantizan una protección absoluta, pero reducen la posibilidad de que un programa incluya funciones ocultas destinadas a vigilar el dispositivo o alterar su funcionamiento.
Por su parte, las plataformas piratas suelen ofrecer sus propias aplicaciones mediante enlaces de descarga en sitios alternativos. Al instalar esos archivos, el usuario incorpora un programa que no pasó por los mismos filtros.
Los expertos señalan que ese circuito puede convertirse en una vía de entrada para spyware, troyanos y otras herramientas diseñadas para obtener información privada.
Qué datos puede quedar expuesta en el teléfono
Una aplicación streaming convencional necesita acceso limitado para reproducir videos y conservar ciertos datos básicos. El problema aparece cuando solicita facultades que le permiten revisar documentos, fotografías, videos, grabaciones de voz o contenido almacenado en el dispositivo.
El análisis de ESET sobre Magis TV, una aplicación que se promocionó como acceso gratuito a series, películas y deportes, detectó pedidos de acceso que excedían las necesidades habituales de una plataforma de reproducción.
Esas autorizaciones podrían permitir la lectura de archivos personales y la recolección de datos almacenados en el teléfono, según el uso que haga el desarrollador o un atacante que tome control de la app.
Cómo pueden los ciberdelincuentes robar contraseñas
El robo de claves no siempre ocurre a través de una pantalla que pide de forma directa la contraseña de una cuenta bancaria o de una red social. Una aplicación maliciosa puede mostrar avisos falsos, imitar una actualización o enviar notificaciones con enlaces que conducen a sitios de suplantación de identidad.
Asimismo, puede recopilar información sobre las aplicaciones que se ejecutan en el dispositivo. Ese dato permite conocer qué servicios utiliza una persona y preparar intentos de engaño más precisos.
Si el usuario ingresa sus credenciales en una página falsa que aparenta pertenecer a una plataforma conocida, los ciberdelincuentes pueden obtener el acceso a sus cuentas.
Por qué las ventanas emergentes y las actualizaciones pueden ser una trampa
Entre los riesgos figura la posibilidad de que estas aplicaciones envíen alertas al dispositivo. Esa función puede utilizarse para mostrar publicidad invasiva, aunque puede servir para distribuir mensajes que imiten comunicaciones legítimas y dirijan a portales fraudulentos.
Otra señal de alerta aparece cuando la aplicación pide autorización para instalar software adicional. Un supuesto reproductor de películas puede presentar una descarga como una actualización necesaria y, en realidad, incorporar otro programa con capacidad para vigilar la actividad del usuario o extraer datos.
Qué consecuencias legales tiene acceder a contenido pirata
Las páginas como XUPER TV, Cuevana y Pelisplus basan parte de su atractivo en la disponibilidad gratuita de obras cuyos derechos pertenecen a estudios, distribuidoras y plataformas de suscripción. La retransmisión o distribución sin autorización vulnera la propiedad intelectual de los titulares.
El uso de esos servicios puede derivar en bloqueos por parte de los proveedores de internet o en reclamos judiciales, de acuerdo con el marco normativo de cada país.
Antes de instalar una aplicación, es clave revisar su origen, evitar descargas externas y optar por servicios que cuenten con licencias y canales oficiales de distribución.

articles.title: He convertido una presentación en una web con Gemini Notebook. Solo tuve que pedírselo
articles.text:
Los cuadernos de Gemini son una de las mejores funciones de la IA si necesitas trabajar sobre tus propios documentos. He usado Gemini Notebook (el antiguo NotebookLM, que Google rebautizó en julio) para documentos de estudio y de trabajo: basta con meterle todos los archivos como fuentes para que la IA responda a partir de esos archivos. Sin que se vaya a buscar fuera, lo que reduce (aunque no elimina) las alucinaciones. Y si con un cuaderno no tienes suficiente, puedes convertirlo en una página web. Con sus enlaces y todo.
Tu cuaderno es una web. Google ha introducido una novedad en Gemini Notebook: la opción de convertir cualquiera de los cuadernos en una página web interactiva. Basta con pedírselo a la IA con solo escribir “Móntame una página web”. Gemini se pondrá a la tarea y convertirá el cuaderno en una página que queda guardada dentro del propio cuaderno. Google permite abrirla en local como pestaña nueva y compartirla con otras personas.
Una manera más práctica de centralizar la información. Una vez subidas todas las fuentes, ya sean documentos, archivos o enlaces, Gemini puede generar todo tipo de contenido a partir de ellas. Al crear una página web, la herramienta organiza todo el contenido para que quede más accesible, navegable y visual. Y como todos sabemos movernos por una web, consultar así el cuaderno resulta más cómodo.
El proceso de creación es sencillo y solo necesita un pequeño prompt. La generación tarda unos minutos, según el volumen de fuentes que tenga el cuaderno. Una vez terminada la página, aparece en el área de Studio de Gemini Notebook: al pulsar sobre el icono se abre la web en pantalla.
Diseño pulido y minimalista. He estado probando la nueva herramienta y he creado una página completa a partir de una presentación que tenía guardada en Gemini Notebook. La calidad del resultado ha sido realmente buena: me parece un excelente complemento a los demás formatos que ya genera, como las presentaciones (descargables en PDF o PowerPoint) o las infografías.
No es del todo nuevo. Google acaba de anunciarlo, pero, en sí misma, la creación de páginas web no era algo extraño para quien ya usaba sus cuadernos: bastaba con añadir el cuaderno como fuente en la app de Gemini y pedirle la web a la herramienta Canvas. Lo que sí es nuevo es que ahora se hace sin salir de Gemini Notebook, y que la página queda a mano en el apartado Studio. Bajo mis pruebas, Google mejoró la calidad del resultado y la forma en que la IA organiza el contenido.
Si utilizas Gemini Notebook habitualmente, ahora puedes convertir tu contenido en una web de manera más sencilla. No debes activar nada: la función se está desplegando en todo el mundo. Si aún no te aparece, toca esperar un poco. Google no aclara si hay diferencias entre la versión gratuita y los planes de pago.
