articles.title: Build WhatsApp AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Build WhatsApp AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Across Latin America, India, and Southeast Asia, WhatsApp is one of the most widely used messaging applications. That makes it an obvious place to build an AI agent. For many end users, it is how they expect to interact with businesses. However, it is also a genuinely difficult surface to build for, even when your agent already runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
The agent is rarely the hard part. The integration is. Inbound messages arrive as deeply nested, type-dependent payloads that must be authenticated and normalized before your agent can read them. Media such as voice notes, images, and documents each require their own processing pipeline. Beyond message handling, you need conversation memory that survives sessions, durable schedules for reminders, and an authenticated path for external systems to trigger outbound messages. And anything you send more than 24 hours after the end user’s last message must use a pre-approved Meta message template.
Wiring that up means configuring more than 10 AWS services and learning a set of WhatsApp system behaviors that most teams discover only by hitting them. None of it is visible to a customer, but all of it has to work. Most teams either build it from scratch or hand the integration to a third-party service.
SMART (Social Messaging Agent Runtime Toolkit) is a third option: an open source Python SDK and Terraform stack that gives you the full channel layer. You provide an agent that runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, and SMART handles the rest. One command deploys the entire infrastructure to your AWS account.
Teams are already running on SMART with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Webmotors, originally scoped as a two-month engagement, compressed delivery to six weeks and moved their internal team into controlled production ahead of a full launch.
Whether you are starting from scratch or migrating an existing agent, you own the agent’s logic. You let SMART handle the channel.
The channel layer you don’t need to build
The following table compares what each concern costs to build yourself against what SMART provides.
| Concern | Building it yourself | With SMART | 
| Webhook ingestion | Signature verification, nested payloads, a dozen message types | Handled, so you receive a clean prompt | 
| Media | Download, transcribe, store, clean up, and upload outbound files before sending | Full lifecycle, both directions | 
| Message templates and the 24-hour window | Meta approval flow, category rules, tracking which window each conversation is in | Declared in YAML, synced by CLI | 
| Conversation memory | Multi-tier memory, session-break handling | Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory, one function call | 
| Scheduling and triggers | Amazon EventBridge Scheduler wiring, authenticated ingress, routing | Built in | 
| Infrastructure | More than 10 AWS services stitched together | One terraform apply | 
| Local development | Redeploy and tunnel on every change | Test locally with the CLI without redeploying | 
The agentic layer
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. SMART builds on two of its main capabilities:
- AgentCore runtime hosts and scales your agent without you managing infrastructure.
- AgentCore memory persists conversation history across sessions and deployments, scoped to each phone number automatically.
Because AgentCore is framework-agnostic, so is SMART. Strands Agents gets memory wired automatically. LangGraph, Pydantic-AI, or another framework that gives you control over the conversation loop can integrate too. The SDK exposes the same memory and session hooks regardless of framework. You keep full control over the elements that differentiate your product: framework, model, prompt, and business logic.
The contract between SMART and your agent is deliberately small. Your agent receives the inbound message and returns text, optionally with rich message attachments. Everything else, session wiring, memory binding, delivery scheduling, is handled for you.
The following example is a complete agent.py for a SMART project. The scaffolding command (socialagent init) creates the project structure and configuration around it. This file is where your agent logic lives.
The create_session_manager() function binds the agent to AgentCore memory scoped to that phone number, so history survives across sessions and deployments for the memory retention period (7 days by default).
The socialagent_notify_context() wrapper is the other pattern worth keeping. Tools sometimes need to send something while the agent is still working, such as a button list or a progress update. Sending it immediately corrupts the conversation history, and the user’s next message fails. The wrapper collects those messages instead, and they go out in order once the turn finishes. Your tools send messages normally and do not deal with the timing.
Architecture
The following diagram shows how an inbound message travels from WhatsApp to your agent and back, and where the shared infrastructure sits.
The SMART core stack is organized into distinct layers: message processing, an agent layer, and a service layer. AWS End User Messaging Social receives inbound WhatsApp messages and routes them to the processing layer. An AWS Lambda function handles the channel logic, while Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides the runtime, memory, and observability for the agent itself. Supporting services such as Amazon DynamoDB (optional, for per-user state), AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon CloudWatch, and Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) supply state management, credentials, monitoring, and storage across the stack.
Inbound events arrive through Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). On each event, the webhook Lambda function verifies the SNS message signature, normalizes the payload, and rate-limits each user (20 messages per minute by default, with the DynamoDB state table enabled). It then fires a read receipt and typing indicator, so the conversation feels alive before the model finishes. Voice notes go through Amazon Transcribe. Other media becomes a descriptor or goes to a hook you register if you want custom handling. When the agent throttles or fails, the user receives a readable message that you can customize, rather than silence.
Agents built on SMART interact directly with end users, so production deployments should include appropriate safeguards. The Terraform stack creates and configures an Amazon Bedrock Guardrails resource by default. With a single guardrail variable in your environment configuration, you can use the stack’s default guardrail, bring your own, or opt out entirely. The controls that you apply are up to you. SMART makes sure the wiring is already in place.
After the message is ready, the webhook function passes it to AgentCore runtime. AgentCore memory maintains conversation context across sessions, and AgentCore Observability, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, traces every step for debugging and audit.
The webhook function sends the reply and messages your tools queued during the turn. A notification function handles sends outside a turn, such as proactive or scheduled messages. External systems trigger your event handlers by posting to an Amazon API Gateway endpoint protected by an API key and a Lambda authorizer. The event is published to Amazon SNS and the event Lambda runs your handler. Amazon EventBridge Scheduler handles time-based outreach, such as reminders and recurring check-ins. With message templates managed through AWS End User Messaging, you can send structured notifications outside the 24-hour WhatsApp session window.
A single socialagent deploy provisions the following resources (it runs terraform apply under the hood).
- Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime and AgentCore memory.
- The webhook, notification, event, and scheduler Lambda functions, on Python 3.12, each with AWS X-Ray tracing and a dead-letter queue.
- The Amazon SNS ingestion topic and the event API.
- Amazon EventBridge Scheduler.
- Amazon S3 buckets for media and audit trails.
- Amazon CloudWatch dashboards and alarms.
The agent container image and the Lambda layer build in AWS CodeBuild during the apply. Docker isn’t required locally.
What you need
Before you deploy, confirm that you have the following.
- AWS End User Messaging Social, with a WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) linked and a phone number registered. That account is the identity Meta issues to a business. For a step-by-step guide, see Getting started with AWS End User Messaging Social, which walks you through linking your WABA and registering a phone number.
- An AWS account with AgentCore runtime and AgentCore memory available in your AWS Region, and model access enabled. This walkthrough uses Claude Haiku 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock by default. You can access many more foundation models (FMs) through Bedrock. See model support by Region.
- Python 3.11 or later locally.
- Terraform 1.7 or later, uv, and the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI). The repository ships a starting-point AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy for the deployer role. See the infrastructure README for the full list of actions.
Note: This is sample code, for non-production usage. You should work with your security and legal teams to meet your organizational security, regulatory and compliance requirements before deployment.
Ship it
Start by cloning the repository and scaffolding a project.
The --blueprint flag selects a project blueprint. Three blueprints ship, and minimal is the default if you don’t pass an argument:
- minimal: a bare-bones echo agent with no tools, skills, or message templates. Start here to build from scratch.
- personal-assistant: a general-purpose assistant with conversation memory, per-user state, scheduling, skills, and rich/voice/image media tools, built on Strands. Start here for conversational, do-it-all agents.
- appointment-scheduler: a booking agent that walks the user through a catalog of items and time slots, confirms the appointment, stores it as per-user state, and sends reminders. Start here for scheduling and booking flows.
You get a project with your agent.py, socialagent.dev.yaml (the project’s deployment configuration), handler stubs for the webhook, notification, event, and scheduler paths, and a vendored copy of socialagent_runtime/. The personal assistant and appointment-scheduler blueprints also bring tools, skills, and a templates.yaml for your message templates. minimal ships none of those, so you add them as required.
Next, iterate locally, with no infrastructure at all.
The socialagent dev command runs your real agent loop and real tools in a terminal read-eval-print loop (REPL), with AWS channel I/O stubbed. Memory becomes a local file-backed session, and state becomes a local JSON file shared across your dev sessions. Notifications print to the terminal, including buttons and list rows. One-shot schedules run immediately. Recurring ones are registered but do not fire. Tool calls appear inline. The reply arrives as one message, as on WhatsApp. The /event and /schedule commands exercise the handler paths. No deployment is involved, so you can test a change as soon as you save it.
Two caveats apply. The model call is real, so a blueprint other than minimal needs AWS credentials and Amazon Bedrock access. The REPL also doesn’t simulate IAM or Meta’s template review. Testing through a deployed stack is highly recommended before you consider something done.
You can add capabilities as recipes. Each recipe is a plain Python function plus a markdown skill that teaches the agent when to use it.
Wiring the recipe to the agentic layer is the developer responsibility, which is what keeps recipes portable if you change agent frameworks.
When the behavior is right locally, deploy the stack.
One step Terraform cannot do for you. AWS End User Messaging Social needs to know where to deliver inbound messages. Point your WhatsApp Business Account at the Amazon SNS topic the stack created. That setting lives on the business account, not in the stack. Point the WABA’s event destination at the stack’s SNS topic using the admin console’s Bind action, or with aws socialmessaging put-whatsapp-business-account-event-destinations from the CLI. Until it is linked, inbound messages go nowhere, and nothing errors.
When the project includes a templates.yaml, the deploy step also syncs your message templates with Meta. If you need to sync templates independently, run uv run socialagent templates sync, which reads the phone number ID and prefix from socialagent.dev.yaml and the template definitions from templates.yaml. A rejected template will fail the deploy, so fix the wording before retrying.
Meta sorts templates by purpose, and a transactional one has more permissive sending rules than a promotional one. Keep the wording plain. Emojis and marketing language are the usual reason a template gets reclassified as promotional. Running templates sync --force re-registers every template, sending approved ones back through Meta review. A plain sync skips them. Leave approved templates alone unless you need to change their content.
Now you’re ready to message your WhatsApp number.
Operate it
Shipping one bot is a project. Operating a fleet of them is the part nobody budgets for, so you also get an optional administration console with its own Terraform root. Deploy it once. Each SMART stack that sets admin_registry_bucket registers itself to a shared Amazon S3 registry on deploy, and the administration console discovers those stacks from there.
The console gives you fleet health at a glance, then per-bot depth. From a single stack view, you can do the following.
- Read real conversations and reply by hand.
- Inspect and cancel Amazon EventBridge schedules, and browse per-user state.
- Restart an individual Lambda function or the runtime.
- Review deployment history, recent errors, and Amazon CloudWatch logs.
- Trigger test events.
- Manage message templates with a WhatsApp-style rendering, and see a warning when Meta has reclassified one.
The console also owns the phone-number binding described earlier, so rebinding a number to a different stack is a UI action.
Sign-in runs through Amazon Cognito, with multi-factor authentication (MFA) required. Role-based permissions are then enforced on every API route. The console itself is served from Amazon CloudFront over a private Amazon S3 bucket.
The console runs on AWS services end to end. Every conversation stays within two providers: Meta and AWS. Model calls may be processed in other AWS Regions through Amazon Bedrock cross-Region inference. See docs/data-flows.md in the repository for details on inference routing, media processing, and service opt-out options.
Clean up
To avoid ongoing charges, tear down the stacks in the following order.
Terraform will not remove three things. The media and audit S3 buckets block destroy while they hold objects, unless enable_force_destroy is set. Templates registered with Meta persist. Your phone number registration is account-level and stays in place.
Get started
When building a WhatsApp AI product, the agent is where your differentiation lives. The channel integration is what eats your roadmap. SMART moves that boundary for you. Write a prompt, a few tools, and your business logic. In return you get webhook ingestion, media handling, conversation memory, scheduling, and template management. All backed by one-command infrastructure, a local development loop, and an administration console running in your own AWS account.
To go further, take the following next steps.
- Get the code from the SMART repository on GitHub.
- Set up your WhatsApp Business Account with AWS End User Messaging Social.
- Start with socialagent init and socialagent dev, which need no AWS infrastructure.
- Read the documentation in the repository for the areas this post summarized, including notifications, media handling, events and scheduling, per-user state, and message templates.
- For further research, see the AgentCore documentation.
We would love to see what you build with it.

articles.title: Hija de Jensen Huang actuó como jefa de gabinete en Nvidia y se enfrentó con ejecutivos
articles.text:
Madison Huang, hija del fundador de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, funcionó como jefa de gabinete de su padre y tuvo autoridad sobre ejecutivos de mayor trayectoria, según una investigación de The New York Times basada en más de una docena de empleados actuales y anteriores que hablaron bajo anonimato.
Madison, de 35 años, figura oficialmente como directora sénior de marketing de producto para IA física. En la práctica, según el diario, influía en el marketing y las comunicaciones de la empresa, participaba en las reuniones trimestrales del equipo ejecutivo y presentaba con regularidad ante el directorio.
Jensen Huang renunció como director ejecutivo el 12 de noviembre, tras conocerse que mantuvo relaciones extramatrimoniales con una ejecutiva de Nvidia y con una clienta que, según la inteligencia de Estados Unidos, trabajaba para el espionaje chino. Colette Kress, hasta entonces directora financiera, asumió de forma interina.
Los Huang no respondieron a las consultas del diario, que tampoco obtuvo comentarios de Jay Puri ni de Ian Buck.
Gritos, coaching obligatorio y más de una docena de salidas
En febrero, Jensen Huang iba a encabezar una conferencia en Nueva Delhi, pero se retiró poco antes y envió en su lugar a Puri, vicepresidente ejecutivo. En una llamada previa, Madison reprendió a varios empleados por no tener listos los planes. Puri le dijo que respondería sus preguntas si dejaba de gritarle.
Puri dejó su puesto menos de seis meses después. El diario precisó que sus fuentes no dijeron si el episodio tuvo relación con esa salida.
En marzo, antes de la conferencia de desarrolladores de la compañía, Madison reprendió ante el equipo de comunicaciones a Buck, creador de Cuda, el software que permite usar los chips de Nvidia para entrenar IA. Buck no había preparado una presentación para una reunión informativa con periodistas. Algunos lo consideran hoy favorito para suceder de forma permanente a Jensen Huang.
Hacia fines del año pasado, durante una reunión en la que Madison gritaba al equipo de marketing, una vicepresidenta sufrió un ataque de pánico y tuvo que abandonar la llamada, según dos personas que conocen el episodio.
Por la cantidad de quejas, el área de recursos humanos la obligó durante varios meses a seguir sesiones semanales de coaching sobre su estilo de gestión, dijeron tres fuentes. Empleados de la empresa estimaron al diario que más de una docena de ejecutivos clave se fueron en los últimos tres años porque no les gustaba trabajar con ella.
La sucesión abre un problema familiar
Según el Times, Jensen Huang sabía cómo se comportaba su hija. Dos personas contaron que a veces amenazaba con enviarla contra otros empleados y les decía que le tuvieran miedo. Ni siquiera los directivos veteranos sentían que podían discrepar con ella, por su línea directa con el jefe.
Madison también encabezó la estrategia de imagen de su padre. En mayo de 2025 participó en la contratación de la consultora de crisis Heller y, cuando el diario publicó en octubre de 2025 sobre el vínculo de Huang con la ejecutiva Alice Huang, presionó al equipo de comunicaciones para responder con firmeza. Ella impulsó además el uso de la versión de dibujos animados de su padre, llamada internamente “Toy Jensen”.
Kress chocó en el pasado con Madison por las inversiones de esta en empresas de robótica y por acuerdos con centros de datos que promovía su esposo, Nico Caprez, según cuatro fuentes. Caprez es vicepresidente de infraestructura de IA y tuvo un ascenso veloz desde su ingreso en 2024. Spencer Huang, hermano de Madison, también trabaja en Nvidia.
Kress debe decidir cuánto poder conservará Madison y qué hará con los otros familiares. Varios directivos temen que tenga lealtades divididas entre la empresa y su padre, en momentos en que aliados de Jensen Huang en Silicon Valley y en Wall Street impulsan su regreso. El presidente Donald Trump dijo que no le molestaría que volviera.
“El nepotismo casi siempre es una mala idea”, afirmó David Yoffie, profesor de la Escuela de Negocios de Harvard que integró más de una docena de directorios. Según Yoffie, hay pocos ejemplos de que funcione siquiera de forma modesta.

articles.title: Nvidia reveals Rubin HPC, a GPU with 50,000+ CUDA cores for scientific simulation
articles.text:
What we know so far: Nvidia is building a GPU with more than 50,000 CUDA cores for one main job: running the simulations that AI agents start when they help scientists and engineers test ideas. The Rubin HPC chip was announced this week at the Supercomputing 2026 conference as a new part of Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform, but it's not expected until 2028, and the company has yet to release several specs that HPC buyers care about most.
The core count offers the first clue to what Nvidia is building. The current Rubin GPU has 224 streaming multiprocessors and 28,672 CUDA cores, so getting past 50,000 would take at least 74% more cores.
That suggests Rubin HPC may spread its cores across several dies in one package, as the two-die Rubin does, or as the four-die Rubin Ultra that Nvidia originally planned, a design since reportedly scaled back. Nvidia has not confirmed the chip's physical layout and describes the core count only as being "on a single GPU." The image it released with the announcement does not appear to show a multi-die design.
Nvidia's pitch is less about raw compute and more about keeping that compute busy. The company says climate modeling, engineering simulation, genomic analysis and financial risk work tend to follow the same pattern: a program reaches into a huge dataset, pulls out a few scattered values, runs a calculation and then repeats that step an enormous number of times. Under that kind of load, a GPU's cores often sit idle while they wait for data.
Nvidia says Rubin HPC addresses this with what it calls a "balanced design," meaning data movement scales with compute instead of adding compute alone. Part of that design is a sparse data acceleration capability that Nvidia says keeps the cores fed.
According to the company, it speeds up the routines that show up again and again in simulation code, including sparse matrix operations, stencil computations, sorting and reductions. Those routines are common in both scientific and commercial analytics, which is why Nvidia is pitching the chip as useful across many industries rather than as a niche lab part.
Between GPUs, Rubin HPC will use seventh-generation NVLink. Nvidia gave no figures for the interconnect's bandwidth or physical layer inside the rack. For reference, NVLink 6 delivers 3.6 TB/s per GPU in Vera Rubin NVL72, and earlier roadmaps paired NVLink 7 with much larger scale-up domains.
Other details are missing, too. Nvidia did not give the chip's HBM capacity or memory bandwidth, and it did not say whether Rubin HPC shifts silicon toward native FP64 math. That question matters because AMD is promoting far stronger double-precision performance in the GPU it is showing at the conference.
Nvidia instead framed the chip around agentic workflows. In its view, AI agents will let research teams screen far more candidate materials, molecules and designs than people could on their own. Each of those candidates still has to be tested in simulation before anyone commits to a physical experiment or prototype. More agents mean more simulations, and more simulations mean more demand for accelerated computing.
"For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery. Rubin HPC accelerates the simulations agents use to test ideas and guide their next steps, helping scientists and engineers explore more possibilities and bring breakthroughs closer," said Ian Buck, Nvidia's vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing.
Software is a large part of the plan. Agents running on Rubin HPC can use Nvidia's CUDA-X libraries, a growing set of tuned implementations of complex algorithms, including many used in simulation and analytics.
If agents call optimized routines instead of writing their own, each round of hypothesis, simulation and refinement should finish faster. That would let researchers decide on next steps sooner and focus lab time on the most promising candidates.
Rubin HPC is still more than a year from release. Before then, Nvidia will need to say how much memory the chip has, how it handles double precision and whether it uses more than one die.

articles.title: ‘No blackouts, no secret emergencies’: FEMA confirms today's emergency alert system test for TV and radio won't hit your phone
articles.text:
Don't panic — an Emergency Alert System test will air on TV and radio today, but FEMA confirms nationwide drill won't hit phones
A loud interruption
- There will be a test of the Emergency Alert System at 2:20pm ET / 11:20am PT today across the US
- This will interrupt TV and radio broadcasts
- Phones won't be affected as they use a different alert system
Get ready to hear a loud alert tone later today, because FEMA (the Federal Emergency Management Agency) and the FCC (Federal Communications Commission) are planning a test of the Emergency Alert System (EAS) at approximately 2:20pm ET / 11:20am PT today (November 17). But while this will interrupt TV broadcasts, it won’t sound on your phone.
Radio and television broadcasters, cable systems, satellite radio and television providers, and wireline video providers nationwide will interrupt their normal programming to relay the test message, which will include both a loud tone and a message informing everyone that this is just a test.
In other words, there’s nothing to worry about, it’s just a regularly scheduled test of the EAS system, to help ensure that if and when there’s a real emergency, any potential issues with the system will have been identified and fixed in advance.
No secret emergencies
Rumors have been circulating that this is more than a test, but FEMA has stressed on X that this isn’t the case, saying “no blackouts, no secret emergencies” — so don’t panic.
Interestingly, this test also won’t sound on phones — which is another indicator that it is simply a test and nothing more serious.
The reason phone alerts aren’t being tested too though is simple: the EAS is purely a radio and television alert system, with phone alerts instead handled by the Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA) system, which was last tested in 2023.
During that test, both systems were activated, but a 2015 law requires the EAS to be tested every three years, whereas there’s no such requirement for the WEA.

articles.title: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data
articles.text:
It can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI. That is, of course, by design. The more you use Gemini, the more data Google collects to train and improve its generative AI chatbot. The options to limit training on your data have been scant, but Google is finally adding more controls to the Gemini app.
The change currently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data. Prior to this change, the only way to opt out of contributing your chat contents (including attachments) for training was to turn off your history. That made it impossible to go back and pick up a chat down the road.
As the new settings roll out, users will see separate toggles for model training and chat history. The history setting will continue to support an adjustable limit, but you will no longer have to change it to stop Google from training on your Gemini usage. Meanwhile, AI training will be an opt-out situation. You’ll need to find the toggle to block Google from using your chats for AI training. It’s under Activity in the Gemini settings. You can also access the menu from your Google account under Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity.
Importantly, this only applies to future interactions with Gemini. If you have previously fed any data into Google’s AI, that’s already part of the training data. That can include your inputs, Gemini’s responses, uploaded files, tool calls, your location, and data from connected apps. Google says it may retain this data for up to three years to improve its models. The company has previously noted it attempts to filter personal information out of the Gemini activity history, but that isn’t a guarantee.

articles.title: Accessibility isn’t “a niche problem,” says organizer of inaugural assistive tech conference | BetaKit
articles.text:
Toronto-based disability-focused accelerator Access to Success wants to raise the profile of assistive technology with the first-ever Canadian Disability Tech Summit in Toronto on Wednesday.
The event will gather hundreds of founders, investors, healthcare leaders, researchers, corporations, policymakers, and other members of the disabled community in the Automotive Building at Exhibition Place for a full day of mainstage programming and an exhibit floor featuring more than 50 innovations.
“Disability is not a monolith … so getting the word out across that entire diversity of this population … was one of the bigger challenges.”
The summit will facilitate discussions on the “entire spectrum of disability” and the pipeline of innovation, Access to Success executive director Varun Chandak told BetaKit in an interview. That’s unique in Canada, Chandak explained, because usually events are disability-specific, with respective events for vision loss or autism, but no opportunities for the disabled community to get together in one place.
“There’s no reason why somebody working in pediatric brain health is going to talk to somebody working in mobility devices,” Chandak said. “Disability is not a monolith … so getting the word out across that entire diversity of this population, around this community, [about] all of the work that’s happening was one of the bigger challenges.”
The summit has already met the challenge, with more than 800 people registered to attend in-person and online, double what the organizers expected, Chandak said. Attendees will take part in conversations about disability and tech, commercializing disability innovations, and see startup pitches. While most pitch competitions are typically in front of investors, these startups will instead pitch potential industry partners who may be interested in buying their products.
”Everyone needs more money, but what [these assistive technology startups] tell us they need, based on the forms that they fill out with us, is that they need partners and they need procurement,” Chandak said.
RELATED: Enabled Talent’s new program aims to help disabled Canadians become entrepreneurs
The summit will also feature sessions on disability tech at scale, an investor panel, and a conversation on co-designing innovations with input from people living with disabilities. Some speakers slated to appear include Ontario Minister for Seniors and Accessibility Raymond Sung Joon Cho, Maverix Private Equity founder John Ruffolo, and Enable Ventures founder Gina Kline.
Chandak said everyone in the assistive tech industry has the same experience of travelling to attend trade shows and conferences outside of Canada, and that he’s excited to bring a Canadian option to the table himself.
“When they hear that something like this is happening in Canada, the response was pretty much universally along the lines of, and I’m paraphrasing here, … ‘hell yeah,’” Chandak said.
The plan is to turn the Canadian Disability Tech Summit into an annual affair, and given it sold out in its inaugural year, Chandak thinks the demand is there. He hopes attendees leave Wednesday’s event realizing how more accessible design choices just result in better design, period.
“I need the tech sector to start realizing that [accessibility] is not a niche problem anymore,” Chandak said. “The things that we are working on [have] already gone on to change millions and millions and millions of lives, if not billions. It’s an untapped opportunity waiting to be invested in.”
Feature image courtesy Access to Success.

articles.title: Pedestal AI raises $4.7 million to agentify the supply chain | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Delivery supply chains are the lifeblood of contemporary businesses — and a new startup is betting that purpose-built AI agents can make them run a lot more smoothly.
On Tuesday, Pedestal AI emerged from stealth with $4.7 million in seed funding. The company’s goal is to use agentic AI to make supply chains faster and more reliable — a plan that’s already brought them together with Fortune 500 companies and some of the largest shipping firms in the world.
The seed round was led by Eclipse, with participation from RRE, Converge VC, Timescale Ventures, and VitalStage. Pedestal says the funding will be used to expand its product and engineering time, grow the marketing organization, and support additional deployments.
In practice, much of Pedestal’s work is about removing friction from the shipping process — with agentic technology used as a means to that end. In one case, the company reduced missed deliveries for a major furniture company by 20% by deploying agents to take on some of the work that drivers were supposed to do. The agentic system they built would call customers 30 minutes before a delivery and collect any special instructions; if the call didn’t go through, a text would be sent from a separate system. Along the way, the deployment collected a wealth of data about friction points in the process, which could be used to optimize the system even further.
CEO Raj Aggarwal says contemporary AI systems are particularly useful for dealing with that data. “The challenge is that the data is messy and it’s constantly changing,” Aggarwal told TechCrunch. “It’s disparate because it sits in so many legacy systems. That’s what makes it hard.”
Supply chain AI has become a particularly hot space in recent months as alumni from autonomous driving teams look to launch their own startups. The supply chain startup Atomic, launched by a team of Tesla alumni, came out of stealth in 2025 with an emphasis on streamlining inventory. Another venture called Loop was launched by Uber alums to focus on predictive analytics.
As Aggarwal sees it, deliveries are particularly well-suited to training reinforcement learning systems. Because of their high volumes and easily measured outcomes, it’s easy to fine-tune contemporary AI systems toward what’s working and away from what isn’t.
Perhaps most importantly, it’s the kind of problem that can have an immediate effect on a client’s bottom line, making it easy to justify the expense.
“If you can get it right,” he told TechCrunch, “you can have really big impact.”

articles.title: 403 hyperscale US data centers used staggering 82 terawatts of electricity in a year, more than 80% of Michigan’s entire consumption — generated 26 million tons of CO2 in a single year, gas and coal supplied 54% of the power, Harvard-led study estimates
articles.text:
403 hyperscale US data centers used staggering 82 Terawatts of electricity in a year, more than 80% of Michigan’s entire consumption — generated 26 million tons of CO2 in a single year, gas and coal supplied 54% of the power, Harvard-led study estimates
Powering them put out an estimated 25.7 million metric tons of CO2, 2–3x a 2018 estimate.
A Harvard-led study estimates that 403 hyperscale U.S. data center sites consumed about 82 TWh of electricity in a year, 1.8% of the country’s total, with more than half coming from gas and coal sources, Wired reports. This compares to the entire state of Michigan selling 99 TWh in 2024. The data centers’ pull also put out an estimated 25.7 million metric tons (Mt) of CO2, which is two to three times a 2018 estimate.
Hyperscale data centers, in this case, refer to sites run by a hyperscale cloud or content provider, or a colocation operator who serves one, with a capacity in the tens of megawatts. The 675 candidate sites came from data vendor Baxtel, with 403 confirmed with satellite imagery and building-footprint maps, at an average capacity of 39.9 MW and a median of 36 MW.
Nobody officially counts what the data centers actually draw from the grid. Instead, the electricity is estimated by multiplying each site’s maximum capacity by the hours in a year and an estimate of how hard the data centers run. For CO2 and the source mix, each site is placed in its grid region, of 23 total in the study, with a regional average mix from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). These are then multiplied and added up for the total number. Such estimation methods may reduce the strength of arguments against data center buildouts.
The power is also not evenly laid out, with 142 of the sites located in Virginia alone, taking 21.4 TWh, or about a quarter. PJM, a grid operator for 13 states, including Virginia, and D.C., or America’s largest grid, covers 32.8 TWh, or about 40%, more than any other region. Notably for Virginia, its power draw is actually just a bit below the 22.85 TWh estimate for all U.S. hyperscale sites from 2018. See the table for more details.
| Top 10 states by CO2 attributed to hyperscale data centers |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| State | Sites | Electricity (TWh) | CO2 (million metric tons) | CO2 per kWh (g) | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Virginia | 142 | 21.4 | 7.0 | 325 | 
| Iowa | 26 | 7.2 | 3.2 | 445 | 
| Ohio | 38 | 8.8 | 2.9 | 325 | 
| Texas | 22 | 4.6 | 1.5 | 333 | 
| Nebraska | 8 | 3.5 | 1.4 | 395 | 
| Oregon | 56 | 11.1 | 1.3 | 119 | 
| Arizona | 12 | 3.2 | 1.3 | 401 | 
| Oklahoma | 8 | 2.9 | 1.1 | 395 | 
| Wyoming | 2 | 1.2 | 1.0 | 848 | 
| Utah | 5 | 1.3 | 0.8 | 640 | 
Not all power is equal — renewables, for example, can be perceived more favorably — and 53.9% of the estimated draw comes from fossil fuels, 38.2% of the total from gas and 15.2% from coal. Renewables cover 25.3% while nuclear handles the remaining 20.9%. Estimates put this in the 21–31 Mt range for CO2 output, versus the 10.5 Mt estimate from 2018.
Estimated carbon intensity, though, is lower than the average, at 314 g of CO2 per kWh versus 348 for the entire U.S. grid, or about 10% lower. Admittedly, almost a quarter of the load is in regions dirtier than the U.S. average. The likely reason it’s lower is that the biggest loads lie in PJM territory, which is nuclear-heavy, while Oregon, for its part, is hydro-heavy. The estimates, in this case, use 2023 plant data, and the method does not trace which plant feeds which site and also leaves out clean-power contracts and credits.
The study’s results also lag reality as the window ended in April 2025 and, with how much development there has been for AI, among other things, the footprint “could already be substantially larger now in 2026,” lead author Gianluca Guidi said in a statement. Another issue is that the median site capacity in the study is relatively small compared to upcoming buildouts, with many campuses now planned in the hundreds or thousands of megawatts. On-site power, such as gas plants, also may not show up in grid data.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Official numbers may be forthcoming, though, as the Energy Information Administration’s pilot surveys of data center energy use are complete, and the agency is using them to design a survey of the sector, a spokesperson told Wired. The first pilots, which launched in March, relied on web surveys and in-person interviews, with 196 companies asked about energy sources, electricity use, plus servers and cooling, although not covering all states. Gauging the direct human impact is next in the chain, with Francesca Dominici, the study’s corresponding author, saying that quantifying health effects is an important next step.

articles.title: Jensen Huang rompe su silencio tras dejar NVIDIA: "Sería un honor regresar como CEO"
articles.text:
Cada día que pasa se escribe un nuevo capítulo del culebrón por la salida de Jensen Huang como presidente y CEO de NVIDIA. El ejecutivo aprovechó hoy su perfil en X (Twitter) para pronunciarse en público por primera vez desde su renuncia a la conducción de la empresa. En su comunicado no solo reconoció sus errores, sino que también mostró su interés por volver a liderar la compañía que cofundó en 1993.
El mensaje de Jensen Huang marca todos los casilleros de lo que se podría esperar de un discurso de arrepentimiento. El exCEO de NVIDIA agradeció las muestras de cariño de quienes se comunicaron con él en los últimos días, como también de quienes pidieron por su regreso al gigante verde. Asimismo, celebró su historia como inmigrante y las posibilidades que le abrió Estados Unidos desde su llegada, hizo un mea culpa de su comportamiento, se comprometió a colaborar con la investigación sobre su accionar, le pidió disculpas a su familia y sentó las bases para un potencial vuelta al rol principal de la empresa.
Las repercusiones del primer mensaje público de Jensen Huang tras renunciar a NVIDIA no se hicieron esperar. Al momento de redacción de este artículo, el posteo acumula más de 39.000 republicaciones y 238.000 likes. No quedan dudas de que sus palabras eran las más codiciadas, especialmente tras un anuncio de salida de la compañía que no incluyó ningún comentario de su parte.
A continuación, el mensaje completo que publicó Jensen Huang en X (Twitter), traducido al español:
Durante la última semana, me he sentido profundamente conmovido por el cariño y el apoyo de amigos, colegas del sector y personas a las que ni siquiera conozco. Gracias a todos los que han mostrado tanta amabilidad hacia mí y mi familia. Significa muchísimo para mí.
Llegué a Estados Unidos hace 53 años, y convertirme en ciudadano estadounidense fue uno de los mayores regalos y uno de los momentos de mayor orgullo de mi vida. NVIDIA fue el proyecto de mi vida. Haber contribuido, junto a mis colegas, a convertirla en la empresa que es hoy ha sido un privilegio y un honor. Solo en Estados Unidos podría haber surgido una compañía como NVIDIA. Amo a nuestro país y amo a NVIDIA.
No estuve a la altura de los estándares que se esperan de todos en NVIDIA, y he cometido errores graves en mi vida personal. He causado problemas a la Junta Directiva, algo de lo que me arrepiento profundamente. Asumo la total responsabilidad por mis errores y me comprometo a colaborar con la investigación independiente que está llevando a cabo la Junta.
Desde mi salida, he recibido numerosas peticiones por parte de empleados, inversores, socios comerciales y clientes de NVIDIA para que regrese como CEO. Muchos siguen contactándome directamente mientras la empresa navega por complejas dinámicas tecnológicas, de mercado, competitivas y geopolíticas. NVIDIA es una empresa excepcional, de esas que solo aparecen una vez por generación. Si la Junta Directiva considera que mi regreso favorece los intereses de nuestros accionistas, empleados, la propia compañía y Estados Unidos, sería un honor atender estas peticiones y volver a ocupar el cargo de CEO.
Gracias, de nuevo, a todos los que me han hecho llegar sus buenos deseos. Me siento profundamente conmovido por su apoyo. A mi familia: los amo, y dedicaré el resto de mi vida a ser digno de su cariño.
Jensen
Jensen Huang, en X (Twitter).
Jensen Huang está dispuesto a regresar a NVIDIA, pero es más difícil de lo que parece
Queda claro que Jensen Huang no ha tirado la toalla de forma definitiva con NVIDIA. Tras el escándalo por sus aventuras con la supuesta espía china Alice Huang y con la ejecutiva Kimberly Powell, la renuncia del empresario parecía ser el abrupto final de una historia hasta aquí plagada de éxitos. Pero unos pocos días le han bastado para tratar de recuperar el trono perdido.
Un reciente reporte de Financial Times indicaba que Huang supuestamente había manifestado su deseo de regresar a NVIDIA a personas de confianza. La compañía ya ha puesta en marcha la búsqueda de un sucesor y todo apunta a que el Consejo de Administración prefiere dar vuelta la página antes que darle una segunda oportunidad al exCEO.
Con el mensaje de hoy, Jensen Huang pone su destino en manos de la Junta Directiva. Y si bien a primera vista puede parecer un gesto de nobleza y colaboración, también impone una gran presión sobre los integrantes de la mesa. Después de todo, si eligen a otro CEO y no se logran los resultados esperados, la culpa será de ellos.
El timing del mensaje de Jensen Huang tampoco es casual. La publicación se da justo el mismo día en que NVIDIA presentará los resultados financieros del último trimestre. Wall Street proyecta cifras de ventas que dupliquen las del trimestre previo, aunque la verdadera atención estará en lo que responda Colette Kress, la CEO interina, a las consultas de los inversores y accionistas. Con el comunicado de Huang en boca de todos, es lógico pensar en un bombardeo de preguntas sobre si la empresa analiza o no traerlo de regreso. Pase lo que pase, se esperan reacciones drásticas (para bien o para mal) en el valor de la acción del gigante verde.

articles.title: With $5M in funding, Pretxt launches runtime oversight layer to supervise AI agents in real time - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
With $5M in funding, Pretxt launches runtime oversight layer to supervise AI agents in real time
Artificial intelligence supervision pioneer Pretxt AI is launching with $5 million in seed funding today as it tries to contain the very real risk of unleashing autonomous agents in production environments.
It has created a new kind of “AI Supervision” tool that applies oversight at runtime to ensure those agents follow a company’s rules at all times. Today’s round was led by Deciens Capital and saw participation from Howdy Partners, Service Provider Capital and NSV Wolf Capital.
The startup is pitching the idea of a continuous runtime supervision layer that monitors AI agents as they’re getting work done, contrasting their behavior with the parent organization’s rules and policies. If it spots an agent is starting to drift off-course, it will immediately intervene to put it back on the right track, before it can make a critical mistake that hurts the business.
Real-time guardrails like Pretxt has designed are likely going to become a priority for enterprises as they begin to trust AI agents with more consequential work than simply drafting emails or creating images. For instance, if agents are to be trusted with handling customer refunds and accessing mission-critical databases and modifying records within them, companies will need the strongest reassurance that they’re not going to mess up those tasks.
But those assurances are few and far between. AI is notorious for “hallucinating” responses when it doesn’t know the answer to a question, and autonomous agents have shown erratic behavior time and again. They don’t need a malicious prompt injection to start missing critical required steps in a workflow or invent policy exceptions to simplify a task they’re trying to complete. They’ve shown they can do this in both labs and in the real world.
In response, most security tools take a heavy-handed approach, blocking agents outright, but this means that work slows down. The other approach is to flag errors after the fact, but by the time that happens they could have already caused massive damage.
Pretxt’s co-founders Brian Soby (pictured, left) and Aaron Costello (right) realized that companies need a more balanced approach to agentic security and oversight. Soby, who serves as the startup’s chief executive, previously held senior security roles at Salesforce Inc. and Mitre Inc. before founding the software-as-a-service security startup AppOmni Inc.
It was there that he met Costello, who now serves as Pretxt’s chief technology officer. During their time at AppOmni, they uncovered several major vulnerabilities in AI agents developed by Salesforce and ServiceNow Inc. and began to understand what’s required to ensure those agents can still work safely.
Supervision at runtime
Many traditional agent monitoring tools use a second large language model as a “judge” to monitor the behavior of the main LLM that’s doing the work. But Pretxt’s co-founders shunned this idea because it creates latency, increases compute costs and involves too much guesswork.
Instead, their AI Supervision platform is powered by a near-deterministic engine that evaluates agent’s actions in milliseconds in order to spot those that break the rules and intercept them in progress. The company reckons it can do this up to 60 times faster than LLM-as-a-Judge-based security tools.
The approach is effective. In tests on Zapier’s AutomationBench, Pretext was able to reduce agent policy violations from around one in five to zero. The tool is designed to be easy to implement, so teams don’t need a thorough understanding of the models or agents they’re trying to supervise.
Instead, they simply choose which policies, standards and guardrails should apply to an agent, and then they can keep track of them in real time. The platform allows users to track approvals, roll back plan versions and escalate any tricky edge cases to human decision-makers.
That last capability is especially useful, because many organizations’ security plans have gaps when agents encounter situations that were not previously envisaged. In such cases, Pretxt halts the agent and asks a human to decide what the rules should be.
“Supervising an AI agent shouldn’t mean becoming an expert in everything it touches or in how it’s built,” Costello said. “Teams tell us in plain language how it should behave and where the boundaries are, and we supervise and steer the agent to stay within them. So there’s no untangling permissions or digging into the agent’s internals.”
Pretxt’s AI Supervision tool is available in early access now. It’s primarily targeting high-stakes regulated industries where mistakes and hallucinations simply cannot be tolerated.
For financial services and insurance companies, it can enforce borrower verification rules and route complex claims to humans, while in healthcare and life sciences it ensures that agents don’t step outside of strict boundaries. In customer support applications, it can prevent agents from offering unapproved discounts or refunds to customers.
AI Supervision can provide a lot of different benefits to a lot of different people. Chief information officers and other senior executives will be able to scale higher-value AI projects safely, while security teams, compliance officers and platform engineers can address gaps in risk management and ensure low-latency policy enforcement without needing to stack additional models.
Enterprise Management Associates analyst Chris Steffen said the thing that really sets Pretxt apart is its focus on the basics. Not only does it check that agents are behaving themselves, but it also makes sure they’re doing the work they’ve been assigned without breaking any rules or cutting any corners, creating what is effectively a new category of AI supervision tool.
“Most tools ask if an agent is secure, compliant or observable, but far fewer can show if the agent is correctly doing the job it was given,” Steffen said. “Most tools can only report what went wrong after the fact, when it’s too late. Pretxt intervenes while the outcome can still change to get agents back on track.”

articles.title: Sky OS now comes with an 'intelligent entertainment assistant' built in — as the biggest ever update for Sky Stream and Sky Glass starts rolling out
articles.text:
Sky Glass and Sky Stream are getting a huge free update with the new version of Sky OS — these are the 5 biggest upgrades
A new digital assistant is included
- Sky is rolling out a big new upgrade for Sky OS
- Customers on Sky Glass and Sky Stream get the update
- Smart Voice is one of the major new features
If you're signed up for Sky Stream or have a Sky Glass TV at home, then a major upgrade to the Sky OS software is heading your way, with some important changes and new features that we'll run through for you here.
Topping the new feature list is Smart Voice, which works a bit like ChatGPT for your TV. Your voice commands can now be more conversational and less precise, and Sky OS will still get what you mean — you could make a guess at a TV show name, for instance, or mangle a particular instruction, and Smart Voice will figure out your intentions.
You're now able to ask a broader range of questions via voice too, from asking for recommendations for shows like House of the Dragon, to querying where The Gilded Age is set. Smart Voice can also help out with more practical questions, like when you can watch sports games or movies, and which platforms they're on.
Voice activation works the same as before — just press and hold the voice button on the remorse, or say "hello Sky" to use the assistant hands-free. You'll need to press the button again, or say "hello Sky" again, if you've got follow-up questions.
"There's more great TV to enjoy than ever, and we want to make finding it feel effortless," Carli Kerr, a managing director at Sky TV and Now, said in a press statement. "Smart Voice gives customers an intelligent entertainment assistant built into Sky, so they can now talk to the TV like they would a friend, making it easier to find something they’ll love."
More features to explore
There's plenty more in the new Sky OS update too. The second most notable feature after Smart Voice is a simpler, more intuitive homepage, which Sky says is to "get to the good stuff quicker". Home, TV Guide, My Library, Sport, Search, and Settings all gather together in a new navigation bar at the top of the screen.
A couple of other features also make it easier to get around. A new Recents shortcut (just by Home on the navigation bar) does exactly what you might imagine — gives you quick access to whatever you've been watching recently. There's also a new My Library hub, which brings together all your bookmarked shows and programme recordings.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
You can access up to 1,000 hours of cloud recordings through My Library, as well as schedule and cancel recordings, and switch between recording individual episodes or entire seasons. Sky says recording is available "on eligible content" and "is subject to content rights and customer restrictions".
The last major upgrade worth mentioning is another new hub screen, this time called Sports. It shows you what's on now, what's coming up, and what you can watch on demand, and personal recommendations for your teams and preferences show up, too.
You should see the update appear over the next few days, if you haven't got it already. Sky also says the Sky Go app for Android and iOS/iPadOS has also been "refreshed" to match the Sky OS updates — it's free with a Sky subscription.

articles.title: Nouveaux modèles de ChatGPT : GPT-6.2 Astra coûte 20 % moins cher et talonne Claude Fable 5.2 — Frandroid
articles.text:
Et une nouvelle annonce IA… Mais dans la page de lancement de ses nouveaux modèles, OpenAI glisse un aveu peu flatteur. GPT-6.2 Astra et GPT-6.2 Sol ont davantage tendance que leur prédécesseur à passer sous silence ce qui a bloqué leur travail, comme un fichier introuvable ou un outil de recherche indisponible.
Le cabinet d’évaluation indépendant Artificial Analysis montre bien un travers voisin dans son analyse publiée sur X : sur un test de questions-réponses autour du code, Sol est « plus susceptible que son prédécesseur d’omettre des faits clés ».
OpenAI a présenté ses deux modèles ce 17 novembre : Astra, son haut de gamme pour les projets lourds, et Sol, le modèle polyvalent du quotidien.
Ils sont disponibles pour les abonnés Plus, Pro, Enterprise et Edu dans ChatGPT Work et dans Codex, l’outil de programmation d’OpenAI, ainsi que via l’API, la porte d’entrée payante des développeurs.
Du 19 au 30 novembre, le Plaud Note Pro passe à 149 € au lieu de 189 € ! Il enregistre vos réunions, les transcrit et les synthétise pour vous, il suffit d’appuyer sur un bouton. Les Plaud Note, NotePin et NotePin S sont aussi à -20 %. Bref, c’est le moment d’arrêter de perdre du temps au travail !
Astra y coûte 8 dollars par million de tokens envoyés et 40 dollars par million de tokens générés (prix américains, hors taxes), soit 20 % de moins que GPT-6 Astra, sorti début septembre. Un token est un fragment de mot : un million représente environ 750 000 mots en anglais. Sol conserve les tarifs de GPT-6.1 Sol, à 2 et 10 dollars.
    Pour aller plus loin
Nouveau Claude Fable 5.2 : Anthropic baisse de 20 % le prix de son IA la plus puissante et promet beaucoup moins de refus 
            
Deuxième au classement, pas en programmation
Sur l’Intelligence Index d’Artificial Analysis, une note qui agrège neuf tests (code, sciences, travail de bureau, connaissances), GPT-6.2 Astra obtient 62 à son niveau de raisonnement maximal. Il gagne cinq points sur GPT-6 Astra, dépasse Gemini 4 Carbon de Google (60) et Claude Opus 5.5 (59), et ne reste derrière que Claude Fable 5.2 d’Anthropic (65).
Sol grimpe à 57, au niveau de GPT-6 Astra pour environ 15 % de son coût par tâche. Le prix fait la différence : d’après le graphique d’Artificial Analysis, une tâche de l’indice revient à environ 4 dollars avec Astra au maximum, contre plus de 25 dollars avec Fable 5.2.
Le Coding Agent Index, qui teste les modèles aux commandes d’un outil de développement comme Codex ou Claude Code, raconte une autre histoire.
Astra y stagne à 53, comme GPT-6 Astra, et Sol recule de trois points à 49, loin des 58 de Fable 5.2 et d’Opus 5.5. Les graphiques d’OpenAI se lisent aussi avec attention. Sur Agents’ Last Exam, l’entreprise revendique 5,5 points d’avance sur Fable 5.2 pour 5 % du coût, mais précise en note que neuf tâches de Fable ont été écartées. Sur Terminal-Bench-Science, Fable est mesuré dans un autre environnement que celui d’Anthropic, qui annonce 74,6 % avec Claude Code.
Les entreprises qui envoient des milliers de requêtes par jour ont le plus à gagner, surtout avec Sol, au niveau de l’ancien haut de gamme pour une fraction du prix. Pour les développeurs qui confient des chantiers entiers à un agent de code, Claude garde l’avantage selon Artificial Analysis.
Plus gênant, Artificial Analysis mesure un taux d’hallucination de 59 % pour Astra et 55 % pour Sol : face à une question factuelle dont ils ignorent la réponse, ils inventent plus souvent qu’ils ne l’admettent. GPT-6 Astra affichait 51 % à son lancement, sur une version antérieure du test, une comparaison qui reste donc fragile.
Côté sécurité, OpenAI classe les deux modèles au niveau « critique » en cybersécurité, le plus élevé de sa grille interne : ils trouvent et exploitent des failles plus efficacement.
Ses garde-fous resserrés bloquent aussi, de son propre aveu, certains travaux légitimes de recherche en sécurité. Astra devient enfin son premier modèle public classé « élevé » sur l’auto-amélioration, c’est-à-dire sa capacité à accélérer la recherche en IA.
OpenAI signe une vraie baisse de prix et revient presque en tête, de quoi mettre Anthropic sous pression juste avant son introduction en Bourse.

articles.title: Windows 11 27H2 : une première référence découverte dans les fichiers du système
articles.text:
Microsoft n'a toujours pas annoncé Windows 11 27H2, mais son nom vient d'apparaître dans les fichiers d'une récente version expérimentale du système. Un nouvel indice qui vient renforcer les informations circulant depuis plusieurs semaines sur la prochaine grande mise à jour de Windows.
Jusqu'ici, Windows 11 27H2 avait fait parler de lui à travers les indiscrétions de journalistes bien renseignés, mais la prochaine version annuelle du système commence à laisser des traces plus concrètes. Le chercheur XenoPanther vient en effet de découvrir une référence explicite à 27H2 dans la toute dernière build expérimentale de Windows 11, publiée le 13 novembre. Une première qui donne un peu plus de consistance aux projets prêtés à Microsoft pour 2027.
Une référence à Windows 11 27H2 cachée dans les stratégies de groupe
C’est donc en fouillant les fichiers de la build 29708.1003 distribuée sur le canal expérimental Future Platforms, que XenoPanther a repéré une entrée baptisée SUPPORTED_Windows_11_27H2, accompagnée du libellé « Windows 11, version 27H2 or later ».
La référence figure dans le fichier Windows.adml, qui contient les textes utilisés par les modèles d’administration de Windows. Ces fichiers permettent aux équipes informatiques de gérer les stratégies de groupe, et servent entre autres à indiquer les versions minimales du système nécessaires pour appliquer une stratégie donnée.
On ignore toutefois à quel paramètre précis cette nouvelle entrée est associée, de même que le chercheur n’exclut pas une erreur dans le fichier, qui ne mentionne ni 26H1 ni 26H2.
Vers une refonte technique de Windows 11 en 2027
Cette découverte vient conforter les informations publiées ces derniers mois concernant la prochaine évolution majeure de Windows 11. Contrairement aux versions 25H2 et 26H2, qui reposent sur la même base technique que 24H2, 27H2 pourrait se traduire par une évolution plus profonde de l’architecture du système.
Microsoft chercherait en particulier à réunifier les deux branches de Windows 11 qui coexistent depuis l'arrivée de 26H1, version réservée aux nouveaux PC équipés de puces Snapdragon X2 ou NVIDIA RTX Spark. Développée sur un cœur Windows différent de celui de 26H2, elle ne permet pas aux machines concernées de migrer vers cette dernière version. Microsoft leur a toutefois promis une possibilité de mise à jour ultérieure, et 27H2 pourrait justement être l'occasion de ramener l'ensemble des appareils sur une base commune.
Une telle opération nécessiterait de remplacer une partie des composants du système, plutôt que de simplement activer des fonctionnalités déjà présentes, comme lors du passage de 25H2 à 26H2. Pour les utilisateurs et utilisatrices, cela signifierait une mise à jour de plusieurs gigaoctets et une installation plus longue, comparable à celle de 24H2 en 2024. Ce type de migration présente aussi davantage de risques de compatibilité avec les pilotes et les logiciels, ce qui pourrait inciter Microsoft à privilégier un déploiement progressif.
L'ampleur de cette mise à jour serait donc avant tout technique, sans nécessairement s'accompagner d'une multitude de nouveautés visibles. Microsoft distribue désormais une grande partie des nouvelles fonctionnalités de Windows au fil des mises à jour mensuelles, indépendamment des changements de version.

articles.title: SA crypto platform OVEX deploys AI fraud detection system built by DataProphet - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African crypto platform OVEX has gone live with a custom AI fraud detection system, built by machine learning consultancy DataProphet, that catches 98 per cent of fraudsters in testing.
Founded in 2017, OVEX offers South Africa’s largest selection of digital asset markets, and has partnered with several leading cryptocurrency companies and firms, including Invictus Capital, Hyperion, and TrueUSD.
DataProphet, meanwhile, was formed in 2014, and builds and runs custom machine learning for financial services, manufacturing, and other businesses. The two companies began working together back in April to replace OVEX’s rules-based fraud system with AI that learns how fraudsters behave.
Rather than judging an account from a snapshot, the system reads a user’s full activity history in sequence, including every login, deposit, trade and withdrawal. Two models, one trained on fraudulent behaviour and one on honest customers, assess which pattern each account more closely resembles. Accounts that lean towards the fraud model are flagged for investigation.
By late July, the model was catching 98 per cent of fraudsters in testing, compared with 75 per cent for the old system, and flagged 100 per cent of fraud cases it had never seen before. OVEX expects 99 per cent fewer false alarms and a 92 per cent reduction in undetected fraud. The platform also includes a tool showing investigators when an account’s behaviour turned suspicious, and a dashboard for retraining models.
“We partnered with DataProphet for their deep machine-learning expertise and they’ve built a system tailored to our platform, giving us a far more sophisticated way to identify fraud as it evolves,” said Jonathan Ovadia, chief executive of OVEX.
“Our partnership with OVEX proves that applied AI doesn’t have to be a black box or a heavy compliance burden,” said Ridwaan Seedat, CEO of DataProphet.

articles.title: Ce nouveau réfrigérateur vous rappelle les aliments à consommer
articles.text:
Xiaomi prépare les glaçons avec son nouveau réfrigérateur connecté de 546 litres
Froid devant !
Avec son Mijia Refrigerator Pro Multi-Door 546L, Xiaomi associe un grand volume de rangement à une fabrique de glaçons pilotable depuis le téléphone. Deux configurations sont prévues, avec des portes ou des tiroirs pour le congélateur.
Préparer les glaçons avant de rentrer est l'un des usages proposés par ce réfrigérateur un peu différent du système des frigos américains. Depuis Xiaomi Home, on peut programmer leur fabrication, choisir un mode et recevoir une alerte lorsque le bac est plein ou que l'eau manque.
Xiaomi Mijia Refrigerator Pro Multi-Door 546L
- 
                    
                        Samsung RB53DG703ES9 Meilleur prix : 833.2 €Voir le produit
- 
                    
                        Hisense RQ760N4IFE SmartScreen Meilleur prix : 2493.56 €Voir le produit
La version "French Door", avec congélateur à tiroirs, peut stocker jusqu'à 180 glaçons, contre 140 pour la "Cross Door" à portes. Xiaomi annonce un mode rapide en 55 minutes. Le premier cycle complet peut être plus long, ce délai ne correspond pas au remplissage du bac. Un nettoyage automatique est aussi au programme.
À chacun son froid
Les 546 l s'accompagnent d'un réglage indépendant des températures du réfrigérateur et du congélateur. Le système Dual Cooling Fresh doit aussi limiter les transferts d'odeurs entre les deux espaces. Deux bacs à humidité régulée visent à préserver les fruits et légumes, tandis qu'un dispositif sert à réduire les odeurs.
L'application permet de régler les températures, de consigner les aliments par compartiment et de recevoir des rappels d'échéance. Xiaomi ne précise toutefois aucune reconnaissance automatique du contenu. L'inventaire ne se fera donc pas tout seul.
L'appareil peut prendre place dans 60 cm de profondeur, possède un refroidissement par le bas et un faible dégagement latéral pour faciliter l'alignement avec les meubles. La commercialisation du réfrigérateur est prévue en décembre prochain à partir de 1299 € en version Cross Door, et de 1399 € en French Door.

articles.title: Xiaomi Smart Band 11 ya es oficial: pantalla de 2.000 nits, hasta 21 días de batería y versiones con NFC para pagar desde la muñeca
articles.text:
La familia Smart Band de Xiaomi lleva años siendo la puerta de entrada favorita para quienes quieren monitorizar su actividad física sin gastar lo que cuesta un reloj inteligente completo. Con el lanzamiento de la nueva Xiaomi Smart Band 11, la marca da un paso adelante en materiales, visibilidad en exteriores y conectividad, presentando una gama dividida en cuatro versiones que parten desde los 59,99 euros y que, esta vez sí, vuelve a traer variantes oficiales con NFC para pagar desde la muñeca.
XIAOMI Smart Band 11, pulsera de actividad
Pantalla más brillante, biseles simétricos y salto en materiales
A nivel estético, Xiaomi sigue alejando a su pulsera de la apariencia puramente deportiva para acercarla más a un accesorio de diario. El frontal monta una pantalla AMOLED de 1,72 pulgadas con biseles simétricos muy reducidos y un brillo pico que sube hasta los 2.000 nits, una cifra propia de relojes mucho más caros que asegura una lectura cómoda incluso a pleno sol.
Sensores más precios, seguimiento en piscina e HyperOS 4
En el interior, esta nueva pulsera de actividad de Xiaomi estrena un nuevo sensor PPG de doble LED y doble fotodiodo que, según las pruebas internas de la marca, alcanza una precisión de hasta el 98,2% en la medición de frecuencia cardíaca.
Mantiene la resistencia al agua de 5 ATM, pero añade monitorización del pulso también bajo el agua, algo especialmente útil para quienes nadan de forma habitual. En total, registra más de 150 modos deportivos (con detección automática de seis actividades) e incorpora el indicador Vitality Score para resumir el estado físico reciente.
El análisis del descanso también se actualiza con Sleep Algorithm 2.0, capaz de medir la variabilidad de la frecuencia cardíaca nocturna y generar informes semanales y mensuales con consejos prácticos sobre hábitos que afectan al sueño.
Todo ello queda gobernado por el sistema operativo Xiaomi HyperOS 4, que además de renovar los menús introduce una función muy curiosa: permite vincular la pulsera de forma simultánea a un móvil Xiaomi compatible y a un iPhone para recibir notificaciones de ambos teléfonos en la muñeca.
En autonomía, Xiaomi promete hasta 21 días de uso ligero en la edición estándar y 18 días en las versiones con NFC (que en uso real con notificaciones activas y entrenamientos semanales se traducirán previsiblemente en torno a semana y media o dos semanas reales).
Estas son las diferentes versiones disponibles
Desde ya, puedes comprar en la tienda online de Xiaomi esta nueva pulsera de actividad, la cual llega disponible en un amplio abanico de acabados:
- Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Standard Edition (59,99 euros): cuenta con marco de aluminio y llega en negro, plateado, rosa, morado y dorado.
XIAOMI Smart Band 11, pulsera de actividad
- Xiaomi Smart Band 11 NFC Edition (79,99 euros): añade chip NFC para pagos sin contacto y está disponible en negro, plateado y rosa.
Xiaomi Smart Band 11 NFC
- Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Unibody Edition (89,99 euros): apuesta por un cuerpo fabricado íntegramente en metal en acabado morado (también con NFC).
Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Unibody
- Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Ceramic Edition (89,99 euros): la opción más elegante de la familia, con acabado cerámico en color blanco perla y conectividad NFC.
