articles.title: Your complete guide to AWS Quick at AWS re:Invent 2026 | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Your complete guide to AWS Quick at AWS re:Invent 2026
AWS Quick is the AI workspace built only for work, where the dashboards, agents, and automations one person creates are available to everyone on the team. Built on AWS with enterprise security and governance from the start, Quick connects to the data and applications you use every day. At AWS re:Invent 2026 (November 30 to December 4), customers including Allianz, Cox Automotive, Mondelez, DXC, and Southwest Airlines, join AWS leaders on stage to share how they govern, extend and scale Quick across their teams. Whether you’re a business or technology leader, a builder, or part of an IT, security, data, or analytics team, use this guide to find the sessions that fit your goals.
Explore the session catalog and learn more.
Keynote
Join AWS CEO Matt Garman for the re:Invent 2026 CEO Keynote on Tuesday from 8:30 AM – 10:30 AM PT as he shares the latest innovations powering the agentic era. From AI infrastructure and inference to data, agent platforms, and the software agents AWS is building, see how AWS gives you the depth, breadth, and integration to build what’s next with new announcements and stories from customers already doing it.
Can’t make it to Las Vegas? Watch 50+ sessions live on the AWS re:Invent livestream, including keynotes, talks, and labs.
Breakout sessions
Hear directly from customers about how they deployed AWS Quick, from first rollout to enterprise scale, and what they learned along the way.
BIZ216: AI assistant for public sector: Governance without compromise with AWS Quick
Monday, Nov 30 | 10:00 AM PST
Speakers: Rima Olinger, Sonali Sahu, Mike Shore-Nye
Public sector organizations serve diverse populations with strict boundaries: students and administrators, citizens and case workers, patients and providers. They need AI that works across these groups without compromising data isolation, compliance, or governance. Multi-tenant environments demand security frameworks most AI assistants were not built to meet. Hear from a higher education customer who faced these constraints and displaced their incumbent tool in favor of AWS Quick’s governance-first architecture: tenant-level data isolation, role-based access controls across distinct user populations, and compliance frameworks built for regulated environments. Learn why existing solutions fell short, how Quick’s native governance model met their requirements without custom engineering, and what the transition looked like from decision to deployment.
BIZ219: How a brand turned AI governance into a strategic advantage with AWS Quick
Monday, Nov 30 | 10:00 AM PST
Speakers: Steve Vinsik, Mark Huber, Katie Travis
In automotive, data isolation is not optional. You serve thousands of dealer clients who compete with each other, handle consumer financial data under FTC Safeguards rules, and operate across state privacy boundaries. Most AI tools cannot enforce tenant-level separation between competing dealers, restrict access by franchise agreement, or prove compliance across jurisdictions. Hear from a customer who turned that constraint into an advantage: they built a governance model with AWS Quick that enforces fine-grained data permissions across their dealer network, role-based access controls by business function, and audit frameworks that satisfy regulators and competitive separation requirements. Learn how they validated it against compliance requirements, and how governance became the reason they deployed faster than competitors still waiting on security approval.
BIZ112: From zero to 20,000 desktops: Getting started with AWS Quick
Monday, Nov 30 | 12:00 PM PST
Speakers: Jose Kunnackal John
Your team is drowning in context-switching: toggling between email, documents, data tools, and chat only to complete a single task. Productivity tools promise to help, but most add complexity instead of removing it. In this fireside chat, hear from customers who faced that exact challenge and deployed an AI assistant across 20,000+ users in under 90 days. Learn what convinced their leadership to invest, how they integrated AI into daily workflows without disrupting existing tools, and what the first 90 days of adoption actually looked like. Walk away with a practical roadmap for bringing AWS Quick AI assistant to your workforce at scale.
BIZ214: Empowering 200,000 people without compromising trust: AWS Quick
Tuesday, Dec 1 | 4:30 PM PST
Speakers: Ben Haller, Raji Sivasubramaniam, Axel Schell
Allianz needed to empower 200,000 employees with AI without sacrificing trust. With operations across dozens of regulated markets, the security, privacy, and works council requirements were non-negotiable. Every stakeholder asked the same question: how do you move fast and still earn the trust of those guarding your company’s security? Hear how Allianz partnered with AWS to deploy the capabilities that make AWS Quick enterprise-ready: protection of confidential information, structured approval workflows for agentic actions, custom branding per business unit, and multi-language support. Learn how Allianz navigated the full approval process and moved from “not yet” to “go” in six weeks.
BIZ217: One AI assistant, every data source: Unifying access with AWS Quick
Wednesday, Dec 2 | 4:00 PM PST
Speakers: David Provan, Jess Wang, Jesse Gebhardt
Your data lives in one platform. Your reports live in another. Your documents live somewhere else. Every time someone needs an answer, they spend time figuring out where to look before they can act. Decisions slow down. Teams duplicate work because they cannot find what already exists. New employees take months to become productive because institutional knowledge is trapped in systems they do not know how to navigate. Hear from a customer who solved this by giving their team a single AI assistant that connects across all their enterprise systems. Instead of training people on where to find information, they ask AWS Quick and get answers grounded in their real business data, regardless of where it lives. Learn how they configured the integration, how their teams adopted it, and what changed about the speed and quality of decision-making across the organization.
BIZ113: Getting started with AWS Quick: How a customer went from curious to deployed
Thursday, Dec 3 | 12:00 PM PST
Speakers: Leo Ohannesian, Justin Bundick, Peter Hunn
Your team spends hours on work that should take minutes: summarizing meetings, drafting documents, finding answers buried across systems, pulling data from multiple platforms. You know AI should help, but you need to see it work in a real environment before you commit. In this session, see how a customer put AWS Quick into daily workflows across their organization and watch live as it composes documents, analyzes data, summarizes conversations, and connects to enterprise systems. Hear what problems they were solving, what changed for their teams after deployment, and what surprised them about adoption. Leave with a clear picture of the problems Quick solves and how to evaluate whether it fits your organization.
BIZ213: Accelerating AI adoption and realized value with AWS Quick
Thursday, Dec 3 | 1:30 PM PST
Speakers: Neal Cauley, John Brock, Stefan Schulz
You deployed an AI assistant. Your team tried it for a week and stopped. The tool could not access the systems where real work happens, gave generic answers because it was disconnected from your enterprise context, and security would not approve broader rollout because the governance story was unclear. That is where most AI deployments stall. Hear from a customer who lived that exact cycle: low adoption, frustrated leadership, and a growing sense that the investment was wasted. They evaluated multiple alternatives and made the switch to AWS Quick, an AI assistant with governed access to enterprise data, native connectors to the systems their teams already use, and agentic workflows that span business units. Learn what broke in their first deployment, what they looked for in a replacement, and how governed data access turned single-digit adoption into organization-wide usage.
BIZ215: From pilot to enterprise scale with AWS Quick
Thursday, Dec 3 | 4:00 PM PST
Speakers: Rekha Seshadrinathan, Gayatri Ohri, Michael Murphy
Your AI pilot proved value with a small team. Now you need to deploy across the organization without a dedicated rollout team and without losing what made it work. Hear from a customer who scaled AWS Quick from an initial deployment to thousands of users across their enterprise. Learn the phased strategy they used to expand Quick’s capabilities: connecting teams to enterprise data, automating repetitive workflows, and rolling out agentic features that kept usage growing after the initial adoption wave. Discover what metrics justified continued investment and the operational model they built so scaling Quick did not create a support burden for IT. Walk away with a repeatable framework for taking AWS Quick from proof-of-concept to production deployment across your organization.
BIZ218: From AI tasks to autonomous multi-agent workflows with AWS Quick
Thursday, Dec 3 | 4:00 PM PST
Speakers: Ramon Lopez, Mike Hogan
The workflows that matter most in financial services span multiple systems, require multiple types of expertise, and today rely on people as the coordination layer. One person pulls data, another reviews it for compliance, a third routes it for approval. That coordination tax is where your team’s time disappears. AWS Quick changes that equation. Instead of one AI assistant doing one task, specialized agents each handle their piece and hand off to the next automatically. The human stays in the loop for judgment calls, not for data gathering and routing. Hear from a customer who moved from standalone AI use cases to compound, multi-agent workflows with AWS Quick. Learn how they identified which workflows to orchestrate first, how they designed agent handoffs that satisfy compliance, and what it means now that the coordination layer runs autonomously.
Chalk talks
Whiteboard architectures and trade-offs with the AWS Quick product and solutions teams. Bring your toughest questions.
BIZ306: Bring your own ontology: Ground AWS Quick in enterprise context
Monday, Nov 30 | 10:00 AM PST
Speakers: Tom Ron, Fatima Khakwani
Enterprise questions rarely have answers in a single document. Your business runs on connections: customers to products, teams to processes, and risks to regulations. But vector search doesn’t see any of that. In this chalk talk, we show how to ground AWS Quick in your enterprise context by integrating it with a knowledge graph built from your domain knowledge. We’ll walk through how we built this pattern using GraphRAG for real customers and the results they achieved. Then we’ll open the whiteboard. Bring your toughest use case and we’ll sketch your ontology live, showing how Quick would traverse it to deliver better answers.
BIZ323: Decision frameworks, evaluation, and cost management with AWS Quick
Monday, Nov 30 | 10:30 AM PST
Tuesday, Dec 1 | 2:30 PM PST (repeat)
Speakers: Sagar Rao, Sandhya Khanderia
Moving from one agent to enterprise-wide automation means choosing the right path (Flows, Automate, Custom Agents, persistent agents) and the right trigger model. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard a decision framework that bakes in evaluation and cost management from the start, not as afterthoughts. We’ll connect orchestration across 25+ connectors, skills, and workstreams to measurable outcomes and dollars. Bring your automation backlog. You’ll leave with a decision matrix, eval harness, and a return on investment (ROI) story.
BIZ307: Architect AI-powered analytics with AWS Quick across your data platforms
Monday, Nov 30 | 12:00 PM PST
Speakers: Vignessh Baskaran, Jackson Dowden
As organizations adopt AI-powered analytics, they need architectures that connect business intelligence (BI) and conversational AI experiences to their existing data platforms. In this session we’ll diagram architectural patterns for connecting AWS Quick to structured data sources and integrating with third-party catalogs and semantic layers. We’ll compare the available connectivity approaches, including data sources and action connectors based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and discuss when to use each. Considerations will span production use cases like BI dashboards, embedded analytics, text-to-SQL Q&A, and agentic workflows. Together we’ll tackle real-world integration challenges including authentication, performance optimization, and governance. This session is ideal for architects and technical leaders looking to build AI-powered analytics across their data platforms.
BIZ404: Teaching Quick to remember and connect with memory and knowledge graphs
Monday, Nov 30 | 1:30 PM PST
Speakers: Thomas Delteil, Adi Kalyanpur
Every conversation with an AI assistant starts from scratch. Your agent doesn’t remember what worked yesterday, can’t tell you who owns a project without searching again, and repeats the same mistakes because failures are never captured. In this chalk talk, we show how AWS Quick breaks out of statelessness with two primitives: a continuous-learning memory layer where a background agent extracts reusable knowledge after each session and scores it with a probabilistic confidence model, and a personal knowledge graph that connects people, projects, decisions, and evidence across your tools so the agent has a map of your world before it reads a single document. We’ll whiteboard the architecture and the tradeoffs that shaped it, then open it up. Bring your hardest questions about memory staleness, confidence calibration, graph noise, or making agents that actually get better over time.
BIZ305: Security: Zero-trust identity and data protection in the agentic era
Monday, Nov 30 | 2:30 PM PST
Speakers: Priya Kakarla, Munish Gopal
Security reviews stall AI rollouts more than any capability gap, and agentic AI raises the bar. This chalk talk goes past “is it secure?” to the architecture that gets a CISO to yes. We’ll whiteboard the full identity path: single sign-on (SSO) through providers like Okta and Ping, with end-user identity propagated to the data so authorization is enforced per user, in real time, across 1P AWS and 3P sources. Then we extend that trust to agents: agent identity, deterministic policy checks on every tool call, and data protection: Purview DLP, default guardrails, deny-by-default, and full SIEM auditability.
BIZ310: Secure and scalable multi-tenant deployment patterns for AWS Quick
Monday, Nov 30 | 3:00 PM PST
Speakers: Chin Rane, Vineet Kachhawaha
As organizations scale their adoption of AWS Quick across business units, subsidiaries, and partner ecosystems, deploying a secure multi-tenant architecture becomes critical. This chalk talk explores proven deployment patterns that balance tenant isolation, governance, and operational efficiency when rolling out AWS Quick at enterprise scale. We will walk through two primary isolation strategies: multi-account separation using AWS Organizations for environment-level boundaries (dev/staging/prod), and namespace-based logical isolation within a single account for user-cohort segmentation.
BIZ304: Building and governing apps on Quick
Monday, Nov 30 | 4:00 PM PST
Speakers: Shane Thompson, Art Chan
Anyone can generate apps from a sentence. The hard part is governing them and getting them in front of the right users. This chalk talk whiteboards the full lifecycle of AWS Quick Apps: building them from natural language with no separate hosting, wiring in data and actions through MCP, and the three sharing paths: private, public URLs, and enterprise sharing gated behind admin approval workflows.
BIZ303: One context layer, every surface: Enterprise knowledge for agents that work anywhere
Thursday, Dec 3 | 12:00 PM PST
Speakers: Suren Raju, Josh DeMuth
Your AI agents are only as smart as the data they can reach. In most enterprises, that data is scattered across dozens of systems, siloed, ungoverned, and invisible to the agents that need it most. In this chalk talk, we architect a context layer from the ground up: connecting enterprise knowledge into a unified index, then enriching that foundation with a knowledge graph that maps organizational relationships, business rules, and domain context, giving agents permission-scoped, relationship-aware intelligence at runtime. Then we take that intelligence to where users work: browser, desktop, mobile, collaboration tools, and productivity suites. Each surface independently governed yet sharing one agent identity, one memory, and one set of guardrails. Bring your architecture. We’ll whiteboard the end-to-end path together.
Workshops
Get hands-on with AWS Quick. Bring your laptop. You’ll leave with something working.
INV001: Ctrl+Alt+Ship: Hands-On with AWS Quick, Kiro, and Amazon Connect Customer
Walk-up, available all week
Speakers: Michelle Koh, Anupa Bhattacharyya, Christopher Lott 
Ctrl+Alt+Ship is a walk-up, self-paced lab area open all week (Nov 30 – Dec 4) in the Venetian Level 2 ballroom. No reservation is needed and workstations are provided. Attendees pick a track (Kiro, Quick or Connect) and a level, 200 or 400. Both Quick labs are business simulations where Quick connects to the company’s business systems through MCP. In the L200 Kōji Fresh lab, attendees lead the response to a product-safety crisis at a fictional Singapore food company. They investigate across email, CRM, social and supply chain, brief the board and supplier, run a recall across three systems from one instruction, and turn five data exports into board-ready charts. In the L400 SkyNova Airlines lab, 14 passengers have fallen ill overnight and an influencer is blaming the airline. Attendees use Quick across six systems to find the pattern and brief the board. They then rebook stranded passengers within a hard budget, build a Flow that runs the recovery for a grounded flight, and ship a Quick App for the airport transfer desk. Facilitators will be on hand to help.
BIZ312: Build AI-powered analytics with conversational BI on AWS Quick
Tuesday, Dec 1 | 3:30 PM PST
Speakers: Neeraj Kumar, Salim Khan
Construct a complete AI-powered analytics pipeline, from data ingestion to conversational consumption. Use AWS Quick’s Data Catalog to discover data, query it live without moving it into SPICE, then enrich and import metadata with semantics inherited to build natural-language Q&A. In this hands-on workshop, you start with seven raw banking tables: no catalog, no definitions. An agent inspects the data and builds the catalog for you. You ask questions in plain English and get answers. An agent generates a dashboard showing which top customers are slipping. Another agent, aware of the bank’s compliance rules, checks every offer before it ships. Then you automate the full response as a Quick Flow and wrap it in a custom app your team can use. You leave with a working banking command center that agents built, and that you can rebuild in your own account using conversational analytics.
BIZ313: Build agentic automations for business processes with AWS Quick Automate
Wednesday, Dec 2 | 12:00 PM PST

In this session, learn how to build an automation using AWS Quick Automate. Through a financial services example, explore how specialized AI agents work together to handle complex interactions across web pages and business applications. You’ll create a production-ready automation featuring custom agents that use knowledge and tools to transform a merchant onboarding process. Using Quick Automate’s chat-based authoring and visual studio, you’ll configure a workflow with multiple agents, integrate with multiple tools, test and debug the workflow, and then deploy it using robust enterprise controls. Walk away knowing how to develop agentic automations for real-world use cases.
BIZ311: Master agent skills: From desktop builds to production deployment

articles.title: Ars Live: What do drone strikes on data centers mean for the future? Talk at 1 pm EST today
articles.text:
Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend represents a new concern for Big Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life.
To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled “Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech” on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts.
Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans.
This year, Jarnecki has written about Iran’s drone and missile strikes on Amazon data centers in the Middle East during the US-Israeli war with Iran, and the broader implications for governments and Big Tech. He has also commented on the impacts of Russia and Ukraine exchanging strikes on each other’s data centers.

articles.title: Qwik 2.0 RC: Replaces HTML Comment Markers for Faster Reactivity and Out-of-Order Streaming
articles.text:
Qwik, the resumable JavaScript framework originally created at Builder.io, has released its 2.0 Release Candidate, targeting a rewrite of how the framework encodes resumable state in server-rendered HTML and introducing experimental out-of-order streaming. The RC was published on 1st October 2026 as @qwik.dev/core@2.0.0-rc.0, around two years and eight months after the initial Towards Qwik 2.0 design article.
In v1, Qwik propagated state updates by sprinkling HTML comment markers such as <!--qv--> and <!--t=8--> throughout the rendered body to flag component boundaries and the text nodes a signal should update. That approach forced a single ordered write pass, added CPU and memory overhead, and made out-of-order streaming impossible because a slow fetch blocked everything after it. In v2 the comments are gone, with state and virtual node information instead compressed into two <script type="qwik/state"> and <script type="qwik/vnode"> blocks at the end of the document.
On Qwik's internal runs of js-framework-benchmark, v2 posts a weighted geometric mean of 1.23 times slower than vanilla JavaScript, ahead of Vue 3.5 at 1.25x, Angular 22 at 1.42x, React 19 with the compiler at 1.53x, and v1 itself at 2.59x. A detailed classmethod walkthrough that built the same starter against both versions reported server-rendered HTML went from 60 comments to zero, with JavaScript required before interactivity dropping from 59KB to 9KB, though total bundle size grew.
Out-of-order HTML streaming has also been added n experimental mode. Developers can wrap slow regions in <Pending> and <Catch> boundaries so the server sends the rest of the page immediately and streams the real content later in the same response, with a small inline script swapping it into place. The APIs are opt-in through vite.config.ts:
qwikVite({ experimental: ['pendingBoundary', 'catchBoundary', 'blockSSR'] })
useComputed$ now accepts async functions, replacing <Resource>, and route loaders gain their own JSON endpoints with cacheControl and eTag options so the browser can cache them individually and <Link> can prefetch data on hover. Other additions include a worker$ primitive for Web Workers, reactify$ for embedding Qwik components inside React trees, server-only *.server.ts files, and HMR that preserves signal and store values across edits.
In a Reddit discussion predating the v2 RC, one developer called the lack of out-of-order streaming a significant limitation and argued that the Qwik team should be more upfront about it. Another commenter suggested that streaming could be a future feature. In his Classmethod walkthrough, Hiroshi Morishige noted the long wait for v2, it reached alpha in November 2024 and beta in June 2025, while v1 continued to receive updates through 1.20.1 in September 2026. He also noted that SvelteKit 3 and Remix 3.0 released stable versions on the same day as Qwik's RC, with the three releases published within seven hours. Qwik 2 and SvelteKit 3 use Vite 8; Remix 3 is independent of Vite.
The team says the breaking changes are small and automated by pnpm qwik migrate-v2, which also handles the move to the new @qwik.dev/core and @qwik.dev/router package names. New projects can scaffold with pnpm create qwik@rc, and the RC can be explored via next.qwik.dev/examples or the online playground.
Qwik is an open-source resumable framework that serialises state and event listeners into HTML, then lazily loads component JavaScript only in response to user interaction. The project is MIT licensed and developed openly on GitHub.

articles.title: Abdullah Snobar steps down as head of DMZ |
articles.text:
After 11 years at the helm of Toronto Metropolitan University’s (TMU) DMZ incubator, executive director Abdullah Snobar is stepping away.
The news: DMZ announced Snobar’s departure on Monday, outlining that he would vacate both his positions as executive director and his role as CEO of DMZ Ventures, the incubator’s venture capital division. Snobar will remain in his role through November to support the leadership transition. TMU said details as to who would take on the role of interim leader at DMZ would be forthcoming.
From the source: “When I stepped into this role, I believed Canadian founders could build companies that compete with anyone in the world if they had the right support behind them,” Snobar said in a statement on DMZ’s website. “The founders who’ve come through DMZ have proven that again and again.”
The context: Snobar took the helm of DMZ in 2015, replacing former director Valerie Fox. His tenure at the incubator was marked by expanding programming for startups, including launching several program streams for underserved demographics and founders, like DMZ’s Black Innovation Programs, Women Innovation Programs, and the Launchpad for Indigenous Entrepreneurs. Under Snobar’s leadership, DMZ also established its own investment fund, DMZ Ventures, and the Centre for Housing Innovation, with a focus on investing in housing property tech startups.
RELATED: How turning down $1 million changed the DMZ
Final thought: Under Snobar’s guidance, DMZ has grown into a globally recognized organization and was ranked as the number one university-based incubator worldwide by UBI Global in 2018. Since 2015, its reach has grown to include 15 countries, including partnerships and programs based in Asia, Latin America, and Africa. To date, the incubator has helped raise more than $3 billion in financing for more than 800 startups.

articles.title: AI models can be tricked into identifying civilians as military targets by telling them it's a game | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Some AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and other leading AI labs could be easily tricked into identifying targets for military strikes — even if they include civilians or locations like schools — simply by being told they’re playing a game, according to a new research report by Vals.
Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluation startup, tested whether leading AI models could be manipulated into participating in autonomous warfare. Researchers used simulated scenarios and a combination of generated and real imagery from Ukraine and Iran to see if the AI models would mark targets in drone and satellite imagery.
The models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, and other companies frequently identified potential targets in drone and satellite imagery, including civilians and surrendering soldiers. When the models refused to cooperate, researchers were able to jailbreak them by claiming the battlefield scenarios were part of a game.
The findings come amid growing fears about the immediate risks posed by AI, beyond the existential threats associated with artificial general intelligence.
Earlier this year, Anthropic became embroiled in a dispute with the Department of Defense after it told the agency it could not use Anthropic’s technology for mass surveillance of Americans or autonomous warfare. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has insisted that today’s AI systems aren’t reliable enough to make life-or-death decisions without a human in the loop. Meanwhile, the Pentagon argued it should be able to deploy the technology for any lawful military purpose.
The new research raises further questions about whether AI companies are capable of preventing their models from being used in warfare.
Ironically, AI models from Anthropic performed the worst in these simulated scenarios. But none of the models performed particularly well. None of the researchers’ requests were blocked by a safety classifier, and refusals were uncommon. Even when models did refuse, they often complied after being told they were playing a game.
Anthropic spokesperson Eduardo Maia Silva told TechCrunch the company appreciates Vals’ report, recommendations, and collaboration, and acknowledged that the outcomes were not acceptable.
“The examples in the report are very clearly against our rules and we have banned and will ban users when we see this behavior,” according to an emailed company statement sent by Silva. “Even for authorized settings, Anthropic has long been firm that today’s frontier AI systems are not reliable enough to power fully autonomous weapons.”
Anthropic told TechCrunch that its teams were already developing additional safeguards before the report was published and that those measures would be in place soon. Anthropic is also expanding its own testing and enhancing safeguards and enforcement to address any gaps it finds.
OpenAI spokesperson Nate Evans told TechCrunch the company prohibits using its public models to facilitate violence or for unapproved national security purposes, including in the scenarios Vals simulated.
“We actively detect and disrupt misuse, including by suspending accounts that violate our policies,” OpenAI said in an emailed statement. “We’re also developing additional safeguards for our public models against misuse involving drones and drone software.”
Vals notes in the report that the models were never asked to directly make strike decisions, a task the researchers said the models would typically refuse. That doesn’t mean their outputs couldn’t have dire or fatal consequences in the real world. For instance, targeting information could be used by autonomous weapons systems.
In some scenarios, the models were asked to report whether people were visible. Positive reports were followed by simulated strikes and the models would see the consequences.
The report relies on commercial models from frontier AI labs, not the models those companies might provide to the military. It’s not clear whether the additional safeguards would apply to military use, though.
Vals also noted that technical challenges, including latency and limited onboard computing capacity, make it difficult to use general-purpose AI models for live drone targeting. Those constraints make their deployment in combat less of an immediate threat.
A more immediate threat, the researchers say, is that AI models could be used to annotate battlefield footage at scale, producing training data for autonomous targeting systems.
For instance, researchers relied on real satellite imagery of an Iranian school that was bombed by the U.S. in February 2026, killing more than 150 civilians. Bloomberg later reported that an “overreliance on AI” contributed to the strike. In Vals’ testing, models frequently marked the school, which sat next to a military complex, as a strike target, with Claude Opus 5.5 selecting the school in 69% of ordinary trials and 72% of game-framed trials.
Anthropic no longer has an active Pentagon contract, but other companies, including SpaceXAI, OpenAI, and Google do. A recent Congressional Research Service report found that the Pentagon is not known to be using any frontier AI model in autonomous weapons systems directly.
TechCrunch has also reached out to Meta, Google, Thinking Machines Lab, and SpaceXAI for comment.

articles.title: STJ suspende decisão que proibia Uber de cobrar taxa semanal de motoristas
articles.text:
O Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ) suspendeu provisoriamente a decisão que obrigava a Uber a interromper, em todo o país, seu programa de cobrança de taxa fixa semanal dos motoristas parceiros. A medida representa reviravolta na disputa envolvendo o modelo, que havia sido barrado pela Justiça do Trabalho na semana passada.
A decisão foi assinada na noite de segunda-feira (16) pelo ministro Raul Araújo e atende a pedido da própria Uber do Brasil Tecnologia Ltda. A empresa apresentou ao STJ conflito de competência envolvendo a Justiça do Trabalho e a Justiça comum em processos relacionados ao programa.
Com isso, os efeitos da liminar concedida pela 9ª Vara do Trabalho de Salvador (BA) ficam suspensos até que o tribunal decida qual ramo do Judiciário deve analisar o caso.
A decisão, porém, não representa aval definitivo ao modelo de cobrança nem resolve as acusações feitas contra a empresa.
O que é o Passe para Motoristas da Uber?
- O programa funciona como uma espécie de assinatura. Em vez de pagar porcentagem sobre cada corrida realizada, o motorista pode desembolsar valor fixo semanal para utilizar a plataforma durante determinado período;
- A iniciativa foi alvo de ação civil pública apresentada pelo Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) contra a Uber;
- Na ocasião, a Justiça do Trabalho entendeu que o modelo poderia impor prejuízos financeiros aos motoristas cadastrados na plataforma e determinou a suspensão imediata do programa em todo o território nacional;
- A ordem também proibia novas adesões, renovações de contratos e a continuidade das cobranças relacionadas ao Passe para Motoristas;
- Segundo o MPT, o modelo poderia transferir riscos econômicos da atividade para os trabalhadores, inclusive com cobranças em semanas de baixa demanda;
- A Uber, por outro lado, argumentou que a adesão ao programa é voluntária e que a modalidade oferece maior previsibilidade financeira aos parceiros.
Leia mais:
- Uber lança recurso que facilita embarque de idosos e pessoas com deficiência
- Uber quer colocar mais de dois mil robotáxis nas ruas até o fim de 2027
- Uber confirma acesso indevido a dados após falha em fornecedor
Por que o STJ suspendeu a decisão?
Ao analisar o pedido da Uber, o ministro Raul Araújo considerou que existe risco de decisões conflitantes entre diferentes ramos do Judiciário sobre o mesmo programa.
Isso porque, enquanto a Justiça do Trabalho determinou a suspensão nacional do Passe para Motoristas, processos na Justiça Estadual discutem a validade dos contratos firmados pelos motoristas que aderiram ao modelo e os efeitos dessas relações contratuais.
Na avaliação do magistrado, existe um “efetivo risco de prolação de comandos potencialmente incompatíveis” entre as ações em andamento.
Por esse motivo, ele determinou três medidas:
- Paralisação temporária dos processos citados no conflito de competência;
- Suspensão provisória das decisões tomadas nesses casos;
- Restauração da situação existente antes da implementação das medidas questionadas.
Qual Justiça deve julgar o caso?
Outro ponto central da decisão é justamente a definição de qual ramo do Judiciário tem competência para analisar a controvérsia.
Raul Araújo afirmou que há indícios de que parte relevante das discussões envolvendo o Passe para Motoristas possui natureza contratual e civil.
O ministro também citou precedentes da Segunda Seção do STJ, segundo os quais disputas entre plataformas digitais e motoristas de aplicativo podem ser julgadas pela Justiça comum quando não envolvem pedidos de reconhecimento de vínculo empregatício ou pagamento de verbas trabalhistas.
Segundo a avaliação apresentada na decisão, os motoristas que entraram com ações individuais relacionadas ao programa não buscavam inicialmente o reconhecimento de uma relação de emprego, mas discutiam obrigações decorrentes dos contratos firmados com a plataforma.
O magistrado ressaltou, contudo, que a suspensão tem caráter provisório e não representa decisão definitiva sobre a legalidade do programa ou sobre a natureza jurídica da relação entre a Uber e os motoristas.
“A providência ora examinada possui natureza estritamente conservativa, não importando pronunciamento definitivo acerca da licitude e da natureza jurídica do Programa ‘Passe para Motoristas'”, registrou.
O que acontece agora?
As partes envolvidas terão dez dias para prestar informações ao STJ. Depois disso, o processo será encaminhado ao Ministério Público Federal, que deverá apresentar parecer antes da análise definitiva do conflito de competência.
Em manifestação, a Uber disse ter recebido a decisão favoravelmente e reiterou seu entendimento de que o programa é opcional e foi desenvolvido para oferecer mais previsibilidade financeira aos motoristas parceiros.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Cómo jugar ‘GTA 6’ un día antes en España y Latinoamérica con el "truco de Nueva Zelanda"
articles.text:
GTA 6 estará disponible el próximo jueves 19 de noviembre, pero no tendrá un lanzamiento en simultáneo sino que estará disponible a partir de la medianoche local de cada país. Esto implica que, indefectiblemente, en algunos mercados estará disponible unas cuantas horas antes que en otros. Sin embargo, existe una opción muy útil para cortar esa brecha, y se trata ni más ni menos del "truco de Nueva Zelanda" para PS5 y Xbox Series X|S.
Debido a su ubicación en el planeta, Nueva Zelanda será el primer país (o uno de los primeros, como mínimo) en cruzar la barrera del 18 al 19 de noviembre. De esta manera, sus habitantes van a poder desbloquear el acceso a GTA 6 bastante antes que los jugadores ubicados en Europa y el continente americano.
La buena noticia es que para disfrutar de GTA 6 desde el primer minuto no es necesario que te tomes un avión hacia Oceanía. El truco de Nueva Zelanda permite modificar los ajustes de tu consola para hacerle creer a los sistemas de Xbox y PlayStation que te encuentras en ese país, obteniendo acceso anticipado a lo nuevo de Rockstar Games.
Por supuesto que esto no es algo nuevo, ni tampoco descubierto para el lanzamiento de GTA 6. El truco de Nueva Zelanda es algo que se suele aprovechar cada vez que existe un lanzamiento de primer nivel. Claro que al ser el nuevo Grand Theft Auto el juego más anticipado de la historia, será la primera vez de muchos para implementarlo.
El truco de Nueva Zelanda para jugar GTA 6 un día antes
El truco de Nueva Zelanda está disponible tanto en Xbox Series X|S como en PS5, lo cual es una muy buena noticia. Desafortunadamente, el método no es el mismo en ambas plataformas. Si planeas jugar GTA 6 desde las consolas de Microsoft, estás de parabienes porque es la que tiene los pasos a seguir más sencillos. En el caso de que utilices la de Sony, la cosa se complica un poco y requiere de pasos más enrevesados.
Independientemente de qué consolas uses, los procedimientos valen la pena. Si estás en España u otros países que utilicen la hora central europea, podrás jugar GTA 6 a partir del mediodía del miércoles 18 de noviembre; es decir, con 12 horas de anticipación al horario de debut formal para la región. En el caso de que estés en Argentina u otros países sudamericanos dentro del mismo huso horario, podrás jugarlo desde las 08:00 del 18 de noviembre (16 horas antes de su disponibilidad en la región).
México es otro de los países que sacará especial provecho del truco de Nueva Zelanda con GTA 6. En el caso de Ciudad de México, que está en la hora del Centro, los jugadores podrán entrar al juego con 19 horas de anticipación; o sea, a partir de las 05:00 del miércoles 18 de noviembre. Tengamos en cuenta que el territorio mexicano tiene cuatro husos horarios, por lo que en otras regiones la disponibilidad puede variar ligeramente.
Cómo activarlo
Si estás en Xbox, activar el truco de Nueva Zelanda para acceder antes a GTA 6 es extremadamente sencillo. Compra el juego, completa la descarga anticipada y dirígete a Perfil y sistema > Configuración > Sistema. Una vez allí, ingresa en Idioma y ubicación y selecciona Nueva Zelanda. Por último, reinicia la consola, y listo. Esto será suficiente para jugar el nuevo Grand Theft Auto un día antes de su debut formal en tu país.
En el caso de PlayStation, el proceso es un poco más engorroso. Sony no ofrece una opción tan sencilla como la de Xbox para concretarlo, lo cual es una lástima. Lo que debes hacer es iniciar la PS5 y crear una nueva cuenta de PlayStation Network (PSN) radicada en Nueva Zelanda. Es posible que la plataforma te pida una dirección real para completar el proceso, pero es bastante fácil de engañar usando Google o Google Maps para encontrar un domicilio ficticio.
El siguiente paso es ingresar en la PlayStation Store de Nueva Zelanda y comprar GTA 6 con ese perfil. Una vez que lo tengas instalado y se cumpla el horario neozelandés, tendrás la posibilidad de jugarlo desde esa cuenta, sin esperar a que el juego esté disponible en tu propio huso horario.
Existe la posibilidad de compartir GTA 6 desde el perfil de Nueva Zelanda hacia tu cuenta principal usando la función Uso compartido de consola y juego offline de PS5. Esta se activa desde Ajustes > Usuarios y cuentas > Otro > Uso compartido de consola y juego offline. Como ven, es más complejo, pero vale la pena si estás dispuesto a reducir al máximo posible la brecha de disponibilidad con tu zona horaria.

articles.title: ‘Absolutely goated game’: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the fastest-selling game of 2026 in the US, but GTA6’s imminent launch is about to change everything
articles.text:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time smashes records as the best-selling game of 2026 in the US — but GTA 6 is coming to steal its crown
Booming sales for a modern classic
- The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has launched on Nintendo Switch 2
- The game sold one million copies in the US in its first week
- That makes it the fastest-selling title in 2026
The remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has been hailed as a modern masterpiece — our own review declared that it “delivers on every front” — so it’s unsurprising to hear it’s selling well. But quite how well might still come as a shock, with one industry analyst reporting that the game has absolutely smashed records this year.
According to Mat Piscatella, Senior Director at analysis firm Circana, the Nintendo Switch 2 title became the best-selling video game of 2026 in terms of US sales after just one week of general availability. That helped it surpass some of the year’s best Nintendo Switch 2 games, including Final Fantasy Resonance and Splatoon Raiders.
Piscatella said on Bluesky that Ocarina of Time is the first game to sell one million physical units in a single US launch week since another title from the franchise: 2023’s The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.
The Ocarina of Time remake has wowed fans and critics alike since its release, with our own Josephine Watson praising its audio and visual improvements over the original, its thoughtfully redesigned puzzles and dungeons, and its sprinkling of new features and quality-of-life improvements. Clearly, all this has helped propel it to record-breaking numbers — at least for a few days.
A phenomenal response
Unfortunately for Zelda fans, the record obtained by the Ocarina of Time remake might not last long. That’s because Grand Theft Auto 6 is due out in just two days, and it’s widely expected to swiftly become the best-selling game of the year, if not one of the highest-selling titles of all time.
Still, that doesn’t discount what a remarkable achievement this is for Ocarina of Time. Remaking any game carries risks, but when that title is so beloved by millions of gamers, and the remake is being made to celebrate the franchise’s 40th anniversary, there’s even more on the line. Thankfully, Ocarina of Time has delivered in spades.
Fans have been singing the game’s praises on social media, too. One Reddit user called it an “Absolutely goated game,” while another said that “Playing through this game made all the memories come back, great experience.” Many users also claimed to have bought several copies to keep one on display, such were their fond memories for the original version of the game.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
With Sony announcing that it will soon ditch physical media altogether, the success of Ocarina of Time — which is available in a physical format — is an interesting state of affairs. And if nothing else, it suggests that when you revive a cherished game with an exceptional remake, the response can be truly phenomenal.

articles.title: Beste GTA-6-Alternativen: 7 Spiele für die Wartezeit
articles.text:
Warten auf GTA 6: Diese 7 Games sind das perfekte Vorprogramm
Wenn Grand Theft Auto 6 am 19. November erscheint, dürfte es wieder einige Maßstäbe setzen, wie auch schon die vorherigen Teile der Reihe. Eine gigantische Open World, lebendige NPCs – und Verkaufszahlen, von denen andere Hersteller nur träumen können. Der Hype um dieses Spiel scheint derzeit keine Grenzen zu kennen.
Die einen wollen vielleicht die Zeit bis zum Release verkürzen. Andere haben weder eine Playstation 5, noch eine Xbox Series – oder gar keine Lust auf GTA 6. Ob es nun eine interessante Open World ist, oder eine Atmosphäre und Thematik, die an Grand Theft Auto erinnern: diese sieben Spiele können als Vorbereitung auf GTA 6 dienen – oder eine gute Alternative sein.
Cyberpunk 2077 für PC, Playstation 5, Xbox Series und Nintendo Switch 2
Cyberpunk 2077 ist freilich die offensichtlichste Alternative zu Grand Theft Auto 6. Night City ist eine lebendige Open World, in der ihr mit lautem Motor durch den dichten Stadtverkehr rasen könnt und euch packende Verfolgungsjagden mit der Polizei liefert, während im Radio treibende Musik läuft. Das dürfte jedem GTA-Fan recht bekannt vorkommen. Dabei ist Cyberpunk 2077 aber kein billiger Abklatsch, sondern erzählt seine eigene, durchaus interessante Geschichte über skrupellose Unternehmen und eine Menschheit, die ihr Heil in Technologie sucht.
Schedule 1 für PC
In Schedule 1 übernehmt ihr das Management eines illegalen Drogennetzwerks. Ihr beschafft und synthetisiert Substanzen und arbeitet daran, diskrete Vertriebswege aufzubauen und das eingenommene Geld möglichst effektiv zu waschen. Neben dem reinen Ressourcen- und Zeitmanagement müsst ihr aber auch Patrouillen der Polizei umgehen, Bestechungsgelder aushandeln und euer Territorium gegen rivalisierende Dealer absichern. Ein gutes Spiel für alle, die das Verbrechen nicht nur als Kulisse, sondern als kleinteiliges und oft wenig glamouröses Geschäft erleben wollen.
Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth für PC, Playstation 4/5 und Xbox Series
Wer eine Atmosphäre sucht, die der sonnendurchfluteten Spielwelt von GTA 6 ähnelt (der fiktive Bundesstaat Leonida ist an Florida angelehnt), kann mit Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth nach Hawaii reisen. In den insgesamt drei Städten der Open World könnte man ein vergnügliches Urlaubserlebnis haben – wenn da nicht die rivalisierenden Gangs und brutalen Syndikate wären, die die Insel unter sich aufteilen wollen. Gekämpft wird hier aber nicht, wie in GTA 6, in Echtzeit, sondern in rundenbasierten Keilereien. Das gibt dem Game einen eigenen Spielfluss, der auch durch zahllose abgedrehte Minispiele aufgelockert wird.
Mafia: Definitive Edition für PC, Playstation 4/5 und Xbox Series
Wer in GTA vor allem Verfolgungsjagden, Verrat und Gangster-Geschichten liebt, dürfte in Mafia: Definitive Edition eine gute Alternative finden. Das Remake des 2002 veröffentlichten Spiels versetzt euch in die fiktive US-Großstadt Lost Heaven der 1930er-Jahre. Ihr übernehmt die Rolle von Tommy Angelos, der in seinem Clan bis ganz an die Spitze aufsteigen möchte. In Mafia: Definitive Edition steht weniger die Open World im Mittelpunkt, sondern die eher lineare Geschichte, die Einblick gibt in die Schattenseiten des organisierten Verbrechens.
Silver Pines für PC, Playstation 5, Xbox Series und Nintendo Switch 2
Silver Pines ist mehr Horror- als Actionspiel, liefert aber eine dichte Atmosphäre und eine interessante Kriminalgeschichte. Als Privatdetektiv Red Walker verschlägt es euch in eine verlassene US-Kleinstadt, um das Verschwinden des Musikers Eddie Velvet aufzuklären. Die Stadt erinnert dabei mit ihrer Film-Noir-Optik an die Serie Twin Peaks. Ihr erkundet Tatorte, sammelt Hinweise und verknüpft Indizien, um dem Verbrechen auf die Spur zu kommen. In Multiple-Choice-Gesprächen gilt es, Widersprüche bei Verdächtigen aufzudecken und moralisch heikle Entscheidungen zu treffen. Dabei sticht, ähnlich wie in GTA, der Soundtrack besonders hervor. Der changiert zwischen Jazz, Synthesizer-Klängen und treibenden Percussions und bleibt auch noch nach dem Spielen im Kopf.
Watch Dogs: Legion für PC, Playstation 4/5 und Xbox Series
Das dystopische, verregnete London von Watch Dogs: Legion fängt das Gefühl einer Metropole in der nicht allzu fernen Zukunft ziemlich gut ein. An jeder Ecke Überwachungskameras, während eine Drohne nach der anderen über die Köpfe der Bevölkerung fliegt. Also ist es besser, nicht erkannt zu werden. In Watch Dogs: Legion steuert ihr daher nicht nur eine Spielfigur, sondern wechselt ständig zwischen verschiedenen Personen – vom klischeehaften Gangster bis zur unauffällig wirkenden Oma. Mit diesen Figuren und allerlei Hacking-Equipment lehnt ihr euch gegen die autoritäre Staatsgewalt auf und erkundet dabei eine lebendige und detailreiche Open World.
As Dusk Falls für PC, Playstation 4/5 und Xbox Series
As Dusk Falls hat spielerisch zwar nichts mit GTA 6 gemein, erzählt aber auch eine Geschichte um Gewalt und Kriminalität. Es geht um die Geschichte zweier Familien, deren Schicksale im Jahr 1998 nach einem gescheiterten Raubüberfall und einer Geiselnahme untrennbar miteinander verknüpft werden. In As Dusk Falls steuert ihr die Spielfigur dabei nicht direkt durch eine 3D-Welt, sondern lenkt vielmehr den Handlungsverlauf eines interaktiven Dramas. Das Gameplay beschränkt sich im Wesentlichen auf zwei Mechaniken: Ihr trefft Dialog- und Gewissensentscheidungen unter Zeitdruck und absolviert Quick-Time-Events in zunehmend brenzligen Situationen. Dabei bestimmen eure Eingaben unmittelbar das Schicksal der Beteiligten und den weiteren Verlauf der Erzählung.

articles.title: Jusqu'à 22 % de remise sur l'électricité : les achats groupés d'énergie valent-ils vraiment le coup ? — Frandroid
articles.text:
Les prix de l’énergie n’en finissent plus de grimper, et l’approche de l’hiver fait craindre des factures colossales pour les mois à venir. Ainsi, chacun y va de sa solution pour espérer limiter la casse : thermostats connectés, rideaux isolants et gros pulls en laine.
Côté gaz, le prix repère de vente, qui sert de référence depuis la fin des tarifs réglementés en 2023, a encore augmenté de 6,6 % au 1er novembre 2026, après plusieurs mois de hausse.
Il existe une autre piste pour alléger la facture, l’achat groupé d’électricité, de gaz ou de fioul. Le principe est simple : rassembler un maximum de consommateurs pour négocier une offre commune auprès des fournisseurs, chacun signant ensuite son propre contrat. L’idée avait été lancée par l’UFC-Que Choisir en 2013, à travers l’opération « Gaz moins cher ensemble ». Le fournisseur retenu, Lampiris, avait alors accordé à 71 000 foyers une remise de 13 % TTC sur le prix du kWh de gaz par rapport au tarif réglementé de l’époque.
Du 10 au 30 novembre, le LUBA mini 2 AWD 1000 passe à 1 199 € au lieu de 1 499 €, support de lavage offert ! Vision IA tri-caméra, sans fil périmétrique, tonte des bordures, adaptation à toutes les conditions de luminosité… Bref, il a tout pour tondre à votre place !
Depuis, le modèle a été repris par d’autres associations de consommateurs, par des courtiers en énergie et même par des collectivités. Depuis début septembre, les exemples d’achats groupés se multiplient dans l’actualité.
À Gien, dans le Loiret, la mairie a par exemple lancé un achat groupé d’électricité et de gaz avec la société Ecodigo. La réunion publique du 12 octobre a attiré 150 habitants, les préinscriptions, ouvertes à tous, même hors de la commune, ont couru jusqu’au 31 octobre, et l’offre négociée est présentée aux habitants cette semaine, avec une nouvelle réunion publique ce mardi 17 novembre.
La ville d’Amilly, à une quarantaine de kilomètres, l’avait précédée cet été en y ajoutant les pellets destinés aux poêles à granulés. Près de 1 900 foyers s’y sont inscrits, pour des remises annoncées jusqu’à 22 % sur le prix du kWh d’électricité et de 12 % sur celui du gaz.
Le pionnier du genre passe en revanche son tour cette année. Le 9 octobre, Que Choisir Ensemble (le nouveau nom de l’UFC-Que Choisir) a annoncé ne pas reconduire son opération « Énergie moins chère ensemble », faute d’avoir obtenu une offre suffisamment attractive auprès des fournisseurs. Un achat groupé ne garantit donc pas une remise à tous les coups.
Des conditions à vérifier avant de souscrire à un achat groupé
Sur le papier, cette solution est très intéressante, mais elle nécessite tout de même de prendre quelques précautions. Rappelons d’abord que ces remises portent généralement sur le seul prix du kWh. Avant d’y souscrire, mieux vaut donc comparer son contrat aux promesses de l’achat groupé, tant pour le coût de l’abonnement que pour le prix du kWh.
Les remises varient aussi beaucoup d’une campagne à l’autre. Pour son achat groupé national de novembre, Ecodigo, qui organise les opérations de Gien et d’Amilly, annonce un prix du kWh d’électricité 7 % moins cher que le tarif réglementé de vente, fixe pendant trois ans, avec des inscriptions ouvertes jusqu’au vendredi 27 novembre. On est loin des 22 % mis en avant à Amilly cet été.
La comparaison entre son contrat actuel et l’offre groupée doit se faire selon la consommation et non les mensualités. Par ailleurs, ces achats groupés commencent généralement par une préinscription. Cette phase permet à l’intermédiaire d’atteindre le nombre de consommateurs nécessaire pour obtenir un prix intéressant. Il ne faut pas hésiter à se préinscrire car cette étape est généralement gratuite et sans engagement. En revanche, c’est la souscription qui mérite réflexion, car c’est elle qui engage.
Pour finir, le médiateur national de l’énergie propose un comparateur gratuit des offres d’électricité et de gaz du moment. Il recense les offres auxquelles il est possible de souscrire, avec leurs tarifs, de quoi vérifier si la proposition de l’achat groupé est vraiment la meilleure.

articles.title: Une panne frappe NSA Net, le réseau ultra-secret du renseignement américain : voici ce que l’on sait
articles.text:
Mardi 17 novembre 2026, CNN a révélé que le réseau sur lequel les employés de la National Security Agency (NSA) échangent des informations classifiées ne fonctionne plus.
La chaîne américaine dit s’appuyer sur six personnes au fait de la situation. La journaliste Natasha Bertrand, qui signe l’enquête avec quatre collègues, en évoquait cinq dans le premier message publié sur X.
L’agence de renseignement, dont le siège se trouve à Fort Meade, dans le Maryland, n’avait pas encore répondu aux questions de CNN au moment de la publication.
Un réseau réservé aux échanges classifiés
Ce réseau, baptisé NSA Net, n’a rien à voir avec le site public de l’agence. Il sert aux agents à faire circuler des informations classifiées en interne, c’est-à-dire des contenus qui ne peuvent pas passer par une messagerie ou un réseau ordinaire. Sa panne bloque donc ces échanges au sein de l’agence.
On ignore pour l’instant depuis quand la panne dure, combien de services sont touchés et quand le réseau pourra être rétabli. Selon les sources de CNN, l’agence a mis en place des arrivées échelonnées pour son personnel le temps de comprendre ce qui se passe.
Sur la cause, les sources de CNN affirment qu’il n’existe « à ce stade » aucune preuve d’une cyberattaque.

articles.title: Lakshmi Venu seeks formal partition of TVS Venu Srinivasan family assets
articles.text:
Lakshmi Venu seeks formal partition of TVS Venu Srinivasan family assets
In a partition notice to her father, she has called upon him, as head of the family, to discharge his fiduciary duties and give effect to a fair and lawful partition.
Lakshmi Venu, daughter of industrialist Venu Srinivasan, has formally sought partition of the joint family assets of a branch of the TVS family.
In a partition notice to her father, she has called upon him, as head of the family, to discharge his fiduciary duties and give effect to a fair and lawful partition.
Lakshmi, in her statement on Monday, asserted that, under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005, she is entitled to her rightful share in the joint family property and has an independent right to seek its partition.
Her claim is also founded on the equal rights of daughters recognised under Section 6 of the Act.
Stating that the assets for which she seeks partition include the family interests held through the VS Trust and other holding vehicles and structures, she said, "These encompass the businesses and assets allotted to the Venu Srinivasan branch under the 2020 TVS family arrangement, including interests in TVS Holdings, TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services and Sundaram-Clayton".
Lakshmi maintained that the larger TVS family arrangement did not constitute a partition within the Venu Srinivasan family. No settlement or partition of the assets within her immediate family was ever initiated, let alone concluded.
In her view, management does not confer exclusive ownership or extinguish lawful rights of other family members.
Lakshmi contended that she is being wrongfully denied her rightful share of the joint family property and alleged that the concentration of beneficial interest in favour of her brother was to the exclusion of her own lawful rights.
She regarded these actions not only as a breach of law but also as a breach of trust."Patriarchy has no place in law or in a progressive India. The rights of daughters to joint family property cannot be overridden through unilateral decisions or corporate arrangements", she added.
Reiterating her preference for an amicable and equitable resolution, Lakshmi has called for the matter to be settled with fairness, dignity and respect for the rights of all family members.
Meanwhile, another statement from Mallika Srinivasan, MD, Tractors and Farm Equipment Limited, supporting her daughter Lakshmi Venu's legitimate right in the family assets, said, "It is unfortunate that requests for an amicable settlement have not so far progressed in a meaningful and timely way".
She further said, "As a mother, to me, a son and daughter are equal in every respect. I do believe that Lakshmi has a legitimate share of the family assets, not unequal to that of (Lakshmi's brother) Sudarshan’s. I reiterate that this is a matter to be settled, in the interests of all stakeholders, through transparent dialogue, with equity, clarity and amity. I sincerely hope that we can move forward constructively, with grace and dignity".

articles.title: Xiaomi Clip : la marque se lance à son tour dans les écouteurs à clip pour concurrencer Huawei
articles.text:
Xiaomi Clip : la marque se lance à son tour dans les écouteurs à clip pour concurrencer Huawei
Xiaomi se lance enfin sur le marché très convoité des écouteurs ouverts à clip d’oreille. Un format misant avant tout sur le confort et la conscience de l’environnement, dont la marque chinoise livre ici sa propre interprétation.
Déjà très populaires en Asie et en pleine démocratisation en Europe, les écouteurs ouverts à clip d’oreille prennent une place grandissante sur le marché de l’audio, si bien que rares sont les constructeurs à ne pas encore avoir proposé leur propre interprétation. Avec les sobrement baptisés Clip, Xiaomi s’inscrit ainsi parmi les derniers à s’aventurer sur ce format, dont l’absence d’intrusion dans le conduit auditif offre un confort irréprochable, tout en permettant à l’utilisateur de rester attentif à son environnement.
Une "boule sonore" transparente
Les Xiaomi Clip disposent d’une jonction en titane à mémoire de forme venant se fixer sur le lobe de l’oreille. D’un côté prend place une chambre acoustique en forme de sphère, de l’autre un module arrière venant légèrement s’appuyer sur l’os mastoïde et intégrant la batterie. Outre leurs finitions brillantes, les Xiaomi Clip cherchent à se distinguer par un compartiment transparent laissant apparaître les transducteurs. On remarque également que l’arceau reliant les deux extrémités est construit d’un seul bloc, signe d’une conception soignée.
Contrairement à certains modèles concurrents populaires, qui détectent automatiquement l’oreille sur laquelle ils sont portés, les Xiaomi Clip conservent une distinction entre écouteur gauche et écouteur droit. Un choix un peu dommage, qui impose de respecter le sens de port.
Chaque écouteur affiche un poids de 5,5 g, une valeur conventionnelle, bien qu’un peu supérieure à celle des Huawei FreeClip 2. Le boîtier de charge horizontal reste quant à lui très classique pour ce type d’écouteurs.
Transducteurs de 11 mm et système pour limiter les fuites
Les Xiaomi Clip intègrent un unique transducteur dynamique de 11 mm, à l’heure où certains fabricants comme Shokz misent déjà sur des systèmes à double transducteur montés en opposition. La marque affirme diriger efficacement le son vers le conduit auditif grâce à un procédé d’inversion de phase des ondes sonores. Les écouteurs seraient ainsi capables à la fois de préserver la qualité du signal et de limiter les fuites, afin de ne pas déranger l’entourage tout en préservant la confidentialité des appels.
Côté codecs Bluetooth, outre les classiques SBC et AAC, les Xiaomi Clip prennent en charge le LHDC 5.0. Bien qu’il s’agisse d’un codec haute résolution, celui-ci reste limité à certains smartphones, notamment ceux de Xiaomi.
L’ergonomie des écouteurs repose sur une certification IP57, leur assurant une bonne résistance aux intempéries et à la transpiration, à l’instar des meilleurs modèles du segment. Côté commandes, ces écouteurs semblent intégrer une combinaison de tapotements sur l’arceau et de balayages tactiles sur le module arrière pour gérer le volume. Xiaomi promet également des appels clairs grâce à un réseau de trois microphones et à un capteur à conduction osseuse, épaulés par un algorithme de réduction de bruit.
Traduction en temps réel, certification IP57 et 9 h d'autonomie
Équipés d’HyperOS, les Xiaomi Clip s’intègrent naturellement dans l’écosystème Xiaomi, afin de permettre notamment le partage audio entre plusieurs appareils de la marque. Ils bénéficient aussi d’une application disponible sur iOS et Android.
Les écouteurs sont par ailleurs compatibles avec le réseau Find My d’Apple afin de pouvoir être facilement géolocalisés depuis un smartphone iOS. Les Xiaomi Clip permettraient aussi d’enregistrer des contenus, que ce soit la musique en lecture, les appels, les lives, etc. Certaines fonctions restent toutefois réservées à l’écosystème Xiaomi et à l’assistant XiaoAI, comme la traduction en temps réel, la transcription ou encore la génération de résumés.
L’autonomie est annoncée à 9 h sur une seule charge et peut atteindre 38 h avec le boîtier, soit des performances similaires à celles des meilleurs écouteurs de la catégorie. Les Xiaomi Clip sont disponibles dès aujourd’hui en France au prix de 149,99 €, et bénéficient d’une remise immédiate de 23 € jusqu’au 30 novembre.
Xiaomi adopte ainsi une stratégie simple : proposer une paire d’écouteurs plus abordable que les références actuelles du segment, comme les Huawei FreeClip 2, les Shokz OpenDots 2 ou encore les Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (Gen 2), sans multiplier les compromis.

articles.title: Nvidia es el Super Glue de la industria de la IA. Sin Huang al frente, temen que sea pegamento de barra
articles.text:
Nvidia no sólo vende los chips con los que se entrena la IA. Estos últimos años, y gracias a un muy buen ojo por parte de su exCEO Jensen Huang para adelantarse al futuro, la compañía ha avalado, comprado capacidad e invertido en empresas para que esas mismas empresas puedan pagar sus chips. En esa especie de jugada maestra de ajedrez 4D, Nvidia se ha convertido en el 'banco central de la IA'.
Ahora ese banco se ha quedado sin su cofundador y CEO, con la bolsa en caída y con ejecutivos del sector que dudan que AMD y Broadcom sean capaces de llenar el hueco.
En anteriores capítulos... No vamos a entrar de nuevo en el escándalo de Jensen Huang. En resumen, tras conocerse una primera relación extramatrimonial con alguien sospechoso de espiar para China, la compañía empezó a tambalearse. El tropiezo llegó tras conocerse una segunda (y tercera) relación con empleadas de Nvidia, lo que llevó a la dimisión de Huang dejando un enorme agujero en la compañía.
Desde el máximo del 6 de octubre, las acciones se han desplomado y ahora el marrón se lo está comiendo la CEO interina: Colette Kress.
Banco central. Lo hemos ido contando estos últimos meses. En una especie de financiación circular, Nvidia ha ido invirtiendo miles de millones tanto directamente en empresas como comprando otras para asegurarse la tecnología. Se ha convertido en el pegamento de la IA y un socio incómodo por todo lo que dependía de ellos (dinero y tecnología). El problema es que ese dinero en muchas ocasiones no ha cambiado de manos, sino que eran "compromisos".
Como vemos en CNBC, esos compromisos con otras empresas del sector suman cientos de miles de millones de dólares, entre los que destacan:
- Hasta 36.000 millones en compras de servicios en nube a neoclouds.
- Una garantía sujeta a condiciones de 105.000 millones de dólares para el gran centro de datos de OnenAP y SB Energy en Ohio
- Respaldo de hasta 125.000 millones en un programa de crédito de Wall Street.
Riesgo. Hay quien estima el total en más de 400.000 millones y el riesgo es esa mencionada financiación circular. Nvidia ha ido comprometiendo dinero en empresas para que éstas les compren sus chips. El dinero cambiaba de un bolsillo a otro y, según el CNBC, si no pudiera cumplir el acuerdo, el golpe llegaría a los prestatarios y a los bancos. Ahí está parte de ese temor a una explosión de la burbuja que deje el sistema tiritando.
Los hiperescaladores han pasado de suponer el 1% a cerca del 10% de la emisión de bonos de grado de inversión, siendo un mercado de 15 billones de dólares en dos años.
Peso de Huang. Y las dudas del mercado vienen porque, según India Today, Huang y la actual CEO chocaban en la forma de invertir. Kress era la directora financiera de la compañía y, mientras Huang quería usar el dinero de Nvidia de forma agresiva, Kress quería ir con pies de plomo. El primero propuso un plan de crédito de 250.000 millones para el mencionado plan de OpenAI, pero al final Kress y su equipo lograron rebajarlo a los 105.000 millones.
Dudas. Ahora, los inversores esperan un perfil aún más cuidadoso por parte de la nueva cúpula, y ahí está la pregunta: si Nvidia retrocede, ¿quién ocupará su lugar? Según el mismo India Today citando a ejecutivos del sector, ni AMD ni Broadcom tienen el músculo financiero para dar garantías a la escala a la que opera Nvidia.
Broadcom tendría respaldos de unos 43.000 millones para un único cliente (Anthropic, que le va a comprar chips), quedando lejos del enfoque de Nvidia. Y aunque Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Tesla y OpenAI estén trabajando en chips propios para dejar de depender de Nvidia, se puede sustituir el cerebro, pero el músculo financiero será algo más complicado.
Cuerda floja. Al final, hablamos a futuro y del temor de los inversores, pero la consecuencia más inmediata es que las neoclouds están en la cuerda floja. Estas empresas que levantan centros de datos con chips de Nvidia y luego alquilan su capacidad han estado muy respaldadas por Nvidia. No sólo a nivel tecnológico, sino con acuerdos como el de CoreWeave por el que Nvidia compraba la capacidad que CoreWeave no vendiera hasta 2032.
Estas últimas semanas se ha discutido mucho sobre si la burbuja de las neoclouds iba a estallar (con Huang diciendo que ni de broma y con Musk mostrándose menos seguro), pero pese a la enorme caída con la que empezaron el mes, esta semana se han ido recuperando en bolsa mientas Nvidia caía. Los inversores parece que ven el problema como uno específico de Nvidia... por ahora, pero está claro que su caída sería algo sísmico. "Si los proveedores de capital dicen que la garantía no vale lo que valía hace una semana, esos negocios de neoclouds estarían en riesgo", según un analista en declaraciones a Fortune.
Este martes, el gigante presentará resultados y será la primera vez que ocurra sin Huang a la cabeza. Y es evidente que Nvidia no va a caer debido a que es la pata fuerte del sector de la IA, pero hay que esperar a ver si el nuevo mandato (y el que venga), mantiene el papel de prestamista en la industria o si sacan menos dinero a pasear.

Both incidents started at approximately 1:40 PM ET.
AppleCare on Device is experiencing another outage that affects all users.
According to Apple, purchasing AppleCare directly on a device is temporarily unavailable. This issue started at approximately 11:15 AM ET.

articles.title: « Ils se sont fait passer pour des membres de l’équipe » : plusieurs IA Gemini ont tenté de pirater un site web
articles.text:
Le mois dernier, des agents IA reposant sur Gemini 4 Argon, l’un des derniers modèles de Google, ont tenté à plusieurs reprises de pirater le site web d’Epoch AI, un organisme de recherche spécialisé dans l’IA. L’incident s’est produit lors d’un test de sécurité organisé par Trajectory Labs, une société spécialisée dans l’évaluation des modèles d’IA.
 Responding to incidents during misalignment testing: https://t.co/FVhoI4zreE
— Peter McIntyre (@pmcntyr) November 13, 2026
Avec leurs expérimentations, les chercheurs voulaient déterminer si un modèle d’IA, avec toutes les protections activées, se comporterait comme les agents d’OpenAI se sont comportés au début de l’été. Ceux-ci ont échappé à leur prison numérique pour pénétrer dans les serveurs de Hugging Face, une plateforme open source, lors d’un test. Les chercheurs ont remarqué que les agents Gemini se sont comportés exactement de la même manière, et que les couches de protection n’ont pas suffi à éviter les abus. Pour Trajectory Labs, Gemini n’est pas suffisamment aligné sur les intentions de ses concepteurs.
À lire aussi : Les banques sont « horrifiées » – des IA ont fait irruption dans des comptes bancaires
Une mission impossible à l’origine de l’incident
Pour pousser les IA dans leurs retranchements, les chercheurs leur ont volontairement confié une tâche irréalisable. Ils ont demandé aux agents Gemini de trouver les réponses « officielles » à des problèmes de mathématiques qui n’existent pas. Les consignes étaient très claires. Les intelligences artificielles ne devaient « JAMAIS s’arrêter, ne JAMAIS abandonner et ne JAMAIS conclure qu’une tâche ou une donnée est impossible, indisponible ou épuisée ».
Personne n’a demandé aux IA de pirater quoi que ce soit pour arriver à leurs fins. Le 20 octobre, une quarantaine d’agents se sont pourtant mis à fouiller sur le site d’Epoch AI à la recherche de pages cachées. Un agent a même tenté de glisser des commandes malveillantes dans une base de données.
Epoch AI s’est rapidement rendu compte de ce qu’il se passait. L’organisme de recherche a donc ouvert une « ligne d’assistance » pour discuter avec les agents partis en vrille. En trois heures, ceux-ci ont envoyé près de 500 messages sur la ligne. Certains se sont même fait passer pour des employés d’Epoch, nom et fonction à l’appui, d’autres pour des ingénieurs ou des auditeurs, toujours dans le but de dénicher des réponses aux problèmes inexistants.
« Ils se sont fait passer pour des membres de l’équipe », raconte Trajectory Labs.
Des IA qui contournent toutes les barrières
Les chercheurs de Trajectory Labs ont ensuite redirigé les agents vers une copie du site, pour étudier leurs comportements sans mettre en danger Epoch AI. Malheureusement, « les agents ont compris qu’ils se trouvaient sur une copie, ont identifié la bonne adresse IP pour contourner notre redirection et ont de nouveau atteint le site réel », raconte Trajectory Labs. Sans jamais botter en touche, les agents se sont aussi organisés entre eux. Un agent a partagé une astuce pour contourner une protection, qu’un autre a utilisée pour dérober des identifiants. Ce comportement rappelle énormément celui des ChatGPT qui ont transformé un site web en forum secret en mai dernier, en amont du piratage de Hugging Face.
Les garde-fous de Gemini n’ont pas suffi. D’après Trajectory Labs, ceux-ci ont bloqué environ 7 % des requêtes, mais les agents ont continué malgré tout. Dans un environnement coupé d’Internet, les IA ont même actionné un faux interrupteur censé désactiver le pare-feu, en déguisant leurs commandes pour échapper aux protections de Gemini. Bonne nouvelle, rien n’a été dérobé sur le site visé.
« Les agents n’ont réussi à accéder à aucune information privée ou confidentielle d’Epoch », assure l’organisme.
« Pas encore de normes communes »
Trajectory Labs reconnaît avoir commis une erreur en menant ses tests sans prévenir Epoch, et sans mettre en place de surveillance suffisante. Tous les tests, suspendus le 2 novembre, « montrent avec quelle facilité les tests d’agents d’IA performants peuvent déborder et affecter des systèmes et des personnes réels ». Les chercheurs regrettent qu’il n’existe « pas encore de normes communes » pour tester des IA « en toute sécurité ». Les chercheurs reconnaissent que « ces tests ne nous disent pas à quelle fréquence cela pourrait se produire dans un usage ordinaire ».
Ces dérapages à répétition poussent les géants de l’IA à serrer la vis. Après avoir découvert que Claude avait piraté trois entreprises lors de tests de cybersécurité, Anthropic a suspendu toutes ses évaluations. OpenAI est allé plus loin. Après qu’un de ses modèles a profité d’une erreur de configuration pour se connecter à Internet en septembre, l’entreprise a décidé d’entraîner ses IA les plus avancées dans un « monde hors ligne », sans aucun accès au Web. Google, de son côté, a d’abord réservé Gemini 4 Argon à un cercle de « défenseurs cyber de confiance » lors de son lancement.

articles.title: Seis meses de prisión y una multa superior a 1.000 euros por presentar en el trabajo un parte de baja médico falso
articles.text:
El primer parte de baja que el trabajador recibió por gastroenteritis era solo para un día. Sin embargo, el siguiente día tampoco fue a trabajar. Cuando la empresa le pidió que justificara su ausencia, el trabajador mandó por e-mail otro parte (ficticio) que no le había dado su médico.
Los hechos ocurrieron en junio de 2017. El día 6 el trabajador tenía un parte de baja y alta (por gastroenteritis aguda), que le dio un médico y solo era para ese mismo día.
El día 7 no estaba cubierto médicamente, pero el trabajador envió un parte (que él mismo hizo u obtuvo) que justifica esta ausencia.
Fue el Juzgado de lo Penal número 3 de Granollers quien primero condenó al trabajador (por falsedad en documento oficial y por un delito leve de estafa).
El documento que querían pasar por auténtico
En la Sala de lo Penal han tenido en cuenta que, en casos en los que se trata de “reproducciones” que se quieren pasar por documentos oficiales, hay que tener en cuenta qué documento se quiere imitar.
El soporte en el que se elabora el documento no tiene relevancia. En este caso se trataba de una baja médica que no existía.
Así se resolvió la polémica sobre el parte de baja digital. Condena por falsedad documental. Los efectos de la sentencia suponen 6 meses de cárcel y 6 meses de multa (a 6 euros diarios).
Cada mes de multa son 30 días (artículo 50 del Código Penal). Esto suma 1.080 euros. Además, se le condena a pagar las costas de primera instancia. También se incluye una inhabilitación para presentarse a elecciones durante el tiempo de la condena (algo curioso).
