articles.title: “Playing all weekend without needing to resort to an umbilical USB cable is really freeing” — SteelSeries’ wireless Xbox controller has totally won me over with its swappable batteries and seamless dual-platform play
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The SteelSeries Aeon Pro has so many game-changing features it’s hard to squeeze them all in. Both its dual-system connectivity and hot-swappable batteries make it so much more flexible than rival controllers, while its OLED screen, dual-mode triggers, and Hall effect thumbsticks all make it feel really versatile. Its control app makes switching profiles a breeze, although there are a few customization options missing. There’s no getting around that price, though: this is an expensive controller, even compared to its closest rivals.
Reasons to buy
- + Hot-swappable batteries
- + Dual-system dock
- + Useful OLED screen
- + Hall effect triggers and thumbsticks
- + Light, ergonomic design
Reasons to avoid
- - Pricier than some pro rivals
- - No response curves for triggers
- - Can’t map system actions to rear paddles
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
SteelSeries Aeon Pro: two-minute review
The SteelSeries Aeon Pro is a pro-level wireless controller compatible with PC and Xbox Series X / S. Not only does it offer many of the premium features you’d expect from a pad at its price point, but it also offers several huge innovations that separate it from other options in its class.
Let’s start with the most attention-grabbing features. First off, the Aeon Pro offers dual-platform connectivity. That doesn’t mean it has a dongle you can swap between devices or use Bluetooth for your second system — its dock has dual outputs, meaning that you can flip its 2.4GHz Wi-Fi connectivity between PC and Xbox using the pad’s built-in OLED screen. As someone who regularly games on both, I loved how easy this made it to switch between them on the fly.
But honestly, I’d say my favorite feature is SteelSeries’ Infinite Power System. Let’s set aside that slightly grandiose name: essentially, this means the Aeon Pro not only charges on its dock when not in use, but it also comes with hot-swappable rechargeable batteries. Every time I ran out of juice — which didn’t happen often, thanks to the pad’s 12-hour battery life — I could just swap in a fresh battery without having to resort to a cable, giving the Aeon Pro the edge over many of the best PC controllers.
Elsewhere, the Aeon Pro’s design is similarly high-tier. Front and center, it features a built-in OLED screen, which allows you to switch between platforms and profiles straight from your controller. It also felt suitably ergonomic in my hands — every button sat right under my fingertips, even the rear paddles, while the textured grips made it easy to hang onto even during frantic pitched battles in FPS games.
In use, the Aeon Pro is super responsive, thanks to its 1,000Hz polling rate. It also rocks dual-mode triggers, meaning you can switch between analog and micro-switch modes at the flip of a toggle. Meanwhile, both the triggers and thumbsticks are Hall effect — as a result, they’re rapid and drift-free, although they don’t offer quite the same sensitivity and energy efficiency as TMR alternatives.
SteelSeries’ GG software also allows you to create potentially infinite custom profiles for different games, while you can load up to eight at a time onto the controller itself. On PC, you can also create profiles for each game in your library that then auto-switch when you fire the game up — I love the fact that I could have my thumbsticks automatically invert for games like Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, particularly as these profiles are also compatible with SteelSeries’ Arctis Nova Pro Omni gaming headset as well.
There are a couple of improvements I’d like to see to the SteelSeries GG app, though. First of all, unlike the software offered by rivals like Razer or ROG, GG doesn’t currently allow you any control over trigger response curves, and the options for the thumbsticks are pretty limited. Additionally, remapping only allows you to assign existing buttons from the controller to its back paddles — so if you were hoping to be able to tweak system controls or assign keyboard shortcuts there on PC, you’re out of luck.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Aside from these niggles though, the only real hurdle for me is that price. Retailing at $259.99 / £229.99 / AU$529, it’s a pricey package, even compared to the best Xbox controllers, so it might not be the best fit for you if you’re looking for a bargain. But I’d argue that, with its swappable battery system and dual-platform connectivity, it gives a lot in return. So if you can afford it, you’re unlikely to come away disappointed with the SteelSeries Aeon Pro.
SteelSeries Aeon Pro review: price and availability
- Launched September 8, 2026
- List price of $259.99 / £229.99 / AU$529
- Comes with a lot of extras for your spend
Having launched on September 8, 2026, the SteelSeries Aeon Pro is available now. Retailing at a list price of $259.99 / £229.99 / AU$529, it sits firmly at the premium end of the market. By way of comparison, the similarly pro Asus ROG Raikiri II Xbox Wireless has a list price of $189.99 / £199 / AU$349, while the Razer Wolverine V3 Pro originally retailed for $199.99 / £199.99 (around AU$290). So it’s not cheap, even compared to other pro controllers.
But it is worth bearing in mind that the Aeon Pro comes with a dual-platform dock, two spare hot-swappable thumbsticks and two hot-swappable batteries, so you do get quite a lot for your cash. When it comes to your purchase options, SteelSeries’ controller comes in two colorways: black and the white version tested here.
SteelSeries Aeon Pro review: design
When you’re first setting up the SteelSeries Aeon Pro, you’ll likely notice that its dock has two USB-C outputs. That’s because the Aeon Pro is the first controller of its kind to offer dual-platform wireless connectivity. When I plugged it in to both my PC and Xbox Series X, I was able to switch between 2.4GHz connectivity to either system straight from the pad itself — this feels so much more fluid and intuitive than having to faff around with moving dongles or switch to Bluetooth pairing to use a different device.
But for me, this isn’t the Aeon Pro’s most transformative feature. For that, we have to look under the hood: the SteelSeries’ Infinite Power System.
Okay, don’t get carried away with visions of free-energy conspiracy theories — the Aeon Pro’s battery is definitely finite. But — as is the case with the recent SteelSeries Sensei and Rival Pro mice, as well as the Arctis Nova Pro Omni — it is replaceable and can be hot-swapped out for a full one, with the empty battery clipping into a charging port on the controller’s base. As a result, you should always have a full battery waiting in the wings to take over even when your current one is tapped, which is a really smart system. And the batteries are interchangeable with the Arctis Nova Pro Omni, meaning if you’re using both, you’ll always have a steady cycle of juiced-up power packs waiting in the wings.
When you’ve popped in a charged battery and powered on the controller, the thing that will most grab your attention is that OLED smart display. While this is hardly the first pro controller we’ve seen with a screen, I would say this is one of the few I’ve seen that actually has a decent range of use cases. Not only does it allow you to flip between different game profiles, but you can also use it to switch sources between Xbox, PC, and Bluetooth, check battery levels, and even remap buttons on the fly. This definitely elevates it from gimmick to something I actually interacted with a lot.
Elsewhere, the design looks smart and suitably pro, and the Aeon Pro feels nicely ergonomic. The gentle slant of its grips sat nicely in my hands, while their finely textured surface gave me a good amount of traction without getting too sweaty — something I can’t say of other controllers I’ve tested. Elsewhere, its body is fashioned from pleasantly tactile matte plastic and its build quality all feels appropriately premium, while still managing to weigh a light and floaty 10.9oz / 310g.
For the most part, the Aeon Pro adopts the standard Xbox controller format, with asymmetrical thumbsticks. However, as a result of that OLED screen at the top of the pad, the start and menu buttons have been relocated to the bottom. I’ll admit this might be making virtue out of necessity, but this placement does actually feel preferable to me — rather than having to adjust your grip to reach past the left thumbstick or face buttons, you can just move your thumbs laterally and easily access in-game menus without stretching.
Speaking of the thumbsticks, the Aeon Pro has moved away from drift-prone potentiometer-based sensors for its sticks, like most of its contemporaries. Personally, I’d prefer TMR-based thumbsticks and triggers for their marginally higher sensitivity, but the Hall-effect system used here is going to be plenty sufficient for all but professional esports players. And while TMR does provide a slight buff to energy efficiency, the Aeon Pro’s battery system should make this a bit of a non-issue.
SteelSeries has offered another neat trick for this controller’s thumbsticks as well. Included with the Aeon Pro are two alternate sticks — these are magnetic and hot-swappable, meaning that I could quickly pop them off and replace them mid-game in a matter of moments. Another neat design decision here is the fact that the controller’s base has two magnetic docks for the sticks you aren’t using, which is just a thoughtful detail.
I’ve raved before about how much I love dual-mode triggers, so I’m definitely pleased to see them included here on the Aeon Pro. Enabling you to switch between full-range analog and micro-switch triggers at the flip of a toggle, these give a controller huge versatility, whether you want sensitive control of an accelerator pedal in Forza Horizon 6 or want clicky, near-instant parries in Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.
All the Aeon Pro’s other buttons are similarly satisfying. Its face buttons also use micro-switches, feeling super accurate while giving immediate feedback. And its mappable rear paddles are perfectly positioned to sit under your fingertips, while feeling nice and snappy when you activate them. Everything feels easy to reach and quick to activate, which was fantastic when I needed to leap out of harm’s way or pull out my chainsaw to grind through imps in Doom.
SteelSeries Aeon Pro review: performance
All the innovative features in the world don't matter if a controller can't match them with powerful performance. Fortunately, the SteelSeries Aeon Pro doesn't struggle here in the least, offering snappy and fluid control over your games.
Thanks to its 1,000Hz polling rate, the Aeon Pro has the reaction times of a hummingbird that’s just had its third energy drink of the day. Whether I was popping off headshots in FPSes or requiring precise steering to avoid flying off a hairpin bend in racing games, its thumbsticks always felt super responsive, and its micro-switch face buttons never betrayed a hint of lag.
Dual-mode triggers are, once again, a totally worthwhile investment. When toggled on to their micro-switches, they aced my go-to test: helping me perform snappy parries and counters in Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. With their assistance, I comfortably shrugged off even the remorseless combos of Aberrations. In their analog mode, the triggers feel fast and responsive — almost too fast, in fact, as occasionally while racing in Forza Horizon 6 I found myself wishing for a tiny bit more resistance to give me more granular control over my accelerator pedal.
On the whole, SteelSeries GG software offers some fantastic features, although I did find it was lacking in a few options I’d come to take for granted from other brands’ apps.
Not only does SteelSeries GG allow you to create, in theory, an infinite number of profiles, but you can load up to eight at a time on the Aeon Pro and flip between them using its OLED screen. That gives it far more flexibility than something like the Asus ROG Raikiri II, which requires you to swap back to its PC-only software just to change profiles.
But even more innovative is its automatic profiles for your favorite PC games. For example, I was able to set my sticks to be directional rather than circular for the 2D platformer Hollow Knight: Silksong — then when I fired up the game, it automatically switched to the matching profile. Even better, this functionality also extends to the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni gaming headset, meaning I could set it to invert my thumbsticks and crank up the headset’s spatial audio every time I launched Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 without pressing a button. That honestly feels a little like magic.
There’s a decent range of settings you can tweak in SteelSeries GG. These include remapping buttons and the back paddles, setting deadzones for the triggers and thumbsticks, adjusting the response of, or inverting, the sticks, altering the vibration of the grips and triggers, and tweaking the settings of that OLED screen.
However, there are a few options I found myself missing here. First off, while you can change the response of the thumbsticks, there are only three options — default, dynamic, and exponential — while you can’t change the response of the triggers at all. That's a real shame, as I find the fully customizable curves that some apps offer are what really unlock the value of these tailor-made profiles; I definitely found myself missing S-shaped curves for controlling my pedal in Forza Horizon 6, for example.
Secondly, while you can remap the rear paddles, you only seem to be able to set them up as shortcuts for existing buttons. There’s seemingly no way to set them to macros, control system-level functionality, or map them to in-game functions. I’d love to be able to use them to control my media player or bring up the quest menu in Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered, but the range of options is limited enough that it slightly hampers the paddles’ utility for me.
Fortunately, these quibbles aren’t so severe that they detract from the Aeon Pro’s biggest draw for me: that battery system. It really can’t be overstated how fantastic it feels to never need to plug your pad in to charge. Not only did the full charge it got from its dock give me comfortably 12 hours of play per battery, but knowing I always had a full battery waiting in the wings meant I never had to experience range anxiety when I settled in for a marathon gaming sesh. Knowing I could play all weekend without ever needing to resort to an umbilical USB cable is a really freeing experience, and I’m here for it.
Should I buy the SteelSeries Aeon Pro?
Buy it if...
You game on both PC and Xbox
Thanks to the Aeon Pro’s dual-platform system, you can switch between playing on your console and PC with the tap of a button — and without having to sacrifice 2.4GHz connectivity for either.
You never want to run out of battery again
Not only does the Aeon Pro charge when it’s on its base, but so does a backup hot-swappable battery, meaning you’ll never get caught short without charge during an epic GTA 6 session.
Don't buy it if...
You aren’t feeling flush
Look, this almost goes without saying. But at $259.99 / £229.99 / AU$529, the Aeon Pro is an unabashedly premium controller. So if you’re looking for bargain prices, look elsewhere.
You want full customizability
While it’s crammed with great features like auto-detecting game profiles on PC, SteelSeries GG software has a few limitations like a lack of trigger response curves and an ability to map system functions to rear paddles.
SteelSeries Aeon Pro review: also consider
Asus ROG Raikiri II Xbox Wireless
This is the Xbox and PC controller I use at home, and it’s fantastic. Not only does it have the 1,000Hz polling and dual-mode triggers that the Aeon Pro does, but it also rocks TMR thumbsticks and triggers and offers super customizable response curves in its control software. But it lacks SteelSeries’ awesome battery system and dual-platform connectivity, so it’s not an easy choice. Read my full Asus ROG Raikiri II Xbox Wireless review.
Razer Wolverine V3 Pro
There’s a reason that the Wolverine V3 Pro has sat as our best premium PC controller ever since its release. It offers fantastic performance, Hall effect sticks and triggers, dual-mode triggers, 1000Hz polling, and a wonderfully tactile playing experience. And while the fact that it’s slightly older means it lacks some of the latest features that the SteelSeries and Asus controllers do, it also means it comes in at a lower price, costing just $169.99 / £129.99 / AU$235.36. Read our full Razer Wolverine V3 Pro review.
How I tested the SteelSeries Aeon Pro
- Tested over two weeks
- Tried it with multiple devices and many types of games
- Tweaked all of the available settings and created many custom profiles
I tested the SteelSeries Aeon Pro over the course of a couple of weeks. I tested it extensively on both my Xbox Series X and on my desktop PC. On top of that, I made sure to test it on a wide variety of games, whether that was on adventure games like Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, racing games like Forza Horizon 6, RPGs like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, or FPSes like Doom.
Endeavoring to test all of the Aeon Pro’s features, I tried out both its dual-source connectivity and swappable battery system. In addition, I tested all of the settings in SteelSeries’ control app, whether that was tweaking trigger and thumbstick settings, remapping buttons, or creating automatic gaming profiles. I also tested it alongside the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni to see how you can use profiles to switch up the settings of both simultaneously.
When it comes to my own personal experience, I’ve been testing and writing about gadgets for over ten years. During that time, I’ve reviewed a range of controllers, headsets, and portable consoles. On top of that, I’ve been gaming for at least 35 years — having cut my teeth on early NES games, I’m now most likely to be gaming on my PC, Xbox Series X, Steam Deck, or Nintendo Switch 2.
- Read more about how we test
- First reviewed: November 2026
Josh is Reviews Editor at TechRadar. With over ten years of experience covering tech both in print and online, he’s served as editor of T3 and net magazines and written about everything from groundbreaking gadgets to innovative Silicon Valley startups. He’s an expert in a wide range of products from Spatial Audio headphones to gaming handhelds. When he’s not putting trailblazing tech through its paces, he can be found making melodic techno or seeking out the perfect cold brew coffee.

articles.title: Si tu iPhone está desactualizado, hay un motivo urgente para ponerlo al día: pudo infectarse desde la web de IKEA o Zoom
articles.text:
Un ciberataque contra la plataforma web Optimizely permitió la distribución de malware a través de sitios de empresas y marcas genuinas como IKEA, Zoom, CNN, HSBC, BBC, Ledger y Air France-KLM. De acuerdo con Report URI, fueron 178 las organizaciones que se vieron impactadas por esta situación que tuvo lugar ayer, lunes 16 de noviembre. Entre los dispositivos apuntados se encuentran los iPhone y iPad que todavía corren versiones antiguas de sus sistemas operativos, por lo que se está recomendando ponerlos al día.
Según menciona Bleeping Computer, el ataque se produjo a través de una vulnerabilidad en el proceso de creación de cuentas de Optimizely. Esto abrió la puerta a que los piratas informáticos cargaran código JavaScript malicioso en las webs de varias empresas que usan la citada plataforma para personalizar sus sitios.
El malware en cuestión era capaz de realizar varias tareas y podía infectar los dispositivos que visitaran los portales pertenecientes a medios de comunicación, tecnológicas, aerolíneas o tiendas de retail, sin que estas empresas se dieran cuenta de qué sucedía. Si bien los iPhone y iPad no eran los únicos blancos de este ataque, sí se detectó la presencia de malware adicional para los dispositivos de Apple.
Respecto de las capacidades del software malicioso oculto en las webs en cuestión, se indica que podía interceptar datos de tarjetas de crédito, cambiar direcciones de carteras de criptomonedas, tomar capturas de pantalla y más. En el caso de los iPhone o iPad, se detectó la presencia de dos malware adicionales: Coruna y Darksword.
Tu iPhone o iPad pudo infectarse con malware en las webs de IKEA, Zoom o HSBC
Coruna y Darksword son malware que en el pasado ya hicieron estragos en modelos de iPhone o iPad que no ejecutan la última versión de sus sistemas operativos. En el caso de Optimizely, el primero habría apuntado a equipos que todavía usan iOS 13 a iOS 17, mientras que el segundo se habría enfocado en los que corren iOS 18 o superior. Incluso se menciona la aparición de referencias a móviles con iOS 26, aunque solo para listar sus características técnicas.
Vale aclarar, no obstante, que todavía no se han encontrado evidencias de que el hackeo a Optimizely haya permitido que los malware Coruna y Darksword infecten de forma efectiva los iPhone o iPad apuntados. La plataforma web atacada ya eliminó el código malicioso de los sitios de sus clientes y aplicó un parche a la vulnerabilidad que permitió el ingreso de los atacantes en primer lugar.
Los expertos que descubrieron el ciberataque con malware recomiendan actualizar tu iPhone o iPad a iOS 26.3/iPadOS 26.3 o superior. En el caso de que tengas un modelo que no admita dicho software, se sugiere instalar al menos iOS 18.7.3 o iPadOS 18.7.3.

articles.title: Microsoft testing Remote Lock for lost or stolen Windows devices
articles.text:
Microsoft is testing a new feature that lets enterprise IT administrators remotely lock stolen or lost Windows devices without wiping them.
Named Remote Lock, this new feature is shipping to devices upgraded to Windows 11 Insider Preview builds in the Beta (Build 26320.10003) and Experimental (Build 26340.10013) channels.
Admins can use Microsoft Intune custom configuration profiles to lock Microsoft Entra-joined, hybrid-joined, or MDM-enrolled devices that run Windows Enterprise, Education, or Pro.
After the IT department remotely locks the device, the system can only be unlocked via Intune, since PINs, passwords, local admins, or web sign-ins will no longer work. Microsoft added that the user's credentials will remain valid and can still be used to sign into other devices that haven't been locked.
"Windows signs out every active session, hides all sign-in options and shows a locked screen," said Windows Insider communications lead Stephen Lines. "Nothing is erased: the device stays enrolled and managed, BitLocker stays on and user data stays in place. The lock holds across restarts and while offline, and only an admin can lift it remotely, so the user picks up where they left off."
Admins can lock a device from the Intune admin center using the following procedure:
- Go to Devices > Windows > Configuration > Create > New policy. Choose Windows 10 and later, then Templates > Custom.
- Name the profile (for example, Remote lock - ON) and add the settings below, with LockState = 1.
- Assign the profile to a device group reserved for locked devices. To lock a device, add it to that group; the lock applies at the device's next check-in.
- To unlock, create a second profile with LockState set to 0 and assign it to an unlock group. Move the device from the lock group to the unlock group.
After Remote Lock is enabled, the device is not isolated from the enterprise network or erased. To do that, admins must use the device isolation and wipe controls in Intune.
However, users must keep BitLocker enabled to protect their data if the device is reimaged or the drive is removed because the Windows Recovery Environment, Safe Mode, and booting from USB or other media are not blocked.
With these Windows 11 preview builds, Microsoft has also begun testing new advanced security key management features that let users view and manage passkeys stored on a FIDO2 (Fast Identity Online 2) security key individually.
These new features allow admins to configure enterprise settings such as always-required user verification, minimum PIN length, and enterprise attestation.
In August, Microsoft also announced new privacy controls that let Windows 11 users choose which desktop apps can access their microphone, camera, and precise location.

articles.title: Plus de 1 000 km d’autonomie à 37 000 € ? Ce SUV BYD n’arrivera pas chez nous de sitôt
articles.text:
La voiture électrique aux 1 000 km d’autonomie ? C’est un fantasme aussi inutile qu’ancien qui deviendra très bientôt réalité. Chez Mercedes, l’EQS peut aujourd’hui parcourir 925 km. Chez Lucid, la Air pousse même le délire à 960 km. De bien jolies valeurs provenant néanmoins de modèles hors de prix. Avec ses 912 km d’autonomie, la BMW i3 joue déjà dans une gamme tarifaire inférieure, sans se montrer encore accessible, entendons-nous.
Et puis, tout le monde ne veut pas faire de compromis sur la praticité. Mauvaise nouvelle, les véhicules précités sont tous des berlines qui ne sont naturellement pas les reines du déménagement. BYD dégaine donc une solution au problème avec le Denza N8, un SUV électrique aussi habitable qu’endurant. Avec 5,15 mètres de long, 1,99 mètre de large et 1,82 mètre de haut, l’engin est capable de tout engloutir, ou presque.
Jusqu’à 1 003 km d’autonomie et une recharge éclair en 9 minutes
Contrairement au N8L rallongé, le N8 se limite à cinq occupants pour privilégier un volume de coffre grimpant à 1 046 litres. Le tout est complété par un rangement avant de 205 litres, ce qui devrait largement suffire pour ranger les câbles de recharge. Côté technique, le N8 s’octroie des batteries de 105,8 et 130,2 kWh offrant entre 800 et 1 003 km d’autonomie sur le cycle CLTC. Les valeurs dépendront largement de la version choisie.
Car le Chinois propose deux variantes en propulsion de 435 et 503 ch, accompagnées d’une déclinaison trimoteur développant en cumulé 1 210 ch, ce qui n’a pas grand sens, nous sommes d’accord. Côté recharge, les batteries équipées de la technologie Blade 2.0 admettent un 10 à 70 % en 5 minutes et un 10 à 97 % en 9 minutes sur une borne appropriée. Vraiment remarquable vu la taille des batteries, et pas illusoire.
Un tarif équivalent à 37 000 €… mais interdit d’Europe
Les premières stations Flash Charging de BYD sont en cours de déploiement en Europe pour fournir une puissance de charge en courant continu DC de 1 500 kW. Vous pourrez alors y brancher votre Denza Z9GT ou votre BYD Atto 8, mais pas ce Denza N8. Et pour cause, il n’est pas vendu chez nous. On se doute bien que le tarif qui équivaut à 37 000 € est surtout destiné aux Chinois…
Frustrant, mais de plus en plus proche de nous, tout de même… L’équipement peut aussi faire jaser, avec un écran tactile de 30 pouces surmonté d’un bandeau numérique de 1,1 mètre de large, des suspensions pneumatiques intelligentes, quatre roues directrices et la conduite autonome God’s Eye 5.0. Une version hybride rechargeable offrant 435 km d’autonomie en mode électrique suivra.

articles.title: Millionen Dokumente geleakt: Enthüllungen setzen die Deutsche Bank unter Druck
articles.text:
Millionen E-Mails geleakt: Compliance-Vorwürfe setzen Deutsche Bank unter Druck
Die Deutsche Bank soll über Jahre hinweg trotz Warnungen ihrer eigenen Compliance immer wieder Geschäfte mit Hochrisikokunden gemacht haben. Das geht aus Berichten verschiedener internationaler Medien hervor, die gemeinsam ein Datenleck aus mehr als 15 Millionen internen Dokumenten der Bank ausgewertet haben, darunter interne E-Mails, Protokolle von Vorstandssitzungen, Compliance-Akten und Chatprotokolle von Mitarbeitern.
Offenbar mehr Epstein-Transaktionen als zuvor bekannt
So soll die Bank etwa Transaktionen von über 582 Millionen US-Dollar im Zusammenhang mit dem Sexualstraftäter Jeffrey Epstein durchgeführt haben, wesentlich mehr, als bislang öffentlich bekannt war. Bedenken der eigenen Compliance-Teams zur Zusammenarbeit mit Hochrisikokunden soll die Bank ignoriert haben. So wurden Beziehungen zu Kunden fortgesetzt oder angebahnt, obwohl interne Fachleute vor Geldwäsche, Korruption oder Sanktionsverstößen warnten.
Zu den Medien, die die Mails auswerten, gehören unter anderem die Financial Times, Le Monde, die New York Times sowie der Spiegel und das Manager Magazin. Sie werteten gemeinsam Daten aus, die ihnen von Whistleblowern zugespielt wurden.
Laut dem Bericht des Spiegel wollte die Bank etwa ihr Russlandgeschäft noch kurz vor dem Angriff auf die Ukraine ausbauen und setzte trotz Bedenken der Compliance noch stark auf die Zusammenarbeit mit russischen Oligarchen.
Die KYC-Regeln („Know Your Customer“), also die vorgeschriebenen Verfahren zur Identifizierung und Überprüfung von Kunden, sollen zudem nicht so streng angewendet worden sein wie erforderlich. Außerdem sollen interne Kontrollen vernachlässigt worden sein, „um Kosten zu sparen und den Tradern nicht im Weg zu stehen“.
Die Dokumente zeigen auch die Beteiligung der Bank an umstrittenen Steuermodellen für vermögende Kunden sowie neue Details zur Geschäftsbeziehung mit US-Präsident Donald Trump.
„Wir sind heute eine andere Bank“
Die Deutsche Bank verweist in einer Stellungnahme darauf, dass die genannten Fälle viele Jahre zurückliegen. Die Bank habe sie „soweit relevant“ bereits seinerzeit geprüft und eng mit den Regulierungsbehörden zusammengearbeitet. Nennenswerte finanzielle Auswirkungen durch das Datenleck erwartet die Bank nicht.
Unter der Führung von Vorstandschef Christian Sewing habe die Deutsche Bank außerdem einen grundlegenden Wandel durchlaufen, etwa indem massiv in die internen Kontrollsysteme investiert wurde. Die ausgewerteten Daten seien viele Jahre alt, heute sei die Deutsche Bank „eine andere Bank“.
Sewing hatte 2018 die Führung bei der damals krisengeschüttelten Deutschen Bank übernommen. Im Jahr 2015 zahlte die Deutsche Bank etwa wegen der Manipulation des Referenzzinses Libor 2,5 Milliarden Dollar an US- und britische Aufseher. 2017 folgte ein weiterer Vergleich über 7,2 Milliarden Dollar mit dem US-Justizministerium wegen irreführender Verkäufe von Hypothekenpapieren.
Beim Amtsantritt versprach Sewing ein Ende der Skandale und Rechtsstreitigkeiten, intern soll er laut dem Daten-Leak aber zuvor strenge Compliance-Regeln kritisiert haben. Der radikale Umbau unter Sewing brachte der Bank zuletzt Rekordgewinne von 9,7 Milliarden Euro vor Steuern.
Ganz krisenfrei verliefen allerdings auch die vergangenen Jahre nicht: So gab es etwa 2022 eine Razzia wegen des Verdachts, Geldwäscheverdachtsanzeigen zu spät abgegeben zu haben. Wegen der Probleme bei der Postbank-Integration hatte die Finanzaufsicht BaFin zuletzt eine Geldbuße über acht Millionen Euro gegen die Deutsche Bank verhängt. Außerdem kamen erste Details zur Kundenbeziehung mit Epstein heraus, und ein teures Gerichtsverfahren um die Postbank-Übernahme belastete die Bank.
An der Börse brachen die Aktien der Deutschen Bank im frühen Handel ein. Die Papiere gaben in der Spitze um 6,2 Prozent auf 30,88 Euro nach.

articles.title: Los fontaneros expertos avisan: si abres el grifo y cae un chorro de agua débil, el problema ya ha comenzado y puede ser peor de lo que parece
articles.text:
Que el agua salga del grifo con menos fuerza de la habitual puede parecer una molestia menor, pero también puede ser el primer aviso de que algo no funciona en la instalación de tu casa. Y detrás de este problema puede haber muchas cosas, desde un aireador sucio hasta una fuga. Aquí, los fontaneros advierten que no siempre se trata de una avería grave, aunque tampoco conviene dejar pasar semanas antes de mirarlo.
Un grifo o toda la casa. Lo primero es averiguar hasta dónde llega el problema, si es cosa de la fontanería de tu casa o de la red. Por ejemplo, si es solo un grifo ya sabes que el problema está en casa, pero si afecta a toda la vivienda pueden ser más cosasa, desde una llave de paso mal abierta a unas tuberías envejecidas, pasando incluso por un problema en la red pública. Y también importa si el bajón se nota sólo con el agua caliente o en todo.
La cal del aireador. Cuando el culpable es un único grifo, lo más probable es que la pieza que tiene en la boca, el aireador, se haya ido llenando de cal y otras partículas. Lo mismo pasa si el problema sucede solo en las alcachofas de la ducha. La solución es bastante sencilla, y basta con desenroscarlo, dejarlo un rato en vinagre, frotarlo con un cepillo de dientes viejo, aclararlo bien y volver a colocarlo. Eso sí, si el chorro sigue flojo toca revisar la llave de paso de ese grifo, que puede haberse quedado medio cerrada tras una reparación o un golpe accidental.
Cuando falla toda la casa. Las tuberías antiguas, sobre todo las de acero galvanizado, van acumulando depósitos por dentro que acaban estrechando el paso del agua, que también recuerda que la llave general tiene que quedar abierta del todo después de cualquier trabajo de fontanería. Vamos, que el tubo se va estrechando por dentro. Otra posibilidad es que falle la válvula reductora de presión, y en ese caso lo recomendable es que lo revise un fontanero.
La fuga que no se ve. Pero lo complicado llega cuando tenemos una fuga, porque puede manifestarse como una pérdida de presión antes de que aparezca ningún charco. Hay otras pistas, como una factura que sube sin que hayas cambiado tus hábitos, manchas de humedad o pintura que se levanta. Y las paredes que siguen húmedas también son un aviso, algo que la Agencia de Protección Ambiental de Estados Unidos pide vigilar en su lista para detectar fugas.
Agua caliente y pozos. ¿Y si sólo pierde fuerza el agua caliente? Pues entonces conviene mirar el termo o el acumulador, donde se van depositando sedimentos. En las viviendas con pozo, el fallo puede estar en la bomba o en el presostato, que puede quedarse atascado y dejar la casa sin presión, o en un filtro sucio, que también puede restar presión.
Y antes de llamar a nadie, merece la pena preguntar a los vecinos. Si ellos tienen una presión normal, el problema está en tu casa, pero si les pasa lo mismo puede deberse a una rotura en una conducción principal o a un pico de consumo en la zona, o incluso trabajos de mantenimiento en la red. En estos casos, lo que toca es consultar a la compañía de abastecimiento, porque por mucho que revises las tuberías de casa no vas a encontrar nada.
Foto | Jos Speetjens

articles.title: El FBI alertó que la herramienta de IA Artex permite hackear empresas en menos de tres horas
articles.text:
El FBI advirtió que hackers de todo el mundo usan Artex, un programa gratuito que dirige asistentes de IA para atacar redes ajenas. En algunos casos, pasaron de elegir a la víctima a obtener acceso con permisos de administrador en menos de tres horas, según el aviso publicado el 13 de noviembre de 2026.
El documento de 13 páginas describe a Artex como una plataforma que convierte objetivos escritos en lenguaje común en órdenes que ejecutan agentes de IA, asistentes que realizan tareas por su cuenta. Esos agentes exploran la red, buscan fallas, amplían sus permisos y extraen datos con poca intervención humana.
Artex no incluye un modelo de IA propio. Se conecta a los de otras empresas: Claude, de Anthropic, y GPT, de OpenAI, además de DeepSeek, GLM, Grok y Kimi.
En las instalaciones que controlan los atacantes predominan los modelos chinos, sobre todo la familia DeepSeek Flash, según el FBI. La agencia atribuye esa preferencia a su bajo costo y a que casi no ponen límites cuando el pedido se presenta como una prueba de seguridad.
Desde al menos agosto de 2026, distintos grupos usaron la herramienta contra organizaciones de servicios financieros, gobierno, tecnología, defensa, energía, salud y telecomunicaciones, entre otros sectores. El FBI señala que permite a personas con poca experiencia técnica lanzar operaciones complejas contra varios objetivos a la vez.
Dos ataques con miles de afectados
El caso más grande es el de ConnectWise, una empresa estadounidense de software para administrar sistemas informáticos. Los atacantes entraron por su servicio de copias de seguridad en la nube y accedieron a entornos de Microsoft 365 de más de 2.250 clientes, según el FBI. Microsoft atribuyó esa campaña a un grupo alineado con el Estado chino, informó BleepingComputer.
TechCrunch señaló que ConnectWise no respondió a su pedido de comentarios sobre las afirmaciones del FBI.
En Corea del Sur, delincuentes con fines económicos usaron Artex contra entidades financieras y robaron datos personales de unas 67.000 personas, según el aviso. Medios de comunicación han atribuido el éxito de esos ataques en gran parte a defensas débiles, como la falta de verificación en dos pasos.
BleepingComputer informó además que la policía surcoreana arrestó a siete sospechosos por ataques a más de 90 organizaciones, en los que según ese medio se usó Artex en la mayoría de las intrusiones.
La empresa de seguridad Barracuda también sufrió un ataque. Delincuentes encontraron con Artex una credencial de un proveedor externo que la compañía nunca había revocado al terminar su trabajo con él. Desde la compañía de seguridad se señaló que sus registros no permiten descartar un acceso y cambió todas las credenciales de sus clientes por precaución.
“Los defensores que dependen de detectar actividad maliciosa y luego responder suelen llegar cuando el atacante ya terminó”, escribió Arve Kjoelen, director de seguridad de la información de Barracuda.
Las fallas de siempre, ahora más rápido
Según TechSpot, ninguna de las intrusiones descritas usó fallas nuevas: Artex aprovechó contraseñas filtradas, falta de verificación en dos pasos y accesos que seguían activos tras terminar la relación con un proveedor. El FBI agrega que la herramienta es eficaz contra sistemas periféricos, como portales de socios y proveedores, aplicaciones de empleados y servicios antiguos.
Los ataques generan mucho tráfico sospechoso que puede activar alarmas, pero su velocidad deja poco tiempo para que los equipos de defensa reaccionen antes de que el atacante cumpla su objetivo, según el aviso.
Amazon publicó el 13 de noviembre su propio estudio. Su director de seguridad de la información, CJ Moses, describió grupos vinculados con China que robaron credenciales de acceso a modelos de IA, en una operación que se autofinanciaba: las claves robadas pagaban la IA que servía para buscar más claves. Otra campaña apuntó a casas de cambio de criptomonedas, informó The Record.
El creador retiró la herramienta, pero sigue circulando
Artex apareció en julio de 2026 en GitHub, una plataforma para compartir código, publicado por un desarrollador que usa el nombre Autumn-27. Retiró el repositorio el 8 de octubre tras los informes de abuso y dijo que la herramienta servía para pruebas de seguridad autorizadas.
El FBI sostiene que Artex sigue disponible mediante copias, versiones modificadas y una edición comercial llamada Artex Pro. A principios de noviembre, investigadores detectaron más de 1.600 paneles de control de la herramienta expuestos en internet, y el total de instalaciones sería mucho mayor.
El FBI recomienda a las organizaciones inventariar todas sus aplicaciones conectadas a internet, incluidas las periféricas, limitar los permisos de aplicaciones de terceros y conservar los registros de acceso. Quienes tengan aplicaciones de ConnectWise autorizadas en Microsoft 365 deben mantenerlas desconectadas hasta que la empresa dé instrucciones formales para restablecerlas. La agencia pide reportar actividad sospechosa a su centro de denuncias de delitos informáticos, el IC3.

articles.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
articles.text:
Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
By treating qubits like individual molecules, scientists can now predict their behavior faster and more accurately
- Date:
- November 13, 2026
- Source:
- Princeton University
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers.
- Share:
A new computational technique could accelerate the search for diamond materials capable of powering future quantum computers and highly sensitive sensors. Developed by a researcher at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory (PPPL), the method makes it much easier to identify promising materials for quantum technology, potentially opening the door to advances across many areas of science.
The approach has already revealed new candidates for quantum computing and sensing applications. The findings were recently published in ACS Central Science and have attracted attention from other researchers in the field.
One of the biggest challenges in developing quantum technology is finding materials that can maintain delicate quantum states under practical conditions. Many candidates require extremely low temperatures to function reliably. Diamond materials stand out because certain quantum properties can remain useful even at room temperature.
This capability could help advance technologies that are important to national research priorities and the development of next-generation computing. Quantum sensors promise levels of sensitivity and precision beyond those of conventional instruments, while quantum computers could eventually solve certain extraordinarily complex problems much faster than today's most powerful supercomputers.
Why Imperfect Diamonds Could Be the Key to Quantum Computing
Although diamonds are made of carbon atoms, a flawless diamond crystal is not enough to create a useful quantum computing system. The key lies in tiny irregularities within the crystal structure.
These imperfections, known as defects, can occur when a carbon atom is absent from its normal position, when another element replaces a carbon atom, or when both changes occur together. The atoms surrounding these defects can form qubits, the basic units used to store and process quantum information in quantum computers and sensors.
Finding the most useful defects, however, has been difficult. Accurately modeling their quantum behavior traditionally requires enormous computational resources, making it challenging to evaluate large numbers of possible candidates.
A Simpler Way to Discover Better Diamond Qubits
Mark Martirez, a staff research scientist at PPPL, developed a way to dramatically reduce the complexity of these calculations. Instead of simulating a much larger diamond structure, he isolates a small region containing just 16 to 30 atoms around a defect.
By "carving out" this tiny atomic cluster and treating it like a separate molecule, Martirez can use powerful computational methods that chemists have spent decades refining. These established techniques make it possible to analyze the quantum properties of diamond defects much more efficiently without sacrificing the high level of accuracy needed for the calculations.
"Because we're treating the qubits as molecules, the cost of calculating these defects is equivalent to the cost of just modeling a simple molecule," Martirez said. "This method really opened the floodgates" in terms of how qubits can be assessed.
The new technique allows researchers to calculate how different qubits respond to laser light and microwave pulses far more quickly than before. Using this approach, the team identified promising defects involving boron and oxygen that could serve as new types of qubits.
New Diamond Defects Reveal a Spectrum of Quantum Colors
Light plays an important role in how scientists interact with diamond qubits. Researchers use lasers and microwave pulses to manipulate their quantum states and retrieve stored information.
Much of the previous work in this area has centered on a defect known as the nitrogen-vacancy center. This structure forms when a nitrogen atom takes the place of a carbon atom in a diamond crystal, while an adjacent position that would normally contain another carbon atom remains empty.
Under laser illumination, this type of defect can emit red light when it occupies a particular quantum state.
The newly investigated defects offer different optical properties. Oxygen defects can produce blue light, while those involving boron emit ultraviolet light.
These differences could make it possible to combine several types of qubits within a single quantum device. Because each type responds differently to light, researchers might be able to interact with one group of qubits without disturbing another.
"One could imagine, then, combining different qubits of different responses, so you can basically probe one qubit but not the other," Martirez said.
Beyond identifying new candidates, the findings suggest a broader change in how researchers approach quantum technology. Diamond qubits have traditionally been studied primarily through physics, but understanding their underlying chemistry could provide additional ways to design them.
Martirez believes that researchers could eventually engineer qubits for particular functions using principles similar to those applied when chemists create specialized molecules, including compounds designed for new medications.
How Quantum Chemistry Could Transform Future Research
The potential benefits extend well beyond the development of quantum computers themselves. Martirez sees an intriguing possibility in which advances made possible by quantum chemistry eventually lead to quantum technologies that help improve the field of chemistry.
In other words, quantum chemistry could develop the very tools needed to "enrich itself" in the coming decades.
A practical quantum system containing multiple qubits could make molecular calculations substantially more accurate. That would allow scientists to study increasingly complex chemical structures, including large biological molecules and proteins, with a level of detail that is difficult to achieve using conventional methods.
"We could describe larger molecules, biomolecules, proteins and everything like that in a more accurate way, and that could improve all the chemical-adjacent industries, such as pharmaceutical science and materials science. Even our fundamental understanding of molecular systems could be enriched."
Such improvements could have far-reaching implications for pharmaceutical development, materials research, and the fundamental study of how molecules behave.
Martirez also hopes the research will encourage more chemists to explore solid-state physics. Although building advanced quantum computers is often viewed as a challenge primarily for physicists, he argues that chemistry offers valuable expertise that could help accelerate progress.
"At this moment in time, there's a great emphasis on building the first state-of-the-art qubit computer," he said. "But it's not just physicists who should be participating in this research. Chemists have decades of developed intuition about chemical systems that could be easily translated into understanding defects in solids as well."
By bringing these disciplines together, scientists may be able to develop more effective ways to discover, understand, and eventually engineer the quantum materials needed for future technologies.
The research was funded through PPPL's Laboratory Directed Research and Development program under prime contract number DE-AC02-09CH11466, with additional support from the DOE Office of Science, Office of Fusion Energy Sciences.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Princeton University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- John Mark P. Martirez. A Chemist’sGuide to Solid-State Qubits: DiamondColor Centers as Embedded Vacancy-Centered Molecules. ACS Central Science, 2026; 12 (10): 1578 DOI: 10.1021/acscentsci.6c00548

articles.title: Voyage Labs raises $12 million for a specialized AI travel assistant | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Planning a trip is a favorite demo for personal AI assistants — you can try it with Muse, or with Gemini, or half a dozen other choices. But while most pitches use travel-planning as part of a general-purpose agent pitch, a new startup from a Google Maps alum is betting that a specialized travel-planning agent can beat the competition.
The company is called Voyage Labs, and on Tuesday it announced $12 million in seed funding led by Kleiner Perkins, with participation from SignalFire and SV Angel. The company plans to use the funding to expand supplier partnerships and grow its engineering team.
Voyage Labs’ flagship product, called Atlas, is meant to work as a personal assistant for your trip-planning, available today in private beta.
“People can use it to plan and book and manage their entire journey, from the time they have an inspiration to the time they come back home,” says co-founder and CEO Manik Gupta.
Atlas is designed to serve as an always-on assistant throughout the planning process, fielding ideas and doing research on every idea that’s raised. The long time horizon means Atlas can tailor recommendations based on weeks of conversation, while also monitoring real-time price fluctuations and ultimately booking flights and hotels.
For the Voyage founders, it’s an ideal match between technology and use case. “Trip planning is a project that has its own lifecycle,” says Yogesh Jain, co-founder and CTO of the company. “You’re planning across days and weeks — so long-running agents as a technology matches that very well.”
Travel assistants are already a crowded field, but Voyage will be starting with a lot of experience in the space. Gupta was previously the director of Product Management for Google Maps, followed by four years as chief product officer at Uber. As he puts it, “I spent eight years where my only job was to wake up in the morning and go build the map. I’m just very obsessed with that problem.”
The biggest question is how Atlas will compete with the multi-purpose AI assistants built by frontier labs. But as Gupta notes, the space is still changing fast, and it’s hard for anyone to be sure what form factors will thrive in the coming years. Ultimately, Voyage is betting that travel is specialized enough to need a specialized product.
“We are making a bet that this vertical around travel and outdoors is a large enough vertical that it needs a focused product solution,” Gupta told TechCrunch. “Ultimately, we believe we can actually stitch together an end-to-end experience that will help users.”

articles.title: Instagram is helping creators crack down on copycat videos
articles.text:
Instagram is beginning to roll out a “content protection” feature that lets creators see and review copies of their videos posted to the platform.
Instagram is helping creators crack down on copycat videos
Meta will let creators decide to hide copies of their videos flagged by a new ‘content protection’ feature.
“For eligible creators who enroll, content protection is a tool that automatically looks out for visual matches of your original videos, alerts you when we find a match across Instagram and Facebook, and lets you decide what happens next,” Meta says in a blog post. Meta launched a similar tool for Facebook last year to help users “safeguard” their Reels and “maintain control” over their creative work.
When an Instagram creator is notified of a matched video, they can see how many views the match has and decide if they want to track the video, hide it from everyone on Instagram and Facebook, add a credit link, or release their claim on the match.
After a creator enrolls, every “original video” they post on Instagram is protected, and creators can retroactively protect older videos manually. Creators can also put accounts on an allow list that lets them use their videos.
In addition, Instagram will start flagging AI-generated videos that “match the spoken words” in a creator’s original video but have visuals replaced with AI. Initially, Instagram will test this with a “small group of creators” in “the coming weeks.” The platform says it’s exploring ways to limit the reach of content and profiles that “use AI tools to post this type of content repeatedly.”

articles.title: Pionnier de l'ouverture variable sur smartphones, Samsung s'apprêterait à redonner sa chance à la technologie
articles.text:
Alors qu'Apple a lancé son premier smartphone équipé d'un objectif à ouverture variable, Samsung jette un regard envieux à son concurrent américain, et envisage de remettre le couvert pour ses prochaines générations de flagships.
Le géant des smartphones a-t-il du mal à avaler qu'Apple empiète sur ses plate-bandes ? Toujours est-il que, d'après un informateur cité par GSM Arena, Samsung envisage bel et bien le retour d'une optique à ouverture dynamique non pas pour les Galaxy S27, mais pour la génération suivante, laquelle tomberait justement pour les 10 ans du Galaxy S9 — le premier à embarquer cette technologie novatrice (et un peu gadget).
- Qualité de l'écran
- Filtre de confidentialité intégré à l'écran
- Performances globales
Samsung ferait son retour sur les objectifs à ouverture variable
En 2018, Samsung faisait tourner les têtes en parvenant à embarquer dans un smartphone alors assez compact un objectif à ouverture variable. Monté sur un capteur 1/2.55" de 12 mégapixels, il offrait une ouverture impressionnante pour l'époque, oscillant entre f/1.5 et f/2.4. À titre de comparaison, le récent Galaxy S26 Ultra est équipé d'un objectif f/1.4 sur un capteur grand-angle de 1/1.3" et de 200 mégapixels.
Il est évidemment encore tôt pour savoir précisément ce que Samsung a en tête, mais la technologie a bien évolué en 10 ans. Pour preuve, Apple intègre sur ses iPhone 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max une optique capable d'offrir différents niveaux d'ouverture entre f/1.5 et f/4.0. Comme sur un appareil photo conventionnel, l'utilisateur peut choisir finement à quelle ouverture il déclenchera l'obturateur — ou laisser le smartphone sélectionner les réglages les plus adaptés.
D'accord, mais pour quoi faire ?
Offrir un objectif à ouverture variable sur un smartphone, c'est déjà réduire l'écart qui sépare ce type d'appareils d'une véritable caméra. Plus on offre de liberté créative aux utilisateurs, mieux c'est, pas vrai ? En permettant de sélectionner soit une très large ouverture (f/1.5) soit une ouverture moyenne (f/4.0), on joue sur la captation de lumière, et donc directement sur le piqué et l'effet "bokeh". Cela dit, on reste sur des capteurs assez petits, et un f/1.5 sur un smartphone n'équivaut absolument pas à une ouverture similaire sur un objectif d'appareil photo plein format. Toujours est-il que cette technologie a ses adeptes — même si j'ai personnellement trouvé qu'on arrête d'y penser à peu près 15 minutes après avoir déballé le téléphone.
On connait de toute façon la chanson : quand ce n'est pas l'un, c'est l'autre. Après Apple qui s'inspire du Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 pour son iPhone Duo, c'est au tour du géant sud-coréen de reprendre son grand rival en exemple. Notons toutefois que les deux marques ne sont pas les seules à investir ce segment de marché assez niche : Xiaomi avait aussi tenté le coup de l'ouverture variable en 2024 avec son Xiaomi 14 Ultra.
Source : GSM Arena

articles.title: Court clears brothers of $25 million Ethereum crypto heist charges
articles.text:
US District Judge Jessica Clarke has acquitted two brothers accused of stealing $25 million in cryptocurrency in about 12 seconds through a scheme that exploited a bug in the Ethereum blockchain.
Clarke's decision comes one year after a mistrial in the same case, after jurors failed to agree on whether to convict or acquit former Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) students Anton Peraire-Bueno and James Peraire-Bueno in this first-of-its-kind scheme, as Reuters first reported.
"The question before the Court is not whether the Peraire-Buenos' conduct was right or moral, or even whether it violated uncharged crimes. It is simply whether the evidence at trial, construed in a light most favorable to the Government, could support wire fraud and related convictions in this case," the federal judge said.
"Because the Government failed to prove that the Peraire-Buenos made any material misrepresentations in the execution of their scheme, the motion is granted, and a judgment of acquittal is entered for Anton Peraire-Bueno and James Peraire-Bueno."
The Peraire-Bueno brothers were arrested in Boston and New York in May 2024 on wire fraud and money laundering charges and were facing 20 years in prison for each count if convicted.
According to prosecutors, the brothers allegedly manipulated blockchain transaction validation processes by accessing pending private transactions, altering them, obtaining victims' cryptocurrency, and rejecting requests to return the stolen funds.
The indictment claimed they learned their victims' trading behaviors while preparing the attack (starting in December 2022) and took measures to hide the stolen proceeds and their identities.
They were also accused of using multiple cryptocurrency addresses and foreign exchanges and setting up shell companies. After the attack, they also allegedly moved the stolen crypto assets through a series of transactions to obscure their source and ownership.
The prosecutors also said that, while planning and executing the attack, the brothers deployed a series of "bait transactions" designed to identify "victim traders," exploited a vulnerability in the MEV-Boost relay code, causing the relay to release the full content of a proposed block prematurely, and reordered the proposed block to their advantage.
In the next stage of the scheme, they allegedly reordered the block on the Ethereum blockchain, which resulted in the theft of approximately $25 million in cryptocurrency from the victim traders.
Throughout the process, the brothers also allegedly searched online for information on carrying out the attack, concealing their involvement in the Ethereum exploit, and laundering the criminal proceeds through cryptocurrency exchanges with lax verification procedures.
Prosecutors also said they hired attorneys with expertise in cryptocurrency, extradition procedures, and the crimes outlined in the indictment.

articles.title: Les Xiaomi 18 Pro et Pro Max arrivent en France : tout ce qu'il faut savoir sur ces deux smartphones à double écran
articles.text:
Les Xiaomi 18 Pro et Pro Max arrivent en France : tout ce qu'il faut savoir sur ces deux smartphones à double écran
Déjà officiels en Chine, les Xiaomi 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max font leurs débuts en France. Les deux smartphones, positionnés sur un segment tarifaire pour le moins premium, misent sur un bloc photo dorsal niché dans un deuxième écran, mais aussi sur des technologies dédiées à la confidentialité des données. Voici ce qu'il faut retenir des deux appareil, tarif inclus.
L’annonce date de la fin septembre en Chine, et s’inscrit dans un bouleversement du calendrier habituel de la téléphonie. Le Snapdragon Summit de Qualcomm, organisé chaque année aux États-Unis et accueillant les nouvelles puces mobiles du fondeur, est intervenu si tôt que des terminaux habituellement officialisés fin décembre n’attendent plus l’hiver pour faire leurs débuts. C’est le cas du Honor Magic 9 Pro Max, mais aussi du Motorola Signature 27 et, aujourd’hui, de Xiaomi 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max.
Xiaomi 18 Pro Max
Des caractéristiques des deux smartphones, aujourd’hui disponibles sur le marché français, on savait déjà tout, puisqu’ils sont déjà commercialisés en Chine. Les 18 Pro et Pro Max ne lésinent sur rien, qu’il s’agisse de leur écrans, Oled annonçant certes une haute luminosité (4000 cd/m²), mais aussi et surtout une technologie de confidentialité. À l’instar de Samsung - mais attention, il s’agit d’une technologie propriétaire développée pour Xiaomi par un partenaire dont il tait l’identité - l’afficheur des deux smartphone dispose d’un système destiné à dissimuler aux importuns leur contenu. Ce "filtre" peut être activé à la volée sur l’ensemble de l’écran ou être appliquée automatiquement à certaines applications ou notifications ; s’y ajoute même une alerte, à activer par l’utilisateur, pour l’avertir lorsqu’un curieux regarde ostensiblement son téléphone.
Un écran anti-espion à l'avant, et un second écran au dos
Derrière cet écran se cache… un autre écran. Les 18 Pro et Pro Max disposent, au dos, d’une dalle secondaire permettent de consulter des notifications, de visualiser des selfies réalisés aux capteurs dorsaux ou même de faire tourner des mini-applications générées en IA. C’était l’atout de la série 17 Pro qui a boudé l’Europe en 2025, et certainement l’atout charme des deux mobiles.
L’écran dorsal est percé de deux ouvertures dédiées aux appareils photo des smartphones, qui arborent la griffe Leica. Module principal de 200 Mpx compatible avec la technologie Lofic (c’est uniquement le cas du Pro Max), module à téléobjectif de 200 mégapixels également et capteur de 50 Mpx associé à un ultra grand-angle : les terminaux entendent jouer la polyvalence.
Un dernier élément est à retenir : Qualcomm, qui impose son calendrier à ses partenaires, fournit à Xiaomi la puce Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 à son Pro Max, et son Elite Gen 6 au 18 Pro, tous deux flanqués de 12 Go de RAM. Nous avons éprouvé la version Extrême, très prometteuse sur le plan des performances. Il lui reste à prouver sa bonne prestation sur le plan de la gestion de l'énergie. Pour ce faire, Xiaomi opte pour des batteries de 6000 mAh (modèle Pro) et 7050 mAh (Pro Max), un peu moins généreuses toutefois que leurs homologues vendues en Chine. Rappelons que les deux smartphones se distinguent par leur format : si le Pro Max atteint les 6,9 pouces, le 18 Pro dispose d'un écran de 6,4 pouces.
La tendance est à la hausse des prix, et Xiaomi n'y échappe pas
Ce panorama ne serait pas complet sans un mot sur le tarif de lancement des deux appareils. Alors que Find X10 Pro Max a fait ses débuts en octobre 2026 à 1799 € et que le Motorola Signature 27 vient d'être annoncé à 1899 €, nous nous attendions à une ardoise salée. Les prix augmentent certes, mais dans une moindre mesure que ces deux appareils, puisque Xiaomi annonce son 18 Pro à 1399 € en 12/256 Go, et 1599 € en 12/512 Go, tandis que le 18 Pro Max s'affiche à 1599 € en 12/256 Go et à 1799 € en 12/512 Go. Pour leurs débuts et jusqu'au 3 janvier, le fabricant propose le modèle 512 Go de chacun de ses terminaux au prix de sa version 256 Go, et bonifie de 100 € la reprise d'un ancien smartphone.

articles.title: Anthropic pagará hasta USD 120.500 millones a SpaceX por cómputo, pero ambos pueden desistir
articles.text:
Anthropic acordó gastar hasta USD 120.500 millones en capacidad de cómputo de SpaceX hasta 2029, según el prospecto de su salida a bolsa que la empresa de IA presentó el 26 de octubre ante la SEC, el regulador bursátil de Estados Unidos. Cualquiera de las dos partes puede cancelar los acuerdos con 90 días de aviso por escrito.
El prospecto detalla que los acuerdos con SpaceXAI, filial de SpaceX antes llamada X.AI, se firmaron y modificaron entre mayo y octubre de 2026. Dan acceso a computación basada en chips de Nvidia. Los pagos llegarán a unos USD 3.100 millones por mes cuando toda la capacidad esté entregada, algo que Anthropic prevé para diciembre de 2026.
Durante la puesta en marcha, las tarifas son distintas. La cifra de 120.500 millones es un máximo, no un monto garantizado: depende de que ninguna de las partes use la salida contractual antes de que terminen los plazos.
Un compromiso con fecha de salida
Los acuerdos tienen períodos iniciales que no se pueden cancelar y terminan en enero y marzo de 2027, según el prospecto. Después de esas fechas, Anthropic o SpaceX pueden terminar cada contrato con un aviso de 90 días. Si el aviso se enviara el día que vence cada período, los contratos terminarían a partir de fines de abril y fines de junio de 2027, un cálculo aproximado.
La condición contrasta con la de otros proveedores. El medio Data Center Dynamics informó, a partir del prospecto actualizado, que los contratos con Google, Amazon y Microsoft son en su mayoría no cancelables, salvo incumplimientos graves sin corregir, y deben pagarse aunque no se use toda la capacidad.
El pago a SpaceX ya había cambiado de tamaño. Yahoo Finance recordó que Reuters publicó en septiembre una cifra de USD 84.500 millones, tomada del prospecto confidencial. El propio documento de SpaceX, presentado en mayo, indicaba que Anthropic pagaría USD 1.250 millones por mes hasta mayo de 2029 y que cualquiera de las partes podía salir con 90 días de aviso.
La compra de cómputo es el mayor gasto de Anthropic
Fortune informó que, en total, Anthropic asumió compromisos de entre USD 542.000 millones y USD 567.000 millones en cómputo e infraestructura futura. En el segundo trimestre de 2026, la capacidad de cómputo fue su principal gasto operativo, con USD 5.600 millones, frente a ingresos de USD 11.600 millones en el mismo período.
La relación con SpaceX comenzó, según Yahoo Finance, con el uso de todo Colossus 1, un centro de datos de más de 300 megavatios y más de 220.000 chips de Nvidia, y se extendió después a Colossus II. Anthropic también compra capacidad a Amazon, Google y Microsoft, que son a la vez sus inversores, competidores y clientes, según el prospecto.
El prospecto advierte que, si no logra asegurar suficiente cómputo, Anthropic enfrenta un riesgo significativo para entrenar y ofrecer sus modelos. La empresa también inició su propia estrategia de centros de datos, llamada Anthropic Direct, con socios que consiguen terreno, energía e instalaciones y a quienes Anthropic alquila la capacidad.
Un resumen de reunión no confirmado alimenta las dudas
El 11 de noviembre circuló en X un resumen de una reunión de Anthropic con analistas, según el cual el contrato con SpaceX no se extendería más allá de mediados de 2027. La nota fue difundida por la cuenta @jukan05 y ni Anthropic ni SpaceX la confirmaron, según el medio Investus.
Elon Musk respondió en esa red que SpaceX estaría dispuesta a recuperar la capacidad, pero que esperaba que ocurriera lo contrario, según el mismo medio. No se informó de ningún aviso de cancelación.
El prospecto actualizado de Anthropic, enmendado el 10 de noviembre, mantiene las mismas condiciones. El primer período sin posibilidad de cancelación termina en enero de 2027.

articles.title: Facebook a espionné les photos prises par 20 millions de smartphones, comment désactiver cet accès par défaut ?
articles.text:
L’autorité italienne de protection des données a infligé le 14 novembre une amende de 805 millions d’euros à Meta Platforms Ireland, la plus lourde de son histoire. En cause, la fonction de Facebook sur Android qui propose, pendant la navigation, des photos et des vidéos puisées dans la galerie locale du téléphone. L’autorité retient qu’environ 20 millions d’utilisateurs italiens y ont été exposés sans avoir donné d’accord spécifique.
Lire aussi : Facebook veut un accès à vos photos personnelles, mais pas pour entraîner l’IA de Meta (pour l’instant)
Comment désactiver la permission qui ouvre vos photos à Facebook ?
Apparue en 2023 et activée par défaut, la fonction affiche au fil de la navigation des suggestions de publication tirées de la pellicule, y compris des fichiers que leur propriétaire n’a jamais mis en ligne. L’application accédait pour cela aux photos, aux vidéos et à leurs métadonnées sur la base d’une autorisation générale couvrant plusieurs usages à la fois, sans que l’information fournie ne mentionne distinctement ces suggestions.
La décision ne coupe rien à elle seule : l‘inversion du réglage par défaut fait partie des mesures imposées à Meta, qui conteste. La fonction reste donc active à ce jour sur les comptes qui ne l’ont jamais désactivée. Pour la couper dans l’application, direction Paramètres et confidentialité, puis Paramètres, rubrique Préférences, page « Suggestions de partage depuis la pellicule ». Désactivez-y les deux options, les suggestions personnalisées tirées de la galerie et celles proposées pendant la navigation sur Facebook. Le verrou le plus étanche se trouve côté système : retirez à Facebook l’autorisation Photos et vidéos dans les réglages d’Android.
L’instruction a été ouverte en juillet 2025 après l’alerte d’une association de consommateurs de Bolzano. Elle s’appuie sur l’article 122 du code italien de la vie privée, transposition de la directive européenne ePrivacy : lire le contenu d’un terminal exige un consentement préalable et éclairé, même sans transfert de données ni préjudice démontré.
Meta plaidait l’incompétence du régulateur italien, l’affaire relevant à ses yeux de l’autorité irlandaise, son interlocutrice habituelle en Europe. L’argument a été rejeté : la directive ePrivacy ne prévoit aucun guichet unique, et chaque autorité nationale peut sanctionner seule sur son territoire.
805 millions d’euros, et 60 jours pour tout débrancher
Le montant représente environ 0,47 % du chiffre d’affaires mondial du groupe. Pour le fixer, l’autorité a retenu le nombre de personnes touchées, un manquement toujours en cours, un précédent de 2019 visant déjà l’entreprise et une coopération jugée faible pendant l’enquête. Les correctifs apportés après la plainte n’ont d’ailleurs touché que les applications mises à jour.
Lire aussi : Nouveau scandale Facebook : des milliers de photos privées ont été compromises
La sanction s’accompagne d’un calendrier serré : un point d’étape sous 30 jours, puis une demande de consentement distincte et spécifique sous 60 jours. Celle-ci devra expliquer l’objectif de la fonction, son accès à la galerie et la manière de la couper. Les suggestions devront aussi repasser en position désactivée par défaut, y compris chez les utilisateurs qui avaient déjà dit oui, avec un compte rendu final sous 90 jours. Passé ce délai sans mise en conformité, la fonction ne pourra plus s’activer pour personne sans consentement valide.
Meta annonce un appel, juge l’amende « disproportionnée » et assure que les suggestions ne fonctionnent qu’après une autorisation de l’utilisateur, modifiable à tout moment dans les réglages. L’enquête n’a pas porté sur l’usage de ces contenus pour entraîner des modèles d’IA, que l’entreprise dément ; le traitement des galeries dans le cloud, introduit cette année, fera l’objet d’un examen séparé.

articles.title: No pagó el alquiler casi cuatro años y la casera no reparó las humedades: la Audiencia rebaja la deuda en un tercio
articles.text:
La inquilina había denunciado los problemas de humedad de su vivienda. Sin embargo, sin que la propietaria hubiese subsanado estos problemas, dejó de abonar el alquiler. Finalmente, la dueña le reclamó 31.340,07 euros por las rentas pendientes (de mayo de 2020 a marzo de 2024). En la Audiencia Provincial de Barcelona se ha confirmado el deber de pago de la inquilina. Sin embargo, han rebajado la cuota a pagar en un tercio. La arrendadora también tuvo algunos problemas de incumplimiento.
El contrato se firmó en noviembre de 2017 y duraba tres años. La renta era de 650 euros inicialmente. En el momento de este proceso era de 666,81 euros.
La propietaria (Patrimonis Bersach, S.L.) ha reclamado los impagados y, por su parte, la inquilina pidió 6.000 euros por daños. En primera instancia, el juzgado ha fallado a favor de la empresa. Las costas las pone a cargo de la arrendataria.
Los problemas de humedad eran insuficientes para dejar de pagar toda la renta
Los técnicos han manifestado las deficiencias, aunque hay algunas discrepancias. El perito de la propiedad ha constatado la presencia de hongos en la pared de la fachada. Ha hablado de “ambiente muy cargado”. Además, ha señalado que falta ventilación. La empresa para la que trabaja ha presupuestado la obra por 1.800 euros.
Por otro lado, la arquitecta técnica (que actuó a petición de la inquilina) hizo un análisis visual. Indicó que había filtraciones del baño de arriba. También destacó que existían humedades por condensación (en sala y dormitorio) y concluyó que no estaba en condiciones mínimas de habitabilidad.
La Audiencia ha considerado que no estaba en condiciones de inhabitabilidad. La inquilina siguió viviendo en el piso y, por eso, no puede quedar liberada de su obligación de pagar.
Asimismo, está comprobado que la propietaria tenía la obligación de subsanar los problemas. En la Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos (artículo 21) se establece que corresponderá al arrendador efectuar todas las obras y reparaciones que sean precisas para mantener la vivienda en estado de habitabilidad, excepto aquellas que sean atribuibles al inquilino.
El magistrado que no está de acuerdo propone una indemnización
Roberto García Ceniceros coincide en que debe pagar la inquilina. Sin embargo, no acepta la rebaja. En su voto particular considera que el deber de reparar “no es mesurable”. Es decir, o se cumple o no. Considera que la ley permite resolver el contrato y pedir una indemnización; sin embargo, no debe cambiar el precio.
Propondría mantener los 31.340,07 euros. Asimismo, aceptaría los 6.000 euros de daño moral. Ambos se compensarían. Quedarían en 25.340,07 euros. Señala que la rebaja (de 10.446,69 euros) es superior a la indemnización solicitada.
